definition_zh: 放弃；抛弃；遗弃；离弃；放纵
definition_en: to leave a person, place or thing behind for good, or to give up a plan, hope or claim completely
core_image: 松开握紧的手，把原本属于自己的东西留在身后
scene: 深夜的站台上，最后一班列车已经开走。The young man had to abandon his broken bicycle beside the tracks.
sceneCN: 这里 abandon 是「丢下、弃置」（第 1 个义项：丢下无法带走的人或物）；句意为年轻人只好把坏掉的自行车丢在轨道旁。

pos.zh: 放弃；抛弃；遗弃；离弃
放纵；无拘束的状态

derivatives.zh: 由动词 abandon 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「放弃；遗弃；放纵」
由动词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「被遗弃的；废弃的；放纵的」
由动词加 -er 构成施动名词，义为「遗弃者」，较少使用

senses.title: To leave a person or place behind
senses.definition: to leave someone or something behind, especially when you should stay with them
senses.definitionCN: 丢下某人或某物离开，尤指在本该留下陪伴时走开
senses.example: The crew abandoned the sinking ship.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们弃船而走。
senses.why: The core image is an open hand: what was held is no longer held, and the person or thing stays behind.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是松开的手：原本握住的不再握住，人和物被留在原地。

senses.title: To give up a plan or attempt
senses.definition: to stop doing something that one has started or intended to do
senses.definitionCN: 停止已经开始或本来打算做的事情
senses.example: They abandoned the plan when the funding fell through.
senses.exampleCN: 资金落空后他们放弃了这个计划。
senses.why: A plan is something the mind holds; letting go of it is the same release as letting go of an object.
senses.whyCN: 计划是心里握着的东西，放下它与放下实物是同一种松开。

senses.title: To desert a duty or post
senses.definition: to leave a job, post or duty without permission, leaving it uncared for
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许离开岗位或职责，使其无人照管
senses.example: He abandoned his post during the night watch.
senses.exampleCN: 他在夜间值守时弃岗而去。
senses.why: A duty is a tie that binds a person to a place; cutting that tie leaves the place unattended.
senses.whyCN: 职责把人系在某个位置上，松开这条系带，位置就无人看守。

senses.title: To let go of hope or belief
senses.definition: to stop believing that something is true or possible, often after repeated failure
senses.definitionCN: 不再相信某事真实或可能，往往发生在屡次失败之后
senses.example: She refused to abandon hope after the third failure.
senses.exampleCN: 第三次失败后她仍不肯放弃希望。
senses.why: Hope is held in the mind like a small object; once the hand opens, the expectation is dropped.
senses.whyCN: 希望像心里握着的小物件，手一松，期待就掉落。

senses.title: To surrender oneself to an emotion
senses.definition: in abandon oneself to, to give way completely to a feeling or activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于 abandon oneself to，表示完全任由某种情绪或活动支配自己
senses.example: The crowd abandoned itself to the music.
senses.exampleCN: 人群纵情于音乐之中。
senses.why: Here the person releases control over the self, so the emotion is what remains holding the scene.
senses.whyCN: 这里人松开的是对自己的控制，于是由情绪来占据整个场面。

senses.title: To relinquish a legal claim
senses.titleCN: 放弃法律上的索赔或财产
senses.definition: to give up a right, claim or piece of property formally, as in insurance or law
senses.definitionCN: 正式放弃权利、索赔或财产，常见于保险与法律语境
senses.example: The insurer abandoned the claim after the deadline passed.
senses.exampleCN: 期限过后保险公司放弃了这项索赔。
senses.why: A claim is a right held by the hand of law; releasing it means the hand no longer holds it.
senses.whyCN: 索赔是法律之手握着的权利，松开它就意味着不再主张。

senses.title: Complete freedom from restraint
senses.definition: a state of acting freely and without self-control, used as a noun in the phrase with abandon
senses.definitionCN: 毫无自我约束地行动的状态，作名词用于 with abandon 这一短语
senses.example: The dancers threw themselves into the piece with abandon.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者们纵情投入这支作品。
senses.why: The noun names the release itself: nothing is held back, so the whole self moves freely.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是松开这个动作本身：什么都不再收着，整个人就自由地动起来。

senses.title: To discontinue a search or activity
senses.definition: to stop an ongoing search, effort or activity because it seems hopeless
senses.definitionCN: 因希望渺茫而停止正在进行的搜寻、努力或活动
senses.example: Rescuers abandoned the search at nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 搜救人员在夜幕降临时停止了搜寻。
senses.why: An effort is a grip on a goal; when the grip is released, the activity simply ends.
senses.whyCN: 努力是对目标的持续抓握，一旦松手，这项活动就自然结束。

intro.en: Abandon came into English from Old French, and its oldest layer is a Frankish word for a public proclamation or command.
intro.cn: abandon 经古法语进入英语，最古老的一层是一个表示「公开宣告、命令」的弗兰克语词。

items.en: The Frankish word *bann is generally reconstructed as a proclamation, summons or command. The deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为弗兰克语 *bann 表示「宣告、召集、命令」，属重构形式；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin recorded bannum for an edict or ban, and bannire for the act of proclaiming or summoning.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 bannum 表示「敕令、禁令」，用 bannire 表示「宣告、召集」。

items.en: The phrase mettre a bandon meant to put something under another person's command, hence to surrender it; from this came the verb abandoner.
items.cn: 古法语短语 mettre a bandon 意为把某物交到他人支配之下，引申为交出、放弃；动词 abandoner 由此而来。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the late fourteenth century. The exact first written date is uncertain, and early spellings vary.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪后期借入这个动词；确切首见年代不确定，早期拼写也不统一。

items.en: The noun use with abandon developed much later, when the idea of a surrendered self became a name for free and unrestrained behaviour.
items.cn: 名词短语 with abandon 出现得晚得多：被交出的自我，后来成了自由无拘行为的名称。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same bann family and two words that merely share the ab- opening; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of leaving and giving up.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 bann 词族的词，以及两个只是同样以 ab- 开头的词；近义组收表示离开与放弃的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of leaving someone or something behind, or the state of being left.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗弃、放弃」或「被遗弃的状态」，由本词加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a person or place that has been left without care.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「被遗弃的、废弃的」，直接由本词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: To send someone away officially; it comes from the same Frankish bann family as abandon.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放逐、驱逐」，与 abandon 同出弗兰克语 bann 词族。

entries.definition: Existing in large amounts; the ab- opening is shared but the root is Latin unda, a wave.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大量的、丰富的」，只是同样以 ab- 开头，词根为拉丁语 unda「波浪」，词源不同。

entries.definition: A rare noun for a person who abandons someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗弃者」，较少使用，由本词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: To leave a person or place in a way that is wrong or illegal, especially a duty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、擅离」，多指背弃责任或岗位，比 abandon 带有更强的失职意味。

entries.definition: To give up someone or something that one is tied to, often used of beliefs and old friends.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、放弃」，语气正式，多用于信念与旧友。

entries.definition: To stop doing something or leave a job, usually by one's own decision.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「停止、辞职」，多指主动决定，不含「抛弃他人」的意味。

entries.definition: To stop resisting and give control to another person or force.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「投降、交出」，强调停止抵抗并把控制权交给对方。

entries.definition: To go away from a place or person; the most neutral verb of departure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「离开」，是最中性的离开说法，不含责备色彩。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Frankish bann root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的弗兰克语 bann 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Bann is a public command: to abandon was to hand a thing over to another's command.
normal.cn: bann 是公开的命令：abandon 原指把东西交到他人支配之下。

normal.en: The same root gives banish, so both words are about putting someone out of reach.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 banish，两个词都与把人或物推到够不着的地方有关。

normal.en: Abandon ship is the fixed order given when a vessel must be left.
normal.cn: abandon ship 是弃船时必须下达的固定命令。

normal.en: With abandon drops all self-control, which is the noun side of the same release.
normal.cn: with abandon 表示丢掉全部自我约束，是同一「松开」动作的名词用法。

normal.en: Abandon hope is the classic phrase for giving up an expectation.
normal.cn: abandon hope 是放弃期待最经典的固定说法。

abstract.en: Picture a hand opening over a railway platform: the bicycle stays, the train leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在站台上松开：自行车留下，列车开走。

abstract.en: The hand can hold a plan, a post, a claim or a hope; opening it works the same way each time.
abstract.cn: 这只手可以握着计划、岗位、索赔或希望；每次松开的方式都一样。

abstract.en: Abandon is not forgetting: the thing left behind is still there, only no longer held.
abstract.cn: abandon 不是遗忘：被留下的东西仍然在，只是不再被握着。

examples.en: The villagers abandoned their homes before the flood arrived.
examples.cn: 洪水到来前村民们离开了家园。

examples.en: She abandoned the argument when she saw it was going nowhere.
examples.cn: 她发现争论毫无进展，便放弃了。

examples.en: The old factory stands abandoned beside the river.
examples.cn: 那座旧工厂废弃在河边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿班登」——班车到站，人却下车走了：丢下、放弃

root: 古法语 abandoner 来自短语 mettre a bandon「交到他人支配之下」，bandon 出自弗兰克语 *bann「宣告、命令」，与中世纪拉丁语 bannum「敕令」同源；*bann 属重构形式，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses describe one release: an object, a plan, a post, a hope, a self, a legal claim, restraint itself, or an ongoing search.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一次松开：松开实物、计划、岗位、希望、自我、法律索赔、约束本身，或一场进行中的搜寻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opens and what it held stays behind while the person moves on.
core.cn: 核心意象：手一松，原本握着的东西留在原地，人继续往前走。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a person, place or thing is left behind when the hand opens.
branches.cn: 实物线：手一松，人、地方或物品被留在身后。

branches.en: THE EFFORT: a plan, an attempt or a search stops because the grip on the goal is released.
branches.cn: 努力线：计划、尝试或搜寻因松开目标而停止。

branches.en: THE DUTY: the tie binding a person to a post is cut, leaving the post unattended.
branches.cn: 职责线：把人系在岗位上的纽带被切断，岗位无人照管。

branches.en: THE INNER STATE: hope is dropped, or control over the self is handed over to a feeling.
branches.cn: 内心线：希望被放下，或对自己的控制被交给某种情绪。

branches.en: THE EXTREME: a legal claim is formally released, and the noun names restraint released altogether.
branches.cn: 两端线：法律索赔被正式放弃，名词则指约束被彻底放开。

intro.en: Abandon is a French borrowing built on a Frankish noun; English later added ordinary suffixes to make its family.
intro.cn: abandon 是建立在弗兰克语名词之上的法语借词；英语后来用普通后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: The relevant Latin records are medieval: bannum and bannire were in use, while the Frankish source itself is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 相关的拉丁记录属中世纪：bannum 与 bannire 均有使用，而弗兰克语源头本身是重构形式。

items.example: The bannum was read aloud in the market square.
items.exampleCN: 敕令在集市广场上被高声宣读。

items.example: The lord could bannire his tenants to assemble.
items.exampleCN: 领主可以召集佃户集合。

items.example: To put a thing a bandon was to hand it over.
items.exampleCN: 把东西置于他人支配之下，就是把它交出去。

items.example: The prefix marks direction toward a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记朝某种状态的方向。

items.example: It forms abandonment.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abandonment。

items.example: It forms abandoned.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abandoned。

items.example: It forms abandoner.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abandoner。

items.example: The city lifted the ban on night markets.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市解除了夜市禁令。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「遗弃；放弃」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「被遗弃的；废弃的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「遗弃者」

definition_zh: 能力；才能；本领；行为能力；财力
definition_en: the power, skill or means that makes it possible for someone to do something
core_image: 一双手稳稳托住重物，说明这双手确实拿得动
scene: 新来的学徒站在车床前，老师傅让他独自车出一个精密零件。Everyone doubted the boy's ability until the finished part passed inspection.
sceneCN: 这里 ability 是「能力、本领」（第 1 个义项：做某事所具备的实际能力）；句意为直到成品通过检验，大家才不再怀疑这个男孩的本事。

pos.zh: 能力；才能；本领
（法律）行为能力；（经济）支付能力

collocations.phrase: to the best of one's ability

derivatives.zh: ability 的形容词对应形式，义为「能够的；有能力的」
由 able 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「能干地；出色地」
由否定前缀 in- 加 ability 构成，义为「无能力；无法」
由否定前缀 dis- 加 ability 构成，义为「残疾；无能力」
由 en- 加 able 构成动词，义为「使能够；使成为可能」

senses.title: The power to do something
senses.definition: the mental or physical power that makes it possible to perform an action
senses.definitionCN: 使人能够完成某项行动的心智或身体力量
senses.example: She has the ability to solve problems under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 她有能力在压力下解决问题。
senses.why: Latin habilitas meant aptness, from habilis, handy: the hand that can actually hold the weight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 habilitas 意为「适宜、灵巧」，出自 habilis「顺手好用的」：能真正托住重量的那只手。

senses.title: A developed talent or skill
senses.titleCN: 经过培养的才能或技能
senses.definition: a particular competence that has been trained and can be relied on
senses.definitionCN: 经过训练、可以依靠的某项具体本领
senses.example: Her ability to read a room made her a good negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 她察言观色的本领使她成为出色的谈判者。
senses.why: The same hand can be trained: a natural aptness becomes a specific skill through practice.
senses.whyCN: 同一双手可以经过训练：天生的灵巧通过练习变成具体技能。

senses.title: Legal capacity
senses.definition: the legal competence to make binding decisions or perform valid acts
senses.definitionCN: 作出有约束力的决定或实施有效行为的法律资格
senses.example: Minors may lack the ability to sign such a contract.
senses.exampleCN: 未成年人可能不具备签署此类合同的资格。
senses.why: Law asks whether the hand is entitled to act, not merely whether it is strong enough.
senses.whyCN: 法律问的是这只手有没有资格行动，而不只是它够不够有力。

senses.title: Financial means
senses.definition: the money or resources needed to pay for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事付款所需的金钱或资源
senses.example: The bank checked his ability to repay the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行核查了他的还贷能力。
senses.why: Means are the material version of power: what the hand can reach with money behind it.
senses.whyCN: 财力是能力在物质层面的版本：手背后有钱，才够得着东西。

senses.title: Intellectual aptitude
senses.definition: the capacity to understand, learn and reason
senses.definitionCN: 理解、学习与推理的能力
senses.example: The test measures ability rather than memorized facts.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试衡量的是理解力，而不是背下来的知识。
senses.why: Aptness sits in the mind as it sits in the hand; the root covers both kinds of grip.
senses.whyCN: 灵巧既在手上，也在心里；这个词根同时涵盖两种握持。

senses.title: Practical competence in work
senses.titleCN: 工作中的实际胜任能力
senses.definition: the demonstrated capacity to carry out a task to an acceptable standard
senses.definitionCN: 把任务做到合格水平所展现出的实际能力
senses.example: He proved his ability by finishing the job alone.
senses.exampleCN: 他独自完成工作，证明了自己的能力。
senses.why: Ability is judged by what the hand produces, not by what it promises.
senses.whyCN: 能力由手做出来的东西来评判，而不是由它的承诺来评判。

senses.title: Power to act or influence
senses.definition: the effective power to bring about change or to affect others
senses.definitionCN: 带来改变或影响他人的实际力量
senses.example: The committee had the ability to block the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会有能力否决这项提案。
senses.why: What the hand grips can be a lever: ability here is the leverage one holds over events.
senses.whyCN: 手握住的也可以是一根杠杆：这个义项指的是对事态所握有的影响力。

senses.title: Best effort in a fixed phrase
senses.titleCN: 固定短语中的「最大努力」
senses.definition: in to the best of one's ability, with as much effort and skill as one can manage
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「to the best of one's ability」，表示尽其所能、竭尽全力
senses.example: She answered every question to the best of her ability.
senses.exampleCN: 她尽其所能回答了每一个问题。
senses.why: The phrase measures the hand against its own limit: all the power there is, used fully.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语是拿手去对照它自身的极限：可用的力量全部用上。

intro.en: Ability goes back to a Latin verb meaning to hold, and the family keeps that sense of a hand that is fit to take something up.
intro.cn: ability 可追溯到表示「握持」的拉丁动词，整个词族保留了「手能拿得起」这一层意味。

items.en: *ghabh- is generally reconstructed as to take or hold; the deeper connections of this root are source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ghabh- 表示「拿、握」，这一词根更早的关联不确定。

items.en: The verb habere meant to have, hold or keep, and it is the source of a large family in Latin and in English.
items.cn: 动词 habere 意为「有、握、保有」，是拉丁语与英语中一大群词的来源。

items.en: The adjective habilis meant handy, apt or fit for use, formed from habere with the suffix -ilis.
items.cn: 形容词 habilis 意为「顺手的、适宜的、合用的」，由 habere 加后缀 -ilis 构成。

items.en: Habilitas named the quality of being apt, and this noun is the direct model for English ability.
items.cn: habilitas 指「适宜、有能力」的性质，这个名词是英语 ability 的直接原型。

items.en: Old French carried the word as ablete and later habilite, with spellings that shifted before the word reached English.
items.cn: 古法语先后以 ablete 与 habilite 的形式使用这个词，拼写在进入英语前有过变化。

items.en: English ability is recorded from the fourteenth century; the exact first date and the early spelling range are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 ability 自十四世纪有记录；确切首见年代与早期拼写范围不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the hab- family and its negative forms; the near-meaning group gathers words for capacity and trained skill.
note.cn: 形近组收 hab- 词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示「容量」与「训练有素的技能」的词。

entries.definition: Having the power or means to do something; the adjective behind ability.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能够的、有能力的」，是 ability 的形容词形式。

entries.definition: In a competent and skilful way; formed from able plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地、出色地」，由 able 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being unable to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「无能力、无法」，由否定前缀 in- 构成。

entries.definition: A condition that limits a person's physical or mental capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「残疾、无能力」，由否定前缀 dis- 构成。

entries.definition: A settled way of behaving; it comes from the same Latin verb habere, to hold.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「习惯」，同样出自拉丁语 habere「握持」，指被长期保持的行为方式。

entries.definition: The power or potential to do something, often of a system or an organization.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力、潜力」，常用于系统或组织，比 ability 更强调可发挥的潜力。

entries.definition: The maximum amount something can hold or produce, or a person's power to understand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「容量、能力」，强调可容纳或可产出的上限。

entries.definition: A learned ability to do something well, especially with the hands or in a craft.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「技能、技艺」，指通过训练获得的熟练本领，多用于手工或专业技艺。

entries.definition: A natural ability to do something well, seen as a gift rather than a trained skill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天赋、才干」，指天生的能力，与后天训练的技能不同。

entries.definition: The ability to do something to a required standard, often in a job.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胜任、称职」，指达到工作要求的能力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin habere root and the collocations the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 habere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Habere is to hold: ability is the hand that can hold the task.
normal.cn: habere 是「握」：ability 就是能握得住任务的那只手。

normal.en: Habilis meant handy, so the same root gives habit, something the mind holds on to.
normal.cn: habilis 意为「顺手的」，同一词根还给出 habit，指心里握持不放的行为。

normal.en: The phrase to the best of one's ability marks the outer limit of that hand.
normal.cn: 短语「to the best of one's ability」标出这只手能达到的外沿。

normal.en: Ability to pay is the money version of the same grip.
normal.cn: ability to pay 是同一握持在金钱上的版本。

normal.en: Inability adds in-, so the hand is no longer able to hold the task.
normal.cn: inability 加上 in-，这只手就不再握得住任务。

abstract.en: Picture a hand testing a weight: it lifts once, steadied, and the lift itself is the ability.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手试着提起重物：稳稳抬起来的那一下，本身就是能力。

abstract.en: The same hand can hold a tool, a idea, a contract or a sum of money.
abstract.cn: 同一只手可以握住工具、想法、合同或一笔钱。

abstract.en: Ability is not a promise but a proven grip: it shows only when the weight actually leaves the ground.
abstract.cn: 能力不是承诺而是被证明的握力：只有重物真的离开地面时才显现。

examples.en: The job requires the ability to work with numbers.
examples.cn: 这份工作需要与数字打交道的本领。

examples.en: He has the ability to explain difficult ideas simply.
examples.cn: 他有把复杂道理讲得浅显的能力。

examples.en: She played the sonata to the best of her ability.
examples.cn: 她尽其所能演奏了那首奏鸣曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额比乐涕」——手一比，活儿就乐着干完：能力、本事

root: 拉丁语 habilitas「适宜、能力」来自 habilis「顺手的、合用的」，而 habilis 又由动词 habere「有、握持」加 -ilis 构成；更早的原始印欧语 *ghabh-「拿、握」属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of ability all measure what a hand can hold: raw power, trained skill, legal capacity, money, understanding, proven competence, leverage, and the limit named by a fixed phrase.
sensesIntro.cn: ability 的八个义项都在衡量一只手能握住什么：原始力量、训练出的技能、法律资格、金钱、理解力、被证明的胜任、影响力，以及固定短语标出的极限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifts a heavy object and holds it steady.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手提起重物，并稳稳托住。

branches.en: THE HAND: physical and mental power to perform an action.
branches.cn: 手与心线：完成行动的体力与心智力量。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: trained skill and competence proven by finished work.
branches.cn: 技艺线：经训练的技能，由完成的工作证明。

branches.en: THE LAW: legal capacity to act and to bind oneself.
branches.cn: 法律线：实施行为与受约束的法律资格。

branches.en: THE LEVER: money and influence extend what the hand can move.
branches.cn: 杠杆线：金钱与影响力放大手能搬动的东西。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: the fixed phrase measures the hand against its own outer edge.
branches.cn: 极限线：固定短语拿这只手对照它自身的外沿。

intro.en: Ability is a Latin noun of quality built on an adjective of fitness, which in turn rests on the verb to hold.
intro.cn: ability 是一个表示性质的名词，建立在表示「合用」的形容词之上，而形容词又依托「握持」这一动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere, habilis and habilitas are all recorded; only the Indo-European root before them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere、habilis 与 habilitas 均有文献记录，它们之前的印欧词根才是重构形式。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的词根。

items.example: It forms habilis from habere.
items.exampleCN: 它使 habere 构成 habilis。

items.example: A habilis tool fits the hand that uses it.
items.exampleCN: 合用的工具正好贴合使用它的手。

items.example: It forms habilitas.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 habilitas。

items.example: The noun names the quality of being fit.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指「合用」这一性质。

items.example: It forms ability from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁词干构成 ability。

items.example: It forms inability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inability。

items.example: It forms disability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 disability。

items.example: It forms enable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 enable。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「能够的；有能力的」
由 in- 加本词构成，义为「无能力」
由 dis- 加本词构成，义为「残疾；无能力」
由 en- 加 able 构成，义为「使能够」
由 able 加 -ly 构成，义为「能干地」

definition_zh: 能够的；有能力的；能干的；体格健全的
definition_en: having the power, skill, means or opportunity to do something
core_image: 肩膀挺得住，手上有劲，能接下这副担子
scene: 车间里一台老机器突然停转，几个人围着束手无策。Only the quiet apprentice was able to restart it before the shift ended.
sceneCN: 这里 able 是「能够做到」（第 1 个义项：具备做某事的能力）；句意为只有在旁边不出声的学徒能在交班前把机器重新启动。

pos.zh: 能够的；有能力的；能干的
（组合形式）体格健全的；熟练的

derivatives.zh: 由 able 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「能干地；出色地」
由 able 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「能力；才能」
由 en- 加 able 构成动词，义为「使能够；使成为可能」
由 dis- 加 able 构成动词，义为「使丧失能力；使无法使用」
由否定前缀 un- 加 able 构成，义为「不能的；不会的」

senses.title: Having the power to do something
senses.definition: having the physical or mental power to carry out an action
senses.definitionCN: 具备完成某项行动的体力或心智力量
senses.example: She was able to lift the box on her own.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个人就能抬起那只箱子。
senses.why: Latin habilis described something handy: able is the person whose hand is fit for the task.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 habilis 形容东西顺手好用：able 就是那只手适合这项任务的人。

senses.title: Having the means or opportunity
senses.definition: having the resources, chance or freedom needed to do something
senses.definitionCN: 具备做某事所需的资源、机会或自由
senses.example: We were able to finish early because the train came on time.
senses.exampleCN: 因为列车准点，我们得以提前完成。
senses.why: The hand is fit, and the road is open: ability also depends on circumstances outside the body.
senses.whyCN: 手足够合用，路也畅通：能力还取决于身体之外的境况。

senses.title: Skilful and competent
senses.definition: having more than ordinary skill or competence in a job or craft
senses.definitionCN: 在工作或手艺上具备超出一般水平的技能
senses.example: The firm hired an able accountant to clean up its books.
senses.exampleCN: 公司请了一位能干的会计来整理账目。
senses.why: A hand that is fit can also be practised: the adjective then praises the quality of the work.
senses.whyCN: 合用的手也能经过练习：这时这个形容词称赞的是工作的质量。

senses.title: Legally competent
senses.definition: having legal capacity or authority to act in a particular matter
senses.definitionCN: 在特定事务上具有法律行为能力或权限
senses.example: He is able to sign the lease once he turns eighteen.
senses.exampleCN: 他满十八岁后便有资格签署这份租约。
senses.why: Law tests whether the hand is entitled to make the mark, not whether it is strong.
senses.whyCN: 法律检验的是这只手有没有资格落笔，而不是它有没有力气。

senses.title: Physically fit and strong
senses.definition: sound in body and fit for physical work, as in able-bodied
senses.definitionCN: 身体健全、能胜任体力劳动，用于 able-bodied 等说法
senses.example: All able-bodied residents helped clear the road.
senses.exampleCN: 所有体格健全的居民都来帮忙清理道路。
senses.why: The concrete root meaning: a body that can take the load without giving way.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的词根义：一个扛得住重压而不会垮的身体。

senses.title: Capable of being affected
senses.definition: open to a particular influence or treatment, as in able to be changed
senses.definitionCN: 可受到某种影响或处理，如 able to be changed 之类的结构
senses.example: The material is able to withstand high heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料能够承受高温。
senses.why: Fit for use works both ways: what a hand can hold can also be held and changed by something else.
senses.whyCN: 「合用」是双向的：手能握住东西，东西也能被别的力量握住并改变。

senses.title: The suffix meaning can be done
senses.definition: in the ending -able, forming adjectives that mean capable of receiving the action
senses.definitionCN: 用于词尾 -able，构成表示「可以被……的」形容词
senses.example: The ending turns read into readable.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 read 变成 readable。
senses.why: The same idea of fitness became a productive ending: a thing able to be carried, read or washed.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「合用」观念变成了能产的词尾：能被搬动、阅读或清洗的东西。

senses.title: A rating of a ship's crew
senses.definition: in able seaman, the official rating of an experienced sailor
senses.definitionCN: 用于 able seaman，指熟练水手的正式等级
senses.example: He served as an able seaman for six years.
senses.exampleCN: 他当了六年熟练水手。
senses.why: A crew rates a hand by what it can do at sea, so able became the word for a qualified sailor.
senses.whyCN: 船队按一个人在海上能做些什么来评级，able 于是成了合格水手的称谓。

intro.en: Able came through Old French from the Latin adjective for handy, and its family includes ability, enable and disable.
intro.cn: able 经古法语来自表示「顺手合用」的拉丁形容词，其词族包括 ability、enable 与 disable。

items.en: *ghabh- is generally reconstructed as to take or hold; deeper links are source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为原始印欧语 *ghabh- 表示「拿、握」，更早的关联不确定。

items.en: Habere meant to have or hold and supplied the stem for habilis.
items.cn: habere 意为「有、握持」，为 habilis 提供词干。

items.en: Habilis meant handy, apt or fit, said of tools and later of people.
items.cn: habilis 意为「顺手的、适宜的、合用的」，先说工具，后来说人。

items.en: Old French used able and hable side by side, and both spellings circulated before English settled on able.
items.cn: 古法语 able 与 hable 两种拼写同时通行，英语最终才定形为 able。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English from the fourteenth century; exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个形容词自十四世纪在英语中有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The ending -able became highly productive, and able-bodied and able seaman fixed two specialist uses.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 变得极为能产，able-bodied 与 able seaman 则固定下两个专门用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the hab- family with its prefixed opposites; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of competence and fitness.
note.cn: 形近组收 hab- 词族及其加前缀的相反形式；近义组收表示「胜任」与「适合」的形容词。

entries.definition: In a skilful, competent manner; able plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地」，由 able 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The noun for the power or skill to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「能力、才能」，是 able 的名词对应形式。

entries.definition: To give someone the power or means to do something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使能够」，由 en- 加 able 构成。

entries.definition: To make someone or something unable to act or work.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使丧失能力、使无法运转」，由 dis- 加 able 构成。

entries.definition: Not having the power or means to do something; the direct negative of able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不能的、不会的」，是 able 的直接否定形式。

entries.definition: Having the ability or potential to do something, often with room to develop.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有能力的、有潜力的」，常含「尚有发展余地」之意。

entries.definition: Having enough skill or knowledge to do a job properly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「胜任的、称职的」，强调达到工作要求。

entries.definition: Trained and practised in a particular activity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟练的、有技术的」，强调经过训练。

entries.definition: Suitable, or in good physical condition for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「合适的、健康的」，强调身体状况或适应性。

entries.definition: Having the official training or legal right needed for a role.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有资格的、合格的」，强调正式的资质。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin habilis root and the two fixed uses of able.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 habilis 词根，以及 able 的两个固定用法。

normal.en: Habilis is handy: an able worker is one whose hands fit the job.
normal.cn: habilis 是「顺手」：able 的劳动者就是手正好合得上这份活的人。

normal.en: Able-bodied joins the adjective to a body that can take the load.
normal.cn: able-bodied 把这个形容词接到一副扛得住重量的身体上。

normal.en: An able seaman is a sailor rated by proven skill at sea.
normal.cn: able seaman 是在海上以实际技能评定等级的熟练水手。

normal.en: The ending -able turns verbs into things that can be done: readable, washable.
normal.cn: 词尾 -able 把动词变成「可以被做」的东西：readable、washable。

normal.en: Enable adds en- to make the hand fit; disable removes the fitness.
normal.cn: enable 用 en- 使手合用；disable 则拿掉这份合用。

abstract.en: Picture a shoulder under a yoke: able means the shoulder does not sag when the load comes.
abstract.cn: 想象一副肩膀顶在轭下：able 意味着重量压来时肩膀不塌。

abstract.en: Fitness can belong to a hand, a tool, a ship's rating or a legal signer.
abstract.cn: 「合用」可以属于一只手、一件工具、一个船员等级或一位合法签署人。

abstract.en: Able is always relative: it answers the question fit for what, and under what conditions.
abstract.cn: able 总是相对的：它回答的是「对什么合用、在什么条件下合用」。

examples.en: He was able to repair the pump without any help.
examples.cn: 他不用别人帮忙就能修好水泵。

examples.en: She is an able organizer who keeps every detail in view.
examples.cn: 她是一位能干的组织者，每个细节都看在眼里。

examples.en: The bridge is able to carry heavy trucks.
examples.cn: 这座桥能够承受重型卡车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶步」——抬脚就能迈过去：有能力做到

root: 拉丁语 habilis「顺手的、适宜的」由动词 habere「有、握持」加 -ilis 构成，经古法语 able/hable 进入英语；原始印欧语 *ghabh-「拿、握」属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of able all apply one idea of fitness: to a task, to circumstances, to a craft, to the law, to the body, to being acted upon, to the suffix -able, and to a sailor's rating.
sensesIntro.cn: able 的八个义项都在使用同一个「合用」观念：对任务、对境况、对手艺、对法律、对身体、对被作用、对词尾 -able，以及对水手等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shoulder takes the weight of a yoke without sagging.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副肩膀扛住轭的重量而没有塌下去。

branches.en: THE BODY: the hand and the frame are strong enough for the task.
branches.cn: 身体线：手与骨架都足够强壮，能担起任务。

branches.en: THE CIRCUMSTANCE: resources open the way, and materials can also withstand treatment.
branches.cn: 境况线：资源打开通路，材料也能承受处理。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: practised skill turns fitness into work of high quality.
branches.cn: 手艺线：熟练的技能把合用变成高质量的工作。

branches.en: THE LAW AND THE SEA: both rate a hand by official entitlement or proven rating.
branches.cn: 法律与海上线：两者都按正式资格或已证明的等级来评定一个人。

branches.en: THE ENDING: the same fitness becomes the productive suffix -able.
branches.cn: 词尾线：同一个「合用」变成能产的词尾 -able。

intro.en: Able rests on a Latin adjective of fitness; English builds the rest of the family with en-, dis-, un- and the endings -ly and -ity.
intro.cn: able 依托一个表示「合用」的拉丁形容词；英语用 en-、dis-、un- 以及 -ly、-ity 等词尾构建其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin habere and habilis are recorded; the Indo-European root behind them is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 habere 与 habilis 有记录，它们背后的印欧词根是重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供这一词族的词干。

items.example: It forms habilis.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 habilis。

items.example: The adjective describes what fits the hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述贴合手的东西。

items.example: It forms enable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 enable。

items.example: It forms disable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 disable。

items.example: It forms unable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unable。

items.example: It forms ably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ably。

items.example: It forms ability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ability。

items.example: It forms readable and washable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 readable 与 washable。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「能干地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「能力」
由 en- 加本词构成，义为「使能够」
由 dis- 加本词构成，义为「使无法」
由 un- 加本词构成，义为「不能的」

definition_zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的；不合规范的
definition_en: different from what is usual, expected or considered normal, often in a way that causes concern
core_image: 一把本该方正的木尺歪了一角，量出来的线全跟着偏
scene: 体检报告上有一项指标远远超出参考范围，医生反复看了两遍。The scan showed an abnormal growth in the patient's left lung.
sceneCN: 这里 abnormal 是「异常的、偏离正常范围的」（第 2 个义项：医学指标超出正常范围）；句意为扫描显示病人左肺有一处异常增生。

pos.zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的
反常的人或事物（较少使用）

derivatives.zh: 由 abnormal 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「异常地；反常地」
由 abnormal 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「异常；畸形」
abnormal 的肯定对应形式，义为「正常的；标准的」

senses.title: Departing from what is usual
senses.definition: differing from the ordinary or expected pattern of things
senses.definitionCN: 与平常或预期的模式不同
senses.example: An abnormal silence fell over the usually noisy hall.
senses.exampleCN: 平日喧闹的大厅里出现了一阵反常的寂静。
senses.why: Latin norma was a carpenter's square, the rule by which things are measured straight; ab- takes the measure away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 norma 是本工用的曲尺，是量正东西的准绳；ab- 把这条准绳拿走，量出来的就偏了。

senses.title: Outside the medical reference range
senses.titleCN: 医学指标超出正常范围
senses.definition: of a test value or body condition, falling outside the range considered healthy
senses.definitionCN: 检查数值或身体状况落在健康范围之外
senses.example: The blood test returned an abnormal reading for iron.
senses.exampleCN: 血液检查的铁含量读数异常。
senses.why: Medicine applies the same square to the body: a reading off the healthy line is flagged as abnormal.
senses.whyCN: 医学把同一把尺子用在身体上：读数偏离健康线，就被标为异常。

senses.title: Socially or morally deviant
senses.definition: departing from accepted social or moral standards in a way others notice
senses.definitionCN: 偏离被接受的社会或道德标准，并为他人察觉
senses.example: Neighbours called his abnormal habits a public nuisance.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居把他反常的习惯称为公害。
senses.why: The square is also a social rule; behaviour that will not line up with it is judged deviant.
senses.whyCN: 这把尺子也是社会规范；对不齐的行为就会被判为越轨。

senses.title: Unusually large or small in degree
senses.definition: markedly greater or smaller in amount or intensity than is typical
senses.definitionCN: 在数量或强度上明显大于或小于通常水平
senses.example: An abnormal demand for ice cleared every shelf in the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 异常旺盛的冰块需求把店里的货架清空了。
senses.why: Beyond the rule is not only wrong but extreme: the measure has moved far from the centre.
senses.whyCN: 超出准绳不只是错，还意味着极端：刻度已经离中心很远。

senses.title: Irregular in structure or form
senses.definition: having a shape, structure or pattern that departs from the regular form
senses.definitionCN: 形状、结构或图案偏离规则形态
senses.example: The crystal showed an abnormal pattern under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 这块晶体在显微镜下呈现不规则的花样。
senses.why: Norma is literally a shape-making square, so a form that will not square up is abnormal.
senses.whyCN: norma 本义就是定形的曲尺，形状对不上这把尺，就是异常。

senses.title: Statistically atypical
senses.definition: lying far from the centre of a distribution or outside the expected range of data
senses.definitionCN: 远离分布中心或落在预期数据范围之外
senses.example: The model flagged an abnormal spike in traffic at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 模型标出了午夜流量的异常尖峰。
senses.why: The rule becomes a statistical baseline; a point off that baseline is what the model calls abnormal.
senses.whyCN: 准绳变成统计基线；偏离基线的点，模型就称为异常。

senses.title: Worrying in behaviour or mood
senses.titleCN: 行为或情绪上令人担忧
senses.definition: showing behaviour or emotional responses that suggest a disorder needing attention
senses.definitionCN: 表现出提示某种障碍、需要关注的行为或情绪反应
senses.example: The teacher reported abnormal withdrawal in the child.
senses.exampleCN: 老师报告了这个孩子反常的退缩表现。
senses.why: When behaviour falls away from the expected line, the observer fears something is wrong inside.
senses.whyCN: 当行为偏离预期的那条线，观察者就会担心里面出了问题。

senses.title: Outside the normal course of development
senses.definition: of growth or development, following a course that is not the usual one
senses.definitionCN: 在生长或发展上走了一条并非通常的路线
senses.example: The doctor monitored the child's abnormal development closely.
senses.exampleCN: 医生密切监测这个孩子异常发育的情况。
senses.why: Development has an expected line of growth; a branch off that line is measured against the same square.
senses.whyCN: 发育有一条预期的生长线；从这条线岔出去，同样要拿这把尺来量。

intro.en: Abnormal is a modern word built on Latin norma, the square used to keep lines straight, and it has a Greek cousin in anomaly.
intro.cn: abnormal 是一个建立在拉丁语 norma「定线曲尺」之上的现代词，它在希腊语一侧还有个近亲 anomaly。

items.en: Norma meant a carpenter's square and, figuratively, a rule or standard. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: norma 指木工的曲尺，引申为规则与标准；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Normalis meant made according to the square, hence regular or standard; English normal comes from it.
items.cn: normalis 意为「按曲尺做成的」，引申为规则的、标准的；英语 normal 由此而来。

items.en: Greek anomalos meant uneven or irregular, and it produced the separate English word anomaly.
items.cn: 希腊语 anomalos 意为「不平整的、不规则的」，后来产生另一个英语词 anomaly。

items.en: French formed anormal in the early nineteenth century; some accounts link it to the Greek word rather than to Latin norma.
items.cn: 法语在十九世纪初造出 anormal；有说法认为它上承希腊语那个词，而非拉丁语 norma，两种解释并存。

items.en: English abnormal appears in the 1810s and 1820s. The exact first date is uncertain, and the word spread with medical and statistical writing.
items.cn: 英语 abnormal 见于十九世纪一十至二十年代；确切首见年代不确定，这个词随医学与统计写作传播开来。

items.en: The word moved from anatomy and medicine into psychology, statistics and ordinary speech about behaviour.
items.cn: 这个词从解剖学与医学走进心理学、统计学，以及日常对行为的谈论。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on norma, including one word that hides the same root; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of deviation.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 norma 之上的形式，其中包括一个隐藏着同一词根的词；近义组收表示「偏离」的形容词。

entries.definition: In an abnormal manner or to an abnormal degree.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「异常地、反常地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being abnormal, or an abnormal feature.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常、畸形」，由本词加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: Conforming to the usual standard; the positive counterpart of abnormal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正常的、标准的」，是 abnormal 的肯定对应词，同出 norma。

entries.definition: Extremely large; it comes from Latin enormis, literally outside the square.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，出自拉丁语 enormis「离开曲尺的」，与本词共享 norma 词根。

entries.definition: Something that deviates from the standard; it comes from Greek anomalos, not from Latin norma.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常事物」，出自希腊语 anomalos；与 abnormal 意义接近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: Not common or ordinary; neutral and without the concern that abnormal can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不寻常的」，语气中性，不像 abnormal 那样常带担忧。

entries.definition: Not representative of a type or group; common in medical and technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非典型的」，多用于医学与技术写作。

entries.definition: Not following a regular pattern in time, shape or occurrence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不规则的」，强调时间、形状或出现方式上没有规律。

entries.definition: Departing from the accepted course, especially in biology or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「偏离常规的」，语气正式，多用于生物学或行为描述。

entries.definition: A very unusual event or thing; informal and often harsh when applied to people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「反常的（事物）」，口语用词，用于人时带有冒犯意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin norma, the square that keeps lines true.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 norma，也就是让线条保持平直的那把曲尺。

normal.en: Norma is a square: normal lines follow it, abnormal lines do not.
normal.cn: norma 是一把曲尺：正常的线顺着它走，反常的线对不上它。

normal.en: Normal is the positive twin; abnormal simply puts ab- in front.
normal.cn: normal 是它的肯定孪生词；abnormal 只是在前面加了 ab-。

normal.en: Enormous hides the same square: enormis meant outside the rule, and great things seemed to be outside it.
normal.cn: enormous 藏着同一把尺：enormis 意为「离开规则的」，巨大的东西看起来就在规则之外。

normal.en: Abnormal psychology studies behaviour measured against a social baseline.
normal.cn: abnormal psychology 研究的是拿社会基线来衡量的行为。

normal.en: An abnormal test result is a reading that will not lie on the healthy line.
normal.cn: abnormal 的检查结果就是落不到健康线上的读数。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a drawing: one line bends away, and the eye finds it at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横放在图样上：有一条线弯开了，眼睛立刻就能找到它。

abstract.en: The same ruler measures bodies, behaviour, crystals and data.
abstract.cn: 同一把尺可以量身体、行为、晶体和数据。

abstract.en: Abnormal is not simply rare: it means far enough from the line that someone has to take notice.
abstract.cn: abnormal 不只是稀少：它意味着离那条线远到必须有人注意。

examples.en: The doctor ordered more tests after an abnormal result.
examples.cn: 结果异常后，医生安排了更多检查。

examples.en: Such abnormal weather is rare in this region.
examples.cn: 这样的异常天气在本地区很罕见。

examples.en: The machine shut down when it detected abnormal pressure.
examples.cn: 机器检测到异常压力后停机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布诺莫」——尺子一歪，量出来的全是怪数：反常、异常

root: 现代英语 abnormal 由否定前缀 ab- 加 normal 构成；normal 出自拉丁语 norma「木工曲尺、准则」与 normalis「按曲尺做成的」。希腊语 anomalos「不平整」是另一条词源线，产生英语 anomaly。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of abnormal all measure something against a line: ordinary expectation, a healthy range, a social rule, a normal degree, a regular shape, a statistical baseline, expected behaviour, and a normal course of growth.
sensesIntro.cn: abnormal 的八个义项都在拿某样东西去对一条线：通常预期、健康范围、社会规范、正常程度、规则形状、统计基线、预期行为，以及正常发育路线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square is laid on a drawing and one line refuses to follow it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把曲尺放在图样上，有一条线偏偏不肯顺着它。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: ordinary expectation and ordinary degree are the baseline the word departs from.
branches.cn: 模式线：通常预期与通常程度是这个词偏离的基线。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: medicine and statistics both read a value that falls outside the accepted range.
branches.cn: 数值线：医学与统计都在读一个落在可接受范围之外的数值。

branches.en: THE PERSON: social rule and emotional expectation judge behaviour that worries others.
branches.cn: 人的线：社会规范与情绪预期都在评判令他人担忧的行为。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the square is literal here, and a form that will not square up is irregular.
branches.cn: 形状线：这里曲尺是本义，对不上尺的形状就是不规则的。

branches.en: THE COURSE: development has a line of its own, and a branch away from it is abnormal.
branches.cn: 进程线：发育有自己的路线，从这条线岔出去就是异常。

intro.en: Abnormal is a prefix plus a Latin-derived adjective; English adds -ly and -ity to complete the set.
intro.cn: abnormal 是一个前缀加一个来自拉丁语的形容词；英语再加 -ly 与 -ity 补全这一组词。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma and normalis are recorded; the deeper origin of norma is source uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma 与 normalis 有文献记录，norma 更早的来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks distance from the rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记与规则的偏离。

items.example: The square kept the timber straight.
items.exampleCN: 曲尺让木料保持平直。

items.example: A normalis wall stands true.
items.exampleCN: 按准绳砌的墙是正的。

items.example: It forms normal and abnormal.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 normal 与 abnormal。

items.example: It forms abnormally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormally。

items.example: It forms abnormality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormality。

items.meaningCN: 离开准则的，因而巨大的
items.example: The word produced English enormous.
items.exampleCN: 这个词产生了英语 enormous。

items.example: It produced the separate word anomaly.
items.exampleCN: 它产生了另一个词 anomaly。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「异常地」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「异常；畸形」
与本词同根的肯定形式，义为「正常的」

definition_zh: 异常；反常；畸形；异常事物
definition_en: the state of being abnormal, or a feature, condition or event that departs from the normal
core_image: 一排整齐的砖里夹着一块歪斜的，一眼就看出不对
scene: 产检的屏幕上，医生停在一处反复放大查看。The scan revealed a small abnormality in the baby's heart.
sceneCN: 这里 abnormality 是「异常结构、畸形」（第 2 个义项：身体结构上的异常）；句意为扫描发现婴儿心脏有一处小的异常。

pos.zh: 异常；反常；畸形
异常的事物或现象

derivatives.zh: abnormality 的形容词对应形式，义为「反常的；异常的」
由 abnormal 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「异常地」
与本词同根的肯定形式，义为「正常的；标准的」

senses.title: The state of being abnormal
senses.definition: the condition of differing from what is usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 与通常或预期情况不同的状态
senses.example: The report noted the abnormality of the reading without explaining it.
senses.exampleCN: 报告指出了读数的异常，却没有解释原因。
senses.why: The noun names the state itself, the quality that the adjective abnormal describes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指状态本身，也就是形容词 abnormal 所描述的那种性质。

senses.title: A physical malformation
senses.definition: a structural defect or unusual formation in a body part or organ
senses.definitionCN: 身体部位或器官上的结构缺陷或不寻常形态
senses.example: The ultrasound found an abnormality in the kidney.
senses.exampleCN: 超声检查发现肾脏有一处畸形。
senses.why: Medicine turns the abstract state into a countable thing: one specific place where the body departs from its form.
senses.whyCN: 医学把抽象状态变成可数的事物：身体偏离应有形态的某一个具体位置。

senses.title: An anomalous test value
senses.definition: a measurement or finding that falls outside the healthy reference range
senses.definitionCN: 落在健康参考范围之外的测量值或发现
senses.example: The lab flagged two abnormalities in the blood sample.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室标出了血样中的两处异常。
senses.why: A reading away from the healthy line is packaged as a countable abnormality for the report.
senses.whyCN: 偏离健康线的读数被打包成报告里可数的「异常项」。

senses.title: Irregularity in behaviour
senses.definition: a pattern of behaviour that departs from what is expected or accepted
senses.definitionCN: 偏离预期或被接受标准的行为模式
senses.example: Teachers were trained to notice behavioural abnormalities early.
senses.exampleCN: 教师们受过训练，要及早注意行为上的反常。
senses.why: Behaviour can also be measured against a social line, and a deviation becomes a named abnormality.
senses.whyCN: 行为同样可以对着社会那条线来衡量，偏离就被命名为异常。

senses.title: A statistical deviation
senses.definition: a data point or pattern that lies far from the expected distribution
senses.definitionCN: 远离预期分布的数据点或模式
senses.example: The system reported an abnormality in the overnight figures.
senses.exampleCN: 系统报告了夜间数据中的一处异常。
senses.why: Once a baseline is drawn, anything far from it can be listed as an abnormality in the data.
senses.whyCN: 基线一旦画出，离它很远的东西就能被列为数据中的异常。

senses.title: A genetic or chromosomal defect
senses.definition: an alteration in genes or chromosomes that departs from the typical pattern
senses.definitionCN: 基因或染色体上偏离典型模式的改变
senses.example: The clinic screens for chromosomal abnormalities before birth.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在出生前筛查染色体异常。
senses.why: The blueprint has a standard form; a change in that form is the most literal kind of abnormality.
senses.whyCN: 蓝图有标准形态；这一形态发生改变，就是最本义的异常。

senses.title: A structural defect in materials
senses.definition: an irregularity in the structure of a material or object that may weaken it
senses.definitionCN: 材料或物件结构上的不规则，可能使其强度下降
senses.example: Inspectors found an abnormality in the weld.
senses.exampleCN: 检验员发现焊缝处有一处结构异常。
senses.why: The square measures metal as it measures bodies: a place that will not line up is a defect.
senses.whyCN: 曲尺量金属和量身体一样：对不齐的地方就是缺陷。

senses.title: A rare or strange occurrence
senses.definition: an event or thing that is so unusual that it stands out from ordinary experience
senses.definitionCN: 罕见到足以从日常经验中凸显出来的事件或事物
senses.example: The sudden snow in June was called a weather abnormality.
senses.exampleCN: 六月突降大雪被称作天气异常。
senses.why: The countable noun can leave the body and the lab: any departure from the ordinary course can be one.
senses.whyCN: 这个可数名词可以离开身体与实验室：任何偏离寻常进程的事物都能算一处异常。

intro.en: Abnormality is the noun of quality built on abnormal, which in turn rests on the Latin square called norma.
intro.cn: abnormality 是由 abnormal 构成的表性质名词，而 abnormal 又依托拉丁语那把名为 norma 的曲尺。

items.en: Norma was a carpenter's square and, by extension, a rule or standard. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: norma 是木工曲尺，引申为规则与标准；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Normalis meant according to the square, and English normal developed from it.
items.cn: normalis 意为「按曲尺做成的」，英语 normal 由此发展而来。

items.en: The adjective abnormal appeared in the early nineteenth century, first in scientific and medical writing.
items.cn: 形容词 abnormal 在十九世纪初出现，最初见于科学与医学写作。

items.en: The noun abnormality followed soon after, when writers needed a countable name for specific defects and deviations.
items.cn: 名词 abnormality 紧随其后出现，因为写作者需要一个可数的名称来指具体的缺陷与偏离。

items.en: The word now covers medicine, genetics, engineering and statistics, wherever a baseline can be drawn.
items.cn: 如今这个词覆盖医学、遗传学、工程与统计，凡能画出基线的领域都可使用。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the norm- family; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for defects and deviations.
note.cn: 形近组收 norm- 词族；近义组收表示缺陷与偏离的名词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning departing from the normal; abnormality is its noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「异常的」，abnormality 是其名词形式。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in an abnormal way or degree.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「异常地」，由 abnormal 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Conforming to the standard; the opposite pole of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「正常的」，与本词处于相反的两端。

entries.definition: A standard or expected level of behaviour; the bare noun behind the family.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规范、标准」，是这一词族最基础的名词。

entries.definition: A deviation from the standard; close in meaning but from Greek anomalos.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常事物」，意义接近，但出自希腊语 anomalos，词源不同。

entries.definition: Something that deviates from what is standard or expected.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常、反常事物」，是 abnormality 最常用的近义词。

entries.definition: A fault or imperfection in something that makes it less than complete.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺陷、瑕疵」，强调事物不完整或有毛病。

entries.definition: A departure from a regular pattern or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不规则、违规」，强调与规律或规则不符。

entries.definition: A badly formed part of the body, present from birth.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「畸形」，多指先天形成的身体结构缺陷。

entries.definition: A difference from an expected course, value or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「偏离、偏差」，强调与预期路线或数值的差距。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real norma root and the medical and technical phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 norma 词根，以及这个词实际出现的医学与技术搭配。

normal.en: Norma is the square, so an abnormality is a place that will not square up.
normal.cn: norma 是曲尺，abnormality 就是一处对不上尺的地方。

normal.en: Abnormal is the adjective, abnormality the countable thing it points at.
normal.cn: abnormal 是形容词，abnormality 是它指出的那个可数事物。

normal.en: A congenital abnormality is one present from birth, before any habit could form.
normal.cn: congenital abnormality 指出生就有的异常，习惯还来不及形成。

normal.en: Chromosomal abnormality moves the image to the blueprint of the body.
normal.cn: chromosomal abnormality 把意象移到身体的那张蓝图上。

normal.en: Inspectors look for structural abnormalities in welds and bones alike.
normal.cn: 检验员在焊缝和骨骼里找的都是结构异常。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of straight bricks with one brick tilted: the eye stops there.
abstract.cn: 想象一面整齐的砖墙里有一块砖歪了：目光会停在那里。

abstract.en: The tilted brick can be in a body, a gene, a weld or a data table.
abstract.cn: 这块歪砖可以出现在身体、基因、焊缝或数据表里。

abstract.en: Abnormality is countable: each departure gets its own name in a report.
abstract.cn: abnormality 是可数的：报告里每一处偏离都有自己的名字。

examples.en: The scan detected an abnormality near the joint.
examples.cn: 扫描在关节附近发现一处异常。

examples.en: Doctors monitor children for growth abnormalities.
examples.cn: 医生监测儿童是否存在发育异常。

examples.en: There was no abnormality in the final inspection.
examples.cn: 最终检验中没有发现异常。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布诺马利提」——墙里那块歪砖：异常、畸形

root: abnormality 由 abnormal 加 -ity 构成；abnormal 由 ab- 加 normal 构成，normal 出自拉丁语 norma「曲尺、准则」与 normalis「按曲尺做成的」；norma 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of abnormality all give a name to one place where something refuses to line up: a state, a body part, a test value, behaviour, data, genes, a material, or a rare event.
sensesIntro.cn: abnormality 的八个义项都在为某一处「对不上线」命名：状态、身体部位、检查数值、行为、数据、基因、材料，或罕见事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tilted brick stands out in a wall of straight ones.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排笔直的砖里，一块歪砖格外显眼。

branches.en: THE STATE: the bare quality of departing from the standard.
branches.cn: 状态线：偏离标准的性质本身。

branches.en: THE BODY: a malformation or a genetic change names the defect in the flesh.
branches.cn: 身体线：畸形或基因改变为肉体上的缺陷命名。

branches.en: THE READING: test values and data points that fall outside the range.
branches.cn: 读数线：落在范围之外的检查值与数据点。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE WORLD: behaviour and rare events are judged against expectation.
branches.cn: 外部世界线：行为与罕见事件要对照预期来评判。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: a weld or structure that will not square up is a defect.
branches.cn: 材料线：对不上尺的焊缝或结构就是缺陷。

intro.en: Abnormality chains a negative prefix, a Latin-based adjective and a noun ending; each piece marks distance from a standard.
intro.cn: abnormality 把否定前缀、源自拉丁语的形容词与名词词尾连成一串，每个部件都标记与标准的距离。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma and normalis are recorded, so only norma's deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma 与 normalis 均有记录，只有 norma 更早的来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks distance from the rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记与规则的偏离。

items.example: The square set the standard.
items.exampleCN: 曲尺设定了标准。

items.example: It produced English normal.
items.exampleCN: 它产生了英语 normal。

items.example: It forms abnormal.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormal。

items.example: It forms abnormality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormality。

items.example: It forms abnormally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormally。

items.example: The norm varies between cultures.
items.exampleCN: 规范在不同文化之间会有差异。

items.example: It forms normalization.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 normalization。

derivatives.zh: 本词的形容词形式，义为「反常的」
由 abnormal 加 -ly 构成，义为「异常地」
与本词同根的肯定形式，义为「正常的」

definition_zh: 在船（飞机、火车）上；上船（飞机、火车）
definition_en: on or onto a ship, aircraft, train, or other vehicle
core_image: 脚跨过舷梯，落在摇晃的甲板上
scene: 码头上旅客排队登船，汽笛已经响过两遍。The last passengers were already aboard when the gangway was lifted.
sceneCN: 这里 aboard 是「在船上」（第 1 个义项：在船等水上交通工具上）；句意为舷梯收起时，最后一批旅客已经在船上了。

pos.zh: 介词：在（船、飞机、火车）上；上（船、飞机、火车）
副词：在船上；上船

derivatives.zh: 基础词 board 义为「木板、船舷」，无后缀；aboard 由 a- 加 board 构成，义为「在船上」
由 board 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「登船；登机」，语义从「上板」偏移为「上交通工具」
由 on 与 board 复合，与 aboard 同源近形，义为「船上的；机上的」，语义偏向「设备或人员随行的」
由 sea 与 board 复合，义为「沿海地区」，语义从「船板」偏移为「海岸线」

senses.title: On a ship or boat
senses.definition: on or onto a ship, boat, or other vessel on the water
senses.definitionCN: 在水上的船或其他船只之上，或登上这类船只
senses.example: The fishermen were already aboard when the tide turned.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水转向时，渔民们已经在船上了。
senses.why: The prefix a- meant on, and board was the side or deck of a ship; aboard began as the plain phrase on board.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「在」，board 原指船舷或甲板；aboard 最初就是「在船板上」，因此本义指人在船上。

senses.title: On an aircraft
senses.definition: on or onto an aircraft, as a passenger or crew member
senses.definitionCN: 作为乘客或机组人员待在飞机上、登上飞机
senses.example: All passengers must be aboard before the doors close.
senses.exampleCN: 舱门关闭前，所有乘客都必须登机就座。
senses.why: Air travel borrowed the nautical word and treated the aircraft as if it were a ship.
senses.whyCN: 航空旅行沿用这个航海词，把飞机当作一艘船来看待，于是「在船上」自然延伸为「在飞机上」。

senses.title: On a train or bus
senses.definition: on or onto a train, coach, or other land vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 在火车、长途客车或其他陆上交通工具上
senses.example: The conductor walked through the carriages to see who was aboard.
senses.exampleCN: 列车员走过各节车厢，查看谁已经上了车。
senses.why: Once the word named any vehicle a person can step onto, land transport was included without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词可以指任何能踏上去的交通工具，陆上交通就顺理成章地被纳入，词形却不必改动。

senses.title: Onto a vehicle, the act of boarding
senses.definition: into or onto a vehicle, viewed as the act of getting on
senses.definitionCN: 进入或踏上交通工具，强调登上去这个动作
senses.example: The mechanic climbed aboard and tested the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 机械师登上飞机，试了试发动机。
senses.why: A position word can also mark the movement that reaches it: to be aboard becomes to go aboard.
senses.whyCN: 表示位置的词也能标记到达该位置的动作：从「在船上」引申出「上船」这一移动义。

senses.title: As a new member of a team
senses.definition: in or into a team, company, or project as a new member
senses.definitionCN: 作为新成员进入团队、公司或项目
senses.example: The new designer came aboard at the start of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 新设计师在赛季开始时加入了团队。
senses.why: The greeting welcome aboard treats a company as a ship that a newcomer steps onto.
senses.whyCN: 招呼语 welcome aboard 把公司当成一艘船，新来的人踏上船板，于是「在船上」有了「在团队里」的比喻义。

senses.title: Loaded on a vessel, of goods
senses.definition: loaded or carried on a ship or aircraft, of cargo or goods
senses.definitionCN: 货物已经装上船或飞机并由其运载
senses.example: The cargo was already aboard when the manifest was checked.
senses.exampleCN: 核对舱单时，货物已经装上了船。
senses.why: Goods cannot be 'on board' in the human sense, but they occupy the same deck, so the same word serves them.
senses.whyCN: 货物不会像人那样「在船上」，但它们占据同一块甲板，于是同一个词也用来指货物已装载。

senses.title: The fixed call all aboard
senses.definition: used in the fixed call all aboard to tell passengers to get on
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定呼语 all aboard，提醒乘客立刻上船或上车
senses.example: The guard shouted all aboard just before the doors closed.
senses.exampleCN: 车门关闭前，列车员喊了一声「全体上车」。
senses.why: This is the word frozen into a single shout, still used at quays and stations.
senses.whyCN: 这是词被凝固成一句呼喊的用法，至今仍在码头和车站使用。

senses.title: Serving or travelling as crew
senses.definition: serving or travelling as a member of a crew on a ship or aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 作为船员或机组人员在一艘船、一架飞机上服役或随行
senses.example: He served aboard a destroyer for five years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一艘驱逐舰上服役了五年。
senses.why: Living and working on a vessel is the human version of being physically on board for a long stretch.
senses.whyCN: 在一艘船上生活和工作，就是「人在船上」这一状态在时间上的延长，于是特别用来指随船服役。

intro.en: Aboard is an English compound of a prefix meaning on and a Germanic noun meaning board or ship's side, later reinforced by Old French.
intro.cn: aboard 是英语复合词，由表示「在」的前缀与表示「木板、船舷」的日耳曼语名词构成，后来又受到古法语形式的强化。

items.en: Bord meant a plank or board, and by extension the side or deck of a ship. The word is Germanic and has no Latin cognate.
items.cn: bord 意为「木板」，引申指船舷或甲板；该词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: The prefix a-, from Old English on, combined with bord to give abord, 'on board, on a ship'. The exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 来自古英语 on 的前缀 a- 与 bord 结合，产生中古英语 abord，义为「在船上」；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Old French abord, 'arrival at a port, landing', reinforced the Middle English form and its spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 abord 意为「靠岸、登陆」，强化了中古英语的形式与拼写。

items.en: aboard is recorded in English from the late fourteenth century as a nautical term.
items.cn: aboard 自十四世纪后期起作为航海用语见于英语记录。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word extended from ships to aircraft, trains, and buses.
items.cn: 二十世纪，这个词从船只扩展到飞机、火车与巴士。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same board root; the near-meaning group gathers words about being on, off, or around a vessel.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 board 词根构成的一族词；近义组收表示在船上、离船或在水上的词。

entries.definition: A noun for a plank or the side of a ship, and a verb meaning to get on a vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「木板、船舷」；动词，义为「登（船、机）」，是 aboard 的构词基础。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of getting on a ship, plane, or train.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「登船、登机」，由 board 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning carried on a ship or aircraft, or a verb meaning to bring a new employee in.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「船上的、机上的」；动词，义为「使新员工入职」，由 on 与 board 复合。

entries.definition: The land along a coast, seen as the border of the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沿海地区、海岸线」，同样以 board 为构词成分，但语义已转向地理。

entries.definition: The full phrase that aboard shortened, still used of ships, planes, and teams.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「在船上、在飞机上、在团队中」，是 aboard 的完整说法。

entries.definition: On or onto land, away from a ship; the direct opposite of being aboard.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在岸上、上岸」，与 aboard 正好相反。

entries.definition: Floating on water, of a boat or a person in the water.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「漂浮的、在水上」，强调浮在水面而非登船。

entries.definition: On the ocean, especially of a ship that has left port.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「在海上」，强调已经离港航行。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real a- plus board structure and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 a- 加 board 结构，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: a- means on and board means the deck: aboard is literally on board.
normal.cn: a- 意为「在」，board 意为甲板：aboard 字面就是「在船板上」。

normal.en: board also gives boarding and onboard, all about getting on or being on a vessel.
normal.cn: board 还给出 boarding 与 onboard，都与登船或待在船上有关。

normal.en: All aboard is the traditional shout at a station or quay.
normal.cn: all aboard 是车站与码头传统的催促声。

normal.en: Welcome aboard greets a newcomer as if the team were a ship.
normal.cn: welcome aboard 把团队当作一艘船来欢迎新成员。

normal.en: The word moved from ships to planes and trains without changing its shape.
normal.cn: 这个词从船只走到飞机和火车，词形始终没有改变。

abstract.en: Picture one foot on the gangway and one on the deck: the moment the step is completed, you are aboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚在舷梯上、一只脚在甲板上：这一步踏完，人就在船上了。

abstract.en: The same deck can be a plane cabin or a train carriage; the picture simply changes its shell.
abstract.cn: 同一块甲板可以是机舱，也可以是车厢；画面只是换了外壳。

abstract.en: A team is also a vessel: coming aboard means taking a place on that deck.
abstract.cn: 团队也是一艘船：come aboard 就是在那块甲板上占一个位置。

examples.en: The children were told to stay aboard until the ferry docked.
examples.cn: 孩子们被告知在渡轮到岸前不要下船。

examples.en: She came aboard the project as a translator.
examples.cn: 她以译员身份加入了该项目。

examples.en: All aboard, the train leaves in two minutes.
examples.cn: 请全体上车，列车两分钟后开动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额波得」——额头冒汗，踏着舷梯上了船：在船上

root: 古英语 bord「木板、船舷」加前缀 a-（在……上）构成中古英语 abord「在船上」；古法语 abord「靠岸、登陆」对拼写有影响。该词属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one picture: a person or thing placed on the deck of a vessel, whether that vessel sails, flies, runs on rails, or is a team.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一幅画面：人或物被放到某艘「船」的甲板上，这艘船可以是海船、飞机、列车，也可以是一个团队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one foot crosses the gangway and lands on the deck of a vessel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚跨过舷梯，落在船只的甲板上。

branches.en: THE VEHICLE: a ship, an aircraft or a land vehicle all provide the same deck to stand on.
branches.cn: 交通工具线：船、飞机与陆上车辆都提供同一块可以站立的甲板。

branches.en: THE STEP: the word also names the movement that ends on that deck.
branches.cn: 动作线：这个词也指最终落在甲板上的那个动作。

branches.en: THE TEAM: a company or project is pictured as a vessel a newcomer steps onto.
branches.cn: 团队线：公司或项目被比作一艘船，新成员踏上去。

branches.en: THE CARGO AND THE CALL: goods occupy the deck, while the shout orders everyone onto it.
branches.cn: 货物与呼语线：货物占据甲板，呼语则命令所有人上船。

branches.en: THE CREW: long service on a vessel is being aboard stretched over years.
branches.cn: 船员线：长期在船上服役，就是把「在甲板上」拉长到许多年。

intro.en: Aboard is a prefix plus a Germanic noun; English later built a small family of compounds and suffixes around board.
intro.cn: aboard 是一个前缀加一个日耳曼语名词；英语后来围绕 board 造出一小族复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate: aboard rests on the Germanic word bord, and the Old French form is a parallel borrowing.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同族词：aboard 建立在日耳曼语 bord 之上，古法语形式只是平行的借词。

items.example: It forms aboard and ashore.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 aboard 与 ashore。

items.example: Bord named the deck a sailor stood on.
items.exampleCN: bord 指水手站立的那块甲板。

items.meaning: plank; to get on a vehicle
items.example: Passengers board the ferry at the pier.
items.exampleCN: 乘客在码头登上渡轮。

items.example: The crew slept aboard during the storm.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间船员们睡在船上。

items.meaning: carried on a ship or aircraft
items.example: The onboard computer failed during the flight.
items.exampleCN: 机载计算机在飞行中失灵。

items.example: Boarding begins twenty minutes before departure.
items.exampleCN: 起飞前二十分钟开始登机。

items.example: The seaboard towns depend on fishing.
items.exampleCN: 沿海城镇靠渔业为生。

items.structure: adverb with the same a- prefix
items.example: The sailors went ashore at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 水手们天亮时上岸。

derivatives.zh: 由 board 加 -ing 构成，义为「登船；登机」
由 on 与 board 复合，义为「船上的；机上的」
由 sea 与 board 复合，义为「沿海地区」

definition_zh: 废除；取消（法律、制度、习俗）
definition_en: to end a law, system, practice, or institution officially and completely
core_image: 一张旧告示被当众撕下，墙上只留下空框
scene: 镇公所前的公告栏换了新纸，旧的那张被撕下来揉成一团。Parliament voted to abolish the outdated tax on salt.
sceneCN: 这里 abolish 是「废除法律或规定」（第 1 个义项：正式终止一项法律或规定）；句意为议会投票废除了过时的盐税。

pos.zh: 及物动词：废除；废止；取消

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁动词 abolere 加名词后缀 -ition 构成，义为「废除；废止」
由 abolition 加施动后缀 -ist 构成，义为「主张废除某项制度的人」，尤指废奴主义者
由 abolitionist 加 -ism 构成，义为「废奴主义；废除主义」
由 abolish 加 -able 构成，义为「可废除的」

senses.title: To end a law or regulation
senses.definition: to end a law, rule, or regulation officially, so that it no longer has force
senses.definitionCN: 正式终止一项法律、规则或规定，使其不再有效力
senses.example: Parliament voted to abolish the outdated tax on salt.
senses.exampleCN: 议会投票废除了过时的盐税。
senses.why: The Latin verb abolere meant to destroy or efface; a law that is effaced leaves no valid text behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 abolere 意为「销毁、抹去」；被抹去的法律不再留下有效条文，这正是「废除」。

senses.title: To end a system or institution
senses.definition: to put a complete end to a system, such as slavery or a monarchy
senses.definitionCN: 彻底终止某种制度，如奴隶制或君主制
senses.example: The movement spent decades trying to abolish slavery.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动花了数十年试图废除奴隶制。
senses.why: A system is a structure that holds many practices together; destroying it is the largest scale of the same erasure.
senses.whyCN: 制度是把许多做法固定在一起的结构；摧毁它，是同一「抹去」动作最大的尺度。

senses.title: To close down an office or post
senses.definition: to close an office, agency, or official position permanently
senses.definitionCN: 永久撤销一个机构、部门或官方职位
senses.example: The agency was abolished in the budget reform.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构在预算改革中被撤销。
senses.why: An office is an institutional object; once abolished, the post itself no longer exists.
senses.whyCN: 机构是制度性的物件；一旦被废除，那个职位本身就不复存在。

senses.title: To end a custom or practice
senses.definition: to stop a long-standing custom, ceremony, or habitual practice
senses.definitionCN: 停止一项长期存在的习俗、仪式或习惯做法
senses.example: The school abolished the custom of morning detentions.
senses.exampleCN: 学校取消了早晨罚留堂的惯例。
senses.why: A custom has no statute behind it, but the same word is used because the community formally lets it go.
senses.whyCN: 习俗背后并没有成文法，但群体正式地把它放下，用的仍是同一个词。

senses.title: To remove a fee or penalty
senses.definition: to remove a charge, fine, or punishment that was previously imposed
senses.definitionCN: 取消此前设定的收费、罚款或处罚
senses.example: The city abolished parking fees on Sundays.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市取消了周日停车费。
senses.why: A fee is a rule with a price attached; abolishing it erases both the rule and its price.
senses.whyCN: 收费是附有价格的规则；废除它，规则与价格一并被抹掉。

senses.title: To remove a distinction or barrier
senses.definition: to remove a difference, boundary, or barrier between groups or things
senses.definitionCN: 消除群体或事物之间的差别、界限或障碍
senses.example: Good design should abolish the distinction between work and play.
senses.exampleCN: 好的设计应当消除工作与娱乐之间的界限。
senses.why: If a line is drawn, erasing it is the same gesture as erasing a rule; the difference simply stops existing.
senses.whyCN: 界线是被画出来的，擦掉它与废除一条规则是同一个动作；差别就此不再存在。

senses.title: To eradicate a social evil
senses.definition: to end a social problem such as poverty or discrimination completely
senses.definitionCN: 彻底终结贫困、歧视等社会问题
senses.example: No single policy can abolish poverty on its own.
senses.exampleCN: 没有任何单项政策能独自根除贫困。
senses.why: Poverty is treated as an institution that keeps people in place; abolishing it means destroying that structure.
senses.whyCN: 贫困被视为一种把人困住的制度；废除它，就是摧毁这套结构。

senses.title: To erase an inner fear or feeling
senses.titleCN: 消除内心的恐惧或情绪
senses.definition: to remove a fear, doubt, or feeling completely, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指彻底消除恐惧、疑虑或某种情绪
senses.example: The campaign aimed to abolish fear of speaking in public.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动旨在消除当众讲话的恐惧。
senses.why: The outermost extension: what is erased is no longer a document or a system but a state of mind.
senses.whyCN: 这是最外圈的引申：被抹去的不再是文件或制度，而是一种心理状态。

intro.en: Abolish comes from Latin through French, and its noun abolition shares the same recorded Latin base.
intro.cn: abolish 经由法语来自拉丁语，其名词 abolition 共享同一个有文献记录的拉丁词干。

items.en: abolere meant to destroy, efface, or put an end to something. The second element is traditionally read as olere, 'to grow', but this analysis is disputed.
items.cn: abolere 意为「销毁、抹去、终止」。第二成分传统上读作 olere「生长」，但这一分析存在争议。

items.en: The noun abolitio named the act of cancelling or annulling; it is the direct source of English abolition.
items.cn: 名词 abolitio 指「取消、废止」的行为，是英语 abolition 的直接来源。

items.en: Old French abolir carried the verb into Middle English, with the spelling changing on the way.
items.cn: 古法语 abolir 把这个动词带入中古英语，拼写一路上发生变化。

items.en: English abolish is recorded from the fifteenth century; the exact first written date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 abolish 自十五世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The object widened from statutes to institutions, customs, fees and finally states of mind.
items.cn: 它的宾语从法令扩展到制度、习俗、收费，最后延伸到心理状态。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the abolition family and the same Latin base; the near-meaning group gathers legal and general verbs of cancelling.
note.cn: 形近组收 abolition 词族与同一拉丁词干的词；近义组收法律与一般语境中表示取消的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the official ending of a law, system, or practice.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废除、废止」，与 abolish 同出拉丁 abolitio。

entries.definition: A person who campaigns for the ending of a practice, especially slavery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废奴主义者、主张废除者」，由 abolition 加 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: The movement or doctrine that seeks to end a practice such as slavery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废奴主义、废除主义」，由 abolitionist 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: Capable of being ended or cancelled by authority.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可废除的」，由 abolish 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The removal of material by melting, erosion, or surgery; it only looks related.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消融、切除」，词根是拉丁 auferre「带走」；只是拼写与 abolish 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To end a law formally by a legislative act; narrower and more technical than abolish.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废止（法律）」，专指立法机关正式撤销，比 abolish 更技术化。

entries.definition: To cancel a licence, right, or decision officially.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤销、吊销」，多指官方取消许可证、权利或决定。

entries.definition: To stop an arranged event or order; general and everyday in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取消」，多用于已安排的活动或订单，属日常用语。

entries.definition: To declare a marriage or contract invalid from the start.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣告无效」，多用于婚姻或合同，强调自始无效。

entries.definition: To remove something bad completely, especially disease or poverty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「根除」，强调彻底清除疾病、贫困等有害事物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb abolere, its noun abolitio, and the objects the word is commonly used with.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁动词 abolere、其名词 abolitio，以及这个词常见的搭配对象。

normal.en: abolere is to efface: abolition is the noun for the same erasing act.
normal.cn: abolere 是「抹去」：abolition 就是同一抹去动作的名词。

normal.en: The traditional reading of ab- plus olere is 'grow away', but the second element is disputed.
normal.cn: 传统解释把 ab- 加 olere 读作「长走、长没了」，但第二成分的来历仍有争议。

normal.en: Abolish slavery is the best-known English phrase built on this verb.
normal.cn: abolish slavery 是这个动词最有名的英语搭配。

normal.en: A parliament abolishes a law; a court may annul a contract, which is a narrower act.
normal.cn: 议会 abolish 一条法律；法院则可以 annul 一份合同，后者范围更窄。

normal.en: Abolition, abolitionist and abolitionism all belong to the same reforming family.
normal.cn: abolition、abolitionist 与 abolitionism 都属于同一改革词族。

abstract.en: Picture a notice being torn off a board: the frame stays, but the rule is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张告示被从公告板上撕下：木框还在，规则却消失了。

abstract.en: The same tearing gesture works on a statute, a monarchy, a fee or a fear.
abstract.cn: 同一个撕下的动作，可以用在法令、君主制、收费或恐惧上。

abstract.en: Abolishing is not reforming: the thing is not adjusted, it is removed.
abstract.cn: 废除不是改良：东西没有被调整，而是被拿掉。

examples.en: The country abolished the death penalty in the last century.
examples.cn: 这个国家在上个世纪废除了死刑。

examples.en: Campaigners want to abolish unpaid overtime.
examples.cn: 活动人士希望取消无偿加班。

examples.en: The old rule was abolished after a long debate.
examples.cn: 经过长时间辩论，那条旧规定被废止了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额玻力士」——大力士一挥手，旧告示被撕个干净：废除

root: 拉丁语 abolere「销毁、抹去、废止」经古法语 abolir 进入英语；其名词 abolitio 是 abolition 的直接来源。abolere 的第二成分传统上读作 olere「生长」，但这一分析存疑，更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all perform one act of erasure on different objects: a law, a system, an office, a custom, a fee, a boundary, a social evil, or a fear.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在不同的对象上完成同一次「抹去」：法律、制度、机构、习俗、收费、界限、社会弊病，以及恐惧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a public notice is torn down and only an empty frame remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张公告被当众撕下，只剩空空的木框。

branches.en: THE STATUTE: a law or regulation loses its force when the text is effaced.
branches.cn: 法令线：法律或规定在条文被抹去后失去效力。

branches.en: THE STRUCTURE: a system such as slavery, or a social evil such as poverty, is destroyed at its base.
branches.cn: 结构线：奴隶制这类制度，或贫困这类社会弊病，被从根基上摧毁。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: an agency or post is closed, so the position itself no longer exists.
branches.cn: 机构线：部门或职位被撤销，位置本身不复存在。

branches.en: THE ROUTINE: a custom, a fee or a penalty is formally let go by the community.
branches.cn: 惯例线：习俗、收费或处罚被群体正式地放下。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE LINE: a distinction or an inner fear is erased, though nothing physical is torn.
branches.cn: 无形线：差别或内心的恐惧被抹去，尽管没有撕掉任何实物。

intro.en: Abolish is built from a Latin prefix and a disputed Latin verb; English adds the noun and adjective suffixes of the abolition family.
intro.cn: abolish 由拉丁前缀与一个来历有争议的拉丁动词构成；英语再用名词与形容词后缀扩展出 abolition 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin abolere and abolitio are both recorded, while the deeper analysis of the second element is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abolere 与 abolitio 都有文献记录，而第二成分更深一层的分析并不确定。

items.example: The prefix sets the direction of the erasing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出「抹去」的方向。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的来源。

items.example: Abolitio named the act of annulling a rule.
items.exampleCN: abolitio 指废止一条规则的行为。

items.example: It forms abolition.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abolition。

items.meaningCN: 做某事或主张某事的人
items.example: It forms abolitionist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abolitionist。

items.example: It forms abolitionism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abolitionism。

items.example: It forms abolishable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abolishable。

items.example: The verb entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词经法语进入英语。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ition 构成，义为「废除；废止」
由 abolition 加 -ist 构成，义为「主张废除者」
由 abolitionist 加 -ism 构成，义为「废奴主义」

definition_zh: 堕胎；人工流产；流产；（计划等的）中途失败
definition_en: the ending of a pregnancy before the fetus can survive, or the failure of a plan before it is completed
core_image: 一条尚未走完的路，在半途被硬生生截断
scene: 医院的走廊里，值班表上排着几台手术，护士把知情同意书逐份核对。The hospital reported that abortions there are performed under strict legal rules.
sceneCN: 这里 abortion 是「人工流产」（第 1 个义项：以医疗手段终止妊娠）；句意为该医院报告说，院内的人工流产都严格依法进行。

pos.zh: 名词：堕胎；人工流产；流产；中途失败

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 abortus 去掉名词后缀构成动词，义为「流产；中止；使夭折」
由拉丁 abortus 加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「失败的；夭折的」
由 abortion 加 -ist 构成，义为「施行堕胎者」，带贬义或旧式色彩
由 abort 加 -facient「引起」构成，义为「引起流产的」

senses.title: An induced termination of pregnancy
senses.definition: a medical procedure that ends a pregnancy before the fetus can survive
senses.definitionCN: 在胎儿能够存活之前以医疗手段终止妊娠
senses.example: The clinic offers safe abortion care to local women.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为当地女性提供安全的人工流产服务。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to fail to be born; a procedure that stops the birth keeps that original picture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词本义是「未能出生」；用医疗手段让出生停下来，正保留了这幅原初画面。

senses.title: A natural miscarriage
senses.definition: the loss of a pregnancy before the fetus can survive, without medical intervention
senses.definitionCN: 未经医疗干预而失去胎儿，即自然流产
senses.example: Older medical texts used abortion for what is now called a miscarriage.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的医学文献用 abortion 指如今所说的自然流产。
senses.why: The same failure to be born happens by itself, so the word covers the spontaneous case too.
senses.whyCN: 同样是「未能出生」，只是这次是自然发生的，所以这个词也覆盖自发流产。

senses.title: The act as regulated by law
senses.definition: the act of ending a pregnancy, considered as an event that laws may permit, limit, or forbid
senses.definitionCN: 终止妊娠的行为，被视作法律可以允许、限制或禁止的事件
senses.example: The new law treats abortion as a matter of public health.
senses.exampleCN: 新法律把堕胎视为公共卫生问题。
senses.why: Law turns the medical event into a category it can permit or forbid, but the name stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 法律把一个医学事件变成可以允许或禁止的类别，名称却没有改变。

senses.title: The failure of a plan or attempt
senses.definition: the ending of a plan, attempt, or hope before it can be completed
senses.definitionCN: 计划、尝试或希望在完成之前就终止
senses.example: Poor planning led to the abortion of the whole expedition.
senses.exampleCN: 糟糕的筹划导致整个探险中途夭折。
senses.why: What never comes to birth can also be a plan: the image of a cut-off beginning transfers from body to project.
senses.whyCN: 未能「出生」的也可以是计划：被截断的开端这一形象，从身体转移到工程上。

senses.title: A project stopped before completion
senses.definition: the stopping of a project, building, or enterprise while it is still unfinished
senses.definitionCN: 项目、建筑或事业在尚未完成时被停止
senses.example: The abortion of the bridge scheme wasted two years of work.
senses.exampleCN: 桥梁方案的中途夭折浪费了两年的工作。
senses.why: A half-built structure is visibly unfinished, the most concrete version of a birth that never completes.
senses.whyCN: 半建的建筑一眼就看出没有完成，是「未能出生」最具体的版本。

senses.title: An organ that stops developing
senses.definition: in biology, a part or structure that stops developing or is formed incompletely
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中指停止发育或形成不完全的部位、结构
senses.example: The specimen showed an abortion of the wing bud.
senses.exampleCN: 标本显示翅芽发育不全。
senses.why: In biology the same Latin idea is applied to a structure whose growth is cut off early.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学里，同一个拉丁概念被用到生长过早中断的结构上。

senses.title: The expelled fetus or tissue
senses.definition: a medical use for the fetus or tissue expelled in a miscarriage or abortion
senses.definitionCN: 医学用语，指流产或堕胎时排出的胎儿或组织
senses.example: The older textbook described the abortion as a small, incomplete fetus.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的教科书把排出的胎儿描述为一个很小的、发育不全的胎儿。
senses.why: Metonymy: the event's name is transferred to the physical product that the event leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 这是转喻：事件的名字被转移到事件留下的那个实物上。

senses.title: A badly formed or failed thing
senses.titleCN: 畸形或失败的事物（贬义）
senses.definition: an archaic or figurative use for something misshapen, monstrous, or badly conceived
senses.definitionCN: 古旧或比喻用法，指形态畸形、怪异或构思糟糕的事物
senses.example: Critics called the half-built tower an abortion of design.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把那座半途停工的塔称为设计上的畸形儿。
senses.why: The strongest figurative extension: anything that fails to reach a proper form can be called an abortion.
senses.whyCN: 这是最强的比喻引申：任何没能长成应有形态的东西，都可以被叫作 abortion。

intro.en: Abortion descends from a Latin verb meaning to fail to be born, and the same stem supplies abort and abortive.
intro.cn: abortion 来自一个意为「未能出生」的拉丁动词，同一词干还给出 abort 与 abortive。

items.en: oriri meant to rise, appear, or be born; it is also the source of orient and origin.
items.cn: oriri 意为「升起、出现、出生」，也是 orient 与 origin 的来源。

items.en: ab-, 'away', plus oriri produced aboriri, 'to miscarry, fail to be born'.
items.cn: ab-「离开」加 oriri 构成 aboriri，意为「流产、未能出生」。

items.en: The noun abortio named a miscarriage, and the participle abortus supplied the stem used in English.
items.cn: 名词 abortio 指流产，分词 abortus 提供了英语所用的词干。

items.en: English adopted abortion in the sixteenth century, first as a medical term; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 abortion，最初是医学术语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Legal and political senses grew in the twentieth century, while the older sense of a failed plan survives in formal prose.
items.cn: 法律与政治义在二十世纪发展起来，而「计划夭折」的旧义仍见于正式书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the abort family on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers clinical and neutral terms for the same event.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干的 abort 词族；近义组收指同一事件的临床术语与中性说法。

entries.definition: To end a pregnancy, or to stop a process before it is finished.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「流产；中止」，与 abortion 同出拉丁 aboriri。

entries.definition: Failing to produce the intended result; ending before completion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失败的、夭折的」，由拉丁词干加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: A person who performs abortions, a term now often avoided or used with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「施行堕胎者」，现代常带贬义或被视为旧式说法。
