entries.definition: A drug or substance that causes an abortion.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「引起流产的；堕胎药」，由 abort 加 -facient 构成。

entries.definition: A medical term for the product of an abortion or miscarriage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，医学术语，义为「流产产物」，直接借自拉丁语。

entries.definition: The spontaneous loss of a pregnancy before the fetus can survive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自然流产」，特指未经医疗干预的流产，比 abortion 更中性。

entries.definition: A neutral or euphemistic word for ending a pregnancy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「终止」，在医学与法律语境中常作堕胎的中性委婉说法。

entries.definition: The birth of a dead fetus after the stage at which it could have survived.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「死产」，指在能够存活之后的阶段产下死胎，与流产不同。

entries.definition: The deliberate destruction of a fetus, a legal and medical term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「杀害胎儿」，属法律与医学术语，语气比 abortion 更严厉。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb aboriri and the clinical phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 aboriri，以及这个词出现的医学搭配。

normal.en: oriri is to be born: an abortion is a birth that does not happen.
normal.cn: oriri 是「出生」：abortion 就是没有发生的出生。

normal.en: ab- means away, so the Latin word pictures a birth moving away from life.
normal.cn: ab- 意为「离开」，所以这个拉丁词画的是「出生离开生命」。

normal.en: abort, abortive and abortifacient all keep the same stem.
normal.cn: abort、abortive 与 abortifacient 都保留同一个词干。

normal.en: Spontaneous abortion is the clinical term for a miscarriage.
normal.cn: spontaneous abortion 是自然流产的临床说法。

normal.en: The abortion of a plan borrows the medical image for something that never comes to birth.
normal.cn: the abortion of a plan 借医学形象，指从未「出生」的计划。

abstract.en: Picture a road that stops halfway, with no sign of a destination.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路在半途突然断开，看不到终点。

abstract.en: The same cut can happen in a body, a building, or a scheme.
abstract.cn: 同一道截断可以发生在身体上、建筑上，也可以发生在一项计划里。

abstract.en: Abortion is about something not reaching birth, not about something being destroyed after birth.
abstract.cn: abortion 的关键是「没有抵达出生」，而不是「出生之后被毁掉」。

examples.en: The report compares abortion rates across the region.
examples.cn: 这份报告比较了该地区各地的堕胎率。

examples.en: The abortion of the negotiations left both sides frustrated.
examples.cn: 谈判的中途夭折让双方都感到沮丧。

examples.en: Medical students learn to distinguish abortion from stillbirth.
examples.cn: 医学生学习区分流产与死产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额波神」——神坛前香火一断，胎没保住：流产

root: 拉丁语 aboriri「流产、未能出生」由 ab-「离开」+ oriri「升起、出生」构成；名词 abortio 指流产，分词 abortus 提供英语词干。oriri 同时也是 orient 与 origin 的来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe something that fails to come to birth: a pregnancy, an organ, a plan, a building, or a form that never becomes what it should.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述「未能出生」：妊娠、器官、计划、建筑，或始终没长成应有形态的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road is cut off halfway, before any destination is reached.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在半途被截断，终点从未到达。

branches.en: THE BODY: a pregnancy ends before the fetus can survive, by procedure or by itself.
branches.cn: 身体线：妊娠在胎儿能存活之前结束，或由手术终止，或自然发生。

branches.en: THE LAW: the same event becomes a category that statutes permit or forbid.
branches.cn: 法律线：同一事件成为法条可以允许或禁止的类别。

branches.en: THE PROJECT: a plan, expedition or building is stopped before completion.
branches.cn: 项目线：计划、探险或建筑在完成之前被停止。

branches.en: THE ORGAN: a biological structure stops developing and stays incomplete.
branches.cn: 器官线：生物结构停止发育，永远停留在不完整状态。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: the expelled tissue, and by extension any misshapen or failed thing.
branches.cn: 产物线：排出的组织，进而指任何畸形或失败的事物。

intro.en: Abortion is built on the Latin verb aboriri; English adds -ion and other suffixes to make the family.
intro.cn: abortion 建立在拉丁动词 aboriri 之上；英语用 -ion 等后缀扩展出这一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin oriri, aboriri, abortio and abortus are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European layer is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oriri、aboriri、abortio 与 abortus 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧层次属于重构。

items.example: The prefix turns rising into departure.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「升起」变成「离开」。

items.example: The verb also gives origin and orient.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词还给出 origin 与 orient。

items.meaning: to miscarry, fail to be born
items.example: The compound is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是该词族的直接来源。

items.example: Abortio named the event in medical Latin.
items.exampleCN: abortio 在医学拉丁语中指这一事件。

items.meaning: miscarried; the product of a miscarriage
items.example: The participle supplies the English stem abort-.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供英语词干 abort-。

items.example: It forms abortion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortion。

items.example: It forms abortive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortive。

items.example: It forms abortionist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortionist。

items.example: It forms abortifacient.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortifacient。

derivatives.zh: 由本词词干构成动词，义为「流产；中止」
由本词词干加 -ive 构成，义为「夭折的；失败的」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「施行堕胎者」

definition_zh: 关于；大约；到处；在身边；在……附近；即将
definition_en: on the subject of something, approximately, or in a place or state nearby
core_image: 绕着一样东西走一圈，始终不离它左右
scene: 咖啡馆靠窗的桌上摊着几张旧照片，两个老朋友聊起多年前的旅行。They talked about the trip for nearly three hours.
sceneCN: 这里 about 是「关于」（第 1 个义项：就某个话题谈论）；句意为他们聊那次旅行聊了将近三个小时。

pos.zh: 介词：关于；大约；在……一带；在……身边
副词：大约；到处；在附近；转身

derivatives.zh: 由 about 与 face 复合，义为「转身；立场的彻底转变」，语义从「转过来」偏移为「改弦更张」
由 about 与 turn 复合，义为「转身；政策的急转弯」
由 hereabout 加副词后缀 -s 构成，义为「在这一带」，指大致附近
由 thereabout 加副词后缀 -s 构成，义为「在那附近；大约」

senses.title: On the subject of something
senses.definition: on the subject of, or connected with, a person, thing, or question
senses.definitionCN: 以某人、某物或某问题为话题，或与其相关
senses.example: They talked about the trip for nearly three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们聊那次旅行聊了将近三个小时。
senses.why: About first meant around or on the outside; to speak about a thing is to circle it with words.
senses.whyCN: about 最初意为「在周围、在外侧」；谈论一件事，就是用言语绕着它走一圈。

senses.title: Approximately, with a number
senses.definition: used before a number or amount to mean approximately
senses.definitionCN: 用在数量或数额前，表示大致接近
senses.example: The journey takes about three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这段路程大约要三个小时。
senses.why: A point that is 'around' a number sits near it without landing exactly on it.
senses.whyCN: 一个「在数字周围」的点，停在它附近而不正好落在它上面，这正是「大约」。

senses.title: Scattered in many directions
senses.definition: in or to many places, especially without a fixed order
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方，尤其指没有固定次序地散开
senses.example: Toys lay about the floor after the party.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会结束后，玩具散落了一地。
senses.why: The oldest spatial sense is 'around'; things lying about are spread around a room.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的空间义就是「在周围」；东西 lie about，就是散落在房间各处。

senses.title: Present nearby or available
senses.definition: present in a place, or available to be found nearby
senses.definitionCN: 在场、在附近，或就近可以找到
senses.example: Is your father about this afternoon?
senses.exampleCN: 今天下午你父亲在家吗？
senses.why: If something is around the place, it is close enough to be found, so about comes to mean present.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物就在这一带，它近得可以找到，于是 about 引申为「在身边、在」。

senses.title: Nearly, with a point in time
senses.definition: used with a point in time to mean nearly or almost
senses.definitionCN: 与时间点连用，表示接近某个时刻
senses.example: It was about midnight when the rain stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 雨停的时候将近午夜。
senses.why: Time is treated like a number on a line, and a moment near it is about that moment.
senses.whyCN: 时间被当作线上的数字，靠近某一刻的时刻就是 about 那一刻。

senses.title: In or around a place, British use
senses.definition: in or around a place, used especially in British English
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地方或在其周围，尤其见于英式英语
senses.example: They wandered about the old town all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整个上午都在老城里闲逛。
senses.why: The 'around' sense survives most clearly in British usage with places.
senses.whyCN: 「在周围」这一层意思在英式英语与地点连用时保存得最清楚。

senses.title: On the point of doing something
senses.definition: in the phrase be about to, on the point of doing something very soon
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 be about to，表示马上就要做某事
senses.example: The train is about to leave the platform.
senses.exampleCN: 列车即将离开站台。
senses.why: An event 'around' the present moment is so close that it is about to happen.
senses.whyCN: 一件「在当下这一刻周围」的事近到马上就要发生，于是有了 be about to。

senses.title: Turned to face the opposite way
senses.definition: used with verbs such as turn to mean in the opposite direction
senses.definitionCN: 与 turn 等动词连用，表示转向相反的方向
senses.example: He turned about and walked back to the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他转过身，走回大门。
senses.why: To turn about is to turn around a full half-circle, the physical version of the original 'around'.
senses.whyCN: turn about 是转过半圈，正是「绕一圈」这一原义在身体动作上的体现。

intro.en: About is an Old English compound of a prefix and a word for outside; it has no Latin cognate.
intro.cn: about 是古英语复合词，由前缀与表示「外面」的词构成；没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: butan meant outside, formed from be- plus utan; it is the second element of the older compound.
items.cn: butan 意为「在外面」，由 be- 加 utan 构成，是较早复合词的第二成分。

items.en: a-, 'on', plus butan gave abutan, 'around, on the outside'.
items.cn: a-「在」加 butan 构成 abutan，意为「在周围、在外侧」。

items.en: The form passed through aboute and about, and the sense narrowed toward 'around' and 'concerning'.
items.cn: 形式经 aboute 演变为 about，词义逐渐收拢到「在周围」与「关于」。

items.en: about is recorded from the thirteenth century; the exact first written date is uncertain.
items.cn: about 自十三世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The approximate and 'be about to' senses developed later, from the idea of a point nearby.
items.cn: 「大约」与「be about to」等义发展得较晚，都从「就在附近」这一想法而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds and derivatives built on about; the near-meaning group gathers approximations and prepositions of topic.
note.cn: 形近组收以 about 构成的复合词与派生词；近义组收表示大约与话题的介词、副词。

entries.definition: A turn to face the opposite way, or a complete reversal of policy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转身；立场的彻底转变」，由 about 与 face 复合。

entries.definition: A turn in the opposite direction, used literally and of policy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转身；政策的急转弯」，由 about 与 turn 复合。

entries.definition: In this general area; formed from hereabout plus -s.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在这一带」，由 hereabout 加 -s 构成。

entries.definition: Near that place or approximately that amount.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在那附近；大约」，由 thereabout 加 -s 构成。

entries.definition: A circular road junction, or an indirect route or way of speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「环形交叉路口；绕弯的」，由 round 与 about 复合，语义偏指「绕圈」。

entries.definition: Used of a number or amount that is close but not exact.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大约」，用于接近但不精确的数量，语气比 about 正式。

entries.definition: Approximately, with the added idea of a rough estimate.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「粗略地、大约」，比 about 更强调估计不精细。

entries.definition: On the subject of; a formal preposition used in notices and letters.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于」，语气正式，多用于公告与书信。

entries.definition: With respect to; a formal alternative to about.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于、就……而言」，是 about 的正式替代说法。

entries.definition: On every side of something, or approximately, in American usage.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在周围；大约」，在美式英语中常与 about 互换。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English compound and the everyday phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的古英语复合结构，以及这个词的日常搭配。

normal.en: About began as a- 'on' plus butan 'outside', so its first sense was 'around'.
normal.cn: about 最初是 a-「在」加 butan「外面」，所以本义是「在周围」。

normal.en: Saying something is about a subject is circling it with words.
normal.cn: 说某事 about 一个话题，就是用话绕着它转。

normal.en: Be about to turns 'near' into 'almost now'.
normal.cn: be about to 把「附近」变成「几乎就在此刻」。

normal.en: About ten and about midnight use the same idea of a point nearby.
normal.cn: about ten 与 about midnight 都用了「就在那个点附近」这一想法。

normal.en: Turn about and about-face keep the old picture of going around.
normal.cn: turn about 与 about-face 都保留了「绕过去」的旧画面。

abstract.en: Picture a child running a circle around a table: never far, never touching.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子绕着桌子跑圈：不远，也不碰。

abstract.en: The circle explains both 'concerning' and 'approximately': words and numbers hover around the thing.
abstract.cn: 这个圈同时解释了「关于」与「大约」：言语和数字都围着那件事打转。

abstract.en: When the circle shrinks to nothing, about becomes 'on the point of'.
abstract.cn: 当这个圈缩到几乎没有，about 就变成「即将」。

examples.en: She told us about her first teaching job.
examples.cn: 她跟我们讲了她第一份教书的工作。

examples.en: The repair will cost about forty pounds.
examples.cn: 这次维修大约要四十英镑。

examples.en: There was nobody about when the shop closed.
examples.cn: 商店关门时附近一个人也没有。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额包特」——包裹旁边聊来聊去，说的就是那件事：关于

root: 古英语 abutan 由 a-（在）+ butan（外面）构成，本义「在周围、在外侧」，后引申出「大约」「关于」「即将」等义。该词属日耳曼语复合词，没有拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep the image of a circle: a subject is circled by talk, a number is circled by a value, and a place or moment is circled by the speaker.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留「绕圈」的意象：话题被言语环绕，数字被近似值环绕，地点或时刻被说话者环绕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone walks a circle around one object and never goes far from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人绕着一件东西走圈，始终不离它左右。

branches.en: THE TOPIC: speech circles a subject the way a walker circles an object.
branches.cn: 话题线：言语绕着一个话题转，就像人绕着一件东西走。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a number or a moment is approached but not exactly reached.
branches.cn: 度量线：数字或时刻被靠近，却没有精确抵达。

branches.en: THE SPACE: things lie scattered around a room, or a person wanders around a town.
branches.cn: 空间线：东西散落在房间各处，或人在城里到处走。

branches.en: THE PRESENCE: what is around the place is close enough to be found there.
branches.cn: 在场线：就在这一带的东西近得可以在那里找到。

branches.en: THE EDGE: the circle closes into 'about to happen' or into a half-turn.
branches.cn: 边缘线：这个圈收拢成「即将发生」，或收成一个半转身。

intro.en: About is an Old English compound; English later built compounds and adverbs on it, while its second element survives only inside such words.
intro.cn: about 是古英语复合词；英语后来在它之上造出复合词与副词，而它的第二成分只保存在这类词里。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate: about is a Germanic compound of a- and butan, and the Latin parallels are only semantic.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同族词：about 是 a- 与 butan 的日耳曼语复合词，拉丁语中只有意思相近的词。

items.example: It forms abutan and aboard.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abutan 与 aboard。

items.example: Butan supplied the second element of abutan.
items.exampleCN: butan 提供了 abutan 的第二成分。

items.example: Utan is the core of butan.
items.exampleCN: utan 是 butan 的核心部分。

items.example: They spoke about the weather.
items.exampleCN: 他们谈了谈天气。

items.meaning: a turn to the opposite direction
items.example: The minister performed an about-face on the issue.
items.exampleCN: 部长在这个问题上彻底转变了立场。

items.meaning: a turn in the opposite direction
items.example: The board ordered an about-turn in strategy.
items.exampleCN: 董事会下令对战略作急转弯。

items.example: There is no bakery hereabouts.
items.exampleCN: 这一带没有面包店。

items.example: The cost was fifty pounds or thereabouts.
items.exampleCN: 费用是五十英镑左右。

derivatives.zh: 由 about 与 face 复合，义为「转身；立场彻底转变」
由 about 与 turn 复合，义为「转身；急转弯」
由 thereabout 加 -s 构成，义为「在那附近；大约」

definition_zh: 在……上方；高于；超过；上述的
definition_en: in or to a higher position than something, more than a number or level, or earlier in a text
core_image: 一盏灯挂在桌面之上，光从上往下落
scene: 山谷里的雾沉在脚下，山顶的观景台比云层还高。The observation deck stands above the clouds.
sceneCN: 这里 above 是「位置在……上方」（第 1 个义项：处于比某物更高的位置）；句意为观景台高立在云层之上。

pos.zh: 介词：在……上方；高于；超过
副词：在上面；在上方
形容词：上述的；上面的

derivatives.zh: 由 above 与 mentioned 复合，义为「上文提到的」，语义从「位置在上」偏移到「文字在前」
由 above 与 board 复合，义为「光明正大的」，原指牌桌上不藏牌，语义从「桌面上方」偏移为「公开坦荡」
由 above 与 ground 复合，义为「地面上的」，语义从「上方」具体化为「地表之上」

senses.title: At a higher place than something
senses.definition: in or to a position higher than a thing or a surface
senses.definitionCN: 处于或移到比某物、某表面更高的位置
senses.example: The lamp hung above the table.
senses.exampleCN: 灯挂在桌子上方。
senses.why: The core picture is a lamp higher than a table with light falling downward; this sense states that picture at its plainest.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面是一盏灯高过桌面、光向下落；本义项把这幅画最直白地说了出来。

senses.title: More than a stated amount
senses.definition: more than a particular number, amount, or level
senses.definitionCN: 多于某个数字、数额或水平
senses.example: Temperatures rose above thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 气温升到三十度以上。
senses.why: Height on a scale becomes amount on a scale: whatever sits above the mark is more than the mark.
senses.whyCN: 刻度上的高度转成数量上的高度：位于标记之上的，就是超过这个标记。

senses.title: Higher in rank or authority
senses.definition: of higher rank, status, or authority than another person
senses.definitionCN: 在等级、地位或权力上高于另一个人
senses.example: She ranks above him in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她在办公室里级别高于他。
senses.why: A hierarchy is imagined as a vertical stack, so anyone higher in it is literally above the others.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成垂直的堆叠，位置更高的人就字面意义上「在别人上面」。

senses.title: Too proud to do something
senses.definition: too good, proud, or honest to do something bad or small
senses.definitionCN: 因为品格或自尊而不屑于做某事、不至于做某事
senses.example: He is above such tricks.
senses.exampleCN: 他不屑于这种把戏。
senses.why: Moral height is pictured as physical height: a person who would not stoop is above the act.
senses.whyCN: 道德的高度被画成身体的高度：不肯弯腰的人，就「高于」那种行为。

senses.title: Earlier in a written text
senses.definition: appearing earlier on a page or earlier in a text
senses.definitionCN: 在同一页或同一篇文章中位置更靠前
senses.example: See the note above.
senses.exampleCN: 见上文的注释。
senses.why: On a page, earlier lines sit higher, so the vertical picture transfers from space to reading order.
senses.whyCN: 书页上先写的行位置更高，于是垂直的画面从空间转移到阅读顺序。

senses.title: In the sky, overhead
senses.definition: high in the sky, directly over a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 在高空中，位于某地或某人的正上方
senses.example: The moon was above the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 月亮挂在山冈上方。
senses.why: The same vertical relation is applied to a very large frame, where the sky is the surface that things hang over.
senses.whyCN: 同一个垂直关系被放到极大的框架里：天空成了悬挂之物所在的「上面」。

senses.title: In preference to something
senses.definition: regarded as more important or more desirable than something else
senses.definitionCN: 被认为比另一事物更重要或更可取
senses.example: They put safety above speed.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把安全置于速度之上。
senses.why: A scale of values is again a vertical scale: what matters more is placed higher.
senses.whyCN: 价值次序又被画成垂直刻度：更重要的事被放在更高的位置。

senses.title: Beyond a limit or suspicion
senses.definition: outside the reach of something such as suspicion, reproach, or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 超出怀疑、指责或批评所能触及的范围
senses.example: Her honesty is above suspicion.
senses.exampleCN: 她的诚实毋庸置疑。
senses.why: When something is above a line, the line cannot reach it; the spatial picture turns into immunity from doubt.
senses.whyCN: 当某物位于一条线之上，那条线就够不到它；空间画面于是变成「不受怀疑侵扰」。

intro.en: Above is an Old English compound built from a prefix and a word for above; it has no Latin cognate.
intro.cn: above 是古英语复合词，由前缀与表示「在上」的词构成；没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: ufan meant above or from above; outside compounds it has not survived into modern English.
items.cn: ufan 意为「在上、从上方」；除了复合词，它没有留存到现代英语。

items.en: be- plus ufan gave bufan, 'above'.
items.cn: be- 加 ufan 构成 bufan，意为「在上」。

items.en: a-, 'on', plus bufan produced abufan, the direct ancestor of above.
items.cn: a-「在」加 bufan 构成 abufan，是 above 的直接祖先。

items.en: The form settled as above, and the spatial sense extended to quantity and rank.
items.cn: 形式固定为 above，空间义扩展到数量与等级。

items.en: Preference and 'above suspicion' are later figurative extensions of the same vertical picture.
items.cn: 「优先于」与「above suspicion」是同一垂直画面较晚的比喻引申。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers compounds on above and two words that merely look similar; the near-meaning group gathers vertical and contrastive prepositions.
note.cn: 形近组收以 above 构成的复合词，以及两个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示垂直位置与相反方向的介词、副词。

entries.definition: Honest and open, originally of cards kept in sight on the table.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「光明正大的」，原指牌放在桌面上不藏起来，由 above 与 board 复合。

entries.definition: Mentioned earlier in the same text.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「上述的、前面提到的」，由 above 与 mentioned 复合。

entries.definition: On or above the surface of the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「地面上的」，由 above 与 ground 复合。

entries.definition: A word for 'concerning' or 'approximately'; it shares the a- opening but comes from a different Old English compound.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「关于、大约」，同样以 a- 开头，但出自另一个古英语复合词，只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A dwelling place; it looks close to above but comes from the verb abide.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所、居所」，来自动词 abide，只是拼写与 above 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Directly above, or covering something; often interchangeable with above for position.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……正上方；覆盖」，表示位置时常可与 above 互换，但更强调垂直或覆盖。

entries.definition: Resting on the upper surface of something, with contact.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「在……上面」，强调与表面接触，而 above 不接触。

entries.definition: On the farther side of something, or outside its reach.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……那一边；超出」，强调越过某界限，与 above 的「超出」义相近。

entries.definition: Above the head, in the sky or upper space.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上方」，与 above 的天空义相近。

entries.definition: At a lower position than something; the direct opposite of above.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……下方」，与 above 正好相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English elements of above and the phrases it actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 above 真实的古英语成分，以及它实际构成的搭配。

normal.en: ufan is an old word for 'from above'; it now lives only inside above and a few relatives.
normal.cn: ufan 是表示「从上方」的古词，如今只活在 above 等少数词里。

normal.en: The a- in above is the same 'on' prefix seen in aboard and abroad.
normal.cn: above 里的 a- 与 aboard、abroad 里的 a- 是同一个「在」前缀。

normal.en: aboveboard keeps the idea of cards lying in plain sight on the table.
normal.cn: aboveboard 保留了牌摊在桌面上、人人可见的形象。

normal.en: above all is the fixed phrase for what matters most.
normal.cn: above all 是表示「最重要」的固定说法。

normal.en: above sea level measures height from a known line.
normal.cn: above sea level 从一条已知的线量起，指高出海平面。

abstract.en: Picture a vertical line: a thing, a number, a rank or a value can all sit on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条垂直线：实物、数字、等级或价值都可以排在上面。

abstract.en: The same line explains 'above the table' and 'above average'.
abstract.cn: 同一条线同时解释了 above the table 与 above average。

abstract.en: Whoever or whatever is above the line is out of the reach of what lies below it.
abstract.cn: 在线之上的东西，就够不着线以下的东西，这正是「超出怀疑」的由来。

examples.en: A small plane circled above the village for an hour.
examples.cn: 一架小飞机在村庄上空盘旋了一个小时。

examples.en: Her score was well above the class average.
examples.cn: 她的分数远高于全班平均分。

examples.en: The above example shows how the rule works.
examples.cn: 上面的例子说明了这条规则如何运作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额巴夫」——巴夫大叔站在桌子上头，比谁都高：在……上方

root: 古英语 abufan 由 a-（在）+ bufan（在上）构成，bufan 又由 be- 加 ufan 构成；该词属日耳曼语，与 over、up 有远亲关系，但没有拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place something on one vertical line: an object over a surface, a number over a mark, a person over another, or a value over another value.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物放在同一条垂直线上：物体在表面之上、数字在标记之上、人在他人之上、价值在另一价值之上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp hangs higher than a table and its light falls downward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯挂得比桌面高，光从上往下落。

branches.en: THE POSITION: a thing is simply higher than a surface.
branches.cn: 位置线：某物只是比某个表面更高。

branches.en: THE SCALE: on a numbered scale, whatever is higher is more than the mark.
branches.cn: 刻度线：在带数字的刻度上，位置更高就是数量更多。

branches.en: THE HIERARCHY: rank, authority and moral standing are all drawn as height.
branches.cn: 等级线：等级、权力与道德地位都被画成高度。

branches.en: THE VALUE: what one will not stoop to, or what one prefers, is placed higher.
branches.cn: 价值线：一个人不屑做的事，或更看重的事，被放到更高的位置。

branches.en: THE PAGE AND SKY: earlier lines sit higher on paper, and the moon hangs higher in the air.
branches.cn: 书页与天空线：先写的行在纸上位置更高，月亮则高悬在空中。

intro.en: Above is an Old English compound; English later attached it to nouns to make compounds rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: above 是古英语复合词；英语后来把它与名词组合成复合词，而不是加后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate. Latin super and supra express the same relation but belong to a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同族词。拉丁语 super 与 supra 表达相同关系，却属于另一个词族。

items.example: It forms abufan.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abufan。

items.example: Ufan survives only inside compounds.
items.exampleCN: ufan 只保存在复合词里。

items.example: Bufan is the middle element of abufan.
items.exampleCN: bufan 是 abufan 的中间成分。

items.example: The plane flew above the town.
items.exampleCN: 飞机飞在小镇上方。

items.example: The deal was completely aboveboard.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易完全光明正大。

items.example: The above-mentioned rule still applies.
items.exampleCN: 上述规则仍然适用。

items.example: The bunker was linked to an aboveground store.
items.exampleCN: 地堡与一个地面仓库相连。

items.example: A lamp hung over the table.
items.exampleCN: 一盏灯挂在桌子正上方。

derivatives.zh: 由本词与 board 复合，义为「光明正大的」
由本词与 mentioned 复合，义为「上述的」
由本词与 ground 复合，义为「地面上的」

definition_zh: 删节；节略；缩短；剥夺（权利）
definition_en: to make a text, speech, or period shorter, or to cut down a right or freedom
core_image: 一把红笔在厚书上划掉整段，书页变薄
scene: 出版社的编辑桌上堆着一部厚厚的长篇小说，红笔已经划掉了几十页。The publisher abridged the long novel for young readers.
sceneCN: 这里 abridge 是「删节文字作品」（第 1 个义项：删去部分内容使篇幅变短）；句意为出版社为年轻读者删节了这部长篇小说。

pos.zh: 及物动词：删节；节略；缩短；剥夺；限制

derivatives.zh: 由 abridge 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「删节；节略本」
由 abridge 加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「删节过的、简略的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 abridged 构成，义为「未删节的、完整的」
由 abridge 加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「删节者」

senses.title: To shorten a text by cutting parts
senses.definition: to shorten a book, article, or other text by removing parts of it
senses.definitionCN: 删去书、文章或其他文本的部分内容，使其变短
senses.example: The publisher abridged the long novel for young readers.
senses.exampleCN: 出版社为年轻读者删节了这部长篇小说。
senses.why: breviare, from brevis 'short', is the root; cutting a text is the plainest way to make it short.
senses.whyCN: 词根 breviare 出自 brevis「短」；把文本删掉一部分，正是让它变短最直白的方式。

senses.title: To produce a shortened edition
senses.definition: to prepare a shorter version of a work for publication or performance
senses.definitionCN: 为出版或演出准备一个篇幅更短的版本
senses.example: The play was abridged for a single evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这个剧本被压缩成一场晚会能演完的版本。
senses.why: Here the cutting serves a fixed frame: the edition must fit a page count or a stage time.
senses.whyCN: 这里的删减服务于一个固定框架：版本必须装进规定的页数或演出时长。

senses.title: To shorten a speech or statement
senses.definition: to make a speech, report, or statement shorter
senses.definitionCN: 使讲话、报告或陈述变得更短
senses.example: She abridged her remarks to ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 她把发言压缩到十分钟。
senses.why: Spoken words are cut the same way written ones are: the material is shortened before delivery.
senses.whyCN: 口头的话语与书面文字一样被剪短：材料在说出之前就被压缩。

senses.title: To shorten a period of time
senses.definition: to make a period or process shorter in duration
senses.definitionCN: 使一段时间或过程持续得更短
senses.example: The new route abridges the journey by an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 新路线把行程缩短了一个小时。
senses.why: If a stretch of time is a length, it can be cut like a page; the metaphor is one of measured extent.
senses.whyCN: 如果把一段时间看作一段长度，它就能像书页一样被剪短；这个比喻建立在「可量的长度」上。

senses.title: To shorten a distance or way
senses.definition: to make a distance or route shorter, an older sense still found in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 使距离或路线变短，这一较旧的义项仍见于正式书面语
senses.example: A tunnel would abridge the road between the two towns.
senses.exampleCN: 一条隧道会缩短两镇之间的路程。
senses.why: A road is a line on the ground; cutting it short is the spatial version of the same shortening.
senses.whyCN: 道路是地面上的一条线；把它截短，是同一个「缩短」在空间上的版本。

senses.title: To condense to the essential points
senses.definition: to reduce material to its essential points without losing the main sense
senses.definitionCN: 把材料压缩到要点，同时不丢失主要意思
senses.example: The summary abridges three chapters into one page.
senses.exampleCN: 这份摘要把三章内容压缩成一页。
senses.why: Shortening well is not random deletion: what remains must still carry the whole, so the cut is a condensation.
senses.whyCN: 好的删节不是随意删除：留下来的部分仍要承载整体，所以这种剪切是一种浓缩。

senses.title: To deprive someone of a right
senses.definition: in law, to deprive a person of a right, privilege, or benefit
senses.definitionCN: 法律用语，指剥夺某人的权利、特权或利益
senses.example: The old statute abridged the rights of tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧法令剥夺了租户的权利。
senses.why: A right is treated as something a person holds; cutting it off leaves the holder with less than before.
senses.whyCN: 权利被当作人手里握有的东西；把它切掉，持有人就比原来少了。

senses.title: To limit freedom or power
senses.definition: to restrict or cut down a freedom, power, or authority
senses.definitionCN: 限制或削减自由、权力或权威
senses.example: No law may abridge freedom of speech.
senses.exampleCN: 任何法律都不得限制言论自由。
senses.why: The legal sense widens from a single right to any freedom: whatever is cut down is abridged.
senses.whyCN: 法律义从单项权利扩展到任何自由：凡是被削减的，就是被 abridge。

intro.en: Abridge came through Old French from a Late Latin verb built on the adjective brevis, 'short'.
intro.cn: abridge 经古法语来自一个晚期拉丁动词，其词根是形容词 brevis「短的」。

items.en: brevis meant short or brief, and it is the source of English brief and brevity.
items.cn: brevis 意为「短的、简短的」，是英语 brief 与 brevity 的来源。

items.en: breviare, 'to shorten', was formed from brevis; with ad- it became abbreviare.
items.cn: breviare「缩短」由 brevis 构成；加上 ad- 后成为 abbreviare。

items.en: Late Latin abbreviare, 'to shorten', passed into Old French as abregier.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 abbreviare「缩短」传入古法语，成为 abregier。

items.en: Old French abregier carried the word into Middle English as abreggen.
items.cn: 古法语 abregier 把这个词带入中古英语，作 abreggen。

items.en: English abridge is recorded from the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 abridge 自十四世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the brevity family and the longer Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of cutting and condensing.
note.cn: 形近组收 brevity 词族与较长的拉丁词干；近义组收表示剪切与压缩的动词。

entries.definition: The act of shortening a text, or the shortened text itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「删节；节略本」，由 abridge 加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Shortened by having parts removed, of a text or edition.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「删节过的」，由 abridge 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Complete, with nothing removed; the opposite of abridged.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「未删节的、完整的」，由 un- 加 abridged 构成。

entries.definition: To shorten a word, phrase, or text, from the same Latin brevis.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缩写、缩短」，与 abridge 同出拉丁语 brevis「短」。

entries.definition: Shortness of speech or writing, from Latin brevitas.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「简短、简洁」，同样出自 brevis，但只指风格上的短。

entries.definition: To make something shorter in length, time, or duration; the most general word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使变短」，用于长度、时间或篇幅，是最一般的说法。

entries.definition: To make a text or substance denser by reducing what is in it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「压缩、浓缩」，强调减少内容或体积后更紧凑。

entries.definition: To cut off the end of something, especially in computing or geometry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「截断、截短」，多用于计算机或几何，强调去掉末端。

entries.definition: To reduce or cut short a right, spending, or an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「削减、缩短」，多用于权利、开支或活动，语气正式。

entries.definition: To remove part of a text, film, or budget; the everyday verb behind abridge.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「删剪、削减」，是 abridge 背后最日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root brevis and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 brevis，以及这个词出现的搭配。

normal.en: brevis is Latin for short: abridge is to make short.
normal.cn: brevis 是拉丁语的「短」：abridge 就是使变短。

normal.en: abbreviate and brevity come from the same brevis, so the family shares one idea.
normal.cn: abbreviate 与 brevity 同出 brevis，整个词族共享一个「短」的念头。

normal.en: An abridged edition cuts a text; an unabridged one keeps every word.
normal.cn: abridged edition 删节文本；unabridged 版本则一字不减。

normal.en: abridgement is the noun for both the act and the shortened version.
normal.cn: abridgement 既是「删节」这个动作，也指删节后的版本。

normal.en: In law, to abridge a right is to cut it short.
normal.cn: 在法律里，abridge a right 就是把一项权利切短。

abstract.en: Picture a thick book with a pair of scissors laid beside it: the cut pages are what disappear.
abstract.cn: 想象一本厚书旁边放着一把剪刀：消失的正是被剪下的书页。

abstract.en: The same scissors can cut a speech, a journey, a timetable or a legal right.
abstract.cn: 同一把剪刀可以剪短讲话、旅程、时间表，也可以剪掉一项法律权利。

abstract.en: Good abridging keeps the shape of the whole while removing what can be spared.
abstract.cn: 好的删节保留整体的形状，只去掉可以省去的部分。

examples.en: The editors abridged the report to four pages.
examples.cn: 编辑把报告删节到四页。

examples.en: This is the abridged edition, not the full text.
examples.cn: 这是节略本，不是全文。

examples.en: The court ruled that the new rule abridged free speech.
examples.cn: 法院裁定新规定限制了言论自由。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额布瑞吉」——布里吉拿红笔把厚书剪薄：删节

root: 古法语 abregier 源自晚期拉丁语 abbreviare「缩短」，后者由 ad- 加 breviare 构成，breviare 又出自 brevis「短的」；英语十四世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all shorten something: a text, an edition, a speech, a period, a route, a summary, a right, or a freedom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把某样东西变短：文本、版本、讲话、时间、路程、摘要、权利或自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red pen crosses out whole paragraphs and the book becomes thinner.
core.cn: 核心意象：红笔划掉整段文字，书页随之变薄。

branches.en: THE TEXT: a book or article loses the parts that can be spared.
branches.cn: 文本线：书或文章失去那些可以省去的部分。

branches.en: THE EDITION: a shorter version is made for a fixed frame, keeping the essential points.
branches.cn: 版本线：为固定框架制作较短的版本，同时保留要点。

branches.en: THE SPEECH: spoken words are cut short before they are delivered.
branches.cn: 讲话线：口头内容在说出之前就被压缩。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a period of time or a route is shortened as if it were a length.
branches.cn: 度量线：一段时间或一条路线像长度一样被截短。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: law cuts down a right, a freedom, or a power.
branches.cn: 权利线：法律削减一项权利、自由或权力。

intro.en: Abridge carries a Latin prefix and the Latin root brevis; English adds -ment, -ed and un- to complete the family.
intro.cn: abridge 带有拉丁前缀与拉丁词根 brevis；英语再加 -ment、-ed 与 un- 补全词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin brevis, breviare and abbreviare are all recorded; the pathway through Old French is also documented.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 brevis、breviare 与 abbreviare 均有文献记录，经古法语传入的路径也有据可查。

items.example: It strengthens the verb in abbreviare.
items.exampleCN: 它在 abbreviare 中加强动词。

items.example: The adjective is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是整族词的词根。

items.example: It was formed directly from brevis.
items.exampleCN: 它直接由 brevis 构成。

items.example: It passed into Old French as abregier.
items.exampleCN: 它传入古法语成为 abregier。

items.example: It is the direct source of English abridge.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语 abridge 的直接来源。

items.meaning: to shorten a text or right
items.example: The verb entered English in the fourteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词在十四世纪进入英语。

items.example: It forms abridgement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abridgement。

items.example: It forms unabridged.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unabridged。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「删节；节略本」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「删节过的」
由 un- 加 abridged 构成，义为「未删节的」

definition_zh: 在国外；到国外；广泛地；流传在外
definition_en: in or to a foreign country, or widely over a large area
core_image: 一个人提着行李走出国门，背影落在陌生的街道上
scene: 小城青年毕业后大多去了海外工作，家里餐桌旁常空着一个位置。Their daughter has lived abroad for six years.
sceneCN: 这里 abroad 是「在国外居住」（第 1 个义项：在外国生活）；句意为他们的女儿已经在国外生活了六年。

pos.zh: 副词：在国外；到国外；广泛地；流传在外

derivatives.zh: 基础词 broad 意为「宽的」，无后缀；abroad 由 a- 加 broad 构成，语义从「宽阔」偏移为「到远处、到国外」
由 broad 加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「加宽；扩大」，语义从「宽」偏移为「使范围变大」
由 broad 加名词后缀 -th 构成，义为「宽度；广度」
由 broad 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「大致地；广泛地」

senses.title: Living in a foreign country
senses.definition: in a foreign country, especially as a resident or long-term visitor
senses.definitionCN: 在外国，尤其指作为居民或长期居留者
senses.example: Their daughter has lived abroad for six years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的女儿已经在国外生活了六年。
senses.why: The word began as 'widely, out of doors'; once it meant outside one's own land, residence abroad became its central sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初意为「广泛地、在户外」；一旦指「在本国之外」，在外国居住就成了它的中心义。

senses.title: Going to a foreign country
senses.definition: to or toward a foreign country, especially for travel or study
senses.definitionCN: 前往外国，尤指为了旅行或学习
senses.example: He went abroad to study engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 他去国外学习工程学。
senses.why: A state word also marks the movement that reaches it: being abroad becomes going abroad.
senses.whyCN: 表示状态的词也能标记到达该状态的动作：从「在国外」引申出「到国外去」。

senses.title: From a foreign country
senses.definition: from a foreign country, used in the phrase from abroad
senses.definitionCN: 来自外国，用于短语 from abroad
senses.example: The university attracts students from abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学吸引来自国外的学生。
senses.why: The same outside point can be viewed as a starting place, so abroad also marks origin.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「外面」的点也可以被看作起点，于是 abroad 也标记来源。

senses.title: In circulation, of news or rumour
senses.definition: in circulation among many people, especially of news, rumours, or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 在许多人中间流传，尤指消息、谣言或观念
senses.example: A rumour was abroad that the factory would close.
senses.exampleCN: 外面流传着工厂将要关闭的谣言。
senses.why: The old sense 'widely' survives here: a rumour abroad is one spread far beyond its source.
senses.whyCN: 旧的「广泛地」在这一义项里存活下来：a rumour abroad 就是传得远远超出源头。

senses.title: Scattered over a wide area
senses.definition: over a wide area, or scattered in many places
senses.definitionCN: 分布在大片区域，或散落在许多地方
senses.example: The seeds were scattered abroad by the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 种子被风吹散到各处。
senses.why: This is the original picture of spreading wide, applied to physical things rather than to people.
senses.whyCN: 这是「铺得很开」的原始画面，用在实物上而不是人身上。

senses.title: Out of doors, outdoors
senses.definition: out of doors or outdoors, an older literary sense
senses.definitionCN: 在门外、在户外，属较旧的文学用法
senses.example: Few people walked abroad after the curfew.
senses.exampleCN: 宵禁之后很少有人在外走动。
senses.why: Before it meant foreign lands, abroad meant out in the open, away from the house.
senses.whyCN: 在指外国之前，abroad 指「在露天、离家在外」，这是更早的空间义。

senses.title: At large, free from confinement
senses.definition: at large or free from confinement, an archaic legal use
senses.definitionCN: 逍遥在外、未被拘禁，属古旧的司法用法
senses.example: The prisoner was reported abroad again.
senses.exampleCN: 据报道，那名囚犯又在外逍遥了。
senses.why: To be out of the house extends to being out of a prison: both mean beyond the walls.
senses.whyCN: 「在屋外」可以扩展到「在监牢外」：两者都是「在墙外」。

senses.title: Internationally, across the world
senses.definition: across the world or internationally, especially of reputation, trade, or influence
senses.definitionCN: 遍及世界或在国际上，尤指名声、贸易或影响
senses.example: The brand became known abroad through trade fairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌通过贸易展会而在海外有了名气。
senses.why: When the frame is the whole world, abroad simply means beyond one's own country in any direction.
senses.whyCN: 当框架放大到整个世界，abroad 就只是指「越过本国，朝任何方向」。

intro.en: Abroad is an Old English compound of a- 'on' and broad 'wide'; it has no Latin cognate.
intro.cn: abroad 是古英语复合词，由 a-「在」与 broad「宽」构成；没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: brad meant broad or wide, and it is the source of broad and the second element of abroad.
items.cn: brad 意为「宽的」，是 broad 的来源，也是 abroad 的第二成分。

items.en: The prefix a- meant on or in, as still seen in abed and ashore.
items.cn: 前缀 a- 意为「在、在……里」，仍见于 abed 与 ashore。

items.en: a- plus brod produced abrod, 'widely, out of doors'.
items.cn: a- 加 brod 构成 abrod，意为「广泛地、在户外」。

items.en: The sense 'in a foreign country' appears in the sixteenth century; earlier dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 「在外国」这一义项在十六世纪出现；更早的年代不确定。

items.en: The older senses 'outdoors' and 'at large' survive mainly in literary and legal prose.
items.cn: 较旧的「在户外」与「在逃」义主要残存于文学与法律书面语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the broad family on the same Old English root; the near-meaning group gathers words for being outside one's own country.
note.cn: 形近组收同一古英语词根的 broad 词族；近义组收表示在本国之外的其他说法。

entries.definition: Wide in extent, the adjective from which abroad was built.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽的、广阔的」，是 abroad 的构词基础。

entries.definition: To make or become wider, often of experience or scope.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加宽、扩大」，由 broad 加 -en 构成。

entries.definition: The distance from side to side, or the range of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宽度、广度」，由 broad 加 -th 构成。

entries.definition: In general terms, or over a wide range.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大致地、广泛地」，由 broad 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A Middle English form meaning widely or out of doors, the earlier shape of abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 中古英语形式，义为「广泛地、在户外」，是 abroad 较早的形态。

entries.definition: In or to a country across the sea, from the speaker's point of view.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在海外、到海外」，强调跨海，与 abroad 常可互换。

entries.definition: Between or across nations, often of trade or reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在国际上」，侧重国家之间的关系，而不是个人在外国。

entries.definition: In or to another place, without saying that it is foreign.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在别处、到别处」，不限定是外国，范围比 abroad 宽。

entries.definition: At or to a great distance, a literary word for far away.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在远处、到远方」，属文学用语，只强调距离远。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real a- plus broad structure and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 a- 加 broad 结构，以及这个词的常见搭配。

normal.en: a- means 'on' and broad meant 'wide': abroad first meant widely.
normal.cn: a- 意为「在」，broad 意为「宽」：abroad 最初就是「广泛地」。

normal.en: broad, broaden and breadth all keep the old 'wide' root.
normal.cn: broad、broaden 与 breadth 都保留古老的「宽」词根。

normal.en: go abroad and live abroad keep the modern country sense.
normal.cn: go abroad 与 live abroad 保存了现代的「外国」义。

normal.en: from abroad marks the direction of arrival, not residence.
normal.cn: from abroad 标记的是到达的方向，而不是居住的状态。

normal.en: spread abroad is the old 'widely' sense still in use.
normal.cn: spread abroad 是仍在使用的旧义「广泛地」。

abstract.en: Picture a person stepping over a line drawn around the map of home: the other side is abroad.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人跨过围绕本国地图画的那条线：线的另一边就是 abroad。

abstract.en: The same line can be crossed by seeds, rumours or a reputation.
abstract.cn: 跨过这条线的可以是人，也可以是种子、谣言或名声。

abstract.en: Its oldest sense was simply 'out in the open', which is why it still means outdoors in old texts.
abstract.cn: 它最古老的意思只是「在开阔处」，所以旧文本里它仍然表示「在户外」。

examples.en: She went abroad for a year after university.
examples.cn: 大学毕业后她去国外待了一年。

examples.en: The company has offices at home and abroad.
examples.cn: 这家公司在国内外都设有办事处。

examples.en: News of the discovery spread abroad quickly.
examples.cn: 这一发现的消息很快传播开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额布若德」——布若德一家提着箱子去了国外：在国外

root: 古英语 abrod 由 a-（在）+ brad（宽）构成，本义「广泛地、在户外」，十六世纪起指「在外国」。该词属日耳曼语复合词，没有拉丁同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all move a person or thing across a boundary: the boundary of one's country, of a house, of a prison, or of a narrow area.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把人或物移过一条边界：国界、屋门、监狱的墙，或一片狭小区域的边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a traveller steps over the line that marks home and walks on.
core.cn: 核心意象：旅人跨过标记家乡的那条线，继续向前走。

branches.en: THE COUNTRY: residence in a foreign land, or the journey that reaches it.
branches.cn: 国度线：在外国居住，或踏上前往那里的旅程。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the same outside point becomes the place one comes from.
branches.cn: 来源线：同一个「外面」也变成出发的地方。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: news, rumours, or seeds travel over a wide area.
branches.cn: 散布线：消息、谣言或种子铺展到很大一片区域。

branches.en: THE WALL: out of the house, and by extension out of a prison.
branches.cn: 围墙线：在屋外，进而指在监牢之外。

branches.en: THE WORLD: beyond one's own country in any direction, as reputation or trade grows.
branches.cn: 世界线：名声或贸易增长时，越过本国朝任何方向延伸。

intro.en: Abroad is an Old English compound; its family is built with broad and ordinary suffixes rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: abroad 是古英语复合词；它的词族由 broad 加普通后缀构成，而不是靠前缀派生。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate: abroad rests on the Germanic root brad, 'wide'.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁同族词：abroad 建立在日耳曼语词根 brad「宽」之上。

items.example: It forms abroad and abed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abroad 与 abed。

items.example: Brad is the root of broad and abroad.
items.exampleCN: brad 是 broad 与 abroad 的词根。

items.example: A broad street runs through the town.
items.exampleCN: 一条宽阔的街道穿过小镇。

items.meaning: in or to a foreign country
items.example: He worked abroad for ten years.
items.exampleCN: 他在国外工作了十年。

items.example: Travel broadens the mind.
items.exampleCN: 旅行开阔眼界。

items.example: The breadth of the river surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这条河的宽度让我们吃惊。

items.example: Broadly speaking, the plan is sound.
items.exampleCN: 大体上说，这个计划是合理的。

items.example: Abrood is the earlier spelling of abroad.
items.exampleCN: abrood 是 abroad 较早的拼写。

derivatives.zh: 由 broad 加 -en 构成，义为「加宽；扩大」
由 broad 加 -th 构成，义为「宽度；广度」
由 broad 加 -ly 构成，义为「大致地；广泛地」

definition_zh: 突然的；意外的；陡峭的；唐突的；生硬的
definition_en: sudden and unexpected, steep, or short and rude in manner
core_image: 一句话还没说完，声音就被硬生生折断
scene: 山路忽然断在一处塌方前，队伍不得不停住脚步。The hike came to an abrupt stop when the trail collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里 abrupt 是「突然的、意外的」（第 1 个义项：事情毫无预兆地发生）；句意为小径塌方时，徒步突然中断了。

pos.zh: 形容词：突然的；意外的；陡峭的；唐突的；生硬的

derivatives.zh: 由 abrupt 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「突然地；唐突地」
由 abrupt 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「突然；唐突；陡峭」
由拉丁词干 abrupt- 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「突然分离、中断」，多用于医学

senses.title: Sudden and unexpected
senses.definition: happening suddenly and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 毫无预兆地突然发生
senses.example: The meeting came to an abrupt halt when the power failed.
senses.exampleCN: 停电时会议突然中止了。
senses.why: The Latin participle meant broken off; what is broken off has no warning and no smooth lead-in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「被折断的」；被折断的东西没有预兆，也没有平缓的过渡。

senses.title: Ending a process short
senses.definition: ending a process, discussion, or activity before its natural finish
senses.definitionCN: 让过程、讨论或活动在自然结束之前中断
senses.example: The abrupt end of the talks surprised both delegations.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈的突然终止让两个代表团都很意外。
senses.why: A conversation is a continuous line; breaking it leaves the line cut in the middle.
senses.whyCN: 对话是一条连续的线；把它折断，线就停在中间。

senses.title: Steep, of a slope
senses.definition: rising or falling very steeply, with little horizontal distance
senses.definitionCN: 上升或下降非常陡，水平距离很短
senses.example: The path turned into an abrupt climb near the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 接近山顶时，小路变成一段陡峭的爬升。
senses.why: A steep slope is a surface that breaks sharply upward instead of rising gradually.
senses.whyCN: 陡坡是一面陡然向上折断的表面，而不是缓缓升起的坡。

senses.title: Rude and offhand in manner
senses.definition: speaking or acting in a way that seems rude, cold, and unfriendly
senses.definitionCN: 说话或行事显得无礼、冷淡、不友好
senses.example: His abrupt reply made the room go quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 他唐突的回答让屋里安静了下来。
senses.why: Social smoothness is a gradual slope; a person who cuts the conversation short seems broken off too.
senses.whyCN: 社交上的圆滑是一道缓坡；把话头直接切断的人，也像被折断一样。

senses.title: Short and cold, of an answer
senses.definition: expressed in very few words, with little warmth or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 只用很少几个字表达，缺少温度与解释
senses.example: She gave an abrupt nod and left.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡地点了下头就走了。
senses.why: An answer stripped of explanation is a sentence with its ending cut off.
senses.whyCN: 抽掉解释的回答，就是把句子的结尾剪掉。

senses.title: Disjointed, of style
senses.definition: lacking smooth connections, of writing, speech, or narrative style
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏顺畅衔接，用于文字、言语或叙事风格
senses.example: The abrupt style of the report was hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告生硬的文风让人难以跟上。
senses.why: Style is judged by its transitions; where transitions are missing, the text looks broken into pieces.
senses.whyCN: 文风看的是衔接；衔接缺失，文本就像被折成一段一段。

senses.title: Sharp, of a change in amount
senses.definition: sharp and large, of a change in amount, level, or direction
senses.definitionCN: 数量、水平或方向发生又急又大的变化
senses.example: There was an abrupt rise in temperature at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午气温急剧上升。
senses.why: A graph that jumps instead of sloping gently looks like a line snapped upward.
senses.whyCN: 曲线陡然跳起而不是平缓上升，就像一条被向上折断的线。

senses.title: Without transition, in a sequence
senses.definition: moving from one scene or topic to another with no transition
senses.definitionCN: 从一个场景或话题直接跳到另一个，没有过渡
senses.example: The film makes an abrupt jump from one scene to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片从一个场景突兀地跳到下一个。
senses.why: A sequence is expected to flow; a jump breaks the flow, which is the same broken-line picture again.
senses.whyCN: 序列本应顺畅流动；突然一跳打断了流动，仍是同一条被折断的线。

intro.en: Abrupt comes straight from a Latin participle meaning broken off, built on the verb for breaking.
intro.cn: abrupt 直接来自一个意为「被折断的」拉丁分词，其基础动词表示「折断」。

items.en: rumpere meant to break or burst; it also supplies rupture and erupt.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「折断、爆裂」，还给出 rupture 与 erupt。

items.en: ab-, 'away', plus rumpere gave abrumpere, 'to break off'.
items.cn: ab-「离开」加 rumpere 构成 abrumpere，意为「折断、断掉」。

items.en: The past participle abruptus meant broken off, steep, or hasty, and English took it as an adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 abruptus 意为「被折断的、陡的、仓促的」，英语直接把它当作形容词借用。

items.en: English abrupt is recorded from the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 abrupt 自十六世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word extended from broken terrain and broken speech to abrupt changes on graphs and in narratives.
items.cn: 这个词从断裂的地形与断裂的言语，扩展到图表与叙事中的突变。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the rumpere family and its Latin relatives; the near-meaning group gathers words for suddenness, steepness, and bluntness.
note.cn: 形近组收 rumpere 词族及其拉丁同族；近义组收表示突然、陡峭与生硬的词。

entries.definition: Suddenly and without transition, or in a rude, short manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「突然地；唐突地」，由 abrupt 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being sudden, steep, or blunt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突然；陡峭；唐突」，由 abrupt 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: A sudden breaking off or separation, used especially in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突然分离、中断」，多用于医学，由拉丁词干加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: To burst out, of a volcano or a sudden emotion, from the same Latin rumpere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「爆发、喷发」，与 abrupt 同出拉丁语 rumpere「折断、爆裂」。

entries.definition: A break or burst, of a pipe, a relationship, or tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「破裂、断裂」，同样出自 rumpere。

entries.definition: Happening quickly and unexpectedly; the most general word for the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「突然的」，是第一个义项最一般的说法，但不含「生硬」义。

entries.definition: Not anticipated, whether sudden or not.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「意外的、未料到的」，只强调没有预料，不强调速度快。

entries.definition: Short and rude in speech, often of a reply or a refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简短无礼的」，多指回答或拒绝，比 abrupt 更聚焦于言语的冷淡。

entries.definition: Rising or falling at a sharp angle, of a slope or price.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陡峭的」，用于坡度或价格，与 abrupt 的地形义相近。

entries.definition: Done too quickly, without enough thought.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「仓促的、草率的」，强调做得太快而欠考虑，与 abrupt 的「突然」义不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb rumpere and the phrases abrupt commonly forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 rumpere，以及 abrupt 常见的搭配。

normal.en: rumpere is to break: abruptus is 'broken off'.
normal.cn: rumpere 是「折断」：abruptus 就是「被折断的」。

normal.en: ab- means away, so abrumpere is to break away or snap off.
normal.cn: ab- 意为「离开」，所以 abrumpere 是「折断、断掉」。

normal.en: Erupt and rupture belong to the same rumpere family.
normal.cn: erupt 与 rupture 都属于同一个 rumpere 词族。

normal.en: An abrupt end is a sentence snapped in the middle.
normal.cn: an abrupt end 就是一句话从中间被折断。

normal.en: An abrupt slope and an abrupt manner share the same jump.
normal.cn: 陡坡与唐突的态度，共享同一个「陡然一跳」。

abstract.en: Picture a stick broken in two: one half points up, one half points down, with no curve between.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被折成两截的木棍：一半朝上，一半朝下，中间没有弧线。

abstract.en: The break can happen in a conversation, a graph, a hillside, or a person's voice.
abstract.cn: 这道断口可以出现在对话里、曲线里、山壁上，也可以出现在人的语气里。

abstract.en: Whatever is abrupt has lost its joining part.
abstract.cn: 凡是 abrupt 的东西，都失去了中间那段衔接。

examples.en: The road ended in an abrupt drop to the valley.
examples.cn: 道路在一处陡然落向山谷的地方到了尽头。

examples.en: His abrupt tone told us the subject was closed.
examples.cn: 他生硬的语气告诉我们这个话题到此为止。

examples.en: There was an abrupt change of plan after lunch.
examples.cn: 午饭后计划发生了突然的变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额布拉普特」——布拉普特一脚急刹，事情说断就断：突然的

root: 拉丁语 abruptus 是 abrumpere「折断」的过去分词，abrumpere 由 ab-「离开」+ rumpere「折断」构成；rumpere 还给出 erupt 与 rupture。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a line broken instead of bending: a sudden event, a stopped process, a steep slope, a blunt manner, a cold answer, a disjointed style, a sharp change, an untransitioned jump.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一条被折断而不是弯过去的线：突然的事件、中断的过程、陡峭的坡、唐突的态度、冷淡的回答、生硬的文风、急剧的变化、缺过渡的跳跃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line is snapped in two, leaving a hard edge with no curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线被折成两截，留下没有弧度的硬边。

branches.en: THE EVENT: an occurrence, a process or a change stops or jumps with no warning.
branches.cn: 事件线：一件事、一个过程或一次变化毫无预兆地停住或跳起。

branches.en: THE GROUND: a slope rises or falls at a sharp angle rather than gradually.
branches.cn: 地面线：坡面以很陡的角度升起或落下，而不是缓缓过渡。

branches.en: THE PERSON: speech and replies are cut short, and the cut feels cold or rude.
branches.cn: 人物线：话语与回答被剪短，这种剪断让人感到冷淡或无礼。

branches.en: THE STYLE: missing transitions make a text look broken into pieces.
branches.cn: 风格线：缺少衔接使文本看起来像被折成碎片。

branches.en: THE SEQUENCE: a narrative jumps from one scene to the next without a bridge.
branches.cn: 序列线：叙事从一个场景跳到下一个，中间没有桥。

intro.en: Abrupt is a Latin participle used as an English adjective; English adds -ly, -ness and -ion to it.
intro.cn: abrupt 是直接用作英语形容词的拉丁分词；英语在它之上加 -ly、-ness 与 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere, abrumpere and abruptus are all recorded, so no reconstruction is needed at this level.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rumpere、abrumpere 与 abruptus 均有文献记录，这一层不需要重构。

items.example: The prefix marks the breaking away.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记「断离」的方向。

items.example: The verb also gives erupt and rupture.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词还给出 erupt 与 rupture。

items.example: The compound adds direction to the breaking.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词给「折断」加上方向。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The path made an abrupt turn.
items.exampleCN: 小路陡然转了个弯。

items.example: It forms abruptly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abruptly。

items.example: It forms abruptness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abruptness。

items.example: It forms abruption.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abruption。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「突然地；唐突地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「突然；唐突」
由拉丁词干加 -ion 构成，义为「突然分离；中断」

definition_zh: 缺席；不在；缺乏；没有
definition_en: the state of not being present where one is expected, or the fact that something does not exist
core_image: 长桌旁留着一把空椅子，椅背上还搭着外套
scene: 教室里靠窗的位置空着，桌上摊着一本没合上的书。The teacher marked his absence without saying a word.
sceneCN: 这里 absence 是「缺席、不在场」（第 1 个义项：该在场却不在）；句意为老师一言不发地记下了他的缺席。

pos.zh: 名词：缺席；不在；缺乏；没有

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 absent- 去掉名词后缀 -ia 构成形容词，义为「缺席的、不在的」
由 absent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「心不在焉地」
由 absent 加 -ee「具有某特征的人」构成，义为「缺席者」
由 absentee 加 -ism 构成，义为「经常缺勤、旷工现象」
由 absent 与 minded 复合，义为「心不在焉的」，语义从「不在场」偏移到「心思不在场」

senses.title: The state of not being present
senses.definition: the state of not being present in a place where one is expected
senses.definitionCN: 在一个本应到场的地方却没有出现
senses.example: Her absence from the meeting was noticed at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她缺席会议的事立刻就被注意到了。
senses.why: Latin abesse is 'to be away': absence is simply the noun for that state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abesse 意为「不在」；absence 就是这一状态的名词形式。

senses.title: The period of being away
senses.definition: the period during which someone is away from a place
senses.definitionCN: 某人离开某地、不在其中的那段时间
senses.example: During his absence, the office was reorganised.
senses.exampleCN: 他不在的时候，办公室重新调整了。
senses.why: A state that lasts becomes a stretch of time; the noun shifts from 'not there' to 'the time not there'.
senses.whyCN: 持续的状态会变成一段时间；名词从「不在」转指「不在的那段时间」。

senses.title: Failure to attend school or work
senses.definition: the failure to attend school, work, or a duty that one is expected to attend
senses.definitionCN: 没有去上课、上班或履行应尽的职责
senses.example: The school records every absence from class.
senses.exampleCN: 学校记录每一次缺课。
senses.why: Attendance is counted, so each missed occasion becomes a countable instance of absence.
senses.whyCN: 出勤是要统计的，于是每一次没到都成为一个可数的「缺席」事件。

senses.title: The lack of something
senses.definition: the fact that something is not present or does not exist
senses.definitionCN: 某物不存在或不出现在应有的地方
senses.example: The absence of evidence is not proof of innocence.
senses.exampleCN: 没有证据并不等于证明清白。
senses.why: The same 'not there' is transferred from people to things: evidence can be absent too.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「不在」从人转移到物：证据同样可以「不在」。

senses.title: Absence of mind: a moment of distraction
senses.definition: in the phrase absence of mind, a state of not paying attention to what one is doing
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 absence of mind，指注意力不在当下所做的事上
senses.example: He lost his keys through a moment of absence of mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为一时心不在焉而丢了钥匙。
senses.why: Attention is pictured as a presence in the mind; when it drifts, the mind itself seems absent.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被想象成「在场」于心中；注意力飘走时，心本身就好像不在了。

senses.title: A missing person, in law
senses.definition: in law, the state of a person whose whereabouts are unknown for a long period
senses.definitionCN: 法律上，一个人长期下落不明、行踪无从查明的状态
senses.example: The court declared him dead after seven years of absence.
senses.exampleCN: 在失踪七年后，法院宣告他死亡。
senses.why: Law needs a name for the long, unexplained not-there that can end in a declaration of death.
senses.whyCN: 法律需要一个名称，来指长期且无从解释的「不在」，这种状态可能以宣告死亡告终。

senses.title: The felt lack of someone
senses.definition: the felt lack of a person whose presence is missed
senses.definitionCN: 因为思念而感受到的某人的不在
senses.example: The house felt empty after the children's absence.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们不在之后，屋子显得空荡荡的。
senses.why: Here absence is not a fact but a feeling: the missing person is present in the emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 absence 不是事实而是感受：缺席的人正存在于那片空荡之中。

senses.title: Official permission to be away
senses.definition: in the phrase leave of absence, official permission to be away from work or duty
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 leave of absence，指获准离开工作岗位或职责
senses.example: She took a leave of absence to care for her mother.
senses.exampleCN: 她请假去照顾母亲。
senses.why: Institutions turn absence into something granted, and the phrase leave of absence records that permission.
senses.whyCN: 机构把「不在」变成一种被批准的东西，leave of absence 这一短语正记录着这份许可。

intro.en: Absence comes through Old French from the Latin noun for being away, built on the verb 'to be'.
intro.cn: absence 经古法语来自拉丁语中表示「不在」的名词，其基础是动词「存在」。

items.en: esse is the Latin verb 'to be', the base of English present and essence.
items.cn: esse 是拉丁语动词「存在、是」，是英语 present 与 essence 的基础。

items.en: ab-, 'away', plus esse gave abesse, 'to be away, to be absent'.
items.cn: ab-「离开」加 esse 构成 abesse，意为「不在、缺席」。

items.en: The present participle absens, stem absent-, supplied the adjective, and absentia supplied the noun.
items.cn: 现在分词 absens 的词干 absent- 提供形容词，名词 absentia 提供名词。

items.en: Old French absence carried the noun into Middle English with its modern spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 absence 把这个名词带入中古英语，并带来现代拼写。

items.en: English absence is recorded from the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 absence 自十四世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the absent family on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers nouns for what is missing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干的 absent 词族；近义组收表示「缺失」的名词。

entries.definition: Not present, or lacking; the adjective built on the same Latin stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺席的、缺乏的」，与 absence 同出拉丁词干 absent-。

entries.definition: In a distracted or inattentive manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」，由 absent 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A person who is not present, especially one who stays away from work or school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者」，尤指经常不到岗或不到校的人。

entries.definition: The habit or pattern of staying away from work or school without good reason.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经常缺勤、旷工」，由 absentee 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: Forgetful or distracted, as if the mind is elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心不在焉的」，由 absent 与 minded 复合。

entries.definition: The state of not having enough of something, or none at all.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「缺乏、没有」，强调数量不足，与 absence 的「不存在」义相近。

entries.definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something that is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「短缺、不足」，多用于物资、人力等可计数的资源。

entries.definition: The failure to attend a class, meeting, or duty.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「不出席、缺勤」，是 absence 在考勤语境中的正式同义说法。

entries.definition: A lack or shortage of something needed, often of a nutrient or a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺乏、不足」，多指营养或某种品质的缺失。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb abesse and the fixed phrases absence appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 abesse，以及 absence 出现的固定短语。

normal.en: abesse is 'to be away': absence is the state it names.
normal.cn: abesse 是「不在」：absence 就是它命名的状态。

normal.en: esse is the Latin verb 'to be', hidden inside absent and present alike.
normal.cn: esse 是拉丁语动词「存在」，同样藏在 absent 与 present 里。

normal.en: absence of evidence and absence of mind both use the plain idea of 'not there'.
normal.cn: absence of evidence 与 absence of mind 都用了「不在」这个朴素想法。

normal.en: leave of absence is the formal phrase for permitted time away.
normal.cn: leave of absence 是表示获准离岗的正式短语。

normal.en: absentee and absenteeism extend the same idea to people and to habits.
normal.cn: absentee 与 absenteeism 把同一想法扩展到人，再扩展到习惯。

abstract.en: Picture a chair left empty at a long table: the shape of the person is still there.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌旁空着的一把椅子：人的形状还留在那里。

abstract.en: The empty chair can be a meeting, a classroom, a home, or a legal file.
abstract.cn: 这把空椅子可以出现在会议室、教室、家里，也可以出现在一份法律档案里。

abstract.en: Absence is not nothing: it is a space that someone or something used to fill.
abstract.cn: absence 不是「无」：它是一个曾经被人或物填满的空位。

examples.en: Her absence from the meeting was noticed at once.
examples.cn: 她缺席会议的事立刻就被注意到了。

examples.en: In the absence of a witness, the case is hard to prove.
examples.cn: 没有证人，这个案子很难证明。

examples.en: He returned to work after a long absence.
examples.cn: 长期离开之后，他回到了工作岗位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃布森斯」——布森斯没到场，椅子空着：缺席

root: 拉丁语 absentia 由 absens（absent-）构成，absens 是 abesse「不在」的现在分词，abesse 又由 ab-「离开」+ esse「存在」构成；经古法语 absence 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a place that is not filled: a seat at a meeting, a stretch of time, a class register, a missing fact, a wandering mind, a legal file, a felt emptiness, a granted leave.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一个没有被填满的位置：会议上的座位、一段时间、考勤册、缺失的事实、走神的心思、法律档案、感受到的空荡，以及被批准的离岗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty chair at a long table, with a coat still hanging on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌旁一把空椅子，椅背上还搭着外套。

branches.en: THE STATE: someone expected is simply not there.
branches.cn: 状态线：本应到场的人就是不在。

branches.en: THE TIME: the not-there lasts, and the emptiness is felt while it lasts.
branches.cn: 时间线：不在持续一段时间，而空荡在这段时间里被感受到。

branches.en: THE REGISTER: each missed class or shift becomes a countable absence.
branches.cn: 考勤线：每一次没上课、没到岗，都成为一个可数的 absence。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE: a fact can be missing, and attention can be missing from the mind.
branches.cn: 无形线：事实可以缺失，注意力也可以从心里缺席。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: law names a long disappearance, and employers grant leave of absence.
branches.cn: 制度线：法律为长期失踪命名，雇主则批准 leave of absence。

intro.en: Absence is a Latin noun built on esse; English adds -ee, -ism and compounds to make the family.
intro.cn: absence 是建立在 esse 之上的拉丁名词；英语再加 -ee、-ism 与复合结构扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin esse, abesse, absens and absentia are all recorded, so their forms are attested rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 esse、abesse、absens 与 absentia 均有文献记录，形式有据可查，并非重构。

items.example: It turns 'to be' into 'to be away'.
items.exampleCN: 它把「存在」变成「不在」。

items.example: Esse is the base of essence and present.
items.exampleCN: esse 是 essence 与 present 的基础。

items.example: The verb is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的来源。

items.example: Its stem absent- gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它的词干 absent- 给出英语形容词。

items.example: Absentia is the direct source of English absence.
items.exampleCN: absentia 是英语 absence 的直接来源。

items.example: It forms absence from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁词干构成 absence。

items.example: It forms absentee.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absentee。

items.example: It forms absenteeism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absenteeism。

items.meaning: the state of not being there
items.example: The noun entered English in the fourteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词在十四世纪进入英语。

derivatives.zh: 由本词的拉丁词干构成，义为「缺席的」
由 absent 加 -ly 构成，义为「心不在焉地」
由 absentee 加 -ism 构成，义为「经常缺勤」

definition_zh: 缺席的；不在的；缺乏的；心不在焉的；（动词）使缺席
definition_en: not present in a place, lacking, inattentive, or to keep oneself away from a place
core_image: 长桌旁空着的座位，椅背上搭着没人穿的外套
scene: 晨读开始，靠窗的座位仍空着，值日生把点名册翻到下一页。One student was absent from the morning class.
sceneCN: 这里 absent 是「缺席的」（第 1 个义项：本应到场却不在）；句意为有一名学生缺席了晨读课。

pos.zh: 形容词：缺席的；不在的；缺乏的；心不在焉的
动词（正式）：使缺席；不到场

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁词干 absent- 加名词后缀 -ia 演变来的 -ence 构成，义为「缺席；缺乏」
由 absent 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「心不在焉地」
由 absent 加 -ee 构成，义为「缺席者」
由 absentee 加 -ism 构成，义为「经常缺勤」
由 absent 与 minded 复合，义为「心不在焉的」

senses.title: Not present in a place
senses.definition: not present in a place where one is expected to be
senses.definitionCN: 在本应到场的地方却没有出现
senses.example: One student was absent from the morning class.
senses.exampleCN: 有一名学生缺席了晨读课。
senses.why: The participle absens is 'being away'; the adjective simply describes that condition.
senses.whyCN: 分词 absens 意为「不在的」；这个形容词只是描述这一状态。

senses.title: Away from a post or duty
senses.definition: away from a place, post, or duty, often used with from
senses.definitionCN: 离开某地、岗位或职责，常与 from 连用
senses.example: He was absent from duty for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 他离开岗位两天。
senses.why: A duty is a place one is expected to occupy, so being away from it is the same absence in official language.
senses.whyCN: 职责也是一个人应当占据的位置，离开它就是官方语境中的同一种缺席。

senses.title: Lacking or not existing
senses.definition: not existing or not present in a thing, especially a quality or fact
senses.definitionCN: 某物、某种品质或事实不存在于其中
senses.example: Several key facts are absent from the report.
senses.exampleCN: 报告里缺少几个关键事实。
senses.why: The word moves from people to qualities: what is not there is absent, whether a person or a fact.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从人转到品质：不在的东西就是 absent，不管是人还是事实。

senses.title: Without, as a formal preposition
senses.definition: in formal American usage, without or lacking something
senses.definitionCN: 正式美式用法，表示「如果没有、缺少某物」
senses.example: Absent any objection, the plan will go ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 如果没有异议，这个计划将继续推进。
senses.why: A participle can stand at the head of a clause as a kind of preposition: 'it being absent' becomes simply absent.
senses.whyCN: 分词可以站在从句开头充当介词：本来是「它不在」，省略后就直接说 absent。

senses.title: Distracted, not paying attention
senses.definition: showing that one is not paying attention to what is happening
senses.definitionCN: 表现出没有把注意力放在眼前的事情上
senses.example: She stared at the page with an absent look.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着心不在焉的神情盯着书页。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a place, and a person whose mind is elsewhere has an absent look.
senses.whyCN: 心思被当作一个地方；心思在别处的人，神情自然就是「不在」的。

senses.title: Vague or vacant in expression
senses.definition: empty or vague in expression, as if the mind is somewhere else
senses.definitionCN: 神情空茫或含混，仿佛心思在别处
senses.example: He answered with an absent nod.
senses.exampleCN: 他心不在焉地点了下头。
senses.why: The look carries the absence: the face is present, but the person behind it seems not to be.
senses.whyCN: 神情承载着那种「不在」：脸在眼前，脸后面的人却似乎不在。

senses.title: Of unknown whereabouts
senses.definition: not to be found, of a person whose whereabouts are unknown
senses.definitionCN: 找不到，指一个人行踪不明
senses.example: The file lists him as absent since spring.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记载他从春天起就下落不明。
senses.why: In records, a person who cannot be located is marked absent, the same word as not attending.
senses.whyCN: 在档案里，找不到的人被标记为 absent，与「没到场」用的是同一个词。

senses.title: To keep oneself away, as a verb
senses.definition: to keep oneself away from a place or duty, in the formal phrase absent oneself
senses.definitionCN: 正式短语 absent oneself，指让自己离开某地或不履行职责
senses.example: She absented herself from the vote without explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 她没有解释就没有参加投票。
senses.why: English turned the adjective into a reflexive verb: one makes oneself absent.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个形容词变成反身动词：人使自己「不在」。

intro.en: Absent is the Latin present participle of 'to be away', taken into English through Old French.
intro.cn: absent 是拉丁语「不在」的现在分词，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: esse is the Latin verb 'to be'; it also underlies essence and present.
items.cn: esse 是拉丁语动词「存在、是」，也是 essence 与 present 的基础。

items.en: ab-, 'away', plus esse gave abesse, 'to be away'.
items.cn: ab-「离开」加 esse 构成 abesse，意为「不在」。

items.en: The present participle absens, stem absent-, meant 'being away' and became the English adjective.
items.cn: 现在分词 absens 的词干为 absent-，意为「不在的」，后来成为英语形容词。

items.en: Old French absent carried the adjective into Middle English with its modern spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 absent 把这个形容词带入中古英语，并带来现代拼写。

items.en: English absent is recorded from the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 absent 自十四世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the absence family on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what is not there or not attending.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干的 absence 词族；近义组收表示「不在」「缺席」或「不走神」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of not being present, or for a lack.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席；缺乏」，与 absent 同出拉丁词干 absent-。

entries.definition: In a distracted manner, without full attention.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」，由 absent 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A person who is not present, especially at work or school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者」，由 absent 加 -ee 构成。

entries.definition: The habitual failure to attend work or school.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经常缺勤」，由 absentee 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: Forgetful or easily distracted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心不在焉的」，由 absent 与 minded 复合。

entries.definition: Not present or not found, especially of a person or a thing that should be there.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺失的、失踪的」，强调本该在却找不到。

entries.definition: Not at home or not in the usual place, often for a period.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或副词，义为「不在的、离开的」，多指暂时不在常在地点。

entries.definition: Not having enough of a quality or thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺乏的、不足的」，用于品质或事物。

entries.definition: Not paying attention to what is happening.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不注意的、走神的」，与 absent 的心不在焉义相近。

entries.definition: So absorbed in one's own thoughts that one ignores the present.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心事重重的、出神的」，强调被自己的念头占住。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin participle absens and the phrases absent appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁分词 absens，以及 absent 出现的搭配。

normal.en: abesse is 'to be away', and absens is the person who is away.
normal.cn: abesse 是「不在」，absens 就是那个不在的人。

normal.en: The a- in absent is the same 'away' prefix seen in abduct and avert.
normal.cn: absent 里的 a- 与 abduct、avert 里的前缀一样，含「离开」的意思。

normal.en: Be absent from is the everyday pattern; absented himself is the formal verb.
normal.cn: be absent from 是日常搭配；absented himself 则是正式的动词用法。

normal.en: An absent look means the face is here but the mind is not.
normal.cn: an absent look 指脸在这里，心思却不在。

normal.en: absent without leave shortens to AWL in military records.
normal.cn: absent without leave 在军务记录中缩作 AWL。

abstract.en: Picture a chair with a coat on it but nobody in it: the body is absent, the trace remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一把搭着外套却没人坐的椅子：身体不在了，痕迹还在。

abstract.en: The same chair can be a classroom seat, a desk at work, or a place at a family table.
abstract.cn: 同一把椅子可以是教室座位、工位，也可以是家里餐桌旁的位置。

abstract.en: Absent is always a relation: someone or something is missing from somewhere.
abstract.cn: absent 永远是一种关系：某人或某物从某处缺席。

examples.en: Three students were absent from the first lesson.
examples.cn: 有三名学生缺席了第一节课。

examples.en: He seemed absent and answered only in monosyllables.
examples.cn: 他显得心不在焉，只用单音节词回答。

examples.en: She absented herself from the vote without explanation.
examples.cn: 她没有解释就没有参加投票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃布森特」——布森特今天没来上课，座位空着：缺席的

root: 拉丁语 absens（词干 absent-）是 abesse「不在」的现在分词，abesse 由 ab-「离开」+ esse「存在」构成；经古法语 absent 进入英语，另有反身动词用法 absent oneself。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place someone or something outside an expected spot: a classroom, a post, a report, a clause, a face, a record, or a duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把人或物放在一个应到的位置之外：教室、岗位、报告、从句、神情、档案或职责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty seat at a long table, with a coat no one is wearing.
core.cn: 核心意象：长桌旁空着的座位，椅背上搭着没人穿的外套。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a person is not in the classroom, or not at the post.
branches.cn: 位置线：人不在教室，也不在岗位上。

branches.en: THE THING: a fact or quality is not in the report, so it is absent too.
branches.cn: 事物线：某项事实或品质不在报告里，因此同样是 absent。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE: the participle turns into a formal preposition meaning 'without'.
branches.cn: 从句线：这个分词变成正式的介词，意为「如果没有」。

branches.en: THE MIND: attention leaves, and the face shows the absence.
branches.cn: 心思线：注意力离开，脸上就显出那种「不在」。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a person may be listed as missing, or may absent himself by choice.
branches.cn: 档案线：一个人可能被记为下落不明，也可能主动使自己缺席。

intro.en: Absent is a Latin participle used as an English adjective and then as a verb; suffixes extend it into adverbs and nouns.
intro.cn: absent 是拉丁分词，先作英语形容词，再作动词；后缀把它扩展成副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin esse, abesse and absens are recorded, so the forms are attested rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 esse、abesse 与 absens 均有文献记录，形式有据可查，并非重构。

items.example: It marks the direction of being away.
items.exampleCN: 它标记「不在」的方向。

items.example: The verb underlies essence and present.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 essence 与 present 的基础。

items.example: The verb is the source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的来源。

items.example: Its stem gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它的词干给出英语形容词。

items.example: He was absent from school.
items.exampleCN: 他没去上学。

items.example: It forms absently.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absently。

items.example: It forms absentee.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absentee。

items.example: It forms absenteeism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absenteeism。

items.meaning: having a certain kind of mind
items.example: It forms absent-minded.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absent-minded。

derivatives.zh: 由本词的拉丁词干加 -ence 演变构成，义为「缺席；缺乏」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「心不在焉地」
由本词加 -ee 构成，义为「缺席者」

definition_zh: 绝对的；完全的；确实的；专制的；（语法）独立的
definition_en: complete and total, not limited by anything else, or fixed and true without depending on other things
core_image: 已经松开、彻底解开的绳结，不再被任何条件拴住
scene: 冬夜的田野被厚雪覆盖，四处没有一丝声响。In the absolute silence of the valley, she could hear her own heartbeat.
sceneCN: 这里 absolute 是「完全的、彻底的」（第 2 个义项：程度上的彻底与毫无例外）；句意为在山谷彻底的寂静中，她能听见自己的心跳。

pos.zh: 绝对的；完全的；确实的；专制的
绝对的事物；绝对真理

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 absolute 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「绝对地；完全地；确实地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「绝对性；完全性」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ism 构成，义为「专制主义；绝对主义」
由形容词加 -ist 构成，指「专制主义者；绝对论者」，也可作形容词
与 absolve 同源的名词，来自拉丁语 absolvere，义为「赦免；免除罪责」

senses.title: Total and complete in degree
senses.definition: complete and total, used to stress that there is no exception, doubt or limitation at all
senses.definitionCN: 完全的、彻底的，用来强调毫无例外、毫无疑义或毫无限制
senses.example: The whole project was an absolute disaster from the first day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目从第一天起就是彻底的灾难。
senses.why: Latin absolutus is 'loosened, freed from bonds'; something fully freed from every limit is complete without qualification.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absolutus 是「被松开、从束缚中解脱」，彻底摆脱一切限制的东西，也就是毫无保留的完全。

senses.title: Not dependent on anything else
senses.titleCN: 不受其他事物左右的绝对
senses.definition: existing or measured on its own, not relative to or dependent on something else
senses.definitionCN: 自身存在或自身计量，不相对、不依赖其他事物
senses.example: Physicists still cannot reach absolute zero by any method.
senses.exampleCN: 物理学家至今仍无法用任何方法达到绝对零度。
senses.why: The image is an untied knot: what is absolute stands alone, fastened to no other thing.
senses.whyCN: 意象是解开的绳结：绝对之物独立存在，不拴在任何别的东西上。

senses.title: Certain and beyond doubt
senses.definition: definite and unquestionable, so that no doubt or argument is possible
senses.definitionCN: 明确而无可置疑，因而容不下疑问或争辩
senses.example: There is absolute proof that the manuscript was written in that year.
senses.exampleCN: 有确凿的证据证明这份手稿写于那一年。
senses.why: A fact released from all doubt is at the end of every argument, which is exactly what 'absolute' claims.
senses.whyCN: 摆脱一切疑问的事实，是所有争论的终点，这正是 absolute 所主张的。

senses.title: Unlimited in power or authority
senses.definition: having total power, not limited by law, parliament or any other body
senses.definitionCN: 拥有全部权力，不受法律、议会或任何其他机构限制
senses.example: The old king claimed absolute power over every province.
senses.exampleCN: 老王宣称对每一个行省拥有绝对权力。
senses.why: A ruler freed from every tie of law is the political picture of a knot untied: no restraint, no limit.
senses.whyCN: 不受法律约束的统治者，正是绳结解开的政治图景：没有束缚，没有限制。

senses.title: Pure and not mixed
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean pure and not mixed with anything else, as in absolute alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，表示纯粹、不掺入其他成分，如绝对酒精
senses.example: The laboratory stored absolute alcohol in a locked cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把纯酒精存放在上锁的柜子里。
senses.why: Freeing a substance from every mixture leaves only itself, so 'absolute' comes to mean unmixed.
senses.whyCN: 把一种物质从所有混合物中解放出来，只剩它本身，于是 absolute 引申为不掺杂。

senses.title: Grammar: standing alone
senses.definition: in grammar, describing a phrase or clause that is not grammatically tied to the main clause
senses.definitionCN: 语法术语，指与主句在语法上不相连接的短语或分句
senses.example: The teacher marked the absolute construction in the margin.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在页边标出了那个独立结构。
senses.why: The grammatical phrase is literally 'loosened' from the sentence, which is the old meaning of the Latin source.
senses.whyCN: 语法上的独立结构字面上就是从句子中「被松开」，这正是拉丁原词的老意思。

senses.title: A general principle or truth
senses.definition: a principle or truth believed to be valid always and everywhere, often used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 被认为处处时时都成立的原理或真理，常用复数
senses.example: He argued that moral absolutes do not change with fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 他认为道德的绝对真理不会随潮流改变。
senses.why: The noun turns the adjective into a thing: whatever is true without conditions becomes an absolute.
senses.whyCN: 名词把形容词变成实体：凡无条件成立的东西都成了 absolute。

senses.title: Absolute temperature scale
senses.definition: in science, a temperature scale starting at the lowest possible temperature, measured in kelvins
senses.definitionCN: 科学术语，指从可能最低温度起算的温标，以开尔文计量
senses.example: The readings were converted to the absolute scale for comparison.
senses.exampleCN: 为便于比较，读数被换算成了绝对温标。
senses.why: A scale that depends on nothing external, not even on the properties of one material, is absolute in the strictest sense.
senses.whyCN: 不依赖任何外部条件、甚至不依赖某种物质特性的标尺，才是严格意义的绝对。

intro.en: Absolute goes back to a Latin verb meaning to loosen or set free, and that image of an untied knot still runs through all its senses.
intro.cn: absolute 可追到拉丁语中表示「松开、释放」的动词，解开的绳结这一意象贯穿它的全部义项。

items.en: The verb solvere meant 'to loosen, untie, dissolve, pay a debt'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 solvere 意为「松开、解开、溶解、偿债」；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: The prefix ab- plus solvere formed absolutus, the past participle meaning 'loosened away, freed, finished, complete'.
items.cn: 前缀 ab- 加 solvere 构成 absolutus，这一过去分词意为「被松开、被释放、已完成、完整」。

items.en: Later Latin used absolutus for a ruler free of legal restraint and for a thing perfect and complete in itself.
items.cn: 后世拉丁语用 absolutus 指不受法律约束的统治者，也指自身完美完整之物。

items.en: Old French absolu carried the word to English with the senses 'complete' and 'unlimited' already joined.
items.cn: 古法语 absolu 把这个词带入英语，「完整」与「无限」两个义项当时已经并存。
