items.en: English recorded the word in the late fourteenth century. The exact first date is uncertain and early spellings differ.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪后期记录了这个词；确切首见年代不确定，早期拼写并不统一。

items.en: Science and grammar each took a branch: absolute zero and the absolute construction both keep the idea of being tied to nothing.
items.cn: 科学与语法各取一支：绝对零度与独立结构都保留了「不系于任何事物」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the solvere family and two words that merely share the ab- opening; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of completeness and of lack of limit.
note.cn: 形近组收 solvere 词族的词与两个只是同样以 ab- 开头的词；近义组收表示完整彻底与不受限制的形容词。

entries.definition: To free someone from blame, guilt or a duty; it keeps the literal Latin sense of loosening away.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赦免、免除」，保留拉丁语「松开、解除」的字面义，与 absolute 同根。

entries.definition: The formal act of declaring someone free from guilt or punishment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「赦免、宽恕」，指正式宣告某人无罪或免罚，与 absolute 同根。

entries.definition: To break a solid into a liquid, or to end an organization; solvere is the shared loosening verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「溶解、解散」，共用 solvere 这一「松开」动词，词根同源。

entries.definition: An answer to a problem or a liquid mixture; both senses come from the idea of loosening a difficulty or a solid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「解决办法、溶液」，两个义项都来自「松开难题或固体」的想法，与 absolute 同根。

entries.definition: Ridiculous and unreasonable; it shares the ab- opening but comes from Latin surdus, deaf.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬的、不合理的」，只是同样以 ab- 开头，词根为拉丁语 surdus「聋的」，词源不同。

entries.definition: Whole, with all parts present; it stresses that nothing is missing rather than that nothing limits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「完整的、全部的」，强调不缺任何部分，而不是不受任何限制。

entries.definition: Including everything, often used in the phrase total silence; very close to absolute in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全部的、完全的」，常用于 total silence 一类说法，在程度义上与 absolute 很接近。

entries.definition: Having no limit set by rules or amounts; it describes the absence of a cap, not a fixed truth.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无限的、无限制的」，只说明没有上限，不涉及固定不变的真理。

entries.definition: Clear and sure, with no doubt left; it overlaps with the 'certain' sense of absolute.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明确的、确定的」，与 absolute 的「确凿」义重叠。

entries.definition: Measured in comparison with something else; the direct opposite of the independent sense of absolute.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「相对的、比较而言的」，正与 absolute 的「不受他物左右」义相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin participle absolutus and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁分词 absolutus，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Absolutus is a past participle: it describes something already loosened and set free.
normal.cn: absolutus 是过去分词：它描述已经松开、已被释放的东西。

normal.en: Ab- plus solvere is the same loosening verb that gives dissolve and solution.
normal.cn: ab- 加 solvere 与 dissolve、solution 共用同一个「松开」动词。

normal.en: Absolute zero is the temperature at which nothing moves, so it depends on no other reading.
normal.cn: absolute zero 是万物静止的温度，因此不依赖任何别的读数。

normal.en: An absolute majority means more than half of all possible votes, not just more than the runner-up.
normal.cn: absolute majority 指超过全部可能票数的一半，而不只是多于第二名。

normal.en: In absolute terms compares raw numbers, with no allowance for scale or context.
normal.cn: in absolute terms 指比较原始数字，不考虑规模或背景。

abstract.en: Picture a knot that comes apart completely: whatever it held can now move in any direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一个彻底散开的绳结：原本被它拴住的东西现在可以任意移动。

abstract.en: The same untied knot becomes a king above the law, a truth beyond doubt, or a beam of light with no shadow.
abstract.cn: 同一个解开的绳结可以变成凌驾法律的君王、无可置疑的真理，或没有阴影的一束光。

abstract.en: Absolute never means better, only untied: the word measures freedom from conditions, not quality.
abstract.cn: absolute 从不表示更好，只表示不再被拴住：它衡量的是脱离条件的程度，与好坏无关。

examples.en: She had absolute confidence in the team she had trained.
examples.cn: 她对自己训练出的团队有完全的信心。

examples.en: The room fell into absolute darkness when the last lamp was switched off.
examples.cn: 最后一盏灯熄灭后，房间陷入彻底的黑暗。

examples.en: No government should hold absolute power over the courts.
examples.cn: 任何政府都不应对法院拥有绝对权力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱不湿溜特」——绳子解开不留一点牵挂：彻底的、绝对的

root: 拉丁语 absolutus 是 absolvere「松开、释放」的过去分词，由 ab-「离开」+ solvere「松开、解开」构成；solvere 更早来源不确定。absolutus 原义「被解开的、已完成的」，后引申为「完整、不受限制」，并分出「确凿」「专制」「纯」等义。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one idea: something is freed from every tie, whether the tie is a limit, a comparison, a doubt, a law, a mixture or a grammatical clause.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都守着同一个想法：某物从一切束缚中解脱，无论束缚是限制、比较、疑问、法律、掺杂物还是语法上的从句。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tightly tied knot comes loose, and nothing holds the rope any longer.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个系得很紧的绳结彻底散开，再也没有东西牵住这根绳子。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: freed from every exception, the quality becomes total.
branches.cn: 程度线：摆脱一切例外，性质就变成彻底。

branches.en: THE SCALE: what is tied to nothing else can be measured on its own, from zero upward.
branches.cn: 标尺线：不拴在任何他物上的东西可以自行计量，从零点起算。

branches.en: THE TRUTH: a fact released from doubt needs no argument to support it.
branches.cn: 真理线：脱离疑问的事实不需要任何论证来支撑。

branches.en: THE THRONE: a ruler released from law holds power without limit.
branches.cn: 王座线：摆脱法律的统治者握有不受限制的权力。

branches.en: THE REMAINDER: unmixed substance, a clause cut loose from its sentence, and a truth that holds everywhere.
branches.cn: 余下三支：不掺杂的物质、从句子中松开的从句，以及处处成立的真理。

intro.en: Absolute is built from a Latin prefix plus a Latin loosening verb, and English adds ordinary suffixes to make its family.
intro.cn: absolute 由拉丁语前缀加「松开」动词构成，英语再用普通后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin solvere, absolvere and absolutus are all recorded, so only the deeper root of solvere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 solvere、absolvere 与 absolutus 均有文献记录，只有 solvere 更早的词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks separation from something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记从某物分离。

items.example: The verb images a rope being untied.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词呈现绳子被解开的画面。

items.example: The court could absolvere the accused.
items.exampleCN: 法庭可以宣告被告无罪。

items.meaningCN: 被解开的；被释放的；完整的
items.example: The participle became the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词成了英语的形容词。

items.example: It forms absolutely.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absolutely。

items.example: It forms absoluteness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absoluteness。

items.example: It forms absolutism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absolutism。

items.example: It forms absolutist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absolutist。

items.example: It forms absolution from absolvere.
items.exampleCN: 它与 absolvere 一起构成 absolution。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「绝对地；完全地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「绝对性；完全性」
由本词加 -ism 构成，义为「专制主义；绝对主义」

definition_zh: 吸收；吸引；理解掌握；承受；并入；吸入
definition_en: to take in a liquid, gas, energy or information, or to hold someone's attention completely
core_image: 干海绵贴着水面，把周围的液体一点点吞进去
scene: 厨房地板上打翻了一杯牛奶，纸抹布很快湿透了。The thick towel absorbed every drop before the milk reached the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 absorb 是「吸收液体」（第 1 个义项：液体被材料吸入内部）；句意为厚毛巾在牛奶流到地板前把每一滴都吸住了。

pos.zh: 吸收；吸引；理解；承受；并入

derivatives.zh: 由动词 absorb 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成，义为「能吸收的；吸水的」
由动词加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「吸收；专注；并入」
由动词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「引人入胜的；极有趣的」
由动词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「专心的；被吸收的」
由形容词 absorbent 加 -cy 构成，义为「吸收性；吸水性」

senses.title: To soak up a liquid or gas
senses.definition: to take a liquid, gas or other substance into itself through its surface, as a cloth or a sponge does
senses.definitionCN: 通过表面把液体、气体或其他物质吸入自身，如布或海绵那样
senses.example: Dry sand absorbs water quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 干沙很快吸水。
senses.why: The Latin verb absorbere meant to suck in; the core picture is something drawing liquid into itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absorbere 意为「吸进」，核心画面是某物把液体吸到自身内部。

senses.title: To take in and hold energy
senses.definition: to take in heat, light, sound or another form of energy, so that it does not pass through or bounce back
senses.definitionCN: 吸收热、光、声或其他形式的能量，使其不再穿透或反射
senses.example: Dark surfaces absorb more heat than pale ones.
senses.exampleCN: 深色表面比浅色表面吸收更多热量。
senses.why: Energy behaves like a fluid in this image: it flows in and stays inside instead of leaving.
senses.whyCN: 在这个意象里能量像流体：流进去并留在内部，而不是离开。

senses.title: To occupy the mind entirely
senses.definition: to hold someone's attention so completely that nothing else seems to matter
senses.definitionCN: 完全占据某人的注意力，使其他事情都显得不重要
senses.example: She was completely absorbed in the novel and forgot the time.
senses.exampleCN: 她完全沉浸在这本小说里，忘了时间。
senses.why: Attention is pulled inward the way water is pulled into cloth; the mind is filled and cannot take in anything else.
senses.whyCN: 注意力像水被布吸进去一样被拉向内部，头脑被占满，再也装不进别的东西。

senses.title: To understand and remember
senses.definition: to take in information or ideas and make them part of one's own knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 接收信息或观念，并使之成为自身知识的一部分
senses.example: Young children absorb new words faster than adults.
senses.exampleCN: 幼儿吸收新词比成年人更快。
senses.why: Information is the fluid here: it is taken in and kept, and what is kept becomes knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 此处信息就是流体：被吸入并保存，保存下来的就成了知识。

senses.title: To take costs or effects without harm
senses.definition: to accept the cost, loss or force of something, so that its effect is softened or hidden
senses.definitionCN: 接受某事的成本、损失或冲击，使其影响被缓解或隐藏
senses.example: The firm chose to absorb the extra shipping costs.
senses.exampleCN: 公司选择自行承担额外的运输成本。
senses.why: What is absorbed disappears into the container, so a cost taken in does not strike outside the firm.
senses.whyCN: 被吸收之物消融在容器里，因此被吞入的成本不会打到企业外部。

senses.title: To incorporate and make part of a whole
senses.definition: to take in a group, area or idea so that it becomes part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 接纳一个群体、地区或观念，使其成为更大整体的一部分
senses.example: The company absorbed three small suppliers into its network.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把三家小供应商并入了自己的网络。
senses.why: Absorption is the picture of something swallowed by a larger body, losing its separate outline.
senses.whyCN: 吸收是一个更大的整体吞下某物、使其失去独立轮廓的画面。

senses.title: To cushion an impact
senses.definition: to reduce the force of a blow, a shock or a sudden change by taking part of it in
senses.definitionCN: 通过承受其中一部分来减弱打击、震动或突然变化的力量
senses.example: The foam layer absorbs the shock when the box is dropped.
senses.exampleCN: 箱子落地时泡沫层会缓冲冲击。
senses.why: The cushion's material swallows part of the energy, so less of it reaches what lies behind.
senses.whyCN: 缓冲材料吞掉一部分能量，于是传到后方的冲击就少了。

senses.title: To take in a smaller amount
senses.definition: to take in a substance through the body, such as water, nutrients or a drug
senses.definitionCN: 通过身体摄取水、养分或药物等物质
senses.example: Roots absorb minerals from the surrounding soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根从周围的土壤里吸收矿物质。
senses.why: Biological uptake is the first and most literal branch: the body is the container, the nutrient is the fluid.
senses.whyCN: 生物体的摄取是这条线索最初的、最字面的一支：身体是容器，养分是流体。

intro.en: Absorb is a Latin verb built from 'away' plus 'suck in', and English borrowed it whole.
intro.cn: absorb 是拉丁语动词，由「离开」与「吸」两部分构成，英语整体借入。

items.en: The verb sorbere meant 'to suck in, swallow, sip'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 sorbere 意为「吸进、吞咽、啜饮」；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Ab- plus sorbere formed absorbere, 'to swallow up, suck in, engulf', and later 'to engross the mind'.
items.cn: ab- 加 sorbere 构成 absorbere，意为「吞没、吸进、吞噬」，后来又指「占据心思」。

items.en: The past participle absorptus 'swallowed up' supplied the model for the English past in -ed and the noun in -tion.
items.cn: 过去分词 absorptus「被吞没」为英语的 -ed 过去式和 -tion 名词提供了范式。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English in the fifteenth century, first in physical senses and soon also of the mind.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五世纪见于英语，最初用于物理义，很快也用于心思义。

items.en: Later use extended it to costs, shocks, groups and data, all sharing the same picture of something swallowed in.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它扩展到成本、冲击、群体与数据，全都共享「被吞入」的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the sorbere family and two words that merely share the ab- opening; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of taking things in.
note.cn: 形近组收 sorbere 词族的词与两个只是同样以 ab- 开头的词；近义组收表示「吸收、接纳」的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of taking something in, whether liquid, energy, knowledge or a group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸收、专注、并入」，由本词变来的名词形式，词根相同。

entries.definition: An adjective for a material that can soak up liquid easily.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能吸收的、吸水的」，由本词加 -ent 构成。

entries.definition: A chemistry term for particles clinging to a surface rather than entering the body of a material.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸附」，指微粒附着在表面而不进入内部；只是拼写与 absorb 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Complete and unlimited; it shares the ab- opening but comes from solvere, to loosen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「绝对的、完全的」，只是同样以 ab- 开头，词根为 solvere「松开」，词源不同。

entries.definition: To use something wrongly or treat someone badly; it comes from Latin abuti, to use up.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「滥用、虐待」，词根为拉丁语 abuti「用尽」，与 absorb 词源不同。

entries.definition: To become or make thoroughly wet over time; slower and more everyday than absorb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浸泡、浸湿」，强调随时间渐渐变湿，比 absorb 更日常、速度更慢。

entries.definition: To let something enter the body or the mind; the plain, general version of absorb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「吸入、接纳、理解」，是 absorb 最平实的一般说法。

entries.definition: To take in information or people and make them fully part of a larger system.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同化、吸收」，强调使被接纳者完全成为更大体系的一部分。

entries.definition: To hold all of someone's attention; formal and close to the absorbed-in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使全神贯注」，语气正式，与 be absorbed in 的义项接近。

entries.definition: To send out light, heat, sound or gas; the reverse of taking energy in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发出、释放」，指送出光、热、声或气体，与吸收能量方向相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root sorbere and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词根 sorbere，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Sorbere is to suck in, so a sponge and a thirsty mind use exactly the same verb picture.
normal.cn: sorbere 是「吸进」，因此海绵和求知的心用的是同一幅动词画面。

normal.en: Absorption is the noun twin of the verb; the -tion ending marks the process.
normal.cn: absorption 是这个动词的名词孪生形式，-tion 结尾标记过程。

normal.en: Be absorbed in a book means the book has taken the mind in completely.
normal.cn: be absorbed in a book 意为书把心思整个吸了进去。

normal.en: A company absorbs a smaller firm the way a body absorbs food: the outline disappears.
normal.cn: 公司并入小企业就像身体吸收食物：对方的轮廓消失了。

normal.en: Absorb the cost means the firm swallows the loss itself instead of passing it on.
normal.cn: absorb the cost 指企业自己吞下损失，而不转嫁给别人。

abstract.en: Picture a pale square of paper touching a drop of ink: the drop climbs in and the paper darkens.
abstract.cn: 想象一张浅色纸碰上一滴墨：墨滴向上爬进纸里，纸变暗了。

abstract.en: The same paper can stand for a mind, a firm or a soil: whatever it takes in becomes part of it.
abstract.cn: 同一张纸可以代表头脑、企业或土壤：凡是吸进去的都会变成它的一部分。

abstract.en: Absorption leaves no trace of the boundary: what was outside is now inside, and the edge is gone.
abstract.cn: 吸收不留边界的痕迹：原本在外的东西如今在内，那条边也不见了。

examples.en: These paper towels absorb twice as much water as the old ones.
examples.cn: 这些纸巾的吸水量是旧款的两倍。

examples.en: Black cloth absorbs sunlight and warms up quickly.
examples.cn: 黑布吸收阳光，升温很快。

examples.en: He was so absorbed in the puzzle that he missed his stop.
examples.cn: 他太专注于那道谜题，坐过了站。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿不揍吧」——肚子饿得把桌上的汤一口气吸干：吸收

root: 拉丁语 absorbere「吞没、吸进」由 ab-「离开」+ sorbere「吸、啜」构成；过去分词 absorptus 给出英语的 absorbed 与 absorption。sorbere 更早来源不确定。核心义是「把外部的液体、能量或信息吸进内部」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe something being drawn inside a container: liquid, energy, attention, knowledge, cost, a group, a shock, or a nutrient.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述某物被吸入容器之内：液体、能量、注意力、知识、成本、群体、冲击或养分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge meets a pool of water and draws it inward until the sponge is heavy.
core.cn: 核心意象：干海绵遇到一摊水，把水吸进内部，直到海绵变重。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: liquid, energy and nutrients pass through a surface and stay inside.
branches.cn: 物质线：液体、能量与养分穿过表面，留在内部。

branches.en: THE MIND: attention is drawn inward until nothing outside can enter.
branches.cn: 心智线：注意力被拉向内部，直到外部再也进不来。

branches.en: THE KNOWLEDGE: information taken in and kept becomes part of what a person knows.
branches.cn: 知识线：被吸入并保存的信息成为一个人所知的一部分。

branches.en: THE HARSH SIDE: cost and shock are swallowed so that their force is not passed on.
branches.cn: 硬受线：成本与冲击被吞下，力量因此不再外传。

branches.en: THE GROUP: a smaller body is taken in and loses its separate outline.
branches.cn: 群体线：较小的实体被吸进去，失去独立轮廓。

intro.en: Absorb combines a Latin prefix with a Latin sucking verb; English adds -ent, -ing, -ed and -tion to build the family.
intro.cn: absorb 由一个拉丁前缀与表示「吸」的拉丁动词构成，英语再以 -ent、-ing、-ed 与 -tion 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sorbere, absorbere and absorptus are recorded; only the older root behind sorbere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sorbere、absorbere 与 absorptus 均有记录，只有 sorbere 更早的词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of drawing away from the outside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「从外部拉走」的意思。

items.example: The verb is the sucking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「吸」词根。

items.example: The compound verb already had both the physical and mental senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词当时已有物理义与心智义。

items.example: The participle lies behind absorbed.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词是 absorbed 的来源。

items.example: It forms absorbent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absorbent。

items.example: It forms absorption.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absorption。

items.example: It forms absorbing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absorbing。

items.example: It forms absorbed.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absorbed。

items.example: It forms absorbency.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absorbency。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ent 构成，义为「能吸收的；吸水的」
由本词加 -tion 构成，义为「吸收；专注；并入」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「引人入胜的」

definition_zh: 戒除；节制；禁欲；（宗教）斋戒；（政治）弃权
definition_en: the practice of deliberately not doing or consuming something, especially something pleasurable or harmful
core_image: 一只手伸到酒杯前，又稳稳地收回来
scene: 餐桌上摆着一瓶刚开的红酒，主人却把杯子推开了。After years of trouble, he chose complete abstinence from alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 abstinence 是「戒酒」（第 2 个义项：不再饮酒的自我约束）；句意为在多年麻烦之后，他选择了彻底戒酒。

pos.zh: 名词：戒除；节制；禁欲；斋戒；弃权

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ent 构成，义为「有节制的；戒除的」
同出拉丁语 abstinere 的动词，义为「戒除；弃权」
由本词加 -ious 构成的罕见形容词，义为「惯于节制的」

senses.title: Deliberately not doing something pleasurable
senses.definition: the practice of choosing not to do or take something that one enjoys, usually for a moral or personal reason
senses.definitionCN: 出于道德或个人理由，主动选择不做或不取用自己喜欢的事物
senses.example: His doctor recommended a short abstinence from rich food.
senses.exampleCN: 医生建议他短期戒食油腻食物。
senses.why: Latin abstinere is 'to hold away from'; the picture is a hand held back just before it grasps.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abstinere 意为「握住、使之远离」，画面是一只手在抓住之前被稳稳地收住。

senses.title: Giving up alcohol
senses.definition: the decision to drink no alcohol at all, often as a promise to oneself or to a group
senses.definitionCN: 完全不饮酒的决定，常是对自己或对某个团体作出的承诺
senses.example: He signed a pledge of total abstinence at the clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 他在诊所签下了完全戒酒的承诺。
senses.why: The held-back hand is most often pictured at a glass, so this is the word's best-known branch.
senses.whyCN: 收住的手最常出现在酒杯前，因此这是这个词最广为人知的一支。

senses.title: Sexual continence
senses.definition: the practice of not having sex, usually for religious, moral or personal reasons
senses.definitionCN: 出于宗教、道德或个人原因而不发生性行为
senses.example: The order required abstinence from all members.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会要求全体成员禁欲。
senses.why: The same holding back applies to desire itself: the body is kept from what it wants.
senses.whyCN: 同一种收住被用到欲望本身：身体被拦住，不去得到它想要的东西。

senses.title: A period of staying off an addiction
senses.definition: a period, often in treatment, during which a person stays completely away from a drug or habit
senses.definitionCN: 治疗过程中完全远离某种药物或习惯的一段时间
senses.example: The programme begins with a month of abstinence.
senses.exampleCN: 该疗程从一个月戒断期开始。
senses.why: A period of holding away becomes a measurable stage on the road to recovery.
senses.whyCN: 一段「持续收住」的时间，就成了康复道路上可衡量的阶段。

senses.title: Refusing to vote
senses.definition: the act of choosing not to vote on a question, either by leaving the ballot blank or by formally abstaining
senses.definitionCN: 选择不对某个问题投票，或留白，或正式声明弃权
senses.example: Three members chose abstinence rather than a no vote.
senses.exampleCN: 三名成员选择弃权而不是投反对票。
senses.why: In voting, the hand is held back from the ballot box: not a no, just no mark at all.
senses.whyCN: 在投票中，手被拦在票箱之外：不是反对，只是完全不留痕迹。

senses.title: Religious fasting and self-denial
senses.definition: in religious use, the practice of going without food, meat or other comforts on set days
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语境中在指定日子不吃食物、肉类或其他享受的做法
senses.example: Friday abstinence from meat is traditional in many churches.
senses.exampleCN: 许多教会都有周五戒食肉类的传统。
senses.why: Food is the most ancient thing a hand can be held back from, so fasting is the oldest branch of the word.
senses.whyCN: 食物是手最古老可以收住的对象，因此斋戒是这个词语义最古老的一支。

senses.title: Medical restriction of food or drink
senses.definition: a medical instruction that a patient must not eat or drink anything for a set time, especially before surgery
senses.definitionCN: 医嘱要求病人在一段时间内不得进食饮水，尤指手术之前
senses.example: The nurse checked that the patient had kept the required abstinence.
senses.exampleCN: 护士核对了病人是否遵守规定的禁食。
senses.why: Here the hand is held back not by desire but by rule, and the reason is safety.
senses.whyCN: 这里收住手不是出于欲望，而是出于规定，理由是安全。

senses.title: A general policy of restraint
senses.definition: a stated rule or habit of limiting indulgence in general, not limited to one substance or act
senses.definitionCN: 一种公开的规则或习惯，泛指对各种放纵加以限制，不限某一种物质或行为
senses.example: The community valued abstinence in dress, speech and diet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体在衣着、言谈和饮食上都推崇节制。
senses.why: The picture widens: what is held back is not one cup but every form of indulgence at once.
senses.whyCN: 画面变宽了：被拦住的不是一只酒杯，而是同时对所有形式的放纵。

intro.en: Abstinence comes from a Latin verb meaning to hold oneself away, and every sense is that gesture at a different scale.
intro.cn: abstinence 来自拉丁语中表示「使自己保持远离」的动词，每个义项都是这一姿态的不同尺度。

items.en: The verb tenere meant 'to hold, keep, grasp'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 tenere 意为「握住、保持、抓牢」；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Abs- plus tenere formed abstinere, 'to hold back from, refrain from', literally to keep oneself away.
items.cn: abs- 加 tenere 构成 abstinere，意为「收住、远离、戒除」，字面就是使自己保持在外。

items.en: The abstract noun abstinentia named the habit or virtue of holding back, especially from food and drink.
items.cn: 抽象名词 abstinentia 指「收住」的习惯或美德，尤指在饮食方面的节制。

items.en: Old French carried the noun into English with the religious sense already well established.
items.cn: 古法语把这一名词带入英语，宗教义当时已相当稳固。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English in the thirteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这一名词在十三世纪见于英语；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Medical and parliamentary uses were added later, but all of them still describe a hand held back.
items.cn: 医学义与议会义是后来加上的，但它们都仍在描述一只被收住的手。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the tenere family; the near-meaning group gathers words for restraint, self-denial and the act of staying away.
note.cn: 形近组收 tenere 词族的词；近义组收表示节制、苦修与远离的词语。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to hold back from something or to refuse to vote; the direct source of abstinence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「戒除、弃权」，是 abstinence 的直接来源，同出拉丁语 abstinere。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person who habitually holds back from indulgence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有节制的、戒除的」，由本词加 -ent 构成。

entries.definition: To hold something inside limits; it shares the Latin holding verb tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、控制」，共用拉丁语「握持」动词 tenere，词根同源。

entries.definition: To keep something and not let it go; another English word built on tenere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「保留、留住」，同样建立在 tenere 之上，词根同源。

entries.definition: Ridiculous; it shares the abs- opening but comes from surdus, deaf.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬的」，只是同样以 abs- 开头，词根为 surdus「聋的」，词源不同。

entries.definition: Keeping amounts within reasonable limits; it allows some, while abstinence allows none.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适度、节制」，允许少量，而 abstinence 是完全不许。

entries.definition: Deliberately giving up things one wants, often as a discipline or a religious exercise.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自我克制、苦修」，有意放弃想要的东西，多作修炼或宗教功课。

entries.definition: Going without food for a period, usually for religious or health reasons.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「禁食」，在一段时间内不吃东西，多出于宗教或健康原因。

entries.definition: The virtue of restraining one's desires, especially in drinking; older and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「节制、禁酒」，尤指饮酒有度，语气较古雅正式。

entries.definition: The act of allowing oneself something one enjoys; the direct opposite of holding back.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「放纵、沉溺」，指允许自己享受所好之物，正与收住相反。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real tenere root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 tenere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Tenere is to hold: abstinence is holding yourself away from a thing, not losing it.
normal.cn: tenere 是「握住」：abstinence 是把自己握在远离某物的一侧，而不是失去它。

normal.en: The same root appears in contain and retain, both of which are about keeping hold.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 contain 与 retain，两者都与握持有关。

normal.en: Abstinence from alcohol is the pledge made at the start of many recovery programmes.
normal.cn: abstinence from alcohol 是许多康复疗程开始时作出的承诺。

normal.en: In a vote, abstention is the same held-back hand, just without leaving a mark.
normal.cn: 在投票中，弃权是同一只收住的手，只是不留任何痕迹。

normal.en: Religious abstinence from meat is tied to fixed days in the church calendar.
normal.cn: 宗教上的戒食肉类与教会历法中的固定日子相绑定。

abstract.en: Picture a glass lifted halfway and then set down again while it is still full.
abstract.cn: 想象一只酒杯被举到一半，又原样放回桌面，杯里仍是满的。

abstract.en: The same gesture works for sweets, for speech, for a ballot and for desire itself.
abstract.cn: 同一个动作也适用于甜食、言语、选票以及欲望本身。

abstract.en: Abstinence is not absence: the thing is still there, and the choice is renewed each time.
abstract.cn: abstinence 不是「没有」：东西仍在眼前，只是每次都要重新作出选择。

examples.en: The clinic asks patients to keep strict abstinence during treatment.
examples.cn: 诊所要求病人在治疗期间严格戒断。

examples.en: His abstinence from sweets lasted exactly one week.
examples.cn: 他戒甜食只坚持了整整一周。

examples.en: Two councillors declared their abstinence on the final motion.
examples.cn: 两名议员在最终动议上宣布弃权。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布斯提能斯」——手伸到杯前又停住，能忍住不喝：节制、戒除

root: 拉丁语 abstinentia 由 abstinere「收住、远离、戒除」加抽象名词后缀构成，abstinere 则是 abs-「离开」+ tenere「握持」；tenere 更早来源不确定。核心是「把自己握在远离某物的一侧」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe the same pause: the hand is held back from food, alcohol, sex, a drug, a ballot, meat, a meal before surgery, or indulgence in general.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一个停顿：手被收住，不去碰食物、酒、性、毒品、选票、肉类、术前饮食，或一切放纵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches toward a filled glass and is pulled back before it touches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向斟满的杯子，在触到之前又收了回来。

branches.en: THE GENERAL RULE: any pleasure, and any indulgence at all, can be the thing the hand stays away from.
branches.cn: 通则线：任何享受、任何放纵，都可以成为手所远离的对象。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: alcohol and drugs are met with a held-back hand over a whole period of time.
branches.cn: 物质线：面对酒与毒品，收住的手要持续整段时间。

branches.en: THE BODY: desire itself is what the hand refuses, and the body is kept from acting.
branches.cn: 身体线：手拒绝的是欲望本身，身体因此不作出行动。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE RITE: fasting and medical bans both turn the gesture into a prescribed practice.
branches.cn: 规矩与礼俗线：斋戒与医嘱禁食都把这一姿态变成规定的做法。

branches.en: THE BALLOT: in voting, the hand stops short of the box and leaves no mark.
branches.cn: 选票线：在投票时手停在票箱之外，不留任何痕迹。

intro.en: Abstinence is a Latin prefix plus a Latin holding verb, lengthened into a noun; English adds two small suffixes.
intro.cn: abstinence 由拉丁语前缀加「握持」动词构成，并拉长为名词；英语又加了两个小后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin tenere, abstinere and abstinentia are all recorded, so only the older root of tenere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere、abstinere 与 abstinentia 均有记录，只有 tenere 更早的词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks distance from the object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记与对象的距离。

items.example: The verb is the holding root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「握持」词根。

items.example: The compound verb names the act of keeping away.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词指保持远离的动作。

items.example: The noun turned the act into a virtue.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把动作变成了美德。

items.example: It forms abstinence from abstinentia.
items.exampleCN: 它与 abstinentia 一起构成 abstinence。

items.example: It forms abstinent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstinent。

items.meaning: to refrain, to decline to vote
items.example: Members may abstain on the motion.
items.exampleCN: 成员可以对该动议弃权。

items.example: The same holding verb appears with a different prefix.
items.exampleCN: 同一个「握持」动词配上不同的前缀。

items.example: The company retained its best engineers.
items.exampleCN: 公司留住了最好的工程师。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ent 构成，义为「有节制的；戒除的」
由同一拉丁词根构成，义为「戒除；弃权」

definition_zh: 抽象的；抽象派的；摘要；抽象概念；提取；抽取；转移
definition_en: existing as an idea rather than a physical thing, or a short summary of a longer text, or to remove something
core_image: 从一堆具体杂物里，把共同的骨架单独抽出来
scene: 画家把桌上的苹果、布和陶罐都收进柜子，纸上只剩几道几何色块。The gallery devoted a whole room to abstract painting.
sceneCN: 这里 abstract 是「抽象派的」（第 2 个义项：艺术上的抽象表现）；句意为画廊把整整一个展厅留给抽象绘画。

pos.zh: 抽象的；理论上的；抽象派的
摘要；抽象概念；抽象艺术作品
提取；抽取；转移（注意力）

derivatives.zh: 由动词 abstract 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「抽象；抽象概念；抽取」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「抽象地；理论上地」
由动词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「心不在焉的；抽离的」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「抽象性」
由 abstraction 加 -ism 构成，义为「抽象主义；抽象派」

senses.title: Existing as an idea, not a thing
senses.definition: describing something that exists as an idea or quality rather than as a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 指以观念或性质而非实物形式存在的事物
senses.example: Freedom and justice are abstract ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 自由与正义都是抽象观念。
senses.why: Latin abstrahere is 'to draw away'; a concept is what the mind draws out of many concrete cases.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abstrahere 是「拉走」，概念正是心智从众多具体事例中拉出来的东西。

senses.title: In the style of abstract art
senses.definition: describing art that does not copy real objects but uses shapes, colours and forms to express feeling or structure
senses.definitionCN: 指不摹写实物，而用形状、色彩与形式表达情感或结构的艺术
senses.example: Her later work moved toward abstract painting.
senses.exampleCN: 她后期的作品转向抽象绘画。
senses.why: The painter draws the shape away from the object, leaving the skeleton of colour and form.
senses.whyCN: 画家把形状从实物中拉走，留下色彩与形式的骨架。

senses.title: Theoretical rather than practical
senses.definition: concerned with general theory or principle rather than with real cases and action
senses.definitionCN: 关注一般理论或原理，而不是具体事例与行动
senses.example: The argument stayed abstract and never touched the actual budget.
senses.exampleCN: 这场争论一直停留在理论层面，从未触及实际预算。
senses.why: Theory is the drawn-out outline; it is real, but it has lost the weight of a particular case.
senses.whyCN: 理论就是被抽出的轮廓：它确实存在，却失去了具体事例的分量。

senses.title: A short summary of a longer work
senses.definition: a short piece of writing that gives the main points of an article, paper or book
senses.definitionCN: 给出论文、文章或书籍要点的简短文字
senses.example: Please submit a two-hundred-word abstract with the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 请随论文提交一份两百词的摘要。
senses.why: The summary is the article drawn away from its body: only the outline remains on the page.
senses.whyCN: 摘要就是从正文里抽出的文章：留在纸上的只剩轮廓。

senses.title: To extract a substance
senses.definition: to take a substance out of a material, often by a chemical or industrial process
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学或工业过程把某种物质从材料中取出
senses.example: The plant abstracts sugar from the crushed cane.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂从压碎的甘蔗中提取糖。
senses.why: This is the word at its most physical: the substance is literally drawn away from the mass.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最物理的一端：物质被字面地从整体中拉出来。

senses.title: To take away or remove
senses.definition: to remove something, such as water, money or a document, from where it is normally found
senses.definitionCN: 把水、资金或文件等从通常所在之处移走
senses.example: Farmers abstract water from the river for irrigation.
senses.exampleCN: 农民从河里取水灌溉。
senses.why: Drawing away needs a source and a destination; the word never forgets the gap in between.
senses.whyCN: 拉走需要起点与终点，这个词从不忘记中间那道缺口。

senses.title: To withdraw the mind from something
senses.definition: to draw one's attention or mind away from the present situation, so that one seems absent
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力或心神从当下情境中抽走，显得心不在焉
senses.example: He abstracted himself from the noise and kept writing.
senses.exampleCN: 他从嘈杂中抽离出来，继续写作。
senses.why: The mind is pulled away from the room, and what stays in the chair is only a body.
senses.whyCN: 心神被从房间里拉走，留在椅子上的只剩一具身体。

senses.title: An abstract work of art
senses.definition: a painting, sculpture or other work that uses non-representational shapes and colours
senses.definitionCN: 使用非具象形状与色彩的绘画、雕塑或其他作品
senses.example: The collector paid a fortune for a single abstract.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏家为一幅抽象画付出了巨款。
senses.why: The noun is the adjective made into an object: a thing whose whole point is that it was drawn away from resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 名词是形容词变成的实体：这件作品的全部意义就在于它被拉离了形似。

intro.en: Abstract is a Latin participle meaning 'drawn away', and both its thinking sense and its chemical sense come from that single pull.
intro.cn: abstract 是意为「被拉走」的拉丁语分词，思维义与化学义都出自这同一次拉扯。

items.en: The verb trahere meant 'to draw, pull, drag'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 trahere 意为「拉、拖、牵引」；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: Abs- plus trahere formed abstrahere, 'to draw away, detach, withdraw'.
items.cn: abs- 加 trahere 构成 abstrahere，意为「拉开、分离、抽走」。

items.en: The past participle abstractus meant 'drawn away'; later Latin used it for ideas separated from particular things.
items.cn: 过去分词 abstractus 意为「被拉走的」；后世拉丁语用它指从具体事物中分离出来的观念。

items.en: The noun for a summary appears in the fifteenth century, the adjective in the sixteenth. Early dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 表示「摘要」的名词见于十五世纪，形容词见于十六世纪；早期年代不确定。

items.en: Chemistry kept the literal sense of extracting, while art and philosophy kept the sense of drawing away from appearance.
items.cn: 化学保留了「提取」的字面义，艺术与哲学则保留「拉离表象」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the trahere family; the near-meaning group gathers words for ideas, summaries and drawing something out.
note.cn: 形近组收 trahere 词族的词；近义组收表示观念、摘要与抽取的词语。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of forming an idea or for an idea so formed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抽象、抽象概念」，指形成观念的动作或由此形成的观念，与 abstract 同根。

entries.definition: To pull something toward oneself; trahere is the shared pulling verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸引」，共用 trahere 这一「拉」动词，词根同源，方向相反。

entries.definition: A binding agreement, or to draw together and become smaller; built on trahere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「合同、收缩」，建立在 trahere 之上，词根同源。

entries.definition: To pull something out of a material; the same pulling image with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提取、拔出」，同一「拉」意象配上不同前缀，词根同源。

entries.definition: Ridiculous; it shares the abs- opening but comes from surdus, deaf.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬的」，只是同样以 abs- 开头，词根为 surdus「聋的」，词源不同。

entries.definition: A short statement of the main points; plainer and less technical than abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「总结、概要」，比 abstract 更通俗，不带学术文体色彩。

entries.definition: Based on ideas and principles rather than practice; overlaps with the abstract sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论的」，以观念与原理为依据而非实践，与 abstract 的理论义重叠。

entries.definition: Related to ideas or concepts; it stresses the mental side rather than the removed side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「概念的」，强调观念层面，而不强调「被抽离」。

entries.definition: Real and physical, able to be seen and touched; the direct opposite of abstract.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「具体的、实有的」，能看见摸到，正与 abstract 相对。

entries.definition: Existing only in the mind; it is close in language but means unreal, which abstract does not.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「想象的、虚构的」，字面相近但指不真实，而 abstract 并不含此意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real trahere root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 trahere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Trahere is to draw or pull, so an abstract idea is one drawn out of many cases.
normal.cn: trahere 是「拉」，因此抽象观念就是从众多事例中拉出来的那一个。

normal.en: Attract, contract and extract are all the same pulling verb with different prefixes.
normal.cn: attract、contract 与 extract 都是同一个「拉」动词配上不同前缀。

normal.en: In the abstract means discussing something with the cases taken away.
normal.cn: in the abstract 指把具体事例抽走后再讨论某件事。

normal.en: An abstract of a paper is the paper pulled down to its outline.
normal.cn: 论文的 abstract 就是把文章拉剩成一条轮廓。

normal.en: Abstract art keeps the pull: the object is removed and the shape is left.
normal.cn: 抽象艺术保留这次拉扯：实物被拉走，只剩形状。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pulling a thread out of a woven cloth: the pattern stays, the thread is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从织布里抽出一根线：花纹还在，线却离开了。

abstract.en: A summary, a chemical extract and a painting can all be that same pulled thread.
abstract.cn: 摘要、化学提取物和一幅画，都可以是同一根被抽出的线。

abstract.en: Abstract is not empty: it is what remains when the particular details have been drawn away.
abstract.cn: abstract 并不空：它是具体细节被抽走之后剩下的那部分。

examples.en: The lecture was too abstract for students without any field experience.
examples.cn: 对没有实地经验的学生来说，那场讲座过于抽象。

examples.en: Each paper must include an abstract of no more than one page.
examples.cn: 每篇论文必须附一页以内的摘要。

examples.en: The mill abstracts oil from the seeds without using heat.
examples.cn: 这家工厂不用加热就从种子中提取油脂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布斯拽克特」——把杂乱的实物一拽而空，只剩骨架：抽象、摘要

root: 拉丁语 abstractus 是 abstrahere「拉开、抽走」的过去分词，由 abs-「离开」+ trahere「拉」构成；trahere 更早来源不确定。字面义「被拉走」，由此分出「抽出概念」「摘要」「提取物质」「心神抽离」等义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all perform one pull: an idea is drawn out of cases, a shape out of an object, a summary out of a text, a substance out of a mass, or a mind out of a room.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在做同一次拉扯：从事例抽出观念，从实物抽出形状，从文章抽出摘要，从整体抽出物质，或从房间抽走心神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thread is drawn out of a woven pattern, and the outline of the pattern remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根线从织好的花纹中被抽出，花纹的轮廓留在原处。

branches.en: THE IDEA: drawn out of particular cases, all that is left is a general quality.
branches.cn: 观念线：从具体事例中抽出后，剩下的只是一般性质。

branches.en: THE IMAGE: art pulls the shape away from the object and shows the pull itself.
branches.cn: 图像线：艺术把形状拉离实物，并把这次拉扯本身展示出来。

branches.en: THE TEXT: a summary is the article reduced to its outline.
branches.cn: 文本线：摘要就是把文章压缩成轮廓。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: extraction moves a real material from its source to somewhere else.
branches.cn: 物质线：提取把真实材料从来源处移到别处。

branches.en: THE MIND: attention is drawn out of the present scene, leaving the body behind.
branches.cn: 心智线：注意力被从当下的场景中抽走，只留下身体。

intro.en: Abstract joins a Latin prefix to a Latin pulling verb; English then adds -ion, -ly, -ed and -ness to widen the family.
intro.cn: abstract 把拉丁语前缀与「拉」动词结合，英语再以 -ion、-ly、-ed 与 -ness 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere, abstrahere and abstractus are recorded; only the older root behind trahere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere、abstrahere 与 abstractus 均有记录，只有 trahere 更早的词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks the direction of the pull.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记拉扯的方向。

items.example: The verb is the pulling root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「拉」词根。

items.example: The compound verb names the pulling away.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词指拉开、抽走的动作。

items.example: The participle became the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这一分词成了英语的形容词。

items.example: It forms abstraction.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstraction。

items.example: It forms abstractly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstractly。

items.example: It forms abstracted.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstracted。

items.example: It forms abstractness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstractness。

items.example: It forms abstractionism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstractionism。

items.example: The same pulling verb appears with ad-.
items.exampleCN: 同一个「拉」动词配上 ad- 前缀。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「抽象；抽象概念」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「抽象地；理论上地」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「心不在焉的；抽离的」

definition_zh: 荒谬的；荒唐可笑的；不合理的；荒诞派的；荒诞之事
definition_en: completely unreasonable or ridiculous, so that it seems contrary to common sense or logic
core_image: 有人对着空无一人的房间大声点名，还认真地等回答
scene: 会议开到一半，有人提议把所有文件先烧掉再讨论内容。The suggestion was so absurd that the whole room burst out laughing.
sceneCN: 这里 absurd 是「荒谬得可笑」（第 1 个义项：严重违背常理而显得荒唐）；句意为这个建议太荒唐，全场都笑出声来。

pos.zh: 形容词：荒谬的；荒唐可笑的；不合理的
名词：荒诞；荒诞之事

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 absurd 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「荒谬；荒唐事」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「荒谬地；荒唐地」
由形容词加 -ism 构成，义为「荒诞主义」，一种哲学与文学主张
由形容词加 -ist 构成，义为「荒诞派的」，也可作名词指荒诞派作家
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「荒谬性」，较少使用

senses.title: Wildly contrary to common sense
senses.definition: so unreasonable or illogical that it contradicts what any sensible person would expect
senses.definitionCN: 极不合理、极不合逻辑，违背任何有常识的人所预期
senses.example: It is absurd to expect a child to work twelve hours a day.
senses.exampleCN: 指望一个孩子每天干十二小时的活，实在荒谬。
senses.why: Latin absurdus was used of sounds that did not fit the ear; what does not fit reason sounds just as wrong.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absurdus 原用于形容听起来不对劲的声音；不合理性的东西，听起来同样不对。

senses.title: Ridiculous enough to be funny
senses.definition: so foolish or odd that it makes people laugh rather than angry
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢或古怪到了让人发笑而不是发怒的程度
senses.example: He wore an absurd hat with a tiny plastic bird on it.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一顶荒唐的帽子，上面立着一只塑料小鸟。
senses.why: The misfit that causes offence at one scale causes laughter at a smaller one.
senses.whyCN: 在同一尺度上令人反感的「不合」，缩小到日常尺度就变成了笑料。

senses.title: The theatre of the absurd
senses.definition: in modern drama, a style that shows human life as meaningless and uses illogical dialogue and plots
senses.definitionCN: 现代戏剧中的一种风格，表现人生无意义，并使用不合逻辑的对白与情节
senses.example: The course begins with the theatre of the absurd.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课从荒诞派戏剧讲起。
senses.why: If life has no rational plot, the stage must also refuse a rational plot; the form copies the claim.
senses.whyCN: 如果人生没有理性的情节，舞台也必须拒绝理性的情节：形式本身在模仿这一主张。

senses.title: Logically self-contradictory
senses.definition: in logic, describing a conclusion that contradicts itself, used in the method of reductio ad absurdum
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑上指结论自我矛盾，用于「归谬法」这种方法
senses.example: The proof works by deriving an absurd consequence from the assumption.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明通过从假设推出一个荒谬的结论来成立。
senses.why: Here absurd is a technical verdict: a chain of reasoning that ends in a misfit has condemned itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 absurd 是技术性判词：一条推理若在「不合」处收尾，就等于自我否决。

senses.title: Meaningless in philosophy
senses.definition: in existentialist thought, describing a world or a life without inherent purpose or reason
senses.definitionCN: 在存在主义思想中，指世界或人生没有内在目的或理由
senses.example: The novel treats the absurd as the human condition, not as a joke.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把荒诞当作人的处境，而非笑料。
senses.why: The older word for 'out of tune' becomes the name for a universe out of tune with human hopes.
senses.whyCN: 这个原本表示「走调」的词，成了人与世界彼此走调的宇宙之名。

senses.title: Unacceptably outrageous
senses.definition: used to protest that a situation is so unjust or unreasonable that it should not be allowed
senses.definitionCN: 用来抗议某种情况极不公正、极不合理，不应被容许
senses.example: It is absurd that a nurse must pay for her own gloves.
senses.exampleCN: 护士要自己买手套，这实在荒谬。
senses.why: The word turns the misfit into a complaint: the world is not merely odd, it is wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把「不合」变成抗议：世界不只是古怪，而是不对。

senses.title: Absurd in legal reasoning
senses.titleCN: 法律推理中的荒谬结论
senses.definition: in law, describing a result that is so unreasonable that courts refuse to accept it as the meaning of a statute
senses.definitionCN: 在法律中，指某一结果极不合理，法院因此拒绝把它作为法条的含义
senses.example: The court rejected an absurd reading of the tax rule.
senses.exampleCN: 法院驳回了对这条税则的荒谬解读。
senses.why: Judges inherit the logic of contradiction: an interpretation that ends in nonsense cannot be the intended one.
senses.whyCN: 法官继承了矛盾逻辑：会导致胡说的解释，不可能是立法本意。

senses.title: The absurd as a thing
senses.definition: used as a noun, often with the, for something absurd or for absurdity itself
senses.definitionCN: 作名词使用，常带定冠词，指某件荒诞的事或荒诞本身
senses.example: She collected the small absurdities of daily office life.
senses.exampleCN: 她收集了办公室里日常的小荒诞。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun, and the misfit becomes something that can be pointed at and named.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成名词，那种「不合」就成了可以指着命名的东西。

intro.en: Absurd is probably built from 'away' plus a word for 'deaf', a picture of something that cannot hear and therefore cannot agree; the details remain uncertain.
intro.cn: absurd 一般认为由「离开」加一个表示「聋」的词构成，画面是听不见因而无法与之协和的东西；具体细节仍存疑。

items.en: Surdus meant 'deaf, unhearing, silent' and also 'not sounding, dull'. Writers disagree on its deeper origin.
items.cn: surdus 意为「聋的、听不见的、无声的」，也指「不响的、沉闷的」；其更早来源各家说法不一。

items.en: Absurdus is generally explained as ab- plus surdus, 'out of tune, harsh-sounding, foolish'. The exact semantic path is uncertain.
items.cn: absurdus 一般认为由 ab- 加 surdus 构成，意为「走调的、难听的、愚妄的」；确切语义路径不确定。

items.en: The neuter absurdum was used in logic and rhetoric for a statement whose consequence is impossible.
items.cn: 中性形式 absurdum 用于逻辑与修辞，指后果不可能的陈述。

items.en: Middle French absurde passed the word to English with the sense 'contrary to reason' already fixed.
items.cn: 中古法语 absurde 把这个词传给英语，「违背理性」的义项当时已经固定。

items.en: English recorded the adjective in the sixteenth century. The precise first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪记录了这一形容词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The twentieth century made the word a name: the theatre and philosophy of the absurd.
items.cn: 二十世纪把它变成一个专名：荒诞派戏剧与荒诞哲学。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the surdus family and two words that merely share the ab- opening; the near-meaning group gathers words for what defies reason.
note.cn: 形近组收 surdus 词族的词与两个只是同样以 ab- 开头的词；近义组收表示违背理性的词语。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being absurd, or for an absurd act or situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒谬、荒唐事」，由本词加 -ity 构成，与 absurd 同根。

entries.definition: The philosophical and literary movement that treats existence as meaningless.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「荒诞主义」，指把存在视为无意义的哲学与文学主张，与 absurd 同根。

entries.definition: A mathematics term for an irrational number or root; it keeps the Latin base word for 'deaf'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，数学术语，指无理数或无理性的根式，保留拉丁语「聋」这一原词，词根同源。

entries.definition: Complete and unlimited; it shares the ab- opening but comes from solvere, to loosen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「绝对的」，只是同样以 ab- 开头，词根为 solvere「松开」，词源不同。

entries.definition: To take in liquid, energy or information; it comes from sorbere, to suck in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸收」，词根为 sorbere「吸」，与 absurd 词源不同。

entries.definition: Deserving to be laughed at; more openly mocking and less philosophical than absurd.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可笑的、荒谬的」，嘲笑意味更强，不如 absurd 那样带哲学分量。

entries.definition: Breaking the rules of reasoning; narrower and strictly about logic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不合逻辑的」，范围更窄，严格限于推理规则。

entries.definition: Completely contrary to reason or nature; formal and stronger than absurd in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬绝伦的」，语气正式，在语势上比 absurd 更强。

entries.definition: Without purpose or meaning, or showing no good sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无意义的、不明智的」，兼指没有目的与缺乏判断力。

entries.definition: Based on good reason and practical judgement; the direct opposite of absurd.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明智的、合理的」，正与 absurd 相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the probable surdus root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用一般认为的 surdus 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Surdus is deaf: absurd things are out of tune with reason, as if they could not hear it.
normal.cn: surdus 是「聋」：荒谬之物与理性走调，仿佛根本听不见理性。

normal.en: The same base gives surd, the mathematics word for an irrational root.
normal.cn: 同一词基给出 surd，即数学中的无理根式。

normal.en: Reductio ad absurdum drives an assumption until it produces nonsense.
normal.cn: 归谬法把一个假设一路推到它说出胡话为止。

normal.en: The theatre of the absurd throws away logical plots on purpose.
normal.cn: 荒诞派戏剧故意扔掉合乎逻辑的情节。

normal.en: It is absurd that marks a protest, not just a description.
normal.cn: it is absurd that 标记的是一种抗议，而不只是描述。

abstract.en: Picture a violin playing a tune that no instrument in the room can follow: the notes exist, the harmony does not.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小提琴拉出全屋子乐器都跟不上的调子：音符存在，和谐不存在。

abstract.en: The same broken chord can be a joke, a bad law, a play, or a whole universe without purpose.
abstract.cn: 同一段破碎的和弦可以是一个笑话、一条坏法律、一出戏，或一个没有目的的宇宙。

abstract.en: Absurd is not simply false: it is the sound of something refusing to fit where it is placed.
abstract.cn: absurd 不只是「假」：它是某物被放进一个位置后拒绝合缝时发出的声响。

examples.en: The plan was absurd from the start and cost the city millions.
examples.cn: 这个计划从一开始就荒唐，还让这座城市损失了数百万。

examples.en: She found the rules of the club faintly absurd.
examples.cn: 她觉得俱乐部的规定有点荒唐。

examples.en: Critics place his early plays somewhere between realism and the absurd.
examples.cn: 评论家把他早期的戏剧放在现实主义与荒诞之间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额不死的」——说自己不会死，还当众立誓：荒唐可笑

root: 拉丁语 absurdus 一般认为由 ab-「离开」+ surdus「聋的、不响的」构成，原指「走调的、难听的」，后引申为「违背理性的、愚妄的」。surdus 更早来源不确定，ab- 在此的确切作用也有争议，因此整体词源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all name a misfit: a claim out of tune with reason, a joke, a play without plot, a contradiction, a meaningless world, an outrage, a bad legal reading, or the misfit itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在命名一种「不合」：与理性走调的主张、笑料、没有情节的戏、自相矛盾、无意义的世界、令人愤怒的不公、糟糕的法律解读，或这种「不合」本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note is played that no other instrument in the room can follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个音被奏出，屋里没有任何别的乐器能跟上它。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: a statement or situation so far from reason that it provokes protest.
branches.cn: 主张线：一个说法或处境离理性太远，因而激起抗议。

branches.en: THE JOKE: at a smaller scale the same misfit makes people laugh.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：在更小的尺度上，同一种「不合」让人发笑。

branches.en: THE STAGE AND THE WORLD: drama and philosophy both drop the rational plot on purpose.
branches.cn: 舞台与世界线：戏剧与哲学都故意舍弃理性的情节。

branches.en: THE PROOF: logic and law use contradiction as a test, and a nonsense ending fails it.
branches.cn: 证明线：逻辑与法律用矛盾作检验，以胡说收尾者不能通过。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: once named, the misfit becomes a thing one can point to.
branches.cn: 实体线：一旦被命名，这种「不合」就成了可以指着看的对象。

intro.en: Absurd is probably a Latin prefix plus a Latin adjective for deafness; English adds -ity, -ly, -ism and -ist.
intro.cn: absurd 一般认为由拉丁语前缀加表示「聋」的形容词构成；英语再以 -ity、-ly、-ism 与 -ist 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin surdus and absurdus are recorded, but the semantic step from 'deaf' to 'foolish' is not fully explained in the sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 surdus 与 absurdus 均有记录，但「聋」到「愚妄」的语义过渡在文献中并未完全说清。

items.example: The prefix is generally read as marking a departure from fit.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀一般认为标记偏离「合缝」。

items.example: The adjective supplies the base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供这个词的词基。

items.example: The Latin adjective already carried both the musical and the foolish sense.
items.exampleCN: 这一拉丁形容词当时已兼有音乐与愚妄两义。

items.example: It forms absurdity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absurdity。

items.example: It forms absurdly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absurdly。

items.example: It forms absurdism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absurdism。

items.example: It forms absurdist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absurdist。

items.example: It forms absurdness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absurdness。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「荒谬；荒唐事」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「荒谬地；荒唐地」
由本词加 -ism 构成，义为「荒诞主义」

definition_zh: 丰富的；大量的；充裕的；富饶的；茂盛的
definition_en: existing in large quantities, or present in such plenty that there is more than enough
core_image: 泉水从地下不断涌出，漫过石沿向外流
scene: 雨后的山坡上，野花从溪边一直铺到林间空地。Wild strawberries are abundant in this valley every June.
sceneCN: 这里 abundant 是「大量存在、遍地都是」（第 2 个义项：在某处随处可见）；句意为每年六月这个山谷里野草莓遍地都是。

pos.zh: 形容词：丰富的；大量的；充裕的；富饶的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词词干加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「丰富；充裕；大量」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「丰富地；极其清楚地」
由前缀 super- 加本词构成，义为「过多的；极其丰富的」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「丰富性」，较少使用

senses.title: Existing in large quantities
senses.definition: present in large numbers or amounts, far beyond what is merely sufficient
senses.definitionCN: 以大量或大数目存在，远远超过仅仅够用的程度
senses.example: The region has abundant coal and iron.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区有丰富的煤和铁。
senses.why: Latin abundare is 'to overflow'; plenty is pictured as water rising past the brim.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abundare 意为「溢出」，丰富被画成水越过边缘涨起来。

senses.title: Found everywhere in a place
senses.definition: common in a particular place, so that one meets it again and again
senses.definitionCN: 在某地很常见，因而一次又一次遇到
senses.example: Mosquitoes are abundant near the marsh in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天沼泽附近蚊子很多。
senses.why: Overflowing water spreads across the ground; what spreads everywhere becomes impossible to miss.
senses.whyCN: 溢出的水铺满地面；铺得到处都是的东西，就变得无法忽视。

senses.title: Rich in natural wealth
senses.definition: describing land, water or a country that holds a great deal of natural wealth
senses.definitionCN: 形容土地、水域或国家拥有大量自然财富
senses.example: The delta is an abundant land of fish and rice.
senses.exampleCN: 这片三角洲是鱼米丰饶之地。
senses.why: The overflowing image settles on the ground: the earth itself gives more than its people need.
senses.whyCN: 溢出的意象落到土地上：大地本身给出的，超过人们所需。

senses.title: A plentiful supply
senses.definition: describing goods, food or water that are supplied in amounts large enough to cover every need
senses.definitionCN: 形容货物、食物或水的供应量足以覆盖一切需要
senses.example: The camp had an abundant supply of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 营地的洁净水供应充足。
senses.why: Once the container overflows, no one at the rim goes without.
senses.whyCN: 容器一旦溢出，站在边缘的人就都不会缺。

senses.title: Well supplied with a quality
senses.definition: in the phrase abundant in, having a great deal of a particular quality or element
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 abundant in，表示富含某种特质或成分
senses.example: This soil is abundant in nitrogen but poor in phosphorus.
senses.exampleCN: 这种土壤富含氮，却缺少磷。
senses.why: The same pouring image applies to anything that can fill a space, including a mineral or a trait.
senses.whyCN: 同一个倾注意象适用于任何能填满空间的东西，包括矿物质或某种特质。

senses.title: Ample evidence or data
senses.definition: describing proof, data or examples that are numerous enough to support a firm conclusion
senses.definitionCN: 形容证据、数据或例子多到足以支撑一个确定的结论
senses.example: There is abundant evidence that the climate is shifting.
senses.exampleCN: 有大量证据表明气候正在变化。
senses.why: Evidence fills the space of an argument the way water fills a basin; enough of it leaves no gap.
senses.whyCN: 证据填满论证的空间，就像水填满盆；足够多时，不留空隙。

senses.title: Growing thickly
senses.definition: describing plants that grow densely and in great number in a place
senses.definitionCN: 形容植物在某地密集而大量地生长
senses.example: Wild garlic is abundant along the shaded bank.
senses.exampleCN: 背阴的河岸上野蒜长得十分茂盛。
senses.why: Things that overflow their bounds look like plants crowding over a path, one stem beside another.
senses.whyCN: 溢出边界的东西，看上去就像植物挤满小路，一根茎挨着一根茎。

senses.title: A life of plenty
senses.definition: describing a period or way of life in which there is more than enough of everything needed
senses.definitionCN: 形容一段时期或生活方式中，所需之物样样都多到有余
senses.example: They remembered the abundant years before the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 他们记得干旱之前那些丰足的年头。
senses.why: When the stream keeps overflowing year after year, the whole life beside it becomes rich.
senses.whyCN: 当溪水一年又一年持续溢出，溪边整个生活也跟着富足起来。

intro.en: Abundant comes from a Latin verb meaning to overflow, built on the word for a wave; the picture is water rising past its bank.
intro.cn: abundant 来自拉丁语中表示「溢出」的动词，其词基是「波浪」一词；画面是水涨过堤岸。

items.en: The noun unda meant 'a wave, water'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 名词 unda 意为「波浪、水」；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: The verb undare meant 'to surge, flow in waves, rise like water'.
items.cn: 动词 undare 意为「涌动、像波浪般流动、如水上涌」。

items.en: Ab- plus undare formed abundare, 'to overflow, be plentiful', literally to flow away over the edge.
items.cn: ab- 加 undare 构成 abundare，意为「溢出、丰盛」，字面就是漫过边缘流出去。

items.en: The noun abundantia named plenty itself, and the participle abundans gave the adjective its shape.
items.cn: 名词 abundantia 指「丰盛」本身，分词 abundans 则给出了形容词的形态。

items.en: Old French passed the adjective to English with both the physical and the figurative senses intact.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词传给英语，字面义与比喻义都完整保留。

items.en: English recorded the word in the fourteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录了这个词；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the unda family and two words that merely share the ab- opening; the near-meaning group gathers words for plenty and for scarcity.
note.cn: 形近组收 unda 词族的词与两个只是同样以 ab- 开头的词；近义组收表示丰足与稀缺的词语。

entries.definition: The noun for a very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「丰富、充裕、大量」，由本词加 -ance 构成，同出 abundare。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in large quantities, or very clearly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「丰富地、极其清楚地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: To move in smooth waves; it keeps the Latin wave noun unda.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「起伏波动」，保留拉丁语「波浪」名词 unda，词根同源。

entries.definition: To flood an area with water, or to overwhelm someone with too much of something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「淹没、使应接不暇」，同样出自 undare，词根同源。

entries.definition: More than is needed, especially of words or staff; it comes from redundare, to overflow.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多余的、冗余的」，出自 redundare「溢出」，与 abundant 同根。

entries.definition: Existing in large amounts, especially of things needed; plainer and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的、大量的」，多指所需之物，比 abundant 更平实。

entries.definition: Enough or more than enough for a purpose; it stresses sufficiency rather than sheer volume.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「足够的、充裕的」，强调够用，而不是数量之多。

entries.definition: Very plentiful, often of notes, tears or words; formal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大量的、丰富的」，常用于笔记、泪水或言辞，语气正式。

entries.definition: Able to produce a great deal of growth; it describes productive land rather than amount.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肥沃的、多产的」，描述土地的出产能力，而非数量。

entries.definition: Present in amounts too small for the demand; the direct opposite of abundant.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稀少的、短缺的」，数量不足以满足需求，正与 abundant 相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real unda root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 unda 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Unda is a wave: abundance is water rising over the bank and spreading.
normal.cn: unda 是「波浪」：丰富就是水涨过堤岸、四处漫开。

normal.en: Undulate, inundate and redundant all keep this wave or overflow picture.
normal.cn: undulate、inundate 与 redundant 都保留这层波浪或溢出的画面。

normal.en: Abundant in marks what a place is rich in, from minerals to wild flowers.
normal.cn: abundant in 标出某地盛产什么，从矿物到野花都可以。

normal.en: Abundant evidence means the argument has no empty basin left.
normal.cn: abundant evidence 意为论证的盆里再没有空处。

normal.en: Abundant rainfall is plenty that arrives from the sky, not from a store.
normal.cn: abundant rainfall 是从天上来的丰足，而非仓里的存货。

abstract.en: Picture a spring that keeps rising until water crosses the stone rim and runs down the path.
abstract.cn: 想象一眼泉水不断上涌，直到水漫过石沿、顺着小路流下。

abstract.en: The same overflow can be grain in a barn, fish in a river, or evidence in a report.
abstract.cn: 同一种溢出可以是谷仓里的粮、河里的鱼，或报告里的证据。

abstract.en: Abundant is not endless: it means the edge was crossed, and there is still more coming.
abstract.cn: abundant 不是无穷：它意味着已经漫过边缘，而且还有更多的在涌来。

examples.en: Fish are abundant in the cold currents off the coast.
examples.cn: 近海的冷流中鱼类十分丰富。

examples.en: The report offers abundant evidence of waste in the system.
examples.cn: 报告提供了大量证据，说明该体系存在浪费。

examples.en: In those years, work was abundant and wages were rising.
examples.cn: 那些年工作机会很多，工资也在上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额帮等特」——帮忙的人多到站不下，还得等下一批：丰富、大量

root: 拉丁语 abundare「溢出、丰盛」由 ab-「离开」+ undare「涌动」构成，undare 又出自 unda「波浪」；unda 更早来源不确定。核心是「像水一样漫过边界」，因而表示数量多到有余。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all show the same overflow: too much of a thing, too many in one place, rich land, a full supply, a full quality, full evidence, thick growth, or a full life.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在呈现同一种溢出：东西多得有余、某处多得数不清、土地富饶、供应充足、特质充盈、证据充分、生长茂密，或生活丰足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring rises until water spills over the stone rim and flows outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：泉眼不断上涌，水漫过石沿，向外流去。

branches.en: THE AMOUNT: more is produced than the container can hold, so supply exceeds need.
branches.cn: 数量线：产出超过容器容量，供应因此多过需求。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: what has overflowed is met everywhere, and plants crowd the ground.
branches.cn: 蔓延线：溢出的东西处处可见，植物也挤满地面。

branches.en: THE LAND: overflowing water makes rich soil, and rich soil makes a rich life.
branches.cn: 土地线：溢出的水造就沃土，沃土又养出丰足的生活。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: anything that fills a space, including a mineral, can be abundant in a place.
branches.cn: 特质线：凡是能填满空间的，包括某种矿物，都可以在某处丰盈。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: evidence fills the basin of a claim until no gap remains.
branches.cn: 论证线：证据填满主张的盆，直到不留空隙。

intro.en: Abundant is a Latin prefix plus a wave verb; English adds -ance, -ly and -ness to make the family.
intro.cn: abundant 由拉丁语前缀加「波浪」动词构成；英语再以 -ance、-ly 与 -ness 扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin unda, undare, abundare and abundantia are all recorded, so only the oldest origin of unda is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 unda、undare、abundare 与 abundantia 均有记录，只有 unda 最古老的来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks water flowing away over the edge.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记水漫过边缘向外流。

items.example: The noun is the wave image behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是这一词族背后的波浪意象。

items.example: The verb supplies the movement of the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供意象中的运动。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms abundant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abundant。

items.example: It forms abundance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abundance。

items.example: It forms abundantly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abundantly。

items.example: The road undulates along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 道路沿着山脊起伏。

items.example: Letters inundated the office after the broadcast.
items.exampleCN: 节目播出后，信件淹没了办公室。

items.example: The editor cut the redundant sentences.
items.exampleCN: 编辑删去了多余的句子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「丰富；充裕」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「丰富地；极其清楚地」

definition_zh: 滥用；虐待；辱骂；侵害；恶习；弊端
definition_en: to use something in a wrong or harmful way, or to treat a person or animal cruelly
core_image: 本该用来浇花的清水，被倒进了发动好的汽车油箱
scene: 那人把公司配给他的卡车开去度假，还记成公务行程。The manager was dismissed for abusing his expense account.
sceneCN: 这里 abuse 是「滥用（资源或权限）」（第 1 个义项：把公器或资源用于不当用途）；句意为这名经理因滥用报销账户而被解雇。

pos.zh: 动词：滥用；虐待；辱骂；侵害
名词：滥用；虐待；辱骂；恶习；弊端

derivatives.zh: 由名词词干加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「谩骂的；虐待的；滥用的」
由动词加施动后缀 -er 构成，义为「滥用者；虐待者」
由形容词 abusive 加 -ly 构成，义为「辱骂地；虐待地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「辱骂性；虐待性」

senses.title: Using power or resources wrongly
senses.definition: to use something one is trusted with, such as power, money or an office, for a wrong purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把受托掌握的权力、金钱或职位用于不当目的
senses.example: He abused his position to award contracts to friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他滥用职位把合同批给朋友。
senses.why: Latin abuti is 'to use up'; using a thing outside its purpose wears it out and wastes it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abuti 是「用尽」，把东西用在目的之外，既耗尽它，也浪费它。

senses.title: Treating a person or animal cruelly
senses.definition: to treat a person or animal with cruelty, violence or neglect, especially over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 以残酷、暴力或疏于照顾的方式对待人或动物，尤指长期如此
senses.example: The neighbours reported that the dog was being abused.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居举报有人正在虐待那条狗。
senses.why: A person is not a tool, so using a person as if they were one means using them badly and to their harm.
senses.whyCN: 人不是工具，把人当工具来使用，就等于用坏了、用伤了。

senses.title: Insulting someone in words
senses.definition: to speak to someone with rude, insulting or threatening language
senses.definitionCN: 用粗鲁、侮辱或威胁性的语言对人说话
senses.example: The driver shouted and abused the cyclist at the lights.
senses.exampleCN: 那名司机在红绿灯前叫骂骑车的人。
senses.why: Speech is also a thing that can be used: turned from its purpose, it becomes a weapon.
senses.whyCN: 言语也是一种可以被使用的东西：一旦背离用途，它就变成武器。

senses.title: Sexual or physical violation
senses.definition: to commit a sexual or physical act against someone without consent, especially against a child
senses.definitionCN: 未经同意对他人实施性行为或人身侵犯，尤指对儿童
senses.example: The court heard that the girl had been abused for years.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭了解到，那名女孩多年来一直受到侵害。
senses.why: This is the darkest branch: the other person is treated as a body to be used, not as a person.
senses.whyCN: 这是最黑暗的一支：对方被当作可供使用的身体，而不再是一个人。

senses.title: Misuse of drugs or alcohol
senses.definition: to take drugs, alcohol or medicine in a way that harms the body or is not medically intended
senses.definitionCN: 以伤害身体或不符合医疗目的的方式使用毒品、酒精或药物
senses.example: He began abusing painkillers after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他开始滥用止痛药。
senses.why: Medicine is meant to heal; used past that purpose it turns against the body it was meant to help.
senses.whyCN: 药物本为治病，一旦超出这个用途，就反过来伤害本该被帮助的身体。

senses.title: Betraying trust placed in you
senses.definition: to take advantage of someone's trust, kindness or hospitality for one's own gain
senses.definitionCN: 利用他人的信任、善意或款待来谋取私利
senses.example: She felt he had abused her generosity.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得他辜负并利用了她的慷慨。
senses.why: Trust is handed over like a tool; using it against the giver is the clearest form of misuse.
senses.whyCN: 信任像工具一样被交到手上；反过来用它伤害交付者，是最典型的「用坏」。

senses.title: A corrupt practice or custom
senses.definition: a wrong or harmful custom, system or practice that has become established over time
senses.definitionCN: 长期形成的错误、有害的习俗、制度或做法
senses.example: The report listed the abuses of the old tax system.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列举了旧税制中的种种弊端。
senses.why: The noun names not one act but a settled habit of using things wrongly, repeated until it looks normal.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的不是一次行为，而是一种用坏东西的固定习惯，重复到看起来正常。

senses.title: Misuse of language
senses.definition: to use a word, phrase or form of language incorrectly or in a way that damages its meaning
senses.definitionCN: 错误地使用单词、短语或语言形式，或使其含义受损
senses.example: The editor noted how the term had been abused in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑指出这个术语在媒体中被误用了。
senses.why: Even a word is a tool with a proper use, and stretching it past that use is the same abuse.
senses.whyCN: 连词也是一种有其正确用途的工具，把它拉伸到用途之外，是同一种滥用。

intro.en: Abuse comes from a Latin verb meaning to use up or use wrongly, built on the ordinary verb for using.
intro.cn: abuse 来自拉丁语中表示「用尽、用错」的动词，其词基就是表示「使用」的普通动词。

items.en: The verb uti meant 'to use, employ, make use of'. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 uti 意为「使用、运用、利用」；其更早来源不确定。

items.en: The noun usus meant 'use, practice, custom', and it later gave English use and usage.
items.cn: 名词 usus 意为「使用、实践、习俗」，后来给出英语的 use 与 usage。

items.en: Ab- plus uti formed abuti, 'to use up, misuse, consume wrongly'; the prefix here carries the idea of away or beyond.
items.cn: ab- 加 uti 构成 abuti，意为「用尽、误用、滥用」；此处前缀带「偏离、越出」的意思。

items.en: The noun abusus named misuse and also a corrupt practice; both branches passed into French and English.
items.cn: 名词 abusus 既指误用，也指腐败的做法；两条分支都进入了法语与英语。

items.en: Old French abuser meant to deceive or misuse, and it added the sense of treating a person badly.
items.cn: 古法语 abuser 意为「欺骗、误用」，并附加上「苛待他人」的意思。

items.en: English recorded the verb and noun in the fourteenth century. The exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪记录了动词与名词；确切首见年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the uti family and two words that merely share the ab- opening; the near-meaning group gathers words for wrong use and for cruel treatment.
note.cn: 形近组收 uti 词族的词与两个只是同样以 ab- 开头的词；近义组收表示误用与苛待的词语。

entries.definition: An adjective for language or behaviour that insults, threatens or harms.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「谩骂的、虐待的、滥用的」，由本词加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: A person who mistreats others or uses something wrongly.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滥用者、虐待者」，由本词加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: To use something wrongly; it has the same base verb uti with a different English prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「误用、滥用」，同一个词基 uti 配上不同的英语前缀，词根同源。

entries.definition: To employ something for a purpose; the plain base word behind abuse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使用」，是 abuse 背后那个平实的词基，词根同源。

entries.definition: To take in liquid or energy; it shares the ab- opening but comes from sorbere, to suck in.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸收」，只是同样以 ab- 开头，词根为 sorbere「吸」，词源不同。

entries.definition: To treat a person or animal badly or unfairly; clearer than abuse about cruelty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「虐待、苛待」，在「残酷」这一点上比 abuse 更明确。

entries.definition: To use someone or something for one's own advantage, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「利用、剥削」，常带不公平地为自己谋利的意味。

entries.definition: To say something rude that hurts or offends; it covers only the verbal branch of abuse.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「侮辱」，只覆盖 abuse 的言语辱骂一支。

entries.definition: Wrong use of a thing; neutral in tone and without the cruelty that abuse can carry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「误用」，语气中性，不含 abuse 可能带有的残酷意味。

entries.definition: To treat someone with care and proper regard; the opposite of using them harmfully.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「尊重」，以关切与应有的礼遇待人，正与苛待相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real uti root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 uti 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Uti is simply to use, so abuse is using with an ab- turn: away from the proper purpose.
normal.cn: uti 就是「使用」，abuse 是带 ab- 转折的使用：偏离了正当用途。

normal.en: Abuse of power is the standard phrase for using an office for private gain.
normal.cn: abuse of power 是把职位用于私利的标准说法。

normal.en: Drug abuse and alcohol abuse both describe use that has gone past medical or social limits.
normal.cn: drug abuse 与 alcohol abuse 都指超出了医疗或社会界限的使用。

normal.en: Verbal abuse is the speech branch: words used as weapons.
normal.cn: verbal abuse 是言语那一支：词被当作武器来用。

normal.en: The plural abuses often means settled corrupt practices, not single acts.
normal.cn: 复数 abuses 常指长期形成的腐败做法，而非单次行为。

abstract.en: Picture a garden hose turned away from the flower bed and aimed into a car's fuel tank.
abstract.cn: 想象一支花园水管被从花圃转开，对准了汽车的油箱。

abstract.en: The same turned hose can be an office, a friendship, a drug or a word.
abstract.cn: 同一支被转开的水管可以是职位、友情、药物，或一个词。

abstract.en: Abuse is not lack of use: it is use with the direction reversed, so the good thing does harm.
abstract.cn: abuse 不是不用：它是方向被反过来后的使用，好东西因此造成了伤害。

examples.en: Several officials were charged with abusing their offices.
examples.cn: 几名官员被控滥用职权。

examples.en: The charity has a hotline for reports of abuse.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构设有举报虐待行为的热线。

examples.en: He abused the trust of everyone who had helped him.
examples.cn: 他辜负了每一个帮助过他的人所给的信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额必优死」——好好的东西被用到报废，还伤了人：滥用、虐待

root: 拉丁语 abuti「用尽、误用」由 ab-「离开、越出」+ uti「使用」构成，名词 abusus 兼指误用与腐败做法；uti 更早来源不确定。核心是「把东西用偏、用坏」，由物及人，引申出虐待与辱骂。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all reverse a proper use: power, an animal, speech, a body, a drug, a trust, an institution, or a word is turned away from its purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把一种正当用途反过来：权力、动物、言语、身体、药物、信任、制度或词语，被转离了本来用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water meant for a flower bed is poured into a fuel tank instead.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该浇花的水，被倒进了汽车油箱。

branches.en: THE TRUST: power, money or kindness handed over is used against the giver.
branches.cn: 托付线：交到手上的权力、金钱或善意，被反过来对付交付者。

branches.en: THE BODY: a person or animal is treated as a tool, with cruelty instead of care.
branches.cn: 身体线：人或动物被当作工具，得到的是残酷而非照顾。

branches.en: THE VOICE: words, meant to communicate, are turned into blows.
branches.cn: 声音线：本用于沟通的词，被转成了打击。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: medicine or alcohol goes past its purpose and harms the user.
branches.cn: 物质线：药物或酒越过本来用途，反过来伤害使用者。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM AND THE WORD: repeated misuse hardens into custom, or bends a term out of shape.
branches.cn: 制度与词语线：反复的误用固化成习俗，或把一个术语扭得变形。

intro.en: Abuse is a Latin prefix plus the ordinary Latin verb for using; English adds -ive, -er, -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: abuse 由拉丁语前缀加表示「使用」的普通动词构成；英语再以 -ive、-er、-ly 与 -ness 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin uti, usus, abuti and abusus are all recorded, so only the oldest root of uti is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 uti、usus、abuti 与 abusus 均有记录，只有 uti 最古老的词根不确定。

items.example: The prefix marks a use that goes past its purpose.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记越过用途的使用。

items.example: The verb is the plain using root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「使用」词根。

items.example: The noun lies behind English use and usage.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语 use 与 usage 的来源。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of abuse.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是 abuse 的直接来源。

items.example: The noun carried both branches into French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把两条分支都带进了法语。

items.example: It forms abusive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abusive。

items.example: It forms abuser.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abuser。

items.example: It forms abusively.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abusively。

items.example: It forms abusiveness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abusiveness。

items.example: The label warns against misuse of the tool.
items.exampleCN: 标签警示不要误用该工具。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「谩骂的；虐待的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「滥用者；虐待者」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「辱骂地；虐待地」

definition_zh: 学术的；学院的；理论性的；学业优秀的；大学教师；学者
definition_en: relating to education, study and scholarship, especially at a university, or a person who teaches and researches there
core_image: 学园里成排的书架与围坐辩论的人，纸上写满推理
scene: 图书馆的自习区坐满了人，桌上摊着论文草稿和笔记。She published her first academic paper before finishing her degree.
sceneCN: 这里 academic 是「学术的」（第 1 个义项：与高等教育和研究相关）；句意为她在完成学位之前就发表了第一篇学术论文。

pos.zh: 形容词：学术的；学院的；理论性的；学业优秀的
名词：大学教师；学者；学术人员

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 academic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「学业上；学术上」
由词干加 -ian 构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
借自拉丁语的名词，义为「学术界；学术圈」
由形容词加 -ism 构成，义为「学院主义；拘守成规的学风」
由否定前缀 non- 加本词构成，义为「非学术的」

senses.title: Relating to study and scholarship
senses.titleCN: 学术的、与学问研究相关
senses.definition: connected with education, research and serious study, especially at a college or university
senses.definitionCN: 与教育、研究及严肃的学问相关，尤指在大学层面
senses.example: The journal publishes academic work from many countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这份期刊发表来自许多国家的学术成果。
senses.why: The word comes from the name of Plato's school, where study was the whole point of the place.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自柏拉图学园的名字，在那个地方，做学问就是全部意义。

senses.title: Theoretical rather than practical
senses.definition: concerned with theory and abstract reasoning rather than with practical skills or immediate use
senses.definitionCN: 关注理论与抽象推理，而非实用技能或眼前用途
senses.example: The training was too academic and gave no shop-floor experience.
senses.exampleCN: 这项培训太偏理论，没有提供车间经验。
senses.why: A school can be shut away from the market, and what is learned there can stay inside its walls.
senses.whyCN: 学园可以与市场隔绝，在那里学到的东西也可以一直留在墙内。

senses.title: Doing well in formal study
senses.definition: describing a person, especially a child, who performs well in subjects taught at school
senses.definitionCN: 形容一个人，尤指孩子，在学校所教科目上表现良好
senses.example: She was the most academic student in her year.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那一届最学业出色的学生。
senses.why: If the school is the measure, then a person strong at what the school teaches is 'academic'.
senses.whyCN: 既然以学园为尺度，那么擅长学园所教之事的人就是 academic。

senses.title: A university teacher or researcher
senses.definition: a person who teaches or does research at a university, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 在大学任教或做研究的人，作可数名词
senses.example: The panel included two academics and a judge.
senses.exampleCN: 专家组包括两位学者和一位法官。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a person: one who belongs to the school and lives by its work.
senses.whyCN: 形容词变成了人：属于学园、以学园的工作为业的那个人。

senses.title: Having no practical effect
senses.definition: in the phrase purely academic, describing a question or dispute that cannot change anything real
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 purely academic，形容无法改变任何实际结果的问题或争论
senses.example: Whether the rule was legal is now purely academic.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规定是否合法，如今已纯粹是空谈。
senses.why: When a matter is settled outside the school, further argument inside it has no consequence.
senses.whyCN: 当事情在学校之外已成定局，学校里的继续争论就不产生后果。

senses.title: Belonging to a school's curriculum
senses.definition: relating to the subjects taught and assessed in a school, as opposed to sport or social life
senses.definitionCN: 与学校所教与考核的科目相关，以区别于体育或社交生活
senses.example: His academic record improved after he joined the reading club.
senses.exampleCN: 加入读书会之后，他的学业成绩提高了。
senses.why: The school has its own scoreboard, and academic marks what is counted on it.
senses.whyCN: 学园有自己的记分板，academic 标出的正是板上计分的那一项。

senses.title: Belonging to the academic world
senses.definition: relating to the professional world of universities, journals, conferences and research careers
senses.definitionCN: 与大学、期刊、会议及研究生涯这一职业世界相关
senses.example: She left academic life to work in a museum.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开学术圈，去博物馆工作。
senses.why: Once the school grows into a whole world with its own rules, everything inside it is academic.
senses.whyCN: 当学园长成一个有自身规则的世界，里面的一切都带上 academic 的标签。

senses.title: Belonging to Plato's Academy
senses.definition: in the original historical sense, relating to the school founded by Plato outside Athens
senses.definitionCN: 最早的历史义，指与柏拉图在雅典城外创办的学园相关
senses.example: The academic tradition of the school lasted for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个学园的学术传统延续了好几个世纪。
senses.why: This is the oldest branch: the word was first simply the name of one garden and its school.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一支：这个词最初只是一个园子及其学校的名字。

intro.en: Academic is an adjective made from the name of Plato's school; that name comes from an Athenian hero, and the step before the hero is uncertain.
intro.cn: academic 是由柏拉图学园的名称派生的形容词；学园名来自一位雅典英雄，而英雄名之前更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Akademos was an Athenian hero associated with a grove outside the city walls. The earlier origin of the name is uncertain.
items.cn: Akademos 是一位与城墙外一片林地有关的雅典英雄；这个名字更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The place was called Akedemeia or Akademeia, 'the grove of Akademos'; the exact spelling varies in the sources.
items.cn: 这个地方被称为 Akedemeia 或 Akademeia，即「Akademos 的林地」；文献中的拼写并不完全一致。

items.en: Plato taught in that grove, and his school took the place name, becoming the Academy.
items.cn: 柏拉图在那片林地中授课，他的学校便采用了这个地名，成为「学园」。

items.en: Latin used academia for Plato's school and later for any learned society or university.
items.cn: 拉丁语用 academia 指柏拉图的学园，后来泛指任何学术团体或大学。

items.en: English formed the adjective academic in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪构成形容词 academic；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word widened from one garden to schooling in general, then to theory, to marks, and to a whole profession.
items.cn: 这个词从一个园子扩展到一般学校教育，再扩展到理论、成绩以及整个职业群体。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the academy family; the near-meaning group gathers words for study, theory and the people who teach.
note.cn: 形近组收 academy 词族的词；近义组收表示学问、理论与教书人的词语。

entries.definition: A school or learned society; the noun from which academic is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、学会」，是 academic 由之派生的名词，词根相同。

entries.definition: The world of universities and research, taken directly from Latin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学术界、学术圈」，直接借自拉丁语，词根相同。

entries.definition: A member of a learned academy or national academy of sciences.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「院士、学会会员」，由本词加 -ian 构成，词根相同。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in terms of study or school performance.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「学业上、学术上」，直接由本词加 -ally 构成。

entries.definition: Ridiculous; the two words are close in spelling only through the ak- opening.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬的」，只是开头音节相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Showing careful and serious study; it describes the quality of work rather than the setting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「博学的、学术性的」，描述研究的品质而非所处场所。

entries.definition: Relating to teaching and learning in general, including schools and training.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「教育的」，泛指教学与学习，包括学校与培训。

entries.definition: Based on theory rather than practice; close to the second sense of academic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论的」，以理论而非实践为据，与 academic 的第二个义项接近。
