entries.definition: A person who studies a subject deeply, especially at a university.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学者」，指深入研究某一学科的人，尤指在大学。

entries.definition: Concerned with real action and use rather than theory; the opposite of academic in that sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实用的」，关注真实行动与用途而非理论，正与学术理论义相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek place name behind the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词背后真实的希腊地名，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Akademeia was a grove outside Athens, so every academic word still carries a garden in it.
normal.cn: Akademeia 是雅典城外的一片林地，因此每个 academic 家族词里都还带着一座园子。

normal.en: Academy is the place, academic is the adjective, academia is the whole world.
normal.cn: academy 是场所，academic 是形容词，academia 是整个圈子。

normal.en: Academic year and academic performance mark the calendar and the scoreboard of a school.
normal.cn: academic year 与 academic performance 标出学校的日历与记分板。

normal.en: Purely academic means the answer can no longer change anything.
normal.cn: purely academic 意为答案已无法改变任何事。

normal.en: An academic is also a person: the teacher who lives by the work of the school.
normal.cn: an academic 还可以指人：以学园的工作为业的教师。

abstract.en: Picture a shaded grove with benches in a circle, and a question passed from hand to hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一片树荫下的林地，长凳围成一圈，一个问题在人们手中传递。

abstract.en: The same grove becomes a lecture hall, a journal, a mark on a report card, or a whole career.
abstract.cn: 同一片林地可以变成讲堂、期刊、成绩单上的一个分数，或一整个职业生涯。

abstract.en: Academic starts as a place name: the word remembers a garden even when it speaks of theory.
abstract.cn: academic 起初是个地名：即使在谈理论时，这个词仍记得那座园子。

examples.en: Her academic results were strong enough for a research scholarship.
examples.cn: 她的学业成绩足以拿到研究奖学金。

examples.en: The debate is academic now that the contract has been signed.
examples.cn: 合同既已签署，这场争论已无实际意义。

examples.en: Several academics signed the open letter on research funding.
examples.cn: 几位学者在关于研究经费的公开信上签了名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米克」——园子里人人捧着书辩论，满口学问：学术的

root: 希腊语 Akademeia 指雅典城外「Akademos 的林地」，柏拉图在此授课，其学校遂称「学园」；拉丁语作 academia，英语十六世纪由此构成形容词 academic。英雄名 Akademos 更早的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread outward from one grove: its study, its theory, its successful students, its teachers, its empty debates, its marks, its professional world, and the place itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一片林地向外铺开：其中的学问、理论、优秀学生、教师、空谈、分数、职业圈子，以及那片地方本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grove outside the city walls where a circle of listeners follows a teacher's argument.
core.cn: 核心意象：城墙外的一片林地，一圈听众跟着老师的论证往下想。

branches.en: THE STUDY: the grove's whole business is learning, and that becomes the first sense.
branches.cn: 学问线：林地的全部事务就是求学，这成了第一个义项。

branches.en: THE WALLS: shut inside, study turns theoretical, and what cannot affect the world becomes empty debate.
branches.cn: 围墙线：关在墙内，学问变成理论；影响不了世界时，就变成空谈。

branches.en: THE SCOREBOARD: the school measures its students, and their marks are called academic.
branches.cn: 记分线：学校衡量学生，他们的分数就被称为 academic。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: teachers and researchers become academics, and their world becomes academia.
branches.cn: 人群线：教师与研究者成为 academics，他们的世界成为 academia。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the oldest use still points straight at Plato's garden.
branches.cn: 源头线：最早的用法仍直指柏拉图的那座园子。

intro.en: Academic is a Greek place name fitted with Latin and English endings; the suffixes are ordinary, the base is a proper name.
intro.cn: academic 是一个希腊地名配上拉丁与英语词尾；后缀都很普通，词基却是专名。

latinIntro.en: Latin academia is recorded for the school and for learned bodies; the Greek name before it is a place name, not a root with a meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academia 有文献记录，指学园与学术团体；它之前的希腊名是地名，而非有实义的词根。

items.example: The school took its name from the grove.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校从这片林地得名。

items.meaning: Plato's school, later any learned body
items.meaningCN: 柏拉图学园，后泛指学术团体
items.example: Academia still names the world of universities.
items.exampleCN: academia 至今仍指大学的世界。

items.example: The academy trains young musicians.
items.exampleCN: 这所学院培养年轻音乐家。

items.meaning: relating to study or a school
items.example: The adjective came later than the noun.
items.exampleCN: 形容词的出现晚于名词。

items.example: It forms academic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academic。

items.example: It appears in academical, an older form.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在较早的形式 academical 中。

items.example: It forms academically.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academically。

items.example: It forms academician.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academician。

items.example: It forms academicism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academicism。

items.example: He left academe for a career in publishing.
items.exampleCN: 他离开学界，转行做出版。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ally 构成，义为「学业上；学术上」
由本词加 -ian 构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
由本词加 -ism 构成，义为「学院主义；拘守成规的学风」

definition_zh: 学院；专科学校；学会；研究院；（美国）私立中学；柏拉图学园
definition_en: a school that teaches a particular subject, or a society of scholars and artists, or the school of Plato
core_image: 城墙外一片树荫下的园子，学生围坐成圈听讲
scene: 毕业典礼那天，礼堂里挂着历届学员的照片，正中是一把旧木椅。He trained at the naval academy for four years before going to sea.
sceneCN: 这里 academy 是「专门学院（军校）」（第 1 个义项：教授专门学科或职业的学校）；句意为他在海军学院受训四年后才出海。

pos.zh: 名词：学院；专科学校；学会；研究院

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「学术的；学院的；理论性的」
借自拉丁语的名词，义为「学术界；学术圈」
由词干加 -ian 构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
由本词加 -al 构成的较早形容词，义为「学院的；学术的」，现多用 academic

senses.title: A school for a special subject or profession
senses.definition: a school, often beyond secondary level, that trains people in one subject or profession
senses.definitionCN: 常指中等教育之后的学校，在某一学科或职业上培养人才
senses.example: She enrolled in an academy of design in the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 她进了首都的一所设计学院。
senses.why: The word began as the name of a school, and the school sense is still the plainest one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就是一所学园的名字，学校义至今仍是最平实的一支。

senses.title: A learned society or research body
senses.definition: an official society of distinguished scholars, scientists or artists, often with a national role
senses.definitionCN: 由杰出学者、科学家或艺术家组成的正式团体，常承担国家级职能
senses.example: The academy publishes a monthly journal of physics.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究院出版一份物理月刊。
senses.why: The school grew into a body of learned people who no longer teach pupils but guard knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 学园长成了一个博学之士的团体，不再教小孩，而是守护知识。

senses.title: Plato's original garden school
senses.definition: the school founded by Plato in a grove near Athens, the oldest sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 柏拉图在雅典附近林地中创办的学校，是这个词最古老的义项
senses.example: Historians still debate what was taught in the original academy.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家至今仍在争论最早那所学园教了些什么。
senses.why: Every later sense is a descendant of one garden with a circle of listeners.
senses.whyCN: 后来的每个义项，都是一片林地加一圈听众的后代。

senses.title: A private secondary school
senses.definition: in American use, a private school below university level, often with a traditional curriculum
senses.definitionCN: 美国用法，指大学以下的私立学校，课程往往较为传统
senses.example: He spent three years at a boarding academy in New England.
senses.exampleCN: 他在新英格兰的一所寄宿制私立中学待了三年。
senses.why: The school sense narrows on one side of the Atlantic to a fee-paying school for teenagers.
senses.whyCN: 学校义在大西洋一侧收窄，专指收费的青少年学校。

senses.title: A military or police college
senses.definition: a college that trains officers for the armed forces or the police
senses.definitionCN: 为武装部队或警察培养军官的院校
senses.example: Cadets at the academy learn navigation and drill.
senses.exampleCN: 军校学员要学习航海与操练。
senses.why: A school can train the body as well as the mind, and the name follows the training.
senses.whyCN: 学校既可以训练头脑，也可以训练身体，名字便跟着训练走。

senses.title: A school of music, art or drama
senses.titleCN: 音乐、美术或戏剧专科院校
senses.definition: a conservatory-style institution devoted to one of the fine arts
senses.definitionCN: 专攻某一门造型或表演艺术的院校，类似音乐学院建制
senses.example: The young violinist won a place at the academy of music.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻的小提琴手考进了音乐学院。
senses.why: Once art is taught in a fixed place with masters and pupils, it borrows the school name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦艺术在固定的场所由师傅带徒弟来教，它就借用了学校之名。

senses.title: An honorary body in a profession
senses.titleCN: 某一行业的荣誉性团体
senses.definition: a formal body that honours achievement in a profession, such as film or acting
senses.definitionCN: 为某行业成就颁发荣誉的正式团体，如电影或表演界
senses.example: The academy voted to give the film its top prize.
senses.exampleCN: 该学院投票把最高奖颁给了这部电影。
senses.why: A society of experts can also act as a judge, handing out honours instead of lessons.
senses.whyCN: 专家团体也可以充当裁判，颁发的是荣誉而不是课程。

senses.title: The academic establishment
senses.definition: used with the, for the established community of scholars and the standards it accepts
senses.definitionCN: 与定冠词连用，指既成的学者共同体及其认可的标准
senses.example: Her novels were ignored by the academy for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她的小说被学院派忽视了二十年。
senses.why: When the school becomes an institution, its name can stand for the whole establishment.
senses.whyCN: 当学园变成一种体制，它的名字就能代表整个既成圈子。

intro.en: Academy is the name of one garden outside Athens; everything else is that place name travelling outward.
intro.cn: academy 是雅典城外一座园子的名字；其余一切，都是这个地名向外传播的结果。

items.en: Akademos was an Athenian hero linked to a grove northwest of the city. The earlier origin of the name is uncertain.
items.cn: Akademos 是一位与城西北一片林地有关的雅典英雄；这个名字更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The grove was called Akademeia, 'the place of Akademos'; spellings in the sources vary.
items.cn: 这片林地被称为 Akademeia，即「Akademos 的地方」；文献中的拼写并不统一。

items.en: Plato taught there from about the year we call three eight seven before the common era, and the school took the name.
items.cn: 柏拉图约在公元前三八七年前后在此授课，学校便沿用了这个地名。

items.en: Latin academia named the school and later any society of learned people.
items.cn: 拉丁语 academia 指这所学园，后来泛指任何学者团体。

items.en: English borrowed academy in the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 academy；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word spread into art schools, military colleges, research bodies and finally the establishment itself.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到艺术院校、军校、研究院，最后连既成体制本身也叫这个名字。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the words built on this one place name; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of school and learned body.
note.cn: 形近组收由这一个地名构成的词；近义组收其他类型的学校与学术团体。

entries.definition: The adjective for study, theory and university life.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「学术的、学院的、理论性的」，由本词派生。

entries.definition: The world of universities and research, borrowed straight from Latin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学术界、学术圈」，直接借自拉丁语，词根相同。

entries.definition: A member of a national academy or learned society.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「院士、学会会员」，词根相同。

entries.definition: An older adjective form, still used for academic dress and ceremonies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，较早的形式，至今仍用于学位服与典礼场合的结果。

entries.definition: Ridiculous; it is close in sound only, with no shared history.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「荒谬的」，只在读音上接近，并无共同来源。

entries.definition: A place of higher or further education; broader and less specialised than academy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学院、大学」，范围更宽，不如 academy 那样偏重专门方向。

entries.definition: An organisation set up for research, teaching or a professional purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「研究所、学会、机构」，为研究、教学或专业目的设立。

entries.definition: An organised group with shared interests, including learned societies.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「协会、团体」，指有共同兴趣的正式组织，包括学术团体。

entries.definition: A college that trains priests, rabbis or teachers; narrower and religious.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「神学院、师范学校」，范围更窄，多带宗教色彩。

entries.definition: The most general word for a place of teaching, from nursery to university.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「学校」，是最一般的说法，从幼儿园到大学都可使用。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real place name and the compound names the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的地名，以及这个词实际出现的固定名称。

normal.en: Akademeia is a grove, so academy always begins as a place rather than a subject.
normal.cn: Akademeia 是一片林地，因此 academy 起初总是「一个地方」，而不是一门学科。

normal.en: Academy of sciences is the research body; academy of music is the art school.
normal.cn: academy of sciences 是研究院，academy of music 是艺术院校。

normal.en: A military academy trains officers, which shows how far the school sense can travel.
normal.cn: military academy 培养军官，可见学校义能走多远。

normal.en: Academy Award is the film prize handed out by one such honorary body.
normal.cn: Academy Award 就是这样一个荣誉团体颁发的电影奖。

normal.en: The plural academies usually means several schools or several learned bodies, not one building.
normal.cn: 复数 academies 通常指多所学校或多个学术团体，而不是一栋楼。

abstract.en: Picture a ring of benches under olive trees, with the city wall visible through the leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象橄榄树下摆成一圈的长凳，透过树叶能看见城墙。

abstract.en: That ring can become a design school, a science institute, a naval college or an award ceremony.
abstract.cn: 那一圈人可以变成设计学院、科学研究院、海军学院，或一场颁奖礼。

abstract.en: Academy is a place name doing many jobs: the name stayed, the work kept changing.
abstract.cn: academy 是一个兼做许多工作的地名：名字留下来了，工作一直在变。

examples.en: The academy was founded to train rural teachers.
examples.cn: 这所学院是为培养乡村教师而创办的。

examples.en: He was elected to the national academy at the age of forty.
examples.cn: 他四十岁时当选为国家研究院院士。

examples.en: The film won three Academy Awards that year.
examples.cn: 那部电影当年获得三项学院奖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿卡德米」——林子里的园子，学生围坐听讲：学院、学园

root: 希腊语 Akademeia 指雅典城外一片属于英雄 Akademos 的林地，柏拉图在此讲学，其学校因此得名「学园」；拉丁语作 academia，英语十六世纪借入 academy。Akademos 更早的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all point back to one grove: a school, a learned society, Plato's garden, a private school, a military college, an art school, an honorary body, and the establishment itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都指向同一片林地：学校、学术团体、柏拉图的园子、私立中学、军校、艺术院校、荣誉团体，以及既成体制本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of benches under trees outside the city wall, with a teacher at the centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：城墙外树下摆成一圈的长凳，老师坐在正中。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: one subject, one place, from design to music, keeps the oldest shape.
branches.cn: 学校线：一门学科、一个场所，从设计到音乐，都保留最古老的形状。

branches.en: THE BODY: experts organise, publish, and hand out honours instead of lessons.
branches.cn: 团体线：专家组织起来，出刊物，颁发的不是课程而是荣誉。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: the original sense still names Plato's school directly.
branches.cn: 园子线：最古老的义项至今直接指柏拉图的学园。

branches.en: THE TRAINING: fee-paying schools and officer colleges both teach a way of life.
branches.cn: 训练线：收费中学与军官学校都在教一种生活方式。

branches.en: THE ESTABLISHMENT: the name finally stands for the whole settled academic world.
branches.cn: 体制线：这个名字最后代表整个既成的学术世界。

intro.en: Academy is a Greek place name with a Latin noun form and English adjective endings; its base carries no translatable meaning.
intro.cn: academy 是一个希腊地名，配有拉丁名词形式与英语形容词词尾；其词基本身没有可翻译的实义。

latinIntro.en: Latin academia and the medieval adjective academicus are recorded; the Greek base is a proper name, not a root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 academia 与中世纪形容词 academicus 均有记录；希腊词基是专名，而非词根。

items.example: The school was named after the grove.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校以那片林地命名。

items.example: The Latin noun kept both the place and the society.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词兼指场所与团体。

items.example: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词在十六世纪进入英语。

items.example: It forms academic.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academic。

items.example: It forms academical.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academical。

items.example: It forms academician.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academician。

items.example: It forms academically from academic.
items.exampleCN: 它与 academic 一起构成 academically。

items.example: It forms academicism.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 academicism。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ic 构成，义为「学术的；学院的」
由本词加 -ian 构成，义为「院士；学会会员」
由本词加 -al 构成，义为「学院的；学术的」

definition_zh: 加速；加快；促进；使提前发生；（车辆）提速
definition_en: to make something happen faster or sooner, or to increase the speed of a vehicle or process
core_image: 本来缓缓上坡的车轮，忽然被踩下油门飞转起来
scene: 高速路的入口匝道上，后车贴得很近，前方是一段空路。He accelerated smoothly and merged into the traffic.
sceneCN: 这里 accelerate 是「车辆提速」（第 2 个义项：使行驶速度增加）；句意为平稳提速后，他汇入了车流。

pos.zh: 使加速；加快；促进
加速；加快

derivatives.zh: 由动词 accelerate 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「加速；加速度」
由动词加施动后缀 -or 构成，义为「加速器；油门踏板」
由动词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「不断加快的」
由动词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「加速的；速成的」
由动词词干加 -ive 构成形容词，义为「促进加速的」，较少使用

senses.title: To make a process happen faster
senses.definition: to make an event, process or change take less time than it otherwise would
senses.definitionCN: 使事件、过程或变化比原本所需时间更短地完成
senses.example: The new software accelerated the review of applications.
senses.exampleCN: 新软件加快了申请审核。
senses.why: Latin celer means swift; to accelerate is to add swiftness to something already moving.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 celer 意为「快」，accelerate 就是给本已移动的事物添上速度。

senses.title: To increase the speed of a vehicle
senses.definition: to press the accelerator and make a car or other vehicle go faster
senses.definitionCN: 踩下油门，使汽车或其他交通工具行驶得更快
senses.example: The bus accelerated as it left the stop.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车离开车站时加快了速度。
senses.why: This is the word at its most physical: speed is added to a moving body.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最物理的一端：速度被加到一具正在移动的物体上。

senses.title: To promote or hasten a change
senses.definition: to help a plan, reform or trend move forward more quickly than it would alone
senses.definitionCN: 帮助一项计划、改革或趋势比其自行发展更快地推进
senses.example: The grant accelerated the shift to clean energy.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔拨款加快了向清洁能源的转变。
senses.why: An outside push adds speed to a process already under way, like a hand on a moving cart.
senses.whyCN: 外力给已经在进行的过程加上速度，就像一只手推上正在移动的车。

senses.title: To gain speed in physics
senses.definition: in physics, to increase velocity, or to cause a body to change velocity over time
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中指增大速度，或使物体速度随时间发生变化
senses.example: The particle accelerates as it passes through the field.
senses.exampleCN: 粒子穿过场时被加速。
senses.why: Physics makes the metaphor exact: acceleration is the rate at which speed itself changes.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把比喻精确化：加速度就是速度本身发生变化的比率。

senses.title: To bring an event forward in time
senses.definition: to make something happen at an earlier date than was first planned
senses.definitionCN: 使某事在比原计划更早的日期发生
senses.example: The election was accelerated after the coalition split.
senses.exampleCN: 执政联盟分裂后，选举被提前了。
senses.why: Faster in time means sooner on the calendar: the future is pulled toward the present.
senses.whyCN: 在时间上更快，就是在日历上更早：未来被拉向现在。

senses.title: To grow or develop faster
senses.definition: to make a living thing grow, mature or develop more quickly than normal
senses.definitionCN: 使生物比正常情况更快地生长、成熟或发育
senses.example: Warm water accelerates the growth of the seedlings.
senses.exampleCN: 温水会加快幼苗的生长。
senses.why: Growth has its own speed, and the verb adds to it the way warmth adds to a fire.
senses.whyCN: 生长自有其速度，这个动词给它加速，就像温度给火加势。

senses.title: To make a course of study quicker
senses.definition: to arrange a course or programme so that it is completed in less time, as in an accelerated degree
senses.definitionCN: 把课程或项目安排得更短时间完成，如速成学位
senses.example: The school offers an accelerated programme for adults.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校为成年人提供速成课程。
senses.why: Time itself is the thing being compressed, so a whole course can be accelerated.
senses.whyCN: 被压缩的是时间本身，因此整个课程也可以被 accelerate。

senses.title: To intensify or worsen quickly
senses.definition: to increase in rate or intensity, often of something undesirable such as inflation or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 速度或强度增加，常用于通胀、冲突等不希望出现的事物
senses.example: Inflation accelerated sharply in the second quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第二季度通胀急剧加剧。
senses.why: The same added speed can drive a bad trend faster, not only a good plan.
senses.whyCN: 同一种追加的速度也能让坏趋势跑得更快，而不只是好计划。

intro.en: Accelerate comes straight from Latin, where it meant to add speed to something by giving it the quality 'swift'.
intro.cn: accelerate 直接来自拉丁语，原义是赋予某物「快」这一品质，从而给它加上速度。

items.en: The adjective celer meant 'swift, quick'; the deeper origin of the word is source uncertain.
items.cn: 形容词 celer 意为「迅速的、快的」；这个词更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Celerare meant 'to make swift, to hurry', and celeritas named speed itself.
items.cn: celerare 意为「使迅速、赶紧」，celeritas 则指「速度」本身。

items.en: Ad- plus celerare formed accelerare, 'to hasten, speed up'; the ad- means 'to, toward' and adds direction to the action.
items.cn: ad- 加 celerare 构成 accelerare，意为「加快、催速」；ad- 意为「向、朝」，给动作加上方向。

items.en: English borrowed the verb directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, without a French stage. Early dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪直接从拉丁语借入这个动词，没有经过法语阶段；早期年代不确定。

items.en: The word spread from physical motion to processes, schedules, growth, courses and finally to worsening trends.
items.cn: 这个词从物理运动扩展到过程、日程、生长、课程，最后扩展到恶化的趋势。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the celer family and a related English word; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of speeding up and slowing down.
note.cn: 形近组收 celer 词族的词与一个相关英语词；近义组收表示加快与放慢的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of speeding up, or the rate at which speed changes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速；加速度」，由本词加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: The pedal that makes a car go faster, or a machine that speeds particles up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「油门踏板；加速器」，由本词加 -or 构成。

entries.definition: Formal word for speed or swiftness, built directly on Latin celer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「迅速、快捷」，语气正式，直接建立在拉丁语 celer 之上，词根同源。

entries.definition: An instrument that measures acceleration, used in phones and vehicles.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加速度计」，用于手机与车辆，由 accelerator 与 meter 组合而成。

entries.definition: Complete and unlimited; it shares only the initial a-, not the root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「绝对的」，只共享开头的 a- 音节，词根无关。

entries.definition: To make something happen sooner or faster; slightly more formal and often about events.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快、促成」，语气稍正式，多用于事件。

entries.definition: The everyday phrasal verb for going or making something go faster.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，义为「加快」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To make a formal process move faster, especially paperwork or delivery.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快办理」，多指文书或交付等正式流程，语气正式。

entries.definition: To become or make faster, often of a pulse, step or rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加快」，常用于脉搏、脚步或节奏。

entries.definition: To slow down; built on the same root with a negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「减速」，在同一词根上加否定前缀构成，正与 accelerate 相对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real celer root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 celer 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Celer is swift, so accelerate is simply to give something that quality.
normal.cn: celer 是「快」，accelerate 就是给某物加上这一品质。

normal.en: The same root gives celerity, a formal word for speed.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 celerity，即表示「迅速」的正式用词。

normal.en: Acceleration is the noun and accelerator is the pedal or the machine.
normal.cn: acceleration 是名词，accelerator 是踏板或加速器。

normal.en: Accelerate growth and accelerate the process are the standard business pairings.
normal.cn: accelerate growth 与 accelerate the process 是商业文体里的标准搭配。

normal.en: Decelerate has the same root with a negative prefix, so the pair marks both directions.
normal.cn: decelerate 在同一词根上加否定前缀，这一对词标出两个方向。

abstract.en: Picture a cart already rolling downhill and a hand giving it one more push.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆已经在下坡滚动的小车，一只手又推了它一把。

abstract.en: The push can land on an engine, a reform, a seedling, a timetable or a price index.
abstract.cn: 这一推可以落在引擎、改革、幼苗、时间表或物价指数上。

abstract.en: Accelerate never starts from rest: something must already be moving before speed can be added.
abstract.cn: accelerate 从不从静止开始：必须先有东西在动，才能给它加速度。

examples.en: The company accelerated hiring after the new factory opened.
examples.cn: 新工厂开工后，公司加快了招聘。

examples.en: The car accelerated hard to overtake the lorry.
examples.cn: 汽车猛加速超过了货车。

examples.en: Rising demand accelerated the price of copper.
examples.cn: 需求上升推动铜价加速上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞勒瑞特」——油门一脚踩到底，车子飞出去：加速

root: 拉丁语 accelerare「加快」由 ad-「向」+ celerare「使迅速」构成，celerare 又出自形容词 celer「快的」；celer 更早来源不确定。字面就是「把快这一性质加到某物上」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all add speed to something already moving: a process, a car, a reform, a particle, a date, a plant, a course, or a bad trend.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在给本来就在动的事物添加速度：过程、汽车、改革、粒子、日期、植物、课程，或坏趋势。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cart is already rolling and a hand pushes it harder from behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：小车已在滚动，一只手从后面更用力地推它。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: a plan or a change receives an outside push and finishes sooner.
branches.cn: 过程线：计划或变化得到外力一推，因此更早完成。

branches.en: THE BODY: a vehicle or a particle has speed added to its motion.
branches.cn: 物体线：车辆或粒子在运动中获得了速度。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: the same push on time pulls a future event toward the present.
branches.cn: 日历线：对时间施加同样的推力，把未来的事件拉向现在。

branches.en: THE GROWTH: living things and courses are compressed so they arrive sooner.
branches.cn: 生长线：生物与课程被压缩，因此更早到达终点。

branches.en: THE BAD TREND: added speed can carry a worsening situation faster too.
branches.cn: 坏势线：追加的速度同样能让恶化的局面跑得更快。

intro.en: Accelerate is a Latin prefix plus a Latin speed adjective turned verb; English adds -ation, -or, -ing and -ed.
intro.cn: accelerate 由拉丁语前缀加「快」形容词变来的动词构成；英语再以 -ation、-or、-ing 与 -ed 扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin celer, celerare, celeritas and accelerare are all recorded, so only the oldest origin of celer is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 celer、celerare、celeritas 与 accelerare 均有记录，只有 celer 最古老的来源不确定。

items.example: The prefix adds direction to the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给动作加上方向。

items.example: The adjective supplies the quality of speed.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「快」这一性质。

items.example: The verb turns the quality into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把性质变成动作。

items.example: The compound verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms acceleration.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acceleration。

items.example: It forms accelerator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accelerator。

items.example: It forms accelerating.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accelerating。

items.example: It forms accelerated.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accelerated。

items.example: The order was carried out with celerity.
items.exampleCN: 命令被迅速执行。

items.example: The train decelerated before the curve.
items.exampleCN: 列车在弯道前减速。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ation 构成，义为「加速；加速度」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「加速器；油门踏板」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「加速的；速成的」

definition_zh: 口音；腔调；重音；重音符号；强调；强拍；特色；点缀
definition_en: the way a group or region pronounces a language, or a special force given to a syllable, a musical beat, or a visible detail
core_image: 说话时声音在某一处突然加重，像手指在桌面上敲了一下
scene: 清晨的集市上，卖菜的老人一开口，尾音就高高扬起。The shopkeeper's soft accent told the traveller at once which province she came from.
sceneCN: 这里 accent 是「口音、地方腔调」（第 1 个义项：某一地区的人说话时的发音方式）；句意为摊主柔和的口音让旅人立刻听出她来自哪个省。

pos.zh: 名词：口音；腔调；重音；重音符号
动词：重读；强调；使突出

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ed 构成，义为「带口音的；重读的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ual 构成，义为「重音的；关于重音的」
由本词加动词后缀 -uate 构成，义为「强调；使突出」
由 accentuate 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「强调；重读」

senses.title: The way a group pronounces a language
senses.titleCN: 口音：一个群体的发音方式
senses.definition: the distinctive way in which a particular group, region or social class pronounces a language
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体、地区或社会阶层说话时所特有的发音方式
senses.example: She spoke English with a slight French accent.
senses.exampleCN: 她说英语时带一点法国口音。
senses.why: Latin accentus first named the rise and fall of the voice, so the word began with how a voice sounds rather than with what it says.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accentus 最初指说话声音的高低起伏，所以这个词一开始说的是声音听起来怎样，而不是话说了什么。

senses.title: Stress on a syllable or word
senses.definition: the extra force or higher pitch given to one syllable of a word or one word in a sentence
senses.definitionCN: 给予某个音节或句子中某个词额外的力量或更高的音高
senses.example: In the noun record, the accent falls on the first syllable.
senses.exampleCN: 在名词 record 里，重音落在第一个音节上。
senses.why: The single tap of the voice can land on one syllable, and that louder point is the accent.
senses.whyCN: 声音的那一下敲击可以落在一个音节上，这个更响的点就是重音。

senses.title: To give emphasis to something
senses.definition: to emphasize a part of speech, a detail or a feature so that attention falls on it
senses.definitionCN: 强调言语中的某一部分、某个细节或特征，使注意力落在它上面
senses.example: The designer accented the doorway with a band of dark wood.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师用一条深色木质边框突出了门口。
senses.why: If the voice can stress one point, a hand can also stress one detail; the verb moves the same tap from sound to sight.
senses.whyCN: 既然声音能强调一个点，手也能强调一个细节；动词把同一下敲击从听觉移到了视觉。

senses.title: A strong beat in music
senses.definition: a beat or note played with more force than the beats around it
senses.definitionCN: 以比周围拍子更大的力量演奏的一拍或一个音
senses.example: The drummer placed a heavy accent on every third beat.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓手在每第三拍上打出一个重重的强音。
senses.why: Song is measured by beats, and a beat that is struck harder is literally a stress in the song.
senses.whyCN: 歌曲由拍子来衡量，敲得更重的那一拍正是歌曲里的一次重音。

senses.title: A distinctive quality or flavour
senses.definition: a small but distinct quality that gives something its particular character
senses.definitionCN: 给某物以独特性质的一种细小而分明的特点
senses.example: There was an accent of irony in his polite reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他礼貌的回答里带一点讽刺的味道。
senses.why: One feature made louder than the rest becomes the mark of a thing, just as one stressed syllable marks a word.
senses.whyCN: 一个被放大的特征会成为某物的标记，正如一个被重读的音节标记一个词。

senses.title: A written mark over a letter
senses.definition: a mark placed over a letter to show stress, vowel quality or pronunciation
senses.definitionCN: 标在字母上方，用以表示重音、元音性质或读音的记号
senses.example: The word cafe carries an acute accent on its final letter.
senses.exampleCN: 单词 cafe 的最后一个字母上带一个尖音符。
senses.why: Once the stress of the voice must be written down, the tap becomes a small mark on paper.
senses.whyCN: 当声音的重音必须被写下来时，那一下敲击就变成了纸上的一个小记号。

senses.title: A tone of voice that reveals feeling
senses.definition: the manner or tone of speech that shows the speaker's mood, attitude or origin
senses.definitionCN: 显示出说话者情绪、态度或来历的说话腔调
senses.example: He answered in an accent of mild surprise.
senses.exampleCN: 他用略带惊讶的语气回答。
senses.why: The same rise and fall that marks a region also marks a mood, so accent can name the colour of a voice at a given moment.
senses.whyCN: 标记地域的同一套高低起伏也标记情绪，于是 accent 可以指某一刻声音的色彩。

senses.title: A decorative detail that stands out
senses.definition: a small element of colour, texture or shape used to make a space or an outfit more interesting
senses.definitionCN: 用来让空间或衣着更有趣的细小颜色、质感或形状元素
senses.example: A single yellow chair was the accent in the grey room.
senses.exampleCN: 一把黄色椅子成了灰色房间里唯一的点缀。
senses.why: Attention is drawn by contrast, so one loud detail in a quiet room performs exactly the work of a spoken stress.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被对比吸引，因此安静房间里一个醒目的细节，起到的正是口语重音的作用。

intro.en: Accent reaches English through French, but its pieces are Latin: a prefix meaning to, and a noun meaning song.
intro.cn: accent 经法语进入英语，但它的构件来自拉丁语：一个表示「向」的前缀，和一个表示「歌」的名词。

items.en: The verb canere meant to sing, and it is the source of a wide family of song words in Latin.
items.cn: 动词 canere 意为「唱」，是拉丁语中一大群与歌唱有关的词的来源。

items.en: From canere came the noun cantus, a song or the act of singing; the form is well recorded in classical texts.
items.cn: 由 canere 生出名词 cantus，意为「歌、歌唱」；这一形式在古典文献中有明确记录。

items.en: Ad- meaning to plus cantus meaning song gave accentus, the modulation of the voice; Latin grammarians used it to render Greek prosodia.
items.cn: 表示「向」的 ad- 加表示「歌」的 cantus 构成 accentus，指声音的起伏；拉丁语法学家用它来翻译希腊语 prosodia。

items.en: Old French took the word as accent and kept both the vocal and the written senses.
items.cn: 古法语把这个词写作 accent，同时保留了语音与书写两方面的含义。

items.en: English later split the word into three practical branches: a regional pronunciation, a stress in speech or music, and a small mark or detail.
items.cn: 英语后来把这个词分成三条实用分支：地区发音、说话或音乐中的重音，以及小小的记号或细节。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same cantus family and one near-spelling from a different root; the near-meaning group gathers the speech and stress words it is often confused with.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 cantus 词族的词，以及一个拼写相近但词根不同的词；近义组收常与它混淆的发音与重音类词。

entries.definition: To make a feature or difference more noticeable, especially in speech, design or dress.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调、使突出」，多用于言语、设计或衣着，由本词加动词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Relating to accent or stress, especially in poetry that counts stresses rather than syllables.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「重音的」，常用于按重音而非音节计数的诗歌格律。

entries.definition: Spoken with a particular accent, or given extra force in speech or music.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「带口音的、重读的」，直接由本词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: The act of climbing up or rising; it is nearly spelled like accent but comes from Latin ascendere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上升、攀登」；只是拼写与 accent 相近，词源不同，出自拉丁语 ascendere。

entries.definition: The force given to a syllable or word; the technical term in linguistics, narrower than accent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「重音、重读」，是语言学中的技术术语，范围比 accent 更窄。

entries.definition: The way in which a word or language is spoken, including individual sounds rather than regional colour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「发音」，指词或语言的读法，关注单个音而非地域色彩。

entries.definition: A form of a language used in one region, covering grammar and vocabulary as well as sound.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「方言」，指某一地区使用的语言变体，除语音外还包括语法与词汇。

entries.definition: The rise and fall of the voice across a whole sentence, rather than the stress on one syllable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「语调」，指整句声音的高低起伏，而非单个音节的重读。

entries.definition: Special importance given to something in speech or writing, often by repetition or position.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「强调、重点」，指通过重复或位置等手段给予某事物特别的重要性。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin cantus root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 cantus 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Cantus is a song, so accent is the song-like rise and fall of a voice.
normal.cn: cantus 是「歌」，所以 accent 就是说话时像唱歌一样的高低起伏。

normal.en: Accentus is ad- plus cantus: a song added on top of the syllables.
normal.cn: accentus 是 ad- 加 cantus：在音节之上再加一段歌。

normal.en: The same root gives chant, a song still sung to a fixed pattern.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 chant，指按固定调子吟唱的歌。

normal.en: A written accent is only the mark that tells the reader where the voice must rise.
normal.cn: 书面上的重音符号，只是告诉读者声音该在哪里抬高的记号。

normal.en: In a room, an accent is one loud detail among quiet ones, the same stress moved from sound to sight.
normal.cn: 在房间里，accent 是安静之中一个醒目的细节，是同一次重音从听觉移到视觉。

abstract.en: Picture one finger tapping a table once: that single tap is the accent.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指在桌面上敲了一下：这一下就是 accent。

abstract.en: The tap can land on a syllable, a beat, a colour or a mood, and each landing is a different sense.
abstract.cn: 这一下可以落在音节、拍子、颜色或情绪上，落在哪里就长出哪个义项。

abstract.en: Accent is contrast rather than volume: a thing is heard because its neighbours are softer.
abstract.cn: accent 靠的是对比而不是音量：某样东西被听见，是因为它周围更轻。

examples.en: He speaks English with a strong Spanish accent.
examples.cn: 他说英语时带着浓重的西班牙口音。

examples.en: The accent in photograph falls on the first syllable.
examples.cn: photograph 的重音落在第一个音节上。

examples.en: The director accented the final scene with a single red lamp.
examples.cn: 导演用一盏红灯突出了最后一幕。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克森特」——开口一压，句子末尾敲一下：口音、重音

root: 拉丁语 accentus 由 ad-「向、附加」与 cantus「歌声」构成，是希腊语 prosodia「歌唱般的语调」的仿译；cantus 又来自动词 canere「唱」。因此这个词最初指说话声音的高低起伏，之后才分出口音、重音、强调与细节等义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accent all place one stress somewhere: on a region's speech, a syllable, a detail, a beat, a flavour, a written letter, a mood, or a decorated room.
sensesIntro.cn: accent 的八个义项都是把同一次「加重」放在某处：地域的说话方式、音节、细节、拍子、风味、书写的字母、情绪，或一间被点缀的房间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger taps the table once, making one point louder than the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指在桌面上敲了一下，让某一点比周围更响。

branches.en: THE VOICE: regional pronunciation and the tone that reveals a mood both come from how a voice sounds.
branches.cn: 声音线：地区发音与透露情绪的语调，都来自声音听起来的样子。

branches.en: THE STRESS: one syllable in speech and one beat in music are both made louder than their neighbours.
branches.cn: 重音线：言语中的一个音节与音乐中的一拍，都被做得比周围更响。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb accents a detail so that attention lands on it.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词指把某个细节加重，使注意力落在它上面。

branches.en: THE FLAVOUR: one amplified quality becomes the distinctive mark of a thing.
branches.cn: 风味线：一个被放大的特征成为某物的独特标记。

branches.en: THE MARKS: the stress can be written as a small sign or shown as one bright detail in a room.
branches.cn: 记号线：重音可以写成一个小符号，也可以表现为一处明亮的细节。

intro.en: Accent is a Latin noun of voice built on a prefix and a song root; English adds ordinary endings to make its family.
intro.cn: accent 是建立在拉丁语前缀与「歌」词根之上的名词；英语再用普通词尾扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin canere, cantus and accentus are all recorded, so nothing in the chain is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 canere、cantus 与 accentus 均有文献记录，这一链条上没有重构形式。

items.example: The prefix marks something added to a base.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记加在基础之上的东西。

items.example: The verb is the song root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「歌」词根。

items.example: The noun names the song itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指歌本身。

items.example: The noun joined the prefix and the song root.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把前缀与「歌」词根合在一起。

items.example: It forms accented.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accented。

items.example: It forms accentual.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accentual。

items.example: It forms accentuate.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accentuate。

items.example: It forms accentuation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accentuation。

latinEntries.structure: Latin noun from ad- plus cantus

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「带口音的；重读的」
由本词加 -ual 构成，义为「重音的」
由本词加 -uate 构成，义为「强调；使突出」
由 accentuate 加 -ation 构成，义为「强调；重读」

definition_zh: 接受；收下；同意；承认；承担；接纳；容忍
definition_en: to take something that is offered, or to agree to and take on what is proposed, required or true
core_image: 别人递来一件东西，你伸手把它接过来
scene: 招聘会散场后，年轻人攥着简历站在门口，面试官又把他叫了回去。He did not expect the firm to accept him after only one interview.
sceneCN: 这里 accept 是「接纳、录用」（第 6 个义项：接纳某人加入组织或团队）；句意为只面了一轮，他没料到公司会录用他。

pos.zh: 动词：接受；收下；同意；承认；承担
动词：同意；认可

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「接受；认可；接纳」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可接受的；合格的」
由本词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「公认的；被接受的」
由本词加施动后缀 -or 构成，义为「接受者；承兑人」

senses.title: To take something offered
senses.titleCN: 接过并收下别人的东西
senses.definition: to take hold of a thing that another person offers or hands over
senses.definitionCN: 把别人递来或提供的东西接过来收下
senses.example: He accepted the parcel and signed for it.
senses.exampleCN: 他收下包裹并签了字。
senses.why: Latin capere means to take, and ad- means to, so accipere is literally to take a thing towards oneself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capere 意为「拿取」，ad- 意为「向」，所以 accipere 字面上就是「把东西往自己这边拿」。

senses.title: To agree to an offer or invitation
senses.definition: to say yes to an offer, invitation or arrangement that has been put forward
senses.definitionCN: 对提出的提议、邀请或安排表示同意
senses.example: She accepted the invitation to speak at the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 她接受了在会议上发言的邀请。
senses.why: An offer is held out by another hand; saying yes is the act of taking it.
senses.whyCN: 提议由另一只手递出，答应就是把它接过来的动作。

senses.title: To admit that something is true
senses.definition: to agree that a fact, situation or fault is real, often unwillingly
senses.definitionCN: 承认某一事实、情况或过错真实存在，常带不情愿
senses.example: You must accept that the plan cannot be finished this week.
senses.exampleCN: 你必须承认这个计划本周完不成。
senses.why: A fact is something reality hands to you; refusing it means leaving it in mid-air, accepting means taking it.
senses.whyCN: 事实是现实递给你的东西；不认就是让它悬在半空，承认就是把它接住。

senses.title: To take on a duty or burden
senses.definition: to take responsibility for something, including its costs and consequences
senses.definitionCN: 对某事负起责任，包括其代价与后果
senses.example: The company accepted full responsibility for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对这次延误承担了全部责任。
senses.why: A duty is handed over like a heavy object, and taking it means carrying its weight.
senses.whyCN: 职责像一件重物被递过来，接住它就意味着要扛起它的重量。

senses.title: To approve or adopt an idea
senses.definition: to approve of an idea, method or proposal and allow it to be used
senses.definitionCN: 赞同某种想法、方法或方案，并允许它被采用
senses.example: The committee accepted the new safety rules without debate.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会未经辩论就采纳了新的安全规定。
senses.why: What a group takes into its hands becomes its own, so accepting an idea is adopting it.
senses.whyCN: 一个群体接过来的东西就成了自己的，所以接受一种想法也就是采纳它。

senses.title: To admit someone into a group
senses.definition: to allow a person to join a school, firm, team or other group
senses.definitionCN: 允许某人加入学校、公司、团队或其他群体
senses.example: The college accepted only thirty students that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那所学院当年只录取了三十名学生。
senses.why: The group holds out a place, and the person takes it; being accepted is being taken in.
senses.whyCN: 团体递出一个位置，个人把它接过；被录取就是被接了进来。

senses.title: To tolerate something unpleasant
senses.definition: to put up with an annoyance, criticism or difficult condition without protest
senses.definitionCN: 不加抗议地忍受烦扰、批评或困难处境
senses.example: She accepted the noise because the flat was cheap.
senses.exampleCN: 因为房租便宜，她忍受了那些噪音。
senses.why: Tolerating is taking an unpleasant thing and holding it rather than dropping it, which is the same grip under protest.
senses.whyCN: 容忍是把不愉快的东西接住并拿稳，而不是丢开；这是同一握持，只是心里并不情愿。

senses.title: To honour a bill of exchange
senses.definition: to agree formally to pay a bill of exchange or draft when it falls due
senses.definitionCN: 正式同意在汇票或票据到期时付款
senses.example: The bank accepted the draft on the exporter's behalf.
senses.exampleCN: 银行代表出口商承兑了这张汇票。
senses.why: Commerce makes the promise a piece of paper, and accepting it means taking on the obligation written there.
senses.whyCN: 商业把承诺变成一张纸，承兑就是接下纸上写明的付款义务。

intro.en: Accept keeps a Latin verb of taking behind a French surface, and the whole family stays close to the image of a hand receiving.
intro.cn: accept 表面是法语词形，背后是一个表示「拿取」的拉丁动词，整个词族都离不开伸手接收的画面。

items.en: The verb capere meant to take, seize or grasp, and it is one of the most productive roots in Latin.
items.cn: 动词 capere 意为「拿、抓、握」，是拉丁语中构词能力最强的词根之一。

items.en: Ad- meaning to plus capere gave accipere, to receive or take to oneself; the form is fully recorded.
items.cn: 表示「向」的 ad- 加 capere 构成 accipere，意为「接收、拿过来」；这一形式有完整记录。

items.en: A frequentative form acceptare meant to receive repeatedly or to accept favourably, and it is the closer model for the English verb.
items.cn: 反复动词形式 acceptare 意为「一再接收、乐意接受」，是英语动词更直接的模型。

items.en: Old French accepter carried the word into English usage with the senses of receiving and agreeing already joined.
items.cn: 古法语 accepter 把这个词带入英语，接收与同意两层意思当时已经并存。

items.en: The verb is recorded in English from the late fourteenth century; the exact first written date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在英语中的记录始于十四世纪后期；确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: The commercial sense of accepting a draft, and the noun acceptance, developed in later centuries.
items.cn: 承兑票据的商业义与名词 acceptance 都在更晚的几个世纪里发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same capere root plus one word that borrows the same ending from a different root; the near-meaning group gathers the verbs of receiving and agreeing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 capere 词根构成的词，以及一个借了相同词尾但词根不同的词；近义组收表示接收与同意的动词。

entries.definition: The act of receiving something offered, or the state of being approved and admitted.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受、认可、接纳」，由本词加名词后缀构成。

entries.definition: Good enough to be received or approved, though not necessarily excellent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可接受的、还算合格的」，由本词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: To leave something out or to exclude it; the ending looks the same but the prefix ex- means out, from excipere.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或动词，义为「除……之外、把……排除」，词尾与 accept 相同，但前缀 ex- 表示「向外」，出自 excipere，词源方向相反。

entries.definition: One who accepts, especially a person or bank that accepts a bill of exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「接受者、承兑人」，由本词加施动后缀 -or 构成。

entries.definition: To get something that is given or sent, with less emphasis on agreeing to it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「收到、接到」，强调拿到手，而不强调是否同意。

entries.definition: To agree that something is true, often against one's will; close to the third sense of accept.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认」，常含不情愿，接近 accept 的第 3 个义项。

entries.definition: To have or express the same opinion; it names the mental side without the image of taking.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同意、意见一致」，只讲心理层面，没有「接过来」的画面。

entries.definition: To state that one has noticed or received something, used for facts, letters and greetings.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承认、确认收到」，语气正式，多用于事实、来信与问候。

entries.definition: To accept an idea or change eagerly and make it part of oneself; warmer than accept.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「欣然接受、拥抱」，比 accept 更热情，含主动接纳之意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin capere root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 capere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Capere is to take: accept is ad- plus take, taking what is held out to you.
normal.cn: capere 是「拿」：accept 就是 ad- 加「拿」，把递到面前的东西接过来。

normal.en: The same root gives capture and captive, both about seizing something.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 capture 与 captive，都与抓住有关。

normal.en: To accept a challenge is to take hold of it instead of running from it.
normal.cn: accept a challenge 是把它接住，而不是躲开。

normal.en: Acceptance adds -ance, naming the act of taking something in.
normal.cn: acceptance 加 -ance，指把东西接进来这一行为。

normal.en: Except reverses the direction: ex- means out, so it takes something away from the group.
normal.cn: except 把方向反过来：ex- 表示「向外」，于是它把某物从群体中拿出去。

abstract.en: Picture one hand reaching out and closing around what another hand offers.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸出去，把另一只手递来的东西握住。

abstract.en: What is handed over can be a gift, an offer, a fact, a duty, a person or a promise on paper.
abstract.cn: 递过来的可以是礼物、提议、事实、职责、一个人，或纸面上的承诺。

abstract.en: Accept is the instant when the two hands close on the same object.
abstract.cn: accept 就是两只手在同一件东西上合拢的那一瞬。

examples.en: She accepted the job offer without hesitation.
examples.cn: 她毫不犹豫地接受了这份工作。

examples.en: The company accepted full responsibility for the delay.
examples.cn: 公司对这次延误承担了全部责任。

examples.en: His theory is now widely accepted by researchers.
examples.cn: 他的理论如今已被研究人员广泛接受。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞普特」——别人递来，伸手一接就揣进兜里：接受

root: 拉丁语 accipere 由 ad-「向」与 capere「拿取、抓住」构成，意为「接收」；其反复动词形式 acceptare 是英语 accept 更直接的来源。capere 还生出 capture、captive 等词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accept all describe one hand closing on something handed over: an object, an offer, a fact, a duty, an idea, a person, an annoyance, or a bill.
sensesIntro.cn: accept 的八个义项都在描述同一只手握住所递来的东西：实物、提议、事实、职责、想法、一个人、一桩烦扰，或一张票据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand reaches out and closes on what another hand offers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸出去，把另一只手递来的东西握住。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a parcel or gift is physically taken from the hand that holds it out.
branches.cn: 实物线：包裹或礼物从递出它的那只手上被实际接过来。

branches.en: THE AGREEMENT: an offer or an idea is taken up and made one's own.
branches.cn: 同意线：提议或想法被接过来，成为自己的东西。

branches.en: THE INNER GRIP: a fact is held as true, and an annoyance is held without protest.
branches.cn: 内心线：事实被当作真的握住，烦扰被不声不响地拿住。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: a duty is taken on and carried, cost included.
branches.cn: 重量线：职责被接下并扛起，连同代价一起。

branches.en: THE ADMISSION: a person is taken into a group, and a paper promise is taken into an obligation.
branches.cn: 接纳线：人被接进团体，纸上的承诺被接成义务。

intro.en: Accept is a Latin verb of taking with a French ending; English adds ordinary suffixes to build its family.
intro.cn: accept 是一个带法语词尾的拉丁语「拿取」动词；英语用普通后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere, accipere and acceptare are all recorded, so no form in this chain is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere、accipere 与 acceptare 均有文献记录，这一链条上没有重构形式。

items.example: The prefix turns taking into taking towards oneself.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「拿」变成「往自己这边拿」。

items.example: The verb is the taking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「拿取」词根。

items.example: The compound joins the prefix to the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把前缀与词根合在一起。

items.example: The frequentative form is the closest model for English.
items.exampleCN: 这个反复动词形式是英语最直接的模型。

items.example: It forms acceptance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acceptance。

items.example: It forms acceptable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acceptable。

items.example: It forms accepted.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accepted。

items.example: It forms acceptor.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 acceptor。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- plus capere

latinEntries.meaning: to try to catch, grasp at

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ance 构成，义为「接受；认可」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「可接受的」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「公认的」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「接受者；承兑人」

definition_zh: 通道；入口；接近的机会；使用权；访问；进入；获取
definition_en: a way of entering a place, or the right and ability to reach, use or obtain something
core_image: 一扇窄门被推开，里面的一切忽然可以走进去
scene: 老图书馆的侧门常年上锁，管理员今天把钥匙交给了新来的整理员。Only staff with a special card have access to the closed stacks.
sceneCN: 这里 access 是「进入权、使用权」（第 2 个义项：被允许接近或使用某处的权利）；句意为只有持特别证件的员工才能进入闭架书库。

pos.zh: 名词：通道；入口；接近的机会；使用权
动词：进入；获取；访问

collocations.zh: 通往……的通道；对……的使用权
获得进入或使用的机会

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可到达的；可使用的；易懂的」
由 accessible 加名词后缀 -ibility 构成，义为「可达性；可及性；无障碍程度」
由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「就职；加入；新增藏品」

senses.title: A way in or a passage
senses.definition: a door, path, opening or route by which a place can be entered
senses.definitionCN: 可以进入某处的门、小路、开口或路线
senses.example: The only access to the village is a narrow bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 通往村子的唯一通道是一座窄桥。
senses.why: Latin accessus named a coming near; the first thing that makes coming near possible is a physical way in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accessus 指「走近」，而让走近成为可能的头一件事，就是一实体通道。

senses.title: The right or chance to approach
senses.titleCN: 接近或进入的权利与机会
senses.definition: the permission or opportunity to reach a person, place or thing that is otherwise closed
senses.definitionCN: 获准或有机会接近本来封闭的人、地方或事物
senses.example: Reporters were refused access to the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 记者被拒绝进入会场。
senses.why: If a way in exists, someone must still be allowed to walk through it, and that permission is the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 通道存在之后，还得有人被允许走进去，这份许可就是第二个义项。

senses.title: The use of a service or resource
senses.titleCN: 对服务或资源的使用权
senses.definition: the ability to use a service, resource or institution such as education or health care
senses.definitionCN: 使用某项服务、资源或机构的机会，如教育或医疗
senses.example: Every child should have access to free schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 每个孩子都应享有免费教育的机会。
senses.why: Education is a room with a door; access means being able to go in and use what is inside.
senses.whyCN: 教育像一间有门的屋子，access 指能够走进去并使用里面的东西。

senses.title: Permission to use a computer system
senses.titleCN: 计算机系统的访问权限
senses.definition: the right granted to a user to open, read or change files and systems on a computer
senses.definitionCN: 授予用户在计算机上打开、读取或修改文件与系统的权利
senses.example: The technician was given access to the server room.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员获得了进入服务器机房的权限。
senses.why: Digital space repeats the old image: there is a locked room, a key, and someone allowed through the door.
senses.whyCN: 数字空间重复了旧的画面：有一间上锁的屋子、一把钥匙，以及一个被允许进门的人。

senses.title: To reach or enter a place
senses.definition: to reach, enter or get into a place, especially through a narrow or controlled way
senses.definitionCN: 进入或到达某地，尤指经由狭窄或受管控的通道
senses.example: The rescue team accessed the mine through a side tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 救援队通过一条侧面的坑道进入矿井。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: to access is to make the approach that the noun describes.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：access 就是做出名词所描述的那次接近。

senses.title: To retrieve stored information
senses.titleCN: 读取或获取存储的信息
senses.definition: to retrieve data, files or records that are stored somewhere and bring them into use
senses.definitionCN: 从某处取回已经存储的数据、文件或记录并加以使用
senses.example: She accessed the old records from the archive.
senses.exampleCN: 她从档案库中调出了那些旧记录。
senses.why: Storing is placing something behind a door; accessing is opening that door and taking it out again.
senses.whyCN: 存储是把东西放进门后，读取就是打开那扇门并把它再取出来。

senses.title: To open a website or system
senses.definition: to connect to a website, network or online service and view or use its content
senses.definitionCN: 连接到网站、网络或在线服务并查看或使用其内容
senses.example: Millions of users access the site every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 每天早晨有数百万用户访问这个网站。
senses.why: The internet is the modern building with many doors, and each visit is a small act of going in.
senses.whyCN: 互联网就是那座有许多门的现代建筑，每一次访问都是一次小小的走进去。

senses.title: An outburst of emotion, an old use
senses.titleCN: 情绪的一阵发作（旧用法）
senses.definition: in older writing, a sudden fit or outburst of an emotion or illness
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文献中，指情绪或疾病突然的一阵发作
senses.example: He was seized by an access of anger he could not explain.
senses.exampleCN: 他忽然被一阵莫名的怒火攫住。
senses.why: The word once meant an approach or arrival, and a fit of feeling was pictured as something that comes over a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词早先表示「临近、到来」，一阵情绪发作被想象成某种逼近并罩住人的东西。

intro.en: Access rests on a Latin verb meaning to go, with a prefix of direction, so the word began as a coming towards something.
intro.cn: access 建立在一个表示「走」的拉丁动词上，加方向前缀，因此最初的意思是「走近某物」。

items.en: The verb cedere meant to go, move or yield, and its past stem cess- appears in many English words.
items.cn: 动词 cedere 意为「走、移动、让出」，其过去分词词干 cess- 出现在许多英语词中。

items.en: Ad- meaning to plus cedere gave accedere, to go towards, to approach or to be added to.
items.cn: 表示「向」的 ad- 加 cedere 构成 accedere，意为「走向、接近、附加于」。

items.en: The noun accessus named a coming near, an approach, and also a means of approaching.
items.cn: 名词 accessus 指「走近、接近」，也指接近的手段。

items.en: English borrowed the noun through French in the fourteenth century, and the French form already carried the idea of a way in.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经由法语借入这个名词，当时法语形式已带有「进入之道」的意思。

items.en: The right-to-use sense grew in the twentieth century, and the computing verb appeared with the spread of stored data.
items.cn: 「使用权」义在二十世纪扩展，计算机动词义则随存储数据的普及而出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same cedere family and one near-spelling built on a rival prefix; the near-meaning group gathers words for ways in and rights of entry.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 cedere 词族的词，以及一个由相反前缀构成的近形词；近义组收表示通道与进入权利的词。

entries.definition: Able to be reached, entered or understood; formed directly from access plus -ible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的、可进入的、易懂的」，由 access 加 -ible 直接构成。

entries.definition: The act of taking office, or a thing added to a collection; it shares the root accedere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「就职、加入、新增藏品」，与 access 同出 accedere 词根。

entries.definition: An extra item added to something else; it comes from the same approach root but shifted to mean an addition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「配件、附属品」，同出「接近、附加」的词根，语义偏向「附加之物」。

entries.definition: An amount beyond what is needed; it uses ex- meaning out with the same cedere verb, so the direction is opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「过量、超出的部分」，由表示「向外」的 ex- 加同一 cedere 构成，方向与 access 相反。

entries.definition: The act of coming in, or a place through which one comes in; plainer than access.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入口」，比 access 更朴素直接。

entries.definition: A door or gate by which one enters a building; the physical opening rather than the right.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入口、大门」，指实体的开口，而不是权利。

entries.definition: Permission to enter a place or join an organization, often after a check.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「准许进入、入学许可」，常含经过审核的意味。

entries.definition: The act of moving nearer to something; the literal meaning behind the root of access.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「接近、靠近」，正是 access 词根的字面含义。

entries.definition: Formal permission to enter a building or place, often printed on a sign.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「入场许可」，语气正式，常见于告示牌上。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin cedere root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 cedere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Cedere is to go: access is ad- plus go, a going towards something.
normal.cn: cedere 是「走」：access 就是 ad- 加「走」，朝某物走过去。

normal.en: The same cedere root gives procession and proceed, all about going forward.
normal.cn: 同一 cedere 词根给出 procession 与 proceed，都与向前走有关。

normal.en: Access to is the fixed phrase for the right to enter or use something.
normal.cn: access to 是表示「进入权或使用权」的固定搭配。

normal.en: A password is the modern key that gives access to a system.
normal.cn: 密码就是现代版本的钥匙，用它才能访问系统。

normal.en: Excess uses ex- meaning out, so it names what goes beyond the allowed amount.
normal.cn: excess 用表示「向外」的 ex-，指超出允许额度的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow side door that is suddenly unlocked and pushed open.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇狭窄的侧门忽然被打开锁，又被推开。

abstract.en: Behind the door can be a village, a service, a file or a website; the door is the same idea each time.
abstract.cn: 门后可以是村庄、服务、文件或网站；每次都是同一种「门」的念头。

abstract.en: Access is not the room itself but the ability to walk in and use what is there.
abstract.cn: access 不是屋子本身，而是能够走进去并使用里面东西的那份能力。

examples.en: Students need a card to gain access to the library.
examples.cn: 学生需要一张卡才能进入图书馆。

examples.en: The files can be accessed from any computer on the network.
examples.cn: 在网络上的任何一台电脑都能读取这些文件。

examples.en: The path gives access to the beach only at low tide.
examples.cn: 这条小路只在退潮时才能通往海滩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞斯」——门禁一刷，门就开了：通道、进入

root: 拉丁语 accessus「接近、进入」由 ad-「向」与 cedere「走、让出」构成；cedere 的过去分词词干 cess- 还出现在 process、excess、success 等词里。更早的印欧来源存疑，一般只追溯到拉丁语这一层。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of access all describe a way through a closed boundary: an opening, a permission, a service, a system, an act of entering, a stored record, an online visit, and an old fit of feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: access 的八个义项都在描述穿过一道封闭边界的通道：开口、许可、服务、系统、进入的动作、存档的记录、网上的访问，以及旧用法里的一阵发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow side door is unlocked and pushed open.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇狭窄的侧门被打开锁并推开。

branches.en: THE OPENING: a physical door, bridge or path makes approach possible.
branches.cn: 开口线：实体的门、桥或小路让接近成为可能。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: permission turns an opening into a usable service or institution.
branches.cn: 权利线：许可把一处开口变成可以使用服务或机构的机会。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a locked digital room repeats the door and key.
branches.cn: 系统线：上锁的数字房间重复了门与钥匙的关系。

branches.en: THE ACT: entering a place and visiting a site are two forms of going in.
branches.cn: 动作线：走进某地与访问某网站，都是「走进去」的两种形式。

branches.en: THE STORE: data is fetched from behind a door, while an old sense names a feeling that comes over a person.
branches.cn: 储藏线：数据从门后被取出，旧义则指某种逼近并罩住人的情绪。

intro.en: Access is a Latin noun of approach; English later turned it into a verb and built the adjective with -ible.
intro.cn: access 是表示「接近」的拉丁名词；英语后来把它变成动词，并用 -ible 造出形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cedere, accedere and accessus are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European layer is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cedere、accedere 与 accessus 均有记录，只有更早的印欧语层次存疑。

items.example: The prefix directs the motion towards a goal.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向某个目标。

items.example: The verb supplies the motion in the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供词中的「移动」义。

items.example: The compound means going towards something.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词意为朝某物走去。

items.meaning: a coming near, a means of approach
items.example: The noun is the direct source of access.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 access 的直接来源。

items.example: It forms accessible.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accessible。

items.example: It forms accessibility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accessibility。

items.example: It forms accession.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accession。

items.example: It forms excess with the same cedere root.
items.exampleCN: 它与同一 cedere 词根构成 excess。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from ad- plus cedere

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ible 构成，义为「可到达的；易懂的」
由 accessible 加 -ibility 构成，义为「可达性；可及性」
由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「就职；加入；新增藏品」

definition_zh: 可到达的；可进入的；可得到的；易懂的；平易近人的；无障碍的
definition_en: able to be reached, entered, obtained or understood without great difficulty or special barriers
core_image: 一扇没有门槛的门，谁都能推门进去
scene: 山脚的小博物馆没有台阶，只有一条缓缓上坡的木道。The new ramp made the gallery accessible to visitors in wheelchairs.
sceneCN: 这里 accessible 是「无障碍可进入的」（第 6 个义项：供行动不便者使用的）；句意为新修的坡道让坐轮椅的参观者也能进入展厅。

pos.zh: 形容词：可到达的；可进入的；可得到的；易懂的

collocations.zh: 容易到达的；容易获取的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ibility 构成，义为「可达性；可及性；无障碍程度」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可理解地；易于接近地」
由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成，义为「难以到达的；难懂的」
由本词去掉后缀 -ible 得到的基础词，义为「通道；使用权」

senses.title: Reachable by a route
senses.definition: able to be reached, especially after some travel, by a path, road or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 尤指经过一段路程后，能够通过小路、道路或交通工具到达
senses.example: The village is accessible only by boat.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子只能坐船到达。
senses.why: The base word access is a door one may go through, and -ible adds the idea that the door can in fact be passed.
senses.whyCN: 基础词 access 是一扇人可穿过的门，-ible 加上「这门确实能被穿过」的意思。

senses.title: Entered without obstruction
senses.definition: able to be entered or used without a physical obstacle blocking the way
senses.definitionCN: 没有实体障碍挡住通道，因而能够进入或使用
senses.example: The side entrance is accessible through the garden gate.
senses.exampleCN: 侧门可以穿过花园的小门进去。
senses.why: A way in may exist yet be blocked; accessible says the way is clear enough to use.
senses.whyCN: 通道可能存在却被堵住；accessible 说的是这条路通畅到足以使用。

senses.title: Obtainable or affordable
senses.definition: able to be obtained or bought by ordinary people at a reasonable cost
senses.definitionCN: 普通人以合理代价就能获得或买到
senses.example: The clinic offers accessible care to local families.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为当地家庭提供负担得起的医疗服务。
senses.why: A door with a very high fee is still closed in practice, so accessible extends from reaching to affording.
senses.whyCN: 收费极高的门实际上仍是关着的，于是 accessible 从「够得着」延伸到「付得起」。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: written or explained in a way that ordinary readers can follow without special knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 以普通读者无需专门知识便能读懂的写法表达
senses.example: Her book on physics is surprisingly accessible.
senses.exampleCN: 她那本讲物理的书出人意料地好懂。
senses.why: Understanding is a room too; accessible means the reader is not stopped at the door by jargon.
senses.whyCN: 理解也是一间屋子；accessible 指读者没有被术语挡在门口。

senses.title: Approachable in manner
senses.definition: friendly and easy to talk to, especially for someone in a position of authority
senses.definitionCN: 友善而容易交谈，尤指地位较高的人
senses.example: The new director is accessible to every member of staff.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管对每位员工都很平易近人。
senses.why: A person can also have a door, and accessible says that door stands open to others.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以有一扇门，accessible 说这扇门对别人是敞开的。

senses.title: Usable by people with disabilities
senses.definition: designed so that people with physical disabilities can enter and use it, as by ramps or lifts
senses.definitionCN: 经过设计，使身体有障碍的人也能进入和使用，如借助坡道或电梯
senses.example: All new stations must be accessible to wheelchair users.
senses.exampleCN: 所有新建车站都必须让轮椅使用者可以使用。
senses.why: The older image of a step at the door sharpens here: accessible means the step has been removed.
senses.whyCN: 门口那道台阶的旧画面在这里变得具体：accessible 意味着台阶被去掉了。

senses.title: Reachable on a computer network
senses.definition: available to be opened or reached through a computer, phone or network
senses.definitionCN: 能够通过计算机、手机或网络打开与到达
senses.example: The database is accessible from any campus terminal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个数据库在任何校园终端上都能访问。
senses.why: Digital space keeps the door, only now the door is a login screen that either opens or refuses.
senses.whyCN: 数字空间仍保留那扇门，只是门变成了登录界面，要么打开，要么拒绝。

senses.title: Available to those who need it
senses.definition: offered to everyone who needs it, without hidden conditions or exclusion
senses.definitionCN: 向所有需要的人提供，没有隐藏条件或排斥
senses.example: Legal advice should be accessible to people on low incomes.
senses.exampleCN: 低收入者也应当能够得到法律咨询。
senses.why: An open door is of little use if only some are told where it is, so the word also covers fair availability.
senses.whyCN: 一扇敞开的门若只告诉少数人位置，就没什么用，因此这个词也涵盖「公平可及」。

intro.en: Accessible is a Latin-derived adjective built directly on the English noun access, with a suffix that means able to be.
intro.cn: accessible 是直接建立在英语名词 access 之上的拉丁系形容词，后缀意为「可以被……」。

items.en: The verb accedere, ad- plus cedere, meant to go towards and to approach.
items.cn: 动词 accedere 由 ad- 加 cedere 构成，意为「走向、接近」。

items.en: Its noun accessus named a coming near and, by extension, a means of entering.
items.cn: 其名词 accessus 指「接近」，引申为「进入的手段」。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed accessibilis with the suffix -ibilis, meaning able to be approached; the word is recorded in later Latin.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用后缀 -ibilis 构成 accessibilis，意为「可以被接近的」；该词在后期拉丁文献中有记录。

items.en: English accessible is recorded from the early seventeenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 accessible 自十七世纪早期有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense of easy to understand dates from the nineteenth century, and the disability sense became standard in the twentieth.
items.cn: 「易懂」义见于十九世纪；与残障人士相关的无障碍义在二十世纪成为通行用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the access family and its negated form; the near-meaning group gathers words about being within reach or within budget.
note.cn: 形近组收 access 词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示「够得着」与「付得起」的词。

entries.definition: The noun or verb for a way in and the right to enter; the base word behind accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「通道、进入权、访问」，是 accessible 的基础词。

entries.definition: The quality of being reachable, usable or understandable, especially for disabled people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可达性、可及性、无障碍程度」，由本词加 -ibility 构成。

entries.definition: Impossible or very difficult to reach, enter or understand; the negative of accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以到达的、难懂的」，是 accessible 加否定前缀 in- 的形式。

entries.definition: In a way that can be reached or understood easily; formed with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「可理解地、易于接近地」，由本词加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Able to be used or obtained because it is free or in stock, without reference to distance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可用的、可获得的」，强调未被占用或有现货，不涉及距离。

entries.definition: Able to be arrived at or contacted; it stresses distance rather than permission.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可到达的、可联系上的」，强调距离而非许可。

entries.definition: Friendly and willing to talk; used only of people, matching the fifth sense of accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平易近人的」，只用于人，对应 accessible 的第 5 个义项。

entries.definition: Cheap enough for ordinary people to pay for, matching the cost side of accessible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负担得起的」，对应 accessible 中与价格相关的一面。

entries.definition: Able to be got or acquired, especially after some effort, with no sense of a barrier being removed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可获得的」，强调经过努力取得，不含「障碍被清除」的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real access root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 access 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Access is a door one may go through, and -ible says the door can indeed be passed.
normal.cn: access 是一扇可以穿过的门，-ible 表示这扇门确实能被穿过。

normal.en: The same root gives accession and accessory, all about coming near or being added.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 accession 与 accessory，都与接近或附加有关。

normal.en: Accessible to the public is the phrase used of buildings and services open to all.
normal.cn: accessible to the public 是用于「向所有人开放」的建筑与服务的固定说法。

normal.en: In accessibility, the -ibility ending turns the adjective into the name of the quality.
normal.cn: 在 accessibility 里，-ibility 把形容词变成这种性质本身的名称。

normal.en: Inaccessible adds in-, so the door is there but nobody can get through it.
normal.cn: inaccessible 加上 in-，门虽然还在，却没有人能过得去。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway with the raised step removed, so a wheel can roll straight through.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门口被去掉了那道抬高的台阶，轮子可以直接滚进去。

abstract.en: The same open doorway serves a village, a book, a price, a person and a website.
abstract.cn: 同一个敞开的门口，可以服务一个村庄、一本书、一个价格、一个人和一个网站。

abstract.en: Accessible is always a statement about the one who comes in, not about the room behind the door.
abstract.cn: accessible 说的始终是「进来的人」，而不是门后的那间屋子。

examples.en: The village is accessible only by boat.
examples.cn: 这个村子只能坐船到达。

examples.en: Her writing is accessible to readers without a science background.
examples.cn: 她的文字对没有科学背景的读者也很好懂。

examples.en: The museum made its collection accessible online.
examples.cn: 博物馆让公众可以在网上访问其藏品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克塞瑟波」——门一开，谁都能进：可进入的、易懂的

root: accessible 由名词 access「通道、接近」直接加拉丁形容词后缀 -ible「可以被……」构成；access 出自拉丁语 accessus，而 accessus 又由 ad-「向」与 cedere「走」构成。它与 access 的关系是「基础词 + 后缀」，不是同一个词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accessible all say that some door can be passed: by a route, by a body, by a wallet, by a reader, by a stranger, by a wheelchair, by a browser, or by anyone in need.
sensesIntro.cn: accessible 的八个义项都在说某一扇门可以通过：靠路线、靠身体、靠钱包、靠读者、靠陌生人、靠轮椅、靠浏览器，或靠每一个需要它的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doorway with no raised step, so anyone can go straight in.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个没有台阶的门口，任何人都能直接走进去。

branches.en: THE ROUTE: a place or building can be reached and entered without obstruction.
branches.cn: 路线线：某地或某建筑可以不受阻碍地到达并进入。

branches.en: THE PURSE: a service or resource is obtainable by ordinary people who need it.
branches.cn: 钱包线：服务或资源是普通需要者能够获得的。

branches.en: THE TEXT: a reader is not stopped at the door by difficult language.
branches.cn: 文本线：读者不会被难懂的语言挡在门外。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a friendly manner keeps the door open to strangers.
branches.cn: 人物线：友善的态度让门对陌生人保持敞开。

branches.en: THE BARRIER: ramps serve the body, and logins serve the network.
branches.cn: 障碍线：坡道服务于身体，登录界面服务于网络。

intro.en: Accessible is a base noun of approach plus a Latin suffix meaning able to be; the suffix carries most of the adjective's meaning.
intro.cn: accessible 是表示「接近」的基础名词加一个意为「可以被……」的拉丁后缀；形容词的主要含义来自这个后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin accedere and accessus are recorded, and medieval Latin accessibilis is attested; the deeper Indo-European root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 accedere 与 accessus 均有记录，中世纪拉丁语 accessibilis 也见于文献；更早的印欧词根存疑。

items.example: The prefix points the motion at a goal.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向某个目标。

items.example: The verb supplies the motion inside access.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 access 中的「走」义。

items.meaning: a coming near, a way of approach
items.example: The noun is the base of the English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语这一词族的基础。

items.example: It forms accessible from access.
items.exampleCN: 它使 access 构成 accessible。

items.example: It forms accessibility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accessibility。

items.example: It forms accessibly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accessibly。

items.example: It forms inaccessible.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 inaccessible。

items.meaning: a way in, the right to enter
items.example: The base word carries the door image.
items.exampleCN: 基础词带着那扇门的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ibility 构成，义为「可达性；无障碍程度」
由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「可理解地」
由否定前缀 in- 加本词构成，义为「难以到达的」
由本词去掉 -ible 得到的基础词，义为「通道；使用权」

definition_zh: 事故；意外事件；偶然；意外；机缘
definition_en: an unexpected event that causes damage or injury, or the mere fact of something happening by chance
core_image: 脚下忽然被绊住，整个人不由自主地向前扑倒
scene: 雨后的石板路很滑，送报少年拐过街角时，车轮突然打横。A passing car clipped his bicycle, and the accident left him with a broken wrist.
sceneCN: 这里 accident 是「事故、意外伤害事件」（第 1 个义项：造成人身损伤的突发事故）；句意为一辆驶过的汽车剐到他的自行车，这场事故让他手腕骨折。

pos.zh: 名词：事故；意外事件；偶然；机缘

collocations.zh: 急诊部（英国医院的叫法）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「意外的；偶然的」
由 accidental 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「意外地；偶然地」
由本词加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「词形变化；语法初阶」，语义已明显偏移

senses.title: An event that causes injury or damage
senses.titleCN: 造成伤亡或损坏的事故
senses.definition: a sudden event, such as a crash, that causes injury to people or damage to things
senses.definitionCN: 诸如碰撞之类突然发生、造成人身伤害或财物损坏的事件
senses.example: The accident at the crossroads blocked the road for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 十字路口的那场事故把路堵了好几个小时。
senses.why: Latin accidere meant to fall upon a person; the first sense is exactly something that falls on you unasked.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accidere 意为「落到某人身上」；第一个义项正是某件未经请求就落到你头上的事。

senses.title: An unfortunate unexpected event
senses.definition: an unexpected event that is unwelcome, even when no great damage is involved
senses.definitionCN: 不受欢迎的意外事件，即使并未造成重大损失
senses.example: Losing the keys was a small accident that ruined the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 丢钥匙这件小事把整个晚上都毁了。
senses.why: The falling event does not have to be a crash; any unwelcome surprise that lands on a day belongs here.
senses.whyCN: 落下来的事件不一定非是撞车；任何落在一天里的不受欢迎的意外都归入这个义项。

senses.title: By chance rather than by plan
senses.definition: in the phrase by accident, happening without intention or design
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 by accident，表示没有意图或计划地发生
senses.example: I opened the wrong door by accident.
senses.exampleCN: 我无意中开错了门。
senses.why: If something falls on you, no plan put it there; the phrase keeps that sense of an unplanned landing.
senses.whyCN: 如果东西落到你头上，并没有计划把它放在那里；这个短语保留了「未被安排的落下」之意。

senses.title: A mishap at work or in industry
senses.definition: an unexpected damaging event at a workplace, factory or construction site
senses.definitionCN: 在工作场所、工厂或建筑工地上发生的意外损害事件
senses.example: The factory reported three accidents in one month.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂一个月内报告了三起工伤事故。
senses.why: The general fall becomes specific when it happens on a shop floor, where rules try to prevent it.
senses.whyCN: 当这个「落下」发生在有规章试图防范的车间里，泛指的意外就具体化为工伤事故。

senses.title: A chance circumstance of history
senses.definition: in phrases such as an accident of history, a circumstance that came about by chance rather than design
senses.definitionCN: 用于 an accident of history 一类短语，指出于偶然而非设计形成的条件
senses.example: The border follows an accident of history, not a natural line.
senses.exampleCN: 这条边界是历史偶然造成的，并不是天然的分界。
senses.why: History is pictured as a place where things fall; a circumstance nobody planned is a thing that happened to fall.
senses.whyCN: 历史被想象成一个不断有东西落下的场所；无人计划的条件就是碰巧落下的东西。

senses.title: Accidental damage in insurance
senses.definition: in insurance, damage caused by an unexpected event rather than by wear or deliberate action
senses.definitionCN: 在保险中，由意外事件而非磨损或故意行为造成的损坏
senses.example: The policy covers accidental damage to the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单承保厨房的意外损坏。
senses.why: Insurance must separate what falls on a house from what the owner does to it, so accident becomes a technical category.
senses.whyCN: 保险必须区分「落到房子上的事」与「房主自己做的事」，于是 accident 成了技术类别。

senses.title: An irregularity in the ground
senses.definition: in technical writing, a slight irregularity in the surface of land
senses.definitionCN: 在技术文献中，指地面上一处轻微的不平整
senses.example: The surveyor marked every accident in the slope on the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 测量员在地形图上标出了坡面上每一处起伏。
senses.why: In Latin an accidens was a quality that happened to a thing; in surveying it became a small feature that happens to the ground.
senses.whyCN: 在拉丁语里 accidens 指「附着于事物的性质」；到了测量学，它就成了地面上碰巧存在的小起伏。

senses.title: A fortunate coincidence
senses.definition: an unexpected coincidence that turns out well, often called a happy accident
senses.definitionCN: 结果良好的意外巧合，常说成 a happy accident
senses.example: The two inventors met by a happy accident at the fair.
senses.exampleCN: 两位发明家在展会上幸运地偶遇。
senses.why: The same fall can land kindly: a chance meeting that helps is still a thing nobody planned.
senses.whyCN: 同一次落下也可以落得和善：一场带来帮助的偶遇，仍然是无人计划而成的事。

intro.en: Accident is built from a Latin verb for falling, and every sense still keeps the image of something landing on a person.
intro.cn: accident 建立在一个表示「落下」的拉丁动词上，每个义项都保留着「某物落到人身上」的画面。

items.en: The verb cadere meant to fall, and it is one of the oldest recorded roots in the Latin verb system.
items.cn: 动词 cadere 意为「落下」，是拉丁语动词系统中最古老、记录最完整的词根之一。

items.en: Ad- meaning to plus cadere gave accidere, to fall upon or to happen to someone.
items.cn: 表示「向」的 ad- 加 cadere 构成 accidere，意为「落到……上、发生于某人身上」。

items.en: Its present participle accidens named something that happens or a quality that attaches to a thing; this is the direct model.
items.cn: 其现在分词 accidens 指「发生的事」或「附着于某物的性质」，是英语词更直接的模型。

items.en: Old French accident carried the word into English with the sense of an unexpected happening.
items.cn: 古法语 accident 把这个词带入英语，义为「意外发生的事」。

items.en: The narrow sense of a damaging crash hardened in the nineteenth century, when machines and traffic made such falls common.
items.cn: 「造成损伤的碰撞」这一窄义在十九世纪固定下来，当时机器与交通使这类意外变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same cadere family and one near-spelling from a different prefix; the near-meaning group gathers words for crashes, bad luck and chance.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 cadere 词族的词，以及一个由不同前缀构成的近形词；近义组收表示碰撞、厄运与偶然的词。

entries.definition: Happening by chance or without intention; formed from accident plus -al.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「意外的、偶然的」，由 accident 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that is not planned; formed from accidental plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「意外地、偶然地」，由 accidental 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: An event, often an unpleasant one; it looks close to accident but comes from incidere, to fall into.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件、事变」，常指不愉快的事；与 accident 拼写相近，但出自 incidere「落入」，词源前缀不同。

entries.definition: The part of grammar dealing with word forms; it comes from the same Latin participle but drifted far in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「词形变化、语法初阶」，同出拉丁语分词，但语义已大幅偏移。

entries.definition: A violent collision of vehicles or objects; narrower and louder than accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「撞车、碰撞」，比 accident 更窄、更强调撞击的猛烈。

entries.definition: A small accident or unlucky event with little serious damage.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小意外、不幸的小事」，损失通常不严重。

entries.definition: Bad luck or an unlucky event, with no image of physical collision.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「厄运、不幸」，不带实体碰撞的画面。

entries.definition: The way things happen without a plan; the abstract idea behind by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「偶然、机会」，是 by accident 背后的抽象概念。

entries.definition: A person killed or injured in an accident or war, or the loss itself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「死伤者、伤亡」，指事故或战争中伤亡的人或损失。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin cadere root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 cadere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Cadere is to fall: an accident is something that falls on you without warning.
normal.cn: cadere 是「落下」：accident 就是毫无预警落到你头上的事。

normal.en: Accidere meant to befall, and the word still keeps that image of an event landing on a person.
normal.cn: accidere 意为「降临」，这个词至今保留「事件落在人身上」的画面。

normal.en: Incident uses in- meaning into, a different direction of the same falling root.
normal.cn: incident 用表示「向内」的 in-，是同一「落下」词根的另一个方向。

normal.en: By accident is the fixed phrase for something done without any plan.
normal.cn: by accident 是表示「没有计划地做成某事」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Accident insurance covers the damage such a fall leaves behind.
normal.cn: accident insurance 承保这类意外留下的损害。

abstract.en: Picture a foot catching on a loose stone in the pavement.
abstract.cn: 想象一只脚在人行道上被松动的石块绊住。

abstract.en: The fall comes from outside the plan: nothing in the day asked for it.
abstract.cn: 这一跤来自计划之外：这一天里没有任何东西请求它发生。

abstract.en: The word covers both the falling moment and the damage left on the ground.
abstract.cn: 这个词既指跌倒的那一瞬，也指留在地上的损害。

examples.en: He was injured in a traffic accident on his way home.
examples.cn: 他在回家路上的一场交通事故中受了伤。

examples.en: I found the old photograph by accident while cleaning the attic.
examples.cn: 我在清理阁楼时偶然发现了那张旧照片。

examples.en: Their meeting was a happy accident of two people sharing a train.
examples.cn: 他们的相识是两个人同乘一趟列车带来的幸运巧合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克西登特」——脚下被石子一绊，人就扑倒了：事故、意外

root: 拉丁语 accident 出自 accidere「落到……上、降临」，由 ad-「向」与 cadere「落下」构成；其现在分词 accidens 指「发生的事、附着的性质」。cadere 还生出 incident、occasion、decay 等词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accident all begin with something falling on a person or a plan: a crash, an unlucky event, pure chance, a work mishap, a chance circumstance, insured damage, a bump in the ground, or a lucky coincidence.
sensesIntro.cn: accident 的八个义项都始于「某物落到人或计划上」：撞车、不幸事件、纯粹的偶然、工作事故、历史偶然、承保的损害、地面起伏，或幸运的巧合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot catches on a stone and the body falls forward without warning.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚被石块绊住，身体毫无预警地向前扑倒。

branches.en: THE IMPACT: a crash on the road or a mishap at work brings sudden damage.
branches.cn: 撞击线：路上的碰撞或工作场所的失误带来突发损害。
