branches.en: THE SURPRISE: any unwelcome event that lands on an ordinary day belongs here.
branches.cn: 惊扰线：任何落在平常日子里的不受欢迎事件都归入此处。

branches.en: THE CHANCE: the same fall can be unplanned and neutral, or unplanned and fortunate.
branches.cn: 偶然线：同一次落下可以无计划而中性，也可以无计划而幸运。

branches.en: THE CIRCUMSTANCE: history and terrain both hold small features that merely happened.
branches.cn: 条件线：历史与地形都含有只是碰巧存在的小小特征。

branches.en: THE POLICY: insurance turns the fall into a category of covered damage.
branches.cn: 保单线：保险把这次落下变成一类可以承保的损害。

intro.en: Accident is a Latin participle turned noun, with a prefix of direction and a verb of falling; English adds ordinary suffixes.
intro.cn: accident 是拉丁语分词转成的名词，带方向前缀与「落下」动词；英语再普通后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin cadere, accidere and accidens are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cadere、accidere 与 accidens 均有记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix makes the falling land on someone.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀让「落下」落到某人身上。

items.example: The verb supplies the fall in the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供词中的「落下」义。

items.example: The compound turns falling into befalling.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「落下」变成「降临」。

items.example: The participle is the direct model for accident.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是 accident 的直接模型。

items.example: It forms accidental.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accidental。

items.example: It forms accidentally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accidentally。

items.example: It forms accidence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accidence。

items.example: It forms incident with the same cadere root.
items.exampleCN: 它与同一 cadere 词根构成 incident。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「意外的」
由 accidental 加 -ly 构成，义为「偶然地」
由本词加 -ence 构成，义为「词形变化」

definition_zh: 住处；住宿；适应；调和；便利设施；通融
definition_en: a place to stay, or the act of adjusting something so that it fits a need, a person or a situation
core_image: 把不同尺寸的东西挪一挪，刚好嵌进同一个框里
scene: 展会期间城里酒店全满，主办方临时把学生宿舍改成了客房。The students were moved to a hotel, where the accommodation was simple but clean.
sceneCN: 这里 accommodation 是「住处、住宿」（第 1 个义项：供人居住的房间或住宿安排）；句意为学生们被安排到一家旅馆，那里的住处简朴但干净。

pos.zh: 名词：住处；住宿；适应；调和；便利设施

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀 -ation 得到的动词，义为「容纳；提供住处；适应」
由动词 accommodate 加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「乐于助人的；通融的」
由动词 accommodate 加 -ive 构成形容词，义为「适应性的；调节的」

senses.title: A place to stay
senses.definition: a room, building or arrangement that provides somewhere to live or sleep, especially while travelling
senses.definitionCN: 提供居住或睡眠之所的房间、建筑或安排，尤指旅途中
senses.example: The price includes flights and three nights' accommodation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个价格包含机票和三晚住宿。
senses.why: Latin accommodare meant to make one thing fit another; a room is made to fit the traveller who needs it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 accommodare 意为「使一物适合另一物」；住处就是被安排得适合旅人需要的地方。

senses.title: The act of adapting
senses.definition: the process of changing something so that it fits new conditions or needs
senses.definitionCN: 改变某物使之适合新条件或新需要的过程
senses.example: The accommodation of the schedule to night workers took weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 把时间表调整到适合夜班工人，花了好几周。
senses.why: Fit is the core: one thing is moved until it sits comfortably inside another.
senses.whyCN: 核心就是「合」：把一样东西挪动，直到它舒服地嵌进另一样东西里。

senses.title: A settlement of differences
senses.definition: an arrangement reached by opposing sides after adjusting their demands
senses.definitionCN: 对立双方在调整各自要求之后达成的安排
senses.example: Both sides reached an accommodation over the disputed border.
senses.exampleCN: 双方就争议边界达成了和解。
senses.why: Two claims that do not fit at first are adjusted until both can sit in one agreement.
senses.whyCN: 起初彼此不合的两项主张被不断调整，直到两者都能放进同一份协议里。

senses.title: A helpful facility or device
senses.definition: a device or service provided to make a place easier to use, especially for disabled people
senses.definitionCN: 为使某处更便于使用而提供的装置或服务，尤指为残障人士设置
senses.example: The hall has accommodation for wheelchairs near every entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅每个入口附近都设有轮椅便利设施。
senses.why: A building that must fit every body needs extra pieces, and those pieces are called accommodations.
senses.whyCN: 一座必须适合每个人身体的建筑需要额外的部件，这些部件就被称为 accommodations。

senses.title: Room to sit or move
senses.definition: space or seating made available for a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 为某人或某群体腾出的空间或座位
senses.example: The bus has accommodation for forty passengers.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆巴士可容纳四十名乘客。
senses.why: Space is the simplest thing that must fit people; making it fit is the old verb in a physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 空间是最简单的一项要适合人的东西；把空间腾得合适，就是那个旧动词在实体层面的用法。

senses.title: A favour granted to help someone
senses.titleCN: 给予他人的通融与照应
senses.definition: a special arrangement or favour made to help a person in a difficult position
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助处于困难处境的人而作出的特别安排或照顾
senses.example: The school made an accommodation for the student who was ill.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为那名生病的学生作了特别通融。
senses.why: Rules usually stand straight; an accommodation bends them so a particular person can fit inside.
senses.whyCN: 规则通常是笔直的；一项通融把规则弯一弯，好让某个具体的人能嵌进去。

senses.title: The eye's focusing adjustment
senses.definition: the automatic change by which the eye adjusts its focus for near or distant objects
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛为看清近处或远处物体而自动调整焦点的变化
senses.example: Reading for hours strains the accommodation of the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间阅读会使眼睛的调节功能疲劳。
senses.why: The lens physically reshapes itself to fit the distance of the object, the same fitting image inside the body.
senses.whyCN: 晶状体在物理上改变形状去适应物体的远近，是同一「吻合」画面出现在身体内部。

senses.title: Financial help or a loan
senses.definition: in finance, a loan or special arrangement that helps a person or firm through a shortage
senses.definitionCN: 在金融中，帮助个人或公司渡过资金短缺的贷款或特别安排
senses.example: The bank offered a short-term accommodation to cover the gap.
senses.exampleCN: 银行为填补缺口提供了一笔短期资金通融。
senses.why: Money that does not fit the month's needs can be fitted in temporarily by a lender.
senses.whyCN: 与当月开支不合的钱，可以由放贷者临时安排得合得上。

intro.en: Accommodation is a Latin noun of fitting, built on the word for measure; the lodging sense is a much later branch.
intro.cn: accommodation 是表示「使吻合」的拉丁名词，建立在「尺度」一词之上；住宿义是很晚才分出的分支。

items.en: The noun modus meant measure, manner or limit, and it is the root of a large Latin family.
items.cn: 名词 modus 意为「尺度、方式、限度」，是拉丁语一大词族的根。

items.en: Com- meaning together plus modus gave commodus, fitting, convenient or suitable, literally measured together.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的 com- 加 modus 构成 commodus，意为「合宜的、便利的」，字面是「一同量准」。

items.en: Ad- meaning to plus commodus gave accommodare, to make fit, to adapt or to furnish.
items.cn: 表示「向」的 ad- 加 commodus 构成 accommodare，意为「使适合、调整、供给」。

items.en: The action noun accommodatio named the act of fitting, and French carried it towards English.
items.cn: 动作名词 accommodatio 指「使适合的行为」，法语把它带向英语。

items.en: The lodging sense is a nineteenth-century development, when travel and paid rooms became common.
items.cn: 住宿义是十九世纪才发展出来的，当时旅行与付费房间变得普遍。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same modus family; the near-meaning group gathers words for lodging and for fitting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 modus 词族的词；近义组收表示住宿与适应调和的词。

entries.definition: To provide room for, or to change something so that it fits; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「容纳、提供住处、使适合」，是名词背后的动词形式。

entries.definition: Willing to help and adjust to others; formed with -ing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「乐于助人的、通融的」，由动词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to adaptation or adjustment; formed with -ive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「适应性的、调节的」，由动词加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: A traded good or useful thing; it shares the modus root but has moved to the market.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「商品、有用之物」，同出 modus 词根，但语义已转到市场交易。

entries.definition: A place to sleep, often a rented room; more specific and usually cheaper than accommodation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「寄宿处、出租房间」，比 accommodation 更具体，通常也更便宜。

entries.definition: The supply of homes for people, considered as a social or economic issue.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住房供给」，多从社会或经济角度指人们的居住房屋。

entries.definition: Living space provided for workers or soldiers; formal and often collective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住处、营房」，指为工作人员或军人提供的居住空间，语气正式。

entries.definition: A change made so that something suits a new use or condition, matching the second sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编」，指为使某物适合新用途或新条件而作的改变，对应第 2 个义项。

entries.definition: A building, service or piece of equipment provided for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「设施、设备」，指为特定目的提供的建筑、服务或器具。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin modus root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 modus 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Modus is a measure, so commodus means measured to fit, and accommodation is the fitting itself.
normal.cn: modus 是「尺度」，所以 commodus 意为「量得合身」，而 accommodation 就是这场合身本身。

normal.en: The same root gives commodity, once a convenient thing and now a traded good.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 commodity，原指「合用的东西」，如今指「商品」。

normal.en: Hotel accommodation is the room measured to fit the traveller.
normal.cn: hotel accommodation 就是量得适合旅人的那间房。

normal.en: Reach an accommodation means two sides bend until their claims fit together.
normal.cn: reach an accommodation 指两方各让一步，直到主张能合在一起。

normal.en: In physiology, the accommodation of the eye fits the focus to the distance.
normal.cn: 在生理学中，眼睛的 accommodation 让焦点适应距离。

abstract.en: Picture two boxes of different sizes being shifted until both slide into one shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象两个大小不同的箱子被挪来挪去，直到都能放进同一层架子。

abstract.en: What fits can be a traveller, a timetable, a dispute, a wheelchair, a bus seat, a rule or a loan.
abstract.cn: 要合得上的可以是旅人、时间表、争端、轮椅、巴士座位、规则或一笔贷款。

abstract.en: Accommodation never changes the goal; it changes the shape until the goal can be reached.
abstract.cn: accommodation 从不改变目标，它改变形状，直到目标够得着。

examples.en: The price includes flights and three nights' accommodation.
examples.cn: 这个价格包含机票和三晚住宿。

examples.en: The eye's accommodation lets you focus on objects at different distances.
examples.cn: 眼睛的调节功能让你能看清不同距离的物体。

examples.en: Both sides reached an accommodation over the disputed border.
examples.cn: 双方就争议边界达成了和解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿靠么得申」——房间挪一挪，正好住得下：住处、适应

root: 拉丁语 accommodare「使适合、供以所需」由 ad-「向」与 commodus「合宜的」构成，而 commodus 又由 com-「一起」加 modus「尺度」构成，字面意为「一同量准」。modus 还是 mode、moderate、commodity 的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accommodation all make one thing fit another: a room for a traveller, a plan for new conditions, a deal for two sides, a facility for a body, space for passengers, a rule bent for one person, a lens for distance, and a loan for a shortage.
sensesIntro.cn: accommodation 的八个义项都在让一样东西合上另一样：旅人与房间、计划与新条件、两方与协议、身体与设施、乘客与空间、规则与个人、晶状体与距离、短缺与贷款。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two differently sized objects are shifted until both slide into one shelf.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个大小不同的物件被挪动，直到都能放进同一层架子。

branches.en: THE SPACE: a room fits a traveller, and seats fit a group of passengers.
branches.cn: 空间线：房间合旅人之身，座位合一群乘客之数。

branches.en: THE ADJUSTMENT: a plan is altered for new conditions, and an eye alters its focus for distance.
branches.cn: 调整线：计划为新条件而改，眼睛为距离而改焦点。

branches.en: THE SETTLEMENT: two claims are bent until they fit one agreement.
branches.cn: 和解线：两项主张被弯折，直到能放进同一份协议。

branches.en: THE HELP: a facility fits a body, and a favour fits a rule around one person.
branches.cn: 帮助线：设施合身体之用，通融让规则为某个人弯一弯。

branches.en: THE MONEY: a loan fits a shortage until the month balances.
branches.cn: 金钱线：贷款补上短缺，让当月收支重新合得上。

intro.en: Accommodation is a Latin noun of fitting, formed from a prefix, a root for measure, and a noun ending.
intro.cn: accommodation 是表示「使吻合」的拉丁名词，由前缀、表示尺度的词根与名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus, commodus, accommodare and accommodatio are all recorded, so the chain is documented to the Latin layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modus、commodus、accommodare 与 accommodatio 均有记录，这条链条到拉丁语层都有文献可查。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of things measured together.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「一同量度」的意思。

items.example: The noun is the measure root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是这一词族的「尺度」词根。

items.example: The adjective means measured to fit.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词意为「量得合身」。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms accommodation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accommodation。

items.example: It forms accommodating.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accommodating。

items.example: It forms accommodative.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accommodative。

items.example: The prefix turns fitting into making fit.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「合身」变成「使之合身」。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ation 得到的动词，义为「容纳；适应」
由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「乐于助人的」
由动词加 -ive 构成，义为「适应性的」

definition_zh: 陪伴；陪同；伴随；为……伴奏；与……同时出现
definition_en: to go somewhere with someone, or to happen or exist at the same time as something else
core_image: 两个人并肩走，一个人的影子始终挨着另一个
scene: 夜里末班地铁上，值班员陪最后一位乘客走到出口。The night guard offered to accompany the last passenger to the station exit.
sceneCN: 这里 accompany 是「陪同、陪伴某人走」（第 1 个义项：与人同行作伴）；句意为值班员主动陪同最后一位乘客走到车站出口。

pos.zh: 动词：陪伴；陪同；伴随；为……伴奏

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「伴随物；伴奏」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「伴奏者」
由本词加 -ing 构成形容词，义为「随同的；附带的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 accompanied 构成，义为「无人陪伴的；无伴奏的」

senses.title: To go with a person
senses.definition: to travel or walk somewhere together with another person, usually to keep them company
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人一同前往或走某段路，通常是为了作伴
senses.example: Her brother accompanied her to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥陪她去参加面试。
senses.why: Old French acompaignier meant to be someone's companion, and the first sense is simply walking beside that person.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 acompaignier 意为「做某人的同伴」，第一个义项就是走在那个人的身旁。

senses.title: To happen at the same time
senses.definition: to occur together with another event, often as a natural partner
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事件一同发生，常作为自然的伴随者
senses.example: The storm was accompanied by a sharp drop in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这场暴风雨伴随着气温骤降。
senses.why: If a person can walk beside another, an event can also arrive beside another, and the word extends to things.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个人能走在另一个人身旁，一件事也能在另一件事旁边到来，于是这个词扩展到了事物。

senses.title: To play music for another performer
senses.definition: to play a musical instrument while another person sings or plays the main part
senses.definitionCN: 在他人演唱或演奏主旋律时演奏乐器进行配合
senses.example: A pianist accompanied the choir at the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会上一位钢琴家为合唱团伴奏。
senses.why: The supporting player walks beside the main performer: present, but never leading.
senses.whyCN: 伴奏者走在主唱身旁：在场，却绝不领路。

senses.title: To escort under guard
senses.definition: to go with a person as a guard or escort, sometimes against that person's wish
senses.definitionCN: 作为守卫或押解者随行，有时违背当事人的意愿
senses.example: Two officers accompanied the suspect to the court.
senses.exampleCN: 两名警员把嫌疑人押送到法庭。
senses.why: Companionship turns official: the one beside you is there to control the way you go.
senses.whyCN: 陪伴变成了公事：身旁那个人在那里，是为了控制你走的方向。

senses.title: To be sent along with something
senses.definition: to be supplied together with a document, letter or object
senses.definitionCN: 随文件、信件或物品一同提供
senses.example: A letter accompanied the cheque from the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 银行寄来支票时还附了一封信。
senses.why: Papers travel together, so the word for going beside a person serves for things sent in the same envelope.
senses.whyCN: 文件会一起旅行，于是「与人同行」的词也被用在同一信封里寄出的东西上。

senses.title: To appear together with a symptom
senses.definition: to appear at the same time as a condition or a feature, as a symptom does with an illness
senses.definitionCN: 与某种状况或特征同时出现，如症状伴随疾病而来
senses.example: The fever is often accompanied by a dry cough.
senses.exampleCN: 这种发烧常伴有干咳。
senses.why: The second thing stays beside the first and is read as a sign of it, which is exactly what a symptom does.
senses.whyCN: 第二样东西停在第一样旁边，并被当作它的迹象来读——这正是症状所做的事。

senses.title: To attend someone formally
senses.definition: to go with an important guest or a family member on a formal occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在正式场合陪同贵宾或家属
senses.example: The consul accompanied the visiting minister at the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 领事在仪式上陪同来访的部长。
senses.why: Formal companionship adds rank and courtesy: the one beside you marks your position.
senses.whyCN: 正式陪同加上身份与礼节：身旁那个人标示着你的位置。

senses.title: To go well with food or drink
senses.definition: to be served or eaten together with a dish because the two suit each other
senses.definitionCN: 因彼此相称而与某道菜一同上桌或一同食用
senses.example: A light red wine accompanies the roast chicken well.
senses.exampleCN: 一款清淡的红酒与这道烤鸡很相配。
senses.why: Two things that suit each other travel together on one table, so the word reaches the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 彼此相称的两样东西在同一张桌上同行，于是这个词走进了厨房。

intro.en: Accompany began as a picture of two people sharing bread, and it has kept the idea of standing beside another ever since.
intro.cn: accompany 最初是两个人分食面包的画面，此后一直保留着「站在另一个人身旁」的意思。

items.en: The noun panis meant bread, and it is a well recorded word with a long history in Latin.
items.cn: 名词 panis 意为「面包」，是拉丁语中记录充分、历史悠久的词。

items.en: Com- meaning together plus panis gave companio, one who shares bread with another, hence a companion.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的 com- 加 panis 构成 companio，指「与人分食面包的人」，即同伴。

items.en: Old French compaign kept the sense of a companion or a comrade in arms.
items.cn: 古法语 compaign 保留了「同伴、战友」的意思。

items.en: The verb a- plus compaignier meant to be the companion of someone, to go along with that person.
items.cn: 动词 a- 加 compaignier 意为「做某人的同伴、与之同行」。

items.en: The music sense appeared in the eighteenth century, when the supporting part was pictured as a player walking beside the main one.
items.cn: 音乐义在十八世纪出现，当时伴奏声部被想象成走在主奏身旁的演奏者。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the bread-sharing family and one near-spelling from a folding root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of going beside another.
note.cn: 形近组收「分食面包」词族，以及一个来自「折叠」词根的近形词；近义组收表示走在他人身旁的动词。

entries.definition: A person who spends time with another or travels with them; the noun behind accompany.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「同伴、伴侣」，是 accompany 背后的名词形式，同出「分食面包的人」这一词根。

entries.definition: The state of being with others, a group of people, or a business firm.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陪伴、一群人、公司」，同出「一起」与「面包」的词根。

entries.definition: The feeling of friendship and shared time between companions.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「情谊、陪伴关系」，指同伴之间的友情与共处。

entries.definition: A person who helps another commit a crime; the shape is close but the root is Latin complicare, to fold together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「共犯、从犯」，词形与 accompany 相近，但词根是拉丁语 complicare「折叠在一起」，词源不同。

entries.definition: To go with someone in order to protect or guide them; more official and purposeful.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「护送、陪同」，比 accompany 更具公务性与目的性。

entries.definition: To go with someone as a servant or an official helper; in modern use mostly to be present at an event.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「随侍、陪同」，旧时指仆从或官员随行，现代多指出席活动，语气正式。

entries.definition: To come after a person or thing, usually at a distance rather than beside.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「跟随、跟着」，通常隔一点距离，而不是并肩。

entries.definition: To come into the company of someone or become part of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加入、与某人会合」，强调并入而非一路同行。

entries.definition: To spend time with a person or group, often disapprovingly; literary in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结交、厮混」，常含不满意味，语气偏文学。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin panis root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 panis 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Panis is bread: a companion is a person who shares bread with you.
normal.cn: panis 是「面包」：companion 就是与你分食面包的人。

normal.en: The French a- prefix turned that noun into a verb, to be that bread-sharer.
normal.cn: 法语的 a- 前缀把那个名词变成动词，意为「做那个分面包的人」。

normal.en: Company is the same image at one table: people sitting together.
normal.cn: company 是同一画面在一张桌上：一群人坐在一起。

normal.en: Accompaniment adds -ment, naming the thing that goes along with another.
normal.cn: accompaniment 加 -ment，指与另一物同行的那样东西。

normal.en: An accompanist plays beside the singer, never in front of them.
normal.cn: accompanist 在歌者身旁演奏，从不抢到前面去。

abstract.en: Picture two sets of footprints side by side along a road.
abstract.cn: 想象路上两串脚印并排延伸。

abstract.en: What walks beside you can be a person, a sound, a document or a symptom.
abstract.cn: 走在身旁的可以是人、声音、文件或症状。

abstract.en: Accompany never makes the second thing the main one: it always stays beside.
abstract.cn: accompany 从不把第二样东西变成主体，它始终待在旁边。

examples.en: Her brother accompanied her to the interview.
examples.cn: 她哥哥陪她去参加面试。

examples.en: The storm was accompanied by a sharp drop in temperature.
examples.cn: 这场暴风雨伴随着气温骤降。

examples.en: A pianist accompanied the choir at the concert.
examples.cn: 音乐会上一位钢琴家为合唱团伴奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康破尼」——面包掰两半，两个人一块走：陪伴、伴随

root: 古法语 acompaignier 由 a- 加 compaignier「做同伴」构成，而 compaignier 又出自晚期拉丁语 companio，本义是「与人分食面包的人」，由 com-「一起」加 panis「面包」构成。因此这个词的底色是「同一块面包，同一段路」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accompany all keep one thing beside another: a person, an event, a melody, a guarded prisoner, a document, a symptom, a guest, or a dish.
sensesIntro.cn: accompany 的八个义项都让一样东西待在另一样旁边：一个人、一个事件、一段旋律、一名被押送者、一份文件、一个症状、一位贵宾，或一道菜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two sets of footprints run side by side along one road.
core.cn: 核心意象：两串脚印沿着同一条路并排延伸。

branches.en: THE PERSON: an ordinary companion and a formal guest both walk beside someone.
branches.cn: 人物线：寻常同伴与正式贵宾，都在某人身旁同行。

branches.en: THE EVENT: an event or a symptom arrives at the same time as another.
branches.cn: 事件线：一个事件或症状与另一件事同时到来。

branches.en: THE MUSIC: the supporting player stands beside the main performer.
branches.cn: 音乐线：伴奏者站在主奏者身旁。

branches.en: THE GUARD: the one beside you controls the way you go.
branches.cn: 押送线：身旁的那个人控制着你走的方向。

branches.en: THE ADDITION: papers travel in one envelope, and wine sits on the same table as the dish.
branches.cn: 附加线：文件装进同一个信封，酒与菜摆在同一张桌上。

intro.en: Accompany is a French verb built on a Latin bread word; English adds ordinary suffixes to name the person and the thing.
intro.cn: accompany 是建立在拉丁语「面包」一词上的法语动词；英语用普通后缀命名「人」与「物」。

latinIntro.en: Latin panis and late Latin companio are recorded, so the base of the family is documented, though the exact date of companio is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 panis 与晚期拉丁语 companio 均有记录，词族的基础可查，但 companio 的确切出现年代不确定。

items.example: The prefix gives the word its sense of sharing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给词带来「共享」的意思。

items.example: The noun is the bread at the centre of the image.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词就是画面中心的那块面包。

items.meaning: one who shares bread, a companion
items.example: The noun is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整族词的来源。

items.example: The prefix turns the companion into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「同伴」变成一种动作。

items.example: It forms accompaniment.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accompaniment。

items.example: It forms accompanist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accompanist。

items.example: It forms accompanying.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accompanying。

items.example: It forms unaccompanied.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unaccompanied。

latinEntries.structure: Late Latin noun from com- plus panis

latinEntries.meaning: a group sharing bread, a company

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「伴随物；伴奏」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「伴奏者」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「随同的；附带的」
由否定前缀 un- 加 accompanied 构成，义为「无人陪伴的」

definition_zh: 完成；实现；达到；取得；履行
definition_en: to succeed in doing or finishing something that has been planned, required or attempted
core_image: 最后一块拼图落下，整幅图终于填满
scene: 木工坊的学徒把最后一块榫头敲进木架，整张桌子稳稳立住。After three weeks of work, he had accomplished everything the old carpenter asked for.
sceneCN: 这里 accomplish 是「完成、做成」（第 1 个义项：把任务做完）；句意为经过三周，他把老木匠交代的一切都做成了。

pos.zh: 动词：完成；实现；达到；取得；履行

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「完成；成就；才艺」
由本词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「有造诣的；熟练的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可完成的」

senses.title: To finish a task
senses.definition: to carry a piece of work through to its end, so that nothing remains undone
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作一直做到结尾，没有留下未完成的部分
senses.example: The team accomplished the repairs before nightfall.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在天黑前完成了维修。
senses.why: Latin complere meant to fill up completely; a task is finished when it has been filled to its end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 complere 意为「完全填满」；任务被填到尽头，就算做完了。

senses.title: To reach a goal
senses.definition: to succeed in reaching a goal that was set in advance
senses.definitionCN: 成功达到事先设定的目标
senses.example: They accomplished the target two months early.
senses.exampleCN: 他们提前两个月达到了目标。
senses.why: A goal is an empty shape; accomplishing it means filling that shape with what was planned.
senses.whyCN: 目标是一个空的形状；做成就意味着用计划中的东西把它填满。

senses.title: To achieve something notable
senses.definition: to achieve a notable result that others recognize as significant
senses.definitionCN: 取得他人认可为重要的显著成果
senses.example: She accomplished more in one year than most do in five.
senses.exampleCN: 她一年里做到的事，比多数人五年做的还多。
senses.why: The filled shape can be large, and then what was filled in becomes a record of achievement.
senses.whyCN: 被填满的形状可以很大，于是填进去的东西就成了可记载的成就。

senses.title: To cover a distance or a journey
senses.definition: to complete a distance, route or journey that was planned
senses.definitionCN: 走完预先计划的距离、路线或旅程
senses.example: They accomplished the whole route in four days.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用四天走完了整条路线。
senses.why: A journey is a line with two ends; filling it means walking every part of it.
senses.whyCN: 旅程是一条有两个端点的线；把它填满，就是走遍其中的每一段。

senses.title: To fulfil a duty or promise
senses.definition: to carry out a duty, promise or obligation completely
senses.definitionCN: 把职责、承诺或义务完整地执行到位
senses.example: He accomplished what he had promised the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 他兑现了对村民的承诺。
senses.why: A promise is a shape traced in advance, and fulfilling it fills that shape exactly.
senses.whyCN: 承诺是事先画好的形状，履行就是把这个形状严丝合缝地填满。

senses.title: To bring to perfection, an older use
senses.definition: in older writing, to complete something so that it reaches its full or perfect form
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的文献中，指把某物做到完整或完美的形态
senses.example: The painter spent years accomplishing the design of the dome.
senses.exampleCN: 那位画家花了很多年才把穹顶的设计做到完善。
senses.why: Complete can mean not merely finished but perfect, because a full shape has no gap left.
senses.whyCN: complete 不仅可以是「做完了」，还可以是「完美」，因为填满的形状不留空隙。

senses.title: To finish a work or a piece
senses.definition: to finish making a work of art, a book or a piece of craft
senses.definitionCN: 把一件艺术品、一本书或一件手工艺品制作完毕
senses.example: The weaver accomplished the tapestry in a single winter.
senses.exampleCN: 织工用一个冬天完成了那幅挂毯。
senses.why: A work is a form the maker holds in mind; it is accomplished when the material finally matches that form.
senses.whyCN: 作品是制作者心里的一个形状；当材料终于与那个形状吻合，它就被完成了。

senses.title: To make a wish come true
senses.definition: to succeed in doing what one most wanted to do, so that the wish is no longer empty
senses.definitionCN: 成功做成自己最想做的事，使心愿不再落空
senses.example: He accomplished his boyhood wish of sailing alone across the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 他实现了少年时独自驾船横渡海湾的心愿。
senses.why: A wish is the emptiest shape of all, and accomplishing it is the act of filling that space at last.
senses.whyCN: 心愿是所有形状中最空的一个，实现它就是终于把那个空间填上。

intro.en: Accomplish came into English from Old French, but its core is a Latin verb meaning to fill up.
intro.cn: accomplish 经古法语进入英语，但其核心是一个表示「填满」的拉丁动词。

items.en: The verb plere meant to fill, and it is recorded across the whole history of Latin.
items.cn: 动词 plere 意为「填满」，在拉丁语的全部历史中都有记录。

items.en: Com- meaning altogether plus plere gave complere, to fill up, to complete, and also to fulfil.
items.cn: 表示「完全」的 com- 加 plere 构成 complere，意为「填满、完成」，也有「履行」之义。

items.en: Old French acomp(l)ir meant to fulfil or complete a task, a promise or a period of time.
items.cn: 古法语 acomplir 意为「完成、履行」一项任务、承诺或一段时间。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fifteenth century; early spellings vary and the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词；早期拼写不一，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun accomplishment and the adjective accomplished grew later, the adjective shifting towards the idea of a trained skill.
items.cn: 名词 accomplishment 与形容词 accomplished 出现得更晚，形容词逐渐偏向「训练有素的技能」之义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same plere family plus one word that only sounds like completion; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of finishing and attaining.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 plere 词族的词，外加一个只是听起来像「完成」的词；近义组收表示完成与达到的动词。

entries.definition: Something successfully done, or the act of finishing it; formed with -ment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「成就、完成」，指成功做成的事或完成这一行为，由本词加 -ment 构成。

entries.definition: Skilled and experienced in a field, or successfully completed; formed with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有造诣的、熟练的」或「已完成的」，由本词加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Whole and finished; it comes from the same Latin complere, to fill up.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或动词，义为「完整的、完成」，同出拉丁语 complere「填满」。

entries.definition: Smugly satisfied with oneself; it sounds like a completion word but comes from Latin placere, to please.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「自满的、得意的」，听起来像「完成」类词，实则出自拉丁语 placere「使愉快」，词源不同。

entries.definition: To succeed in reaching a result through effort; it stresses the effort more than the filling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取得、实现」，强调经过努力达成结果，比 accomplish 更突出努力过程。

entries.definition: To carry out a promise, duty or need completely, matching the fifth sense of accomplish.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「履行、满足」，指把承诺、职责或需要完整做到，对应第 5 个义项。

entries.definition: To reach a goal, level or age after effort; formal and often used of long-term aims.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「达到、获得」，语气正式，多用于长期目标或水平。

entries.definition: To bring something to its end; plain and neutral, with no idea of filling a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结束、完成」，朴素中性，不含「把形状填满」的画面。

entries.definition: To carry out an action or a task, often before others or as part of a role.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「执行、表演」，常指在他人面前或按角色要求去做。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin plere root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 plere 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Plere is to fill: to accomplish is to fill a task up to its brim.
normal.cn: plere 是「填」：accomplish 就是把任务填到边沿。

normal.en: Complere added com- meaning altogether, so the filling leaves no gap.
normal.cn: complere 加上表示「完全」的 com-，所以填得没有空隙。

normal.en: The same root gives complete and completion, all about no empty space left.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 complete 与 completion，都指不留空白。

normal.en: Accomplishment adds -ment, the name of the filled-up result.
normal.cn: accomplishment 加 -ment，指被填满之后的结果。

normal.en: Accomplished also describes a person whose skill has been filled out.
normal.cn: accomplished 也形容一个人的技艺被充实到饱满。

abstract.en: Picture the last piece of a puzzle being pressed into place.
abstract.cn: 想象最后一块拼图被按进它该在的位置。

abstract.en: The picture can be a job, a goal, a journey, a promise or a wish.
abstract.cn: 那幅图可以是一项工作、一个目标、一段旅程、一个承诺或一个心愿。

abstract.en: Accomplish is about the shape being complete, not about being praised for it.
abstract.cn: accomplish 说的是形状已经完整，而不是为此受到称赞。

examples.en: She accomplished more in one year than most do in five.
examples.cn: 她一年里做到的事，比多数人五年做的还多。

examples.en: The team accomplished its mission without a single loss.
examples.cn: 团队毫发无损地完成了使命。

examples.en: He accomplished the climb in record time.
examples.cn: 他以创纪录的时间完成了这次攀登。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿康普利什」——拼图一直填，填满最后一格：完成、实现

root: 古法语 acomplir 来自拉丁语 complere「填满、完成」，而 complere 由 com-「完全」与 plere「填」构成。plere 还是 complete、supply、plenty 的词根。因此这个词的底色是「把空处填到没有剩余」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accomplish all fill an empty shape to its end: a task, a goal, a record of achievement, a route, a promise, a perfected design, a work of craft, or a childhood wish.
sensesIntro.cn: accomplish 的八个义项都在把某个空形状填到尽头：任务、目标、成就的纪录、路线、承诺、被做到完美的设计、一件手作，或一个少年时的心愿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last piece of a puzzle is pressed into place and the picture is whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一块拼图被按进原位，整幅图终于完整。

branches.en: THE WORK: a task and a piece of craft are both filled in until nothing is missing.
branches.cn: 工作线：任务与手作都被填到没有缺漏为止。

branches.en: THE AIM: a set goal and a private wish are shapes waiting to be filled.
branches.cn: 目标线：设定的目标与私人的心愿，都是等着被填满的形状。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a large result becomes something others can point to.
branches.cn: 纪录线：很大的成果成为他人可以指认的东西。

branches.en: THE ROUTE: a journey is a line, and finishing it fills every segment.
branches.cn: 路线线：旅程是一条线，走完就是把每一段都填上。

branches.en: THE DUTY: a promise is carried out, and an older sense asks for a perfect form.
branches.cn: 职责线：承诺被履行，较古的义项则要求做到完美的形态。

intro.en: Accomplish is a French verb built on Latin filling; English adds suffixes to make the noun and the adjective.
intro.cn: accomplish 是建立在拉丁语「填满」之上的法语动词；英语加后缀造出名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin plere and complere are recorded; the French verb acomplir is also documented, so only the earliest layer is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plere 与 complere 均有记录，法语动词 acomplir 也见于文献，只有最早的层次存疑。

items.example: The prefix means the filling is total.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示填充是彻底的。

items.example: The verb is the filling root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「填」词根。

items.example: The compound means filled to the top.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词意为填到顶部。

items.example: The French verb carried the word to English.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词把词带入英语。

items.example: It forms accomplishment.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accomplishment。

items.example: It forms accomplished.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accomplished。

items.example: It forms accomplishable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accomplishable。

items.example: The ending survives in the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语词尾保留在英语动词里。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from com- plus plere

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「成就；完成」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「有造诣的」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「可完成的」

definition_zh: 账户；账目；叙述；解释；考虑；价值；（动词）说明、占
definition_en: a record of money received and paid, a description of events, or a reason given for something; as a verb, to explain or to form a part of
core_image: 一本账簿摊开，每一笔进出都被一字一句记下
scene: 月底的杂货店里，老板把一叠单据摊在柜台上核对。Every sale was kept in a separate account so that the tax office could check it.
sceneCN: 这里 account 是「账目、账册」（第 2 个义项：记录钱款进出的账目）；句意为每笔销售都单独记在一本账上，以便税务部门核查。

pos.zh: 名词：账户；账目；叙述；解释；重要性
动词：说明原因；占（比例）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「有责任的；可解释的」
由本词加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「会计；记账」
由本词加表示人的后缀 -ant 构成，义为「会计；会计师」
由 accountable 加名词后缀 -ability 构成，义为「问责；负有责任」

senses.title: A bank account
senses.definition: an arrangement with a bank in which money is kept and can be added or withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 与银行之间存取款项的一种安排
senses.example: She opened a savings account at the local bank.
senses.exampleCN: 她在当地银行开了一个储蓄账户。
senses.why: An account is something reckoned up; a bank keeps the reckoning of what goes in and out of your money.
senses.whyCN: account 本是把数目算清楚；银行替你算清钱进钱出的那本数。

senses.title: A record of money paid and received
senses.definition: a written or stored record of sums of money received, spent or owed
senses.definitionCN: 对收入、支出或欠款的书面或电子记录
senses.example: The clerk entered every sale in the account.
senses.exampleCN: 店员把每一笔销售都记进账里。
senses.why: The word comes from Latin computare, to reckon, so its oldest job is to hold the results of counting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词出自拉丁语 computare「计算」，最古老的任务就是承载数出来的结果。

senses.title: A description of events
senses.definition: a spoken or written description of what happened, given in order
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序口述或书写的、关于所发生之事的描述
senses.example: The witness gave a detailed account of the crash.
senses.exampleCN: 目击者详细叙述了那场撞车。
senses.why: Telling a story is also reckoning: the events are counted out one after another, as entries in a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 讲故事也是算账：事件像账簿条目一样，一件接一件被数出来。

senses.title: A reason or explanation
senses.definition: a statement that explains why something happened or where something went
senses.definitionCN: 解释某事为何发生或某物流向何处的说法
senses.example: He could give no account of the missing money.
senses.exampleCN: 他无法解释那笔钱去了哪里。
senses.why: If a ledger must balance, every missing item needs a line explaining it, and that line is an account.
senses.whyCN: 账簿必须对得上，每一笔缺失都要有一行说明，这一行就是 account。

senses.title: To take into consideration
senses.definition: in phrases such as take account of, to include something in one's judgement
senses.definitionCN: 用于 take account of 一类短语，指把某因素纳入判断
senses.example: The plan takes account of the rising cost of fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划考虑了不断上涨的燃料成本。
senses.why: To account for something is to put it into the reckoning before the total is made.
senses.whyCN: 把某物算进去，就是在总数定下来之前把它写进账里。

senses.title: Importance or worth
senses.definition: in phrases such as of no account, the value or importance that something carries
senses.definitionCN: 用于 of no account 一类短语，指某物所具有的重要性或价值
senses.example: His opinion was of little account in the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他的意见在委员会里无足轻重。
senses.why: A thing of no account carries no weight in the final reckoning, so worthlessness is expressed as zero entries.
senses.whyCN: 无足轻重的东西在最后的结算里没有分量，于是「没有价值」被说成账上为零。

senses.title: A business client
senses.definition: a customer or firm that regularly buys from a business and has a running record with it
senses.definitionCN: 长期向某企业购买、并与之保持往来记录的主顾或公司
senses.example: The agency handles several large accounts in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这家代理公司在该地区负责几个大客户。
senses.why: A client is a ledger page kept open, so the person is named by the record that stands in their name.
senses.whyCN: 客户就是一页一直开着的账簿，于是人就被那本记在他名下的账来称呼。

senses.title: To explain or to make up a share
senses.definition: to give a reason for something, or to form a particular part of a total
senses.definitionCN: 为某事给出理由，或构成某个总数中的一部分
senses.example: Women account for nearly half of the workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 女性占了劳动力的近一半。
senses.why: The verb keeps the ledger: to account for is to answer for a line and to show how much it adds to the sum.
senses.whyCN: 动词延续了账本的意象：说明某一行的去向，也表明它为总数添了多少。

intro.en: Account came through Old French from a Latin verb of reckoning; counting is still the core of every sense.
intro.cn: account 经古法语来自一个表示「计算」的拉丁动词；算数仍是每个义项的核心。

items.en: The verb putare meant to reckon or consider; an older sense, to prune, is generally accepted and its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 动词 putare 意为「计算、考量」；其更早的「修剪」义一般被接受，但更深来源不确定。

items.en: Com- meaning together plus putare gave computare, to reckon together, to calculate.
items.cn: 表示「一起」的 com- 加 putare 构成 computare，意为「合计、计算」。

items.en: The noun computus named a reckoning or a calculation, and it passed into the church language of accounts and calendars.
items.cn: 名词 computus 指「计算、结算」，并进入教会用于账目与历法的语言。

items.en: Old French acont or conte meant a reckoning, and the verb conter meant to recount or to tell, linking money and story.
items.cn: 古法语 acont 或 conte 意为「结算」，动词 conter 意为「叙述、讲述」，把钱与故事连在一起。

items.en: The banking sense appears in the eighteenth century, and the verb sense of accounting for a share grew with modern statistics.
items.cn: 银行账户义在十八世纪出现，动词「占一定比例」义则随现代统计而发展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same reckoning family; the near-meaning group gathers words for records, stories and explanations.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「计算」词族的词；近义组收表示记录、叙述与解释的词。

entries.definition: Required to explain one's actions, or able to be explained; formed with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的、可解释的」，由本词加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The activity or profession of keeping and checking financial records; formed with -ing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计、记账」，指记录与核查财务的活动或职业，由本词加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: To say numbers in order or to find a total; it comes from the same computare root through French conter.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「数、计数」，经法语 conter 同出 computare 词根。

entries.definition: A sum taken off a price; dis- meaning away plus computare, so it is a deduction from the reckoning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「折扣」，由表示「去掉」的 dis- 加 computare 构成，即从结算中扣去一部分。

entries.definition: A formal spoken or written statement about an event or a situation.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「报告」，指关于事件或情况的正式口头或书面陈述。

entries.definition: A clear expression of facts, or a formal record of money owed and paid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「陈述、结算单」，指对事实的清楚表述，或对款项往来的正式记录。

entries.definition: A connected story of events; it stresses the telling rather than the accuracy of the reckoning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述、故事」，强调讲述的连贯，而不强调账目式的精确。

entries.definition: A stored piece of information about what happened, kept for later use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「记录」，指为日后查用而保存的关于所发生之事的信息。

entries.definition: A written statement of money owed for goods or services.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「账单」，指因货物或服务而欠款的书面清单。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin putare root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语 putare 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Putare is to reckon: an account is what comes out when things have been counted up.
normal.cn: putare 是「计算」：account 就是把东西数清楚之后得出的结果。

normal.en: The same root gives computer, a machine that reckons, and accountancy is its older cousin.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 computer，一台会计算的机器；accountancy 则是它更年长的亲戚。

normal.en: Account for is the verb phrase for explaining where something went.
normal.cn: account for 是解释某物去向的动词短语。

normal.en: Take account of means to count something in before deciding.
normal.cn: take account of 指在决定之前先把某因素算进去。

normal.en: Of no account means worth nothing in the final reckoning.
normal.cn: of no account 指在最后的结算里值不了什么。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger open on a desk, with rows of figures in two columns.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上摊开一本账簿，两列数字排成行。

abstract.en: The same ledger can hold a story instead of money: an account of a battle is entries in time.
abstract.cn: 同一本账簿也可以不装钱而装故事：一场战役的叙述就是按时间排的条目。

abstract.en: Account always answers one question: what is there, and why is it there?
abstract.cn: account 永远在回答一个问题：有什么，以及它为什么在那里。

examples.en: She opened a savings account at the local bank.
examples.cn: 她在当地银行开了一个储蓄账户。

examples.en: The witness gave a detailed account of the crash.
examples.cn: 目击者详细叙述了那场撞车。

examples.en: Women account for nearly half of the workforce.
examples.cn: 女性占了劳动力的近一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿靠特」——账本一摊，一笔一笔数清楚：账目、说明

root: 古法语 acont「结算」与动词 conter「叙述」来自拉丁语 computare「合计、计算」，而 computare 由 com-「一起」与 putare「计算、考量」构成。英语借入后先有「叙述」与「账目」两义，银行账户义更晚。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of account all keep a reckoning: a bank balance, a ledger, a story told in order, a reason for a missing sum, a factor counted in, a weight in the final total, a client's open page, and a share of the whole.
sensesIntro.cn: account 的八个义项都保留着「算账」的动作：银行余额、账簿、按序讲出的故事、缺失款项的理由、被算进去的因素、结算时的分量、客户那页开着的账，以及在整体中所占的份额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger lies open and every sum in and out is written down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本账簿摊开，每一笔进出都被写下。

branches.en: THE MONEY: a bank keeps a balance, and a shop keeps a ledger of sales.
branches.cn: 金钱线：银行保存余额，店铺保存销售的账。

branches.en: THE STORY: events are counted out in order and become a narrative.
branches.cn: 故事线：事件按顺序被数出来，成为一段叙述。

branches.en: THE REASON: one line explains a missing sum, and the verb states a share of the total.
branches.cn: 理由线：一行字解释缺失的款项，动词则说明在总数中的份额。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: a factor is counted in, and a thing of no account carries no weight.
branches.cn: 分量线：因素被算进去，而无足轻重之物在账上没有分量。

branches.en: THE CLIENT: a customer is a ledger page left open in their name.
branches.cn: 客户线：主顾就是一页以他之名长期开着的账。

intro.en: Account is a French shortening of a Latin reckoning word; English adds suffixes to name the person, the activity and the duty.
intro.cn: account 是拉丁语「计算」一词经法语缩短后的形式；英语加后缀命名人、活动与责任。

latinIntro.en: Latin putare and computare are recorded; the older sense of putare as to prune is generally accepted, but its deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 putare 与 computare 均有记录；putare 更早的「修剪」义一般被接受，但更深来源不确定。

items.example: Its French form ac- survives at the front of account.
items.exampleCN: 它的法语形式 ac- 保留在 account 的词首。

items.example: The verb is the reckoning root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「计算」词根。

items.example: The compound is the direct source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是这个词的直接来源。

items.example: The noun carried the sense into French.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把词义带入法语。

items.example: It forms accountable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accountable。

items.example: It forms accounting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accounting。

items.example: It forms accountant.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accountant。

items.example: It forms accountability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accountability。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb from com- plus putare

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -able 构成，义为「负有责任的」
由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「会计；记账」
由本词加 -ant 构成，义为「会计；会计师」
由 accountable 加 -ability 构成，义为「问责」

definition_zh: 会计；会计师；会计员；记账人
definition_en: a person whose job is to keep, check or inspect financial records and to prepare accounts
core_image: 一个人坐在账簿前，把每一笔数字都核对三遍
scene: 年末结账的夜里，办公室只剩下一盏台灯和堆成小山的凭证。The accountant checked every figure twice before signing the annual report.
sceneCN: 这里 accountant 是「会计人员、会计师」（第 1 个义项：负责记账与核算的专业人员）；句意为会计在签署年度报告前把每个数字都核对了两次。

pos.zh: 名词：会计；会计师；会计员

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ancy 构成，义为「会计职业；会计工作」
由家族基础词 account 加 -ing 构成，义为「会计；记账」
由本词去掉后缀 -ant 得到的基础词，义为「账户；账目」
由家族基础词 account 加 -able 构成，义为「负有责任的」

senses.title: A person who keeps financial records
senses.definition: a professional who records money received and paid and prepares financial statements
senses.definitionCN: 记录收入与支出、并编制财务报表的专业人员
senses.example: Her father works as an accountant for a shipping company.
senses.exampleCN: 她父亲在一家航运公司做会计。
senses.why: Account is the reckoning, and the suffix -ant names the person who does the reckoning.
senses.whyCN: account 是「算账」，后缀 -ant 指做这件事的人。

senses.title: A licensed or certified professional
senses.definition: an accountant who has passed a professional examination and is licensed to audit or certify accounts
senses.definitionCN: 通过专业考试并取得执照、可审计或签署账目的会计
senses.example: Only a licensed accountant may sign the audit report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持证会计师才能签署审计报告。
senses.why: The basic reckoner becomes a public officer when a body grants a licence and a title.
senses.whyCN: 当某个机构授予执照与头衔，原本的算账人就变成了对公众负责的执业者。

senses.title: A bookkeeper who records daily entries
senses.definition: a person who records the daily transactions of a business, often without auditing them
senses.definitionCN: 记录企业日常交易、通常不负责审计的人员
senses.example: The accountant keeps the day book and posts each entry.
senses.exampleCN: 记账员负责保管日记账并逐笔过账。
senses.why: Reckoning begins with writing each item down, and that first step alone is already an accountant's work.
senses.whyCN: 算账从把每一笔记下开始，而这一步本身就已经是会计的工作。

senses.title: A cost accountant
senses.definition: an accountant who works out the cost of producing goods or running a service
senses.definitionCN: 负责核算生产商品或提供服务的成本的会计
senses.example: The cost accountant compared the price of two suppliers.
senses.exampleCN: 成本会计比较了两家供应商的报价。
senses.why: One branch of reckoning asks what a thing costs, and the person who keeps that page is named by it.
senses.whyCN: 算账有一支专门问「某物花了多少」，守着那一页的人就由此得名。

senses.title: A management accountant
senses.definition: an accountant who prepares figures to help managers plan and control a business
senses.definitionCN: 为管理者规划与控制企业而编制数据的会计
senses.example: The management accountant prepared the budget for next year.
senses.exampleCN: 管理会计编制了下一年的预算。
senses.why: Reckoning made for decision rather than for record is a separate trade, and it has its own name.
senses.whyCN: 为决策而非为存档所做的计算是另一门行当，因此有了自己的名称。

senses.title: A tax accountant
senses.definition: an accountant who deals with tax returns, duties and the rules of the tax office
senses.definitionCN: 处理纳税申报、税款与税务规则的会计
senses.example: They hired a tax accountant before the filing deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在申报截止前请了一位税务会计。
senses.why: The state keeps its own ledger, and someone must read it in the same language as the firm's books.
senses.whyCN: 国家也有一本自己的账，必须有人用企业账簿同样的语言去读它。

senses.title: A forensic accountant
senses.definition: an accountant who examines records to find fraud, hidden money or evidence for a court
senses.definitionCN: 为查明欺诈、隐匿资金或提供法庭证据而审查账目的会计
senses.example: A forensic accountant traced the payments to an offshore firm.
senses.exampleCN: 一名法务会计把这些付款追查到一家离岸公司。
senses.why: When numbers become evidence, the reckoner works for the court and the word takes a legal shade.
senses.whyCN: 当数字成为证据，算账人便为法庭工作，这个词也就带上法律色彩。

senses.title: One who answers for an account, an old use
senses.definition: in older usage, a person who must give an account of money or actions entrusted to them
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法，指必须就受托的钱款或行为作出交代的人
senses.example: In the old guild records, each accountant answered to the master.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的行会记录里，每位报账人都要向行东交代。
senses.why: Before it named a profession, the word named anyone held to answer, and that duty is still the heart of the job.
senses.whyCN: 在成为职业名称之前，这个词指任何被要求作出交代的人；而这份责任至今仍是这行的核心。

intro.en: Accountant is not a Latin word but an English coinage: a reckoning noun plus the agent ending -ant.
intro.cn: accountant 不是拉丁语词，而是英语自造：一个表示「算账」的名词加表示施动者的词尾 -ant。

items.en: Computare, com- plus putare, meant to reckon together and to calculate.
items.cn: computare 由 com- 加 putare 构成，意为「合计、计算」。

items.en: Old French acont meant a reckoning and conter meant to recount, giving English both account and count.
items.cn: 古法语 acont 意为「结算」，conter 意为「叙述」，为英语提供了 account 与 count。

items.en: The noun account is recorded in English from the thirteenth century, at first with the sense of a reckoning or a story.
items.cn: 名词 account 自十三世纪见于英语，起初兼有「结算」与「叙述」两义。

items.en: The ending -ant comes from French and Latin present participles and marks the person who performs the action.
items.cn: 词尾 -ant 来自法语与拉丁语的现在分词，标记执行该动作的人。

items.en: Accountant appears in the fifteenth century; the chartered professional bodies that regulate the title date from the nineteenth.
items.cn: accountant 于十五世纪出现；规范这一头衔的注册会计师团体则始于十九世纪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the account family; the near-meaning group gathers the people who work with money records in different roles.
note.cn: 形近组收 account 词族的词；近义组收以不同角色与账目打交道的职业名称。

entries.definition: The record of money or the story of events; the base noun behind accountant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「账户、账目、叙述」，是 accountant 背后的基础名词。

entries.definition: The profession or practice of keeping and checking accounts; formed with -ancy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计职业、会计工作」，由本词加 -ancy 构成。

entries.definition: The activity or system of recording financial transactions; formed with -ing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「会计、记账」，指记录财务交易的活计或制度，由 account 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Required to explain one's actions to someone; formed from account with -able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负有责任的、须作出交代的」，由 account 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A person who records the daily transactions of a business, narrower than an accountant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「簿记员」，指记录企业日常交易的人，职责范围比会计师窄。

entries.definition: A person who independently checks the accounts of an organization and reports on them.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」，指独立核查机构账目并出具报告的人。

entries.definition: A senior financial officer who directs the accounting of a company.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务总监」，指主管公司会计工作的高级财务人员。

entries.definition: The officer of a club or public body who holds and pays out its money.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财务主管、司库」，指在社团或公共机构中保管并支付款项的人。

entries.definition: An office worker who keeps records or handles routine papers, including simple accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「职员、文书」，指保管记录或处理日常文书（含简单账目）的办公室人员。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real account root and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的 account 词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Account is the reckoning, and -ant marks the person who does it.
normal.cn: account 是「算账」，-ant 标记做这件事的人。

normal.en: The same -ant ending gives servant and assistant, all people in a role.
normal.cn: 同一个 -ant 词尾给出 servant 与 assistant，都是担着某个角色的人。

normal.en: Accountancy is the trade, accounting the activity, and accountant the person.
normal.cn: accountancy 是行业，accounting 是活计，accountant 是人。

normal.en: A chartered accountant is the British name for what Americans call a certified public accountant.
normal.cn: chartered accountant 是英国说法，对应美国的 certified public accountant。

normal.en: An auditor checks the accountant's work, so the two roles always stand side by side.
normal.cn: auditor 核查 accountant 的工作，两种角色总是并立。

abstract.en: Picture a desk lamp over columns of figures at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象午夜时分，一盏台灯照在成列的数字上。

abstract.en: The person is defined by the act: the reckoning is done, and so an accountant exists.
abstract.cn: 人由动作来定义：算账这件事发生了，会计也就存在了。

abstract.en: An accountant is not the ledger itself but the one who must answer for it.
abstract.cn: accountant 不是账簿本身，而是必须为它作出交代的那个人。

examples.en: Her father works as an accountant for a shipping company.
examples.cn: 她父亲在一家航运公司做会计。

examples.en: The accountant found two errors in the quarterly figures.
examples.cn: 会计在季度数字里发现了两处错误。

examples.en: Only a licensed accountant may sign the audit report.
examples.cn: 只有持证会计师才能签署审计报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿考恩坦特」——账本前一坐，数字数到天亮：会计

root: accountant 由英语名词 account「账目、算账」加表示施动者的后缀 -ant 构成，字面就是「做算账这件事的人」。account 又经古法语 acont 出自拉丁语 computare「合计、计算」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accountant all name the same core role under different duties: the general keeper of books, the licensed professional, the daily bookkeeper, the cost, management, tax and forensic specialists, and the older answerer of accounts.
sensesIntro.cn: accountant 的八个义项都是同一个核心角色在不同职责下的名字：总揽账目者、持证执业者、日常记账者、成本、管理、税务与法务专才，以及旧时须报账交代的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person sits at the ledger and checks every figure three times.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人坐在账簿前，把每一笔数字核对三遍。

branches.en: THE BOOKS: the general keeper and the daily bookkeeper both write the entries down.
branches.cn: 账簿线：总揽者与日常记账者都在把条目写下。

branches.en: THE LICENCE: a professional body turns the reckoner into a certified officer.
branches.cn: 执照线：行业团体把算账人变成持证执业者。

branches.en: THE FIGURES FOR USE: cost and management accounting turn records into decisions.
branches.cn: 数据致用线：成本会计与管理会计把记录变成决策。

branches.en: THE RULES: tax work reads the state's ledger, and forensic work reads it as evidence.
branches.cn: 规则线：税务工作读国家的账，法务工作把账读成证据。

branches.en: THE DUTY: the oldest sense is the person who must answer for what was entrusted.
branches.cn: 职责线：最古老的义项，是必须为受托之物作出交代的人。

intro.en: Accountant is a noun plus an agent ending; both parts are ordinary English building blocks rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: accountant 是名词加施动词尾；两部分都是普通的英语构件，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The base goes back to Latin computare, which is recorded; the agent ending -ant came through French from Latin participles.
latinIntro.cn: 其基础可追溯到有记录的拉丁语 computare；施动词尾 -ant 经法语来自拉丁语分词。

items.example: Its French form ac- stands at the front of account.
items.exampleCN: 它的法语形式 ac- 位于 account 的词首。

items.example: The verb is the reckoning root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「计算」词根。

items.example: The verb is the remote source of account.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 account 的远源。

items.meaning: a reckoning, a record, a story
items.example: The base noun carries the ledger image.
items.exampleCN: 基础名词带着账簿的画面。

items.example: It forms accountant from account.
items.exampleCN: 它使 account 构成 accountant。

items.example: It forms accountancy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accountancy。

items.example: It forms accounting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accounting。

items.example: It forms accountable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accountable。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ancy 构成，义为「会计职业」
由 account 加 -ing 构成，义为「会计；记账」
由 account 加 -able 构成，义为「负有责任的」

definition_zh: （利息、款项）累积、自然增长；（权利、利益）产生、归于；积累
definition_en: to increase gradually over time, especially money or interest, or to arise and become due as a right or benefit
core_image: 账本上的数字一点点往上爬，像水慢慢涨过刻度
scene: 老式银行的柜台前，一本存折摊开着，利息按月静静长高。Interest began to accrue on the deposit after the first month.
sceneCN: 这里 accrue 是「利息逐步累积」（第 1 个义项：利息或款项随时间增长）；句意为存款满一个月后，利息开始累积。

pos.zh: 不及物动词：（利息、利益）累积、增长
及物动词：积累、获得（权利、利益等）

derivatives.zh: 由动词 accrue 加名词后缀 -al 构成，义为「自然增长；应计额」
由动词加 -ed 构成形容词，义为「应计的；已累积的」
由动词加 -ment 构成名词，义为「累积的过程」，较少使用

senses.title: Of interest or money: to grow over time
senses.titleCN: 利息或款项随时间增长
senses.definition: to increase as interest or as an amount owed, usually gradually and without any action by the owner
senses.definitionCN: 作为利息或欠款逐步增加，通常不因所有者采取行动而发生
senses.example: Interest accrues on the loan from the day the money is drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款利息从提款当天起开始累积。
senses.why: The Latin root crescere means to grow, and ac- adds the idea of growth toward something, so the amount grows onto the balance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 crescere 意为「生长」，ac- 带「朝向」的意思，于是数额一点点长到账面上。

senses.title: To build up a store of something
senses.definition: to gather or increase gradually, especially benefits, experience, leave, or a store of useful things
senses.definitionCN: 逐步聚拢或增多，尤指益处、经验、假期或有用之物的积累
senses.example: Leave accrued week by week while she stayed on the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她留在项目上期间，假期一周周积累起来。
senses.why: A growing amount need not be money: anything that lies unused and adds up follows the same image of steady growth.
senses.whyCN: 增长的不一定是钱：任何闲置而不断加多的东西，都遵循同一个「稳步生长」的画面。

senses.title: Of a right or benefit: to arise and belong
senses.definition: to come into existence as a benefit or right that belongs to someone, often followed by to
senses.definitionCN: 作为属于某人的利益或权利而产生，常后接 to
senses.example: The right to compensation accrued to the workers after the ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 裁决之后，获得赔偿的权利归于工人。
senses.why: A benefit is pictured as growing on the side of its holder, until it stands there fully and belongs to that person.
senses.whyCN: 利益被想象成在其持有者这一侧生长，长成之后便稳稳地属于那个人。

senses.title: To incur a debt or charge
senses.definition: to come to owe money or to become liable for a charge through the passage of time or continued use
senses.definitionCN: 因时间推移或持续使用而欠下款项或承担费用
senses.example: A penalty of five dollars a day accrues if the form is late.
senses.exampleCN: 表格迟交，每天会产生五美元罚金。
senses.why: A debt also grows onto a person: nothing is paid, yet the amount owed keeps rising with each day.
senses.whyCN: 债务同样长在人身上：什么都没付，欠下的数额却随日子一天天升高。

senses.title: Of a fund: to be left to grow
senses.definition: of money or a fund, to be allowed to add up instead of being paid out, so that it grows larger
senses.definitionCN: 指钱或基金不被支出而任其累加，从而变得更多
senses.example: The trust lets income accrue instead of distributing it each year.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托让收益留存累积，而不是每年分配。
senses.why: Here the growth is intentional: the amount is left on the account precisely so that it keeps growing.
senses.whyCN: 这里的增长是有意为之：把数额留在账上，正是为了让它继续生长。

senses.title: To increase in amount or degree
senses.definition: to grow larger or greater in general, as of advantages, costs, pressure, or any measurable quantity
senses.definitionCN: 泛指变大或变多，如优势、成本、压力或任何可衡量的量
senses.example: The advantages of the new system accrued slowly over the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 新系统的优势在头一年里慢慢累积显现。
senses.why: The image of steady upward growth is not tied to money, so it extends to any quantity that builds up.
senses.whyCN: 「稳步上行」的画面并不绑定金钱，因此可延伸到任何逐渐加多的量。

senses.title: In accounting: to record an accrued item
senses.definition: in accounting, to record income or an expense in the period to which it relates, before any cash changes hands
senses.definitionCN: 会计上在收入或费用所属期间入账，此时现金尚未收付
senses.example: The accountant accrued the rent for December in the year-end books.
senses.exampleCN: 会计在年终账目里把十二月的租金记为应计项目。
senses.why: Accounting borrows the image of growth: the amount has built up during the period, so it is entered even before payment.
senses.whyCN: 会计借用了「生长」的画面：数额在该期间已经长成，所以即便未付款也要入账。

senses.title: Of a legal claim: to become complete
senses.titleCN: （法律请求权）成立；可强制执行
senses.definition: of a right of action, to become complete and enforceable once all the facts that support it have occurred
senses.definitionCN: 指诉权在全部支持事实发生后变得完整并可强制执行
senses.example: The claim for damages accrued when the contract was broken.
senses.exampleCN: 合同被违反时，损害赔偿请求权即告成立。
senses.why: A right is imagined as growing until it is full-grown, and only a full-grown right can be enforced in court.
senses.whyCN: 权利被想象成一个生长过程，长成之后才足够完整，能在法庭上强制执行。

intro.en: Accrue came to English through Old French, and its oldest recorded layer is the Latin verb for growing.
intro.cn: accrue 经古法语进入英语，它最古老的可考层次是表示「生长」的拉丁语动词。

items.en: The Latin verb crescere meant to grow, come into being, and increase; it also lies behind crescent and increase.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 crescere 意为「生长、形成、增加」，crescent 与 increase 也出自它。

items.en: Ad- plus crescere formed accrescere, to grow onto or be added to something. The prefix marks growth toward a thing.
items.cn: ad- 与 crescere 构成 accrescere，意为「长到某物之上、附加于某物」；前缀标记生长所朝向的对象。

items.en: Old French used acreue, the feminine past participle of acreistre, as a noun for growth, increase, or what has grown onto something.
items.cn: 古法语把动词 acreistre 的阴性过去分词 acreue 用作名词，表示「生长、增加、长出来的部分」。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the late fifteenth century, first as a noun and soon after as a verb. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪后期借入这个词，先作名词，随后作动词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The financial sense of interest growing on a sum fixed the word in everyday use, and law and accounting later borrowed the same image.
items.cn: 利息在款项上生长的金融义让这个词进入日常使用，法律与会计随后借用了同一个画面。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin root for growing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of piling up and of rights arising.
note.cn: 形近组收以拉丁语「生长」词根构成的一族词；近义组收表示堆积增多与权利产生的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the process of accumulating, or the amount that has accumulated, especially in accounting.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「累积过程、应计额」，多见于会计语境，由本词加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective for money or benefits that have built up but not yet been paid or received.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「应计的、已累积的」，指已积累但尚未收付的钱款或权益。

entries.definition: Growth by gradual addition from outside, as of sediment, ice, or capital; it shares the Latin root crescere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堆积、增积」，指外部物质或资本逐渐附着而增多，与本词同出拉丁语 crescere。

entries.definition: To grow together or be added gradually, used especially of land formed by deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐增长、附着形成」，多用于沉积形成的土地，与本词同根。

entries.definition: To become larger in size, number, or amount; the plain everyday verb of the same Latin family.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「增加、增大」，是同一拉丁词族中最日常的说法，不带金融色彩。

entries.definition: To gather or pile up more and more of something; it stresses deliberate collecting rather than natural growth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积累、堆积」，强调有意地收集，而非自然生长。

entries.definition: To collect a large amount of something, especially wealth or evidence, over a period of time.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积聚、搜集」，多指长期攒下大量财富或证据。

entries.definition: To increase steadily in amount or intensity, as of costs, pressure, or opposition.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「上升、增加」，多用于成本、压力或反对声浪的持续升高。

entries.definition: To come into being, as of a right, duty, or problem; close to accrue in its legal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「产生、出现」，可用于权利、义务或问题，在法律语境中与 accrue 相近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin root for growing and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「生长」词根，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Crescere is to grow: accrue is what happens when an amount quietly grows on a balance.
normal.cn: crescere 是「生长」：accrue 就是数额在账面上悄悄长大的过程。

normal.en: The prefix ac- is a form of ad-, meaning toward, so the growth is directed onto something.
normal.cn: 前缀 ac- 是 ad- 的变体，意为「朝向」，所以这种生长是长到某物之上的。

normal.en: Accrued interest is the standard banking phrase for interest that has built up but not yet been paid.
normal.cn: accrued interest 是银行业的标准说法，指已经积累但尚未支付的利息。

normal.en: Accrue to is the pattern used when a right or benefit falls to a person.
normal.cn: accrue to 是权利或利益落到某人身上时使用的固定结构。

normal.en: The same root gives increase and crescent, both about getting bigger.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 increase 与 crescent，两者都与变大有关。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger page where one line rises a hair each night, like water in a glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一页账簿，其中一行每晚悄悄升高一点，像杯中的水。

abstract.en: Nothing is added by hand: the number grows because time passes, and that is the whole idea.
abstract.cn: 没有人手动加数：数字变大只因时间流逝，这就是全部要点。

abstract.en: The same quiet rise can be a debt, a right, or a pile of leave days, not only money.
abstract.cn: 同样安静的上升可以是债务、权利或一堆假期，并不限于金钱。

examples.en: Interest accrues daily on any unpaid balance.
examples.cn: 任何未付余额都按日计息。

examples.en: Benefits accrue to the whole village once the well is finished.
examples.cn: 水井建成后，整个村子都会受益。

examples.en: She let her holiday pay accrue until the end of the year.
examples.cn: 她把假期工资攒到年底再一并领取。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿库鲁」——阿库的账户，利息一点点长高：累积、生息

root: 拉丁语 accrescere「长到、附加」由 ad-「朝向」+ crescere「生长」构成；古法语 acreue 是其过去分词形式的名词化，意为「增长、长出的部分」。crescere 一般认为与 crescent、increase 同源，更早的印欧语形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accrue all picture something growing onto a base: interest, leave, rights, debts, a fund, general quantities, accounting entries, and legal claims.
sensesIntro.cn: accrue 的八个义项都在描绘某物长到某个基底之上：利息、假期、权利、债务、基金、一般数量、会计项目与法律请求权。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure on a ledger climbs a little each day, with no hand adding to it.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上的数字每天自己往上爬一点，没有手在加数。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: interest or fund income grows on a balance that is left alone.
branches.cn: 账目线：利息或基金收益在被搁置的余额上自行生长。

branches.en: THE STORE: anything left to add up, from leave days to advantages, follows the same quiet rise.
branches.cn: 积蓄线：凡是任其累加的东西，从假期到优势，都遵循同一种安静的上升。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: a benefit or claim grows on its holder's side until it is complete and enforceable.
branches.cn: 权利线：利益或请求权在持有者一侧生长，直到完整并可强制执行。

branches.en: THE DEBT: an unpaid charge grows onto a person day by day.
branches.cn: 债务线：未付的费用逐日长到一个人身上。

branches.en: THE BOOKS: accounting records the amount in the period when it has built up, before cash moves.
branches.cn: 账簿线：会计在数额已经长成的期间入账，此时现金尚未流动。

intro.en: Accrue is a French borrowing whose core is the Latin verb for growing; English adds ordinary suffixes to make its family.
intro.cn: accrue 是法语借词，其核心是表示「生长」的拉丁语动词；英语再用普通后缀扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin crescere, accrescere and accretio are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crescere、accrescere 与 accretio 均有文献记录，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: The prefix directs the growth toward the thing that grows.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「生长」指向所生长的对象。

items.example: The verb is the growing root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的「生长」词根。

items.meaning: to grow onto, be added to
items.example: The compound is the direct Latin source of accrue.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是 accrue 的直接拉丁语来源。

items.example: Its past participle gave the French noun for growth.
items.exampleCN: 它的过去分词给出了表示「增长」的法语名词。

items.example: It forms accrual.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accrual。

items.example: It forms accrued.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accrued。

items.example: It forms accretion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accretion。

items.example: It forms increase on the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它与同一词根构成 increase。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「自然增长；应计额」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「应计的；已累积的」
由本词加 -ment 构成，义为「累积过程」，较少使用

definition_zh: 积累；积聚；堆积；逐渐增加
definition_en: to gather or pile up more and more of something over time, so that it grows in amount
core_image: 硬币、沙粒一层层往上堆，堆成一座越来越高的堆
scene: 旧书房的角落里，纸箱一层层摞起来，灰尘落在箱顶。Dust and old letters accumulate in the attic year after year.
sceneCN: 这里 accumulate 是「堆积、积聚」（第 1 个义项：物品逐渐聚拢成堆）；句意为灰尘和旧信件年复一年堆积在阁楼上。

pos.zh: 及物动词：积累、积聚（财富、知识、证据）
不及物动词：堆积、逐渐增多

derivatives.zh: 由动词 accumulate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由动词加 -ive 构成形容词，义为「累积的；渐增的」
由动词加 -or 构成施动名词，义为「积累者；蓄能器、累加器」

senses.title: Of objects: to pile up
senses.definition: to gather into a pile or mass, as of things left in one place over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 聚拢成一堆或一团，如物品长期留置在一处
senses.example: Snow accumulated against the barn door.
senses.exampleCN: 雪在谷仓门口堆积起来。
senses.why: Latin cumulus is a heap, and the verb pictures one thing added to another until a heap stands there.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cumulus 意为「堆」，这个动词描绘的是一物加到另一物上，直到堆成形。

senses.title: To gather valuable things over time
senses.definition: to collect or acquire an increasing amount of something valuable, usually over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期收集或获得越来越多有价值的东西
senses.example: He accumulated a fortune through thirty years of quiet saving.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠三十年安静的储蓄积攒了一笔财富。
senses.why: A fortune is a heap in another form: each coin added makes the heap a little higher.
senses.whyCN: 财富是另一种形态的堆：每加一枚硬币，堆就高一点。

senses.title: To increase as a total
senses.definition: to rise in total amount, number, or degree as more is added over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着更多部分加入，总量、数目或程度上升
senses.example: Debts accumulated faster than the family could pay them.
senses.exampleCN: 债务累积的速度快过这个家庭的偿付能力。
senses.why: Once things are added one by one, the sum itself grows, which is the plainest reading of the heap image.
senses.whyCN: 东西一件件加上去之后，总和本身就会变大，这是「堆」的画面最直白的读法。

senses.title: Of evidence or knowledge: to build up
senses.definition: to collect facts, data, or experience until enough is present for use or for proof
senses.definitionCN: 收集事实、数据或经验，直到数量足够可供使用或论证
senses.example: Researchers accumulated evidence for twenty years before the theory was accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者积累了二十年证据，理论才被接受。
senses.why: Knowledge behaves like objects on a pile: single facts are small, but the heap they make can support a conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 知识像堆上的物件：单个事实很小，但它们堆起来就能支撑一个结论。

senses.title: Of dust or dirt: to settle and gather
senses.definition: of dust, dirt, scale, or a similar substance, to settle and gather in a place where nothing removes it
senses.definitionCN: 指灰尘、污垢、水垢等沉积聚集在无人清理的地方
senses.example: Dust accumulated on the shelves while the house stood empty.
senses.exampleCN: 房子空着的时候，灰尘在架子上积了厚厚一层。
senses.why: Even unwanted matter follows the heap image: it settles where nothing removes it, and the layer deepens.
senses.whyCN: 即便是不受欢迎的东西也遵循「堆」的画面：它落在无人清理处，层就越来越厚。

senses.title: Of interest or charges: to add up
senses.definition: of interest, charges, or unpaid amounts, to add up on a sum that has not been cleared
senses.definitionCN: 指利息、费用或未付款项在未结清的数额上不断累加
senses.example: Unpaid fines accumulated until they exceeded the original fine.
senses.exampleCN: 未缴的罚款不断累计，最后超过了最初的金额。
senses.why: Money owed behaves like dust: left alone, it settles and thickens on the account.
senses.whyCN: 欠下的钱像灰尘：放着不管，就在账面上沉积、变厚。

senses.title: To amass power or control
senses.titleCN: 权力或控制权不断积聚
senses.definition: to gain more and more power, influence, or control, often gradually and without open conflict
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐获得越来越多的权力、影响力或控制权，往往不通过公开冲突
senses.example: The director accumulated control over every department in the company.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主管逐步掌握了公司每个部门的控制权。
senses.why: Influence is a heap too: each appointment, favour, or piece of information adds another layer to it.
senses.whyCN: 影响力也是一座堆：每一次任命、人情或消息，都给它添上一层。

senses.title: Of a fund: to reinvest income
senses.definition: of a fund or account, to let income be added to the capital instead of being paid out to investors
senses.definitionCN: 指基金或账户把收益并入本金，而不是支付给投资者
senses.example: The fund accumulates its income rather than distributing it to investors.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金把收益滚存再投，而不是分配给投资者。
senses.why: Here the heap feeds itself: what it earns is put back on top, so the pile grows faster.
senses.whyCN: 这里堆会自己喂养自己：赚到的部分又被放回顶上，于是堆长得更快。

intro.en: Accumulate is a Latin borrowing built directly on the noun for a heap.
intro.cn: accumulate 是直接建立在「堆」这一名词之上的拉丁语借词。

items.en: A cumulus was a heap, pile, or mass. The same word names the rounded cumulus cloud, which looks like a heap in the sky.
items.cn: 拉丁语 cumulus 意为「堆、垛、团块」，同一个词也用来命名天空里像一堆棉花的积云。

items.en: From cumulus came the verb cumulare, to heap up or pile on, already used for both physical and figurative piling.
items.cn: 由 cumulus 生出动词 cumulare，意为「堆起、堆积」，既用于实物，也已用于比喻性堆积。

items.en: Ad- plus cumulare formed accumulare, to heap up, add to a heap, or increase by repeated addition.
items.cn: ad- 与 cumulare 构成 accumulare，意为「堆起、加到堆上、靠反复添加而增多」。

items.en: English took the verb from Latin in the fifteenth or early sixteenth century. The exact first written date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪或十六世纪初从拉丁语借入这个动词；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The idea of a heap widened from objects to knowledge, evidence, money, and power, so the word now covers nearly any gradual build-up.
items.cn: 「堆」的观念从实物扩展到知识、证据、金钱与权力，如今几乎涵盖一切逐渐累积之物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the cumulus family and its Latin-derived relatives; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of collecting and growing.
note.cn: 形近组收 cumulus 词族及其拉丁语派生词；近义组收表示收集与增多的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of building up, or the mass that has been built up.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「积累、堆积」或「堆积物」，由本词加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning tending to build up or growing by repeated addition.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「累积的、渐增的」，由本词加 -ive 构成。

entries.definition: A person or device that collects and stores something, such as a battery cell or a computing register.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「积累者、蓄能器、累加器」，由本词加 -or 构成。

entries.definition: Increasing by successive additions, as of effects or marks; it comes straight from Latin cumulus.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「累积的、渐增的」，指效果或分数逐次相加，直接出自拉丁语 cumulus。

entries.definition: A heap or mass in Latin, and in English the name of a rounded white cloud.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中意为「堆」，英语里指圆顶的积云，是本词词根。

entries.definition: To collect a very large amount of something, especially wealth or information, usually on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「积聚、搜集」，多指有意攒下大量财富或信息，规模感比 accumulate 更强。

entries.definition: To bring things or people together in one place; it stresses the bringing rather than the resulting pile.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「聚拢、收集」，强调把东西或人聚到一处，而不强调最终堆成多高。

entries.definition: To store a supply secretly or greedily, often more than one needs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「囤积、秘藏」，常指超出所需地藏起物资，带负面色彩。

entries.definition: To grow by itself over time, especially interest; it stresses natural growth rather than active piling.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「累积、生息」，多用于利息，强调自然生长而非主动堆积。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin noun for a heap and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁语「堆」名词，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Cumulus is a heap: accumulate is simply to keep adding until a heap exists.
normal.cn: cumulus 是「堆」：accumulate 就是不断往上加，直到堆出现。

normal.en: The same root gives cumulative, where marks or effects add up one after another.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 cumulative，分数或效果一个接一个相加。

normal.en: Accumulate wealth and accumulate knowledge both use the image of a growing store.
normal.cn: accumulate wealth 与 accumulate knowledge 都使用「储藏越积越多」的画面。

normal.en: Dust accumulating on a shelf is the plainest physical version of the word.
normal.cn: 灰尘在架子上积存，是这个词最直白的实物版本。

normal.en: Accumulated over time is the phrase that marks the slow, repeated addition.
normal.cn: accumulated over time 标出的正是缓慢而反复的添加过程。

abstract.en: Picture a table where coins are dropped one at a time, and nobody counts until the pile is tall.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上一次落下一枚硬币，没人去数，直到堆得很高。

abstract.en: The pile can be made of facts, years, debts or influence; the shape of growth is the same.
abstract.cn: 这座堆可以由事实、年头、债务或影响力组成，生长的形状都一样。

abstract.en: Nothing disappears in accumulation: every small addition stays, and that is why the total surprises people.
abstract.cn: 积累中没有东西消失：每一次小小的添加都留着，所以最后的总量常让人吃惊。

examples.en: Dust accumulates quickly in a room that is never opened.
examples.cn: 从不通风的房间里灰尘积得很快。

examples.en: She accumulated enough experience to lead the team within three years.
examples.cn: 三年内她积累了足够的经验来带领团队。

examples.en: Interest on the unpaid loan continued to accumulate each month.
examples.cn: 未偿还贷款的利息每月继续累积。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿丘缪累」——阿丘的麦堆越堆越高，累得直不起腰：堆积、积累

root: 拉丁语 accumulare「堆起」由 ad-「向、加到」+ cumulare「堆积」构成，cumulare 出自 cumulus「堆、垛」；cumulus 也是气象学中积云 cumulus 的名称来源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of accumulate all come from one heap: objects, valuables, totals, knowledge, dust, charges, power, and reinvested income.
sensesIntro.cn: accumulate 的八个义项都出自同一座「堆」：物件、财富、总量、知识、灰尘、费用、权力与滚存收益。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: small units are added one by one until they form a visible heap.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个个小单位不断加上去，最终堆成看得见的一堆。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL PILE: snow, boxes, or dust settles layer by layer where nothing clears it.
branches.cn: 实物线：雪、纸箱或灰尘在无人清理处一层层沉积。

branches.en: THE STORE: wealth and knowledge are heaps of small gains that stay and add up.
branches.cn: 储藏线：财富与知识都是由细小的获得物留下并相加而成的堆。

branches.en: THE TOTAL: once units are added, the sum itself rises without any single jump.
branches.cn: 总量线：单位加上去之后，总和本身上升，没有哪一次是跳跃。

branches.en: THE MONEY LINE: unpaid charges thicken on the account, while a fund puts its own earnings back on top.
branches.cn: 钱款线：未付费用在账面上变厚，基金则把自己的收益放回顶上。

branches.en: THE POWER LINE: each favour, post, or piece of information adds another layer of control.
branches.cn: 权力线：每一次人情、职位或消息，都添上一层控制力。

intro.en: Accumulate is Latin through and through: a prefix, a noun for a heap, and a verb suffix.
intro.cn: accumulate 完全来自拉丁语：一个前缀、一个表示「堆」的名词、一个动词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin cumulus, cumulare and accumulare are all recorded, so the family needs no reconstruction beyond the Indo-European layer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cumulus、cumulare 与 accumulare 均有文献记录，除印欧语层外无需重构。

items.example: The prefix adds the idea of piling onto something.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀加上「往上堆积」的意思。

items.example: The noun is the picture behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整族词背后的画面。

items.example: The verb turns the heap into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「堆」变成动作。

items.meaning: to heap up, add to a heap
items.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It marks the English verb formed on the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它标记由拉丁词干形成的英语动词。

items.example: It forms accumulation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accumulation。

items.example: It forms accumulative.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accumulative。

items.example: It forms accumulator.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 accumulator。

latinEntries.meaning: to heap up, add to a heap

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「积累；堆积物」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「累积的；渐增的」
由本词加 -or 构成，义为「积累者；蓄能器、累加器」

definition_zh: 准确；精确；准确度；正确性
definition_en: the quality of being correct and exact, or the degree to which a measurement, statement, or result matches the truth
core_image: 一支箭稳稳落在靶心，不偏分毫
scene: 测量室里，一支铅笔在图纸上标出靶心一样的圆点。The engineer checked the accuracy of every reading before signing the report.
sceneCN: 这里 accuracy 是「准确度」（第 1 个义项：结果与真实情况相符的性质）；句意为工程师在签字前核对了每个读数的准确度。

pos.zh: 名词：准确、精确；准确度、正确性

derivatives.zh: 由 accuracy 去掉名词后缀 -cy 得到的形容词，义为「准确的、精确的」
由形容词 accurate 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「准确地、精确地」
由 accuracy 加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「不准确；误差之处」
由形容词 accurate 加 -ness 构成，义为「精确性」，较少使用

senses.title: The quality of being correct
senses.definition: the quality of being right, with no mistakes or errors in the facts
senses.definitionCN: 在事实层面正确、没有错误或差错的性质
senses.example: The accuracy of her account was confirmed by three witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的陈述的准确性得到三名证人的确认。
senses.why: Latin cura means care, and accurate meant done with care; when care is taken at every step, the result comes out right.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 cura 意为「关心、用心」，accurate 原指「用心做成的」；每一步都用心，结果自然正确。

senses.title: Exactness in measurement
senses.definition: the degree to which a measurement, instrument, or calculation matches the true value
senses.definitionCN: 测量、仪器或计算结果与真实值相符的程度
senses.example: The accuracy of the scale matters when the doses are so small.
senses.exampleCN: 剂量如此微小，天平的精确度很关键。
senses.why: A measure is like an arrow: the closer it lands to the true mark, the more accuracy it has.
senses.whyCN: 测量像一支箭：落点离真实靶心越近，准确度就越高。

senses.title: Precision in aiming or movement
